chapters.title: Chapter 251: Not That Easy ...
paragraphs: Seris looked at the map.
"This map hasn’t written anything specific about Glassthorn Forest. That means either there was no significant danger here, or the map’s creator didn’t find anything worth recording." Lian continued.

Of course, his information was not only based on a map. In the very limited reports of the tribe that he had read, he had also not been able to find any information about anything specific in this forest.
It wasn’t like he was going to completely ignore it. If they managed to find an opportunity or a special location, they would definitely explore it, but only if they found it.
Otherwise, they would continue on their path and set their main goal as reaching the first evolution and the Emberroot civilization.
"After that?" Seris asked.
"Then we enter Emberroot." Lian moved his finger toward the east.
"What’s there?"
"According to the notes, the largest remaining civilization in this world."
This time, Seris looked at the eastern part of the map with more interest.
Lian recounted all the information he had and then pointed at the mark again.
"But first, we need to find out what this point is. Whoever made this map didn’t mark it for no reason."
"So we hunt, reach the mark, and then go after the civilization." The young Pendragon summarized.
"Exactly."
Lian folded the map, but before moving, he felt One’s exhaustion through Hive Link.
The ant had moved almost non-stop since entering the Giants’ Graveyard, had been forced to run at full speed several times.
The Warden’s chain had caught its leg, the bridge had collapsed under its feet, and the graveyard’s inherent pressure had affected its instincts from the start.
Now that they had left that area, the real exhaustion was showing.
One’s muscle movement had slowed down, its energy reserve had decreased, and even though it tried to hide its weakness, Lian could feel the heaviness of every step through the link.
"We rest first."
Seris did not object. They stopped next to one of the largest trees around.
The tree’s transparent roots had come out of the ground and intertwined in crystalline arches.
Between them, there was a semi-enclosed space protected from three sides by the roots.
The trees in this forest were not as massive as in the Forest of Giants, and on the contrary, they were of standard size.
Before entering, Lian examined the environment with Predator’s Instincts. His vision changed.
The flow of Mana in the environment became clear. The trees of Glassthorn were alive like other plants, but their life was different from normal plants.
Mana moved like sap inside their transparent trunks. Sometimes the flows were calm, and sometimes due to the wind or the movement of a creature nearby, their light would intensify.
Lian looked for a few more seconds. If these trees were in the Ruined Realm, they could be a great source for mages.
A small creature passed behind a tree in the distance. At that same moment, the blue vein inside the trunk near it became brighter for a moment.
So the trees reacted to the presence of Mana. This reaction might not have been intentional, but it could reveal the location of creatures.
He remembered this point. After being relatively sure the environment was safe, they entered the space between the roots.
One sat on the ground. Its large body came down with exhaustion, and its antennae rested on the soil.
Lian took out a few pieces of healthy meat from his storage space and placed them in front of One.
The ant immediately went toward them and swallowed the first piece almost whole.
Seris sat next to one of the roots.
She placed her sword on her legs and calmly examined the blade’s edge. A few shallow scratches could be seen on her armor.
A small part of her shoulder guard had also cracked in the battle with the Doppelgängers.
"Were you wounded?" Lian asked.
"No." The silver-haired girl answered without looking up.
The Vorhelm pointed at the cut on her armor.
"Then what’s that?"
Seris gave a brief look at her shoulder.
"The armor is wounded.
"I meant under the armor."
"No."
A few seconds of silence passed between them, and Seris this time looked at Lian’s forearm, the same hand that had deflected the Warden’s blade strike with Ossuary Armor.
"What about you?"
Lian opened and closed his fingers a few times. The numbness had still not completely gone away.
"My hand is still numb."
"Then use your other hand." The Pendragon answered seriously.
He stared at her for a few moments. There was no sign of joking on Seris’s face. She probably really thought she had offered a suitable solution.
"Thanks, problem solved." Lian said.
"Good."
Lian also sat next to a root, allowing his muscles to relax slightly.
But part of his attention remained on the environment.
It was true that this forest was not a threat to them like the Forest of Giants, but here too, there were its own threats in different forms.
In a forest where distance, light, and even the direction of sound could not be trusted, deep sleep or rest was not a wise decision.
About half an hour later, One had recovered most of its energy.
The feeling of exhaustion was still there, but walking and short fights were not difficult for it.
Lian stood up, and Seris also sheathed her sword and stood up.
This time, neither of them sat on One’s back.
Lian preferred to move beside the ant. In the dense space of Glassthorn Forest, quick reaction on the ground was easier.
They began the journey. With every step, the difference between the Forest of Giants and this place became clearer.
Here, sound came from all directions. The collision of glass leaves, the wind’s flow, the movement of small creatures inside the trunks.
The sound of drops falling from the branches and shattering like crystal upon hitting the ground.
But no sound kept its real path. The sound of their own footsteps was sometimes heard from the front.
Sometimes from the left, sometimes it would return from behind a few seconds after their movement.
Light broke in the trunks and threw reflections in different directions. One’s image was sometimes seen a few meters ahead on a tree’s surface.
Then it would appear on another tree on the right.
Once, Lian saw Seris’s image moving behind a trunk, while the real Seris was walking right to his left.
"Be careful not to attack the reflections." Lian said without stopping.
Seris looked at her own image moving on a distant trunk.
"Even if they attack?"
"Then it’s not a reflection at all, just a monster."
She nodded. The answer was satisfying for her.
They moved for almost an hour without directly encountering a large monster.
But One stopped several times, sending a sense of danger through Hive Link. The problem was that it couldn’t determine the direction either.
A creature’s smell came from the right, the sound of movement was heard from the left, but the Mana pressure was sometimes felt from above and sometimes from behind.
Due to the glass and reflections, tracking danger had become terribly difficult for them. Even their intuition and senses were working with difficulty.
Now they realized that even this forest, contrary to their initial impression, could be dangerous and... annoying.
"At this rate, we could be attacked at any moment without even realizing it." Lian reduced their speed.
The flows of Mana could be seen among the trees.
But unlike the Forest of Giants, here the environmental Mana was much higher. The light inside the trunks not only disrupted normal vision but also Mana detection.
Every flow was reflected several times, and every energy source created several false images in different points.
"Shhhhhhhhhh..." The sound of breaking glass was heard from the right.
Seris drew her sword.
A semi-transparent creature appeared behind one of the trees for a moment.
Its body resembled a large wolf, but it had longer shoulders and thinner legs.
Its skin was transparent, and its blue bones and organs could be seen through its crystalline skin.
Its eyes shone like two purple crystals.
The young girl turned in that direction, but the creature disappeared, and its image appeared on the trunk of another tree on the left.
Then another image.
Then one in front.
Within seconds, dozens of pairs of crystal eyes were watching them from among the trees.
"Are these reflections or real?" She looked at Lian.
And at that same time, a panel appeared before both of their views.
[Prismfang Stalker]
[Level: 18]
[Rank: Normal]
"I guess both?" Lian focused on them, but every body had several Mana flows.
The reflections were not only optical images. The semi-transparent bodies of the creatures also bent the energy and reflected the Mana trace on the surrounding trunks.
And the problem was that even the blood flow in this damn forest was reflected.
Literally, how was such a thing even possible?
For the first time, Predator’s Instincts could not immediately identify the real body. Neither the monster’s mana flow nor its blood flow could be distinguished.
"Which one is real?" Seris raised her sword.
Lian turned his gaze among the reflections.
"You might not believe it, but I have no idea."
"All my senses are useless here, nothing can really be identified."
"Then I’ll hit all of them." The young girl channeled mana into her blade.
"I guess this time we have no choice but to follow your solution." Lian gave her a brief look, he agreed too.
If they couldn’t find the real one, they just had to destroy all of them.
"My solutions have always worked."
One of the Stalkers moved, its image jumped from the right to the front.
But Lian felt the change in air pressure on the left. The real body came out from behind a trunk.
Its transparent jaw opened.
Its prismatic teeth refracted the blue light and came directly toward his forearm.
[Diamond Skin]
The skin on his forearm took on a metallic shine. The monster’s teeth hit it, and a bright spark exploded between them.
The Stalker could not break his skin, but the pressure of its jaw was more than what he expected from Level 18.
Lian turned his hand to grab the creature’s neck, but the monster immediately pulled back.
Its body faded among the lights, and several images scattered in different directions.
Lian activated Echo Adaptation.
[Echo Adaptation Activated.]
[Primary Target Selected: Prismfang Stalker.]
[Analysis: 12%]

This time, he did not only look at the creature itself. He looked at the environment. The lights inside the trees, the changes in the shadows, the intensity of the reflections, and the moment when the real body was placed in the path of one of the light currents.
No matter how annoying this forest might be and how much it tried to disrupt his senses, it didn’t matter. He would always have his ways of dealing with any situation.
Anyway, hunting here was not going to be as easy as they had thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 252: Annoying Monsters
paragraphs: Another monster suddenly prepared to attack from a tree branch.
Its image was seen on three branches, but just before the jump, the blue light inside the trunk behind it went dark for a fraction of a second.
The real body had blocked the light. The reflections did not have this effect.
Lian stepped aside, and the Stalker’s claw passed by his face.
[Analysis: 21%]
The Stalker landed on the ground and faded again. Three other creatures moved among the trees at the same time.
Their images shattered on dozens of surfaces.
"Did you figure anything out?" Seris kept her sword ready. It was clear that even she was not satisfied with the current situation.
Their opponents were extremely weak, but with the help of the environment, they had caused them to lose all their senses and instincts, and they had no idea what they were fighting.
Every strike they made hit nothing, as if they were fighting illusions and air.
To the point that it was becoming so annoying that even Seris was slowly losing her patience.
"When the real body is in front of the light flow, the trunk goes dark for a moment." Lian said quietly.
"But which trunk?" The young girl’s eyes moved over the trees.
Lian focused Echo Adaptation on the Stalker. The purple light in the second tree on the right dimmed for a moment.
"Three o’clock. Behind the second tree."
Seris moved without seeing the enemy.
[King’s Edge]
Mana was compressed on her sword’s edge. She stepped forward and sent a horizontal strike. The blade did not hit the transparent trunk.
At that same moment, the Prismfang Stalker came out from behind the tree.
Seris’s sword went directly into its side. The transparent body was split in half, and a blue liquid splashed on the soil.
The creature rolled a few meters on the ground and remained motionless. Its reflected images disappeared at the same time.
"Finally!"
[Analysis: 39%]
The second Stalker jumped from a high branch toward Lian. This time, he saw the darkening light before the attack.
Thunder Step was activated, and an explosion of lightning formed among the trees.
Lian moved out of the attack path and appeared on a higher branch.
Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his hand.
The Stalker was still in the air when the ice claw landed on its neck.
The cold spread through its transparent body. Its legs and spine froze in an instant, and its body stuck to the branch.
One jumped from below. Its massive jaws closed around the frozen body, and with one squeeze, the Stalker was shattered into several pieces of ice and broken crystal.
Two other creatures attacked at the same time.
One from the front, the other from behind Seris. At least that was what the eye could see.
The first image jumped directly toward her chest. The young Pendragon made no defensive move.
The image passed through her body and shattered on the trunk behind her... it was a reflection.
The real creature attacked from the left a moment later.
Seris, without fully turning her body, lowered her sword. The blade passed through the transparent Stalker’s jaw and went up to its neck.
The monster fell on the ground with a sound like a glass goblet shattering.
"Did you know which one was real from the start?" Lian gave her a brief look.
"Reflections don’t have a smell." Seris shook the blue blood off her blade.
"When did you realize that?"
"Just now."
A deep roar echoed in the forest. The reflections trembled for a moment. All the remaining Stalkers stepped back.
Not to flee, but as if to open a path. A faint light moved among the trunks.
Something larger was slowly approaching. Its body was taller and more muscular than the other Stalkers.
Its skin was more transparent, so much so that from some angles, it almost completely disappeared. Golden and purple veins flowed inside its body.
Its teeth were longer, and prismatic blades had grown along its spine.
Its panel appeared.
[Prismfang Alpha]
[Level: 21]
[Rank: Normal]
The Alpha lowered its head, and its reflection appeared on all the surrounding trees.
Dozens of identical bodies, some on the ground, some on the branches, and some even standing on the transparent trunks in a direction opposite to gravity.
This time, not only the creature’s body was reflected, but its movements were also repeated several times.
The Alpha raised its right claw. At that same moment, dozens of glowing lines resembling claws moved toward them from different angles.
Lian kept Predator’s Instincts active. Most of the attacks were only light reflections, but identifying the real claw among them was not easy.
"Be careful, this one knows even better how to use the environment." He then warned.
The other monsters could use the environment to some extent, but they had obvious weaknesses. However, this Alpha knew much better how to use the environment.
Seris stepped back and held her sword in front of her body.
A few light lines passed by her. One hit her armor and created a scratch on it.
Only one was real.
The Alpha changed its path at that same moment. Instead of Lian or Seris, it moved toward One.
It had probably detected the remaining exhaustion in the ant’s body.
One opened its jaws, but still did not know which direction the attack would come from.
"You thought only you could do it? Two can play that game!" Lian whispered mockingly and activated False Presence.
[False Presence]
A few meters away, a false presence of One formed. The sound of six legs moving on the ground, the smell of the ant’s body, and a weak Mana Signature.
The Alpha turned its head toward the false presence for a fraction of a second.
Its body changed its path, but stopped before completing the attack.
Its prismatic eyes narrowed. The false presence had no natural shadow. Its weight pressure on the ground was not felt.
The Alpha had noticed the difference.
False Presence had not been able to completely fool it, but that fraction of a second was enough.
Seris raised her sword.
[Silver Requiem]
The blade’s movement disappeared from view. Dozens of silver strikes appeared in the space around the Alpha, and each cut collided with one of the attack’s reflections.
The false lines broke, the deflected lights collapsed, and for a moment, only the Alpha’s real body remained.
Lian also did not miss the opportunity and moved.
[Iron Fortress Charge]
Force gathered in his legs and shoulder. He hit the Alpha’s side at high speed.
The monster’s semi-transparent body was lifted off the ground and thrown through two trees into a more open space. A few glass branches shattered under its weight.
Before falling completely, the Alpha spun its body and landed on four legs.
But One had already moved. The ant lunged at it, and its jaws closed around the Alpha’s back leg.
The monster roared and brought its claws down on One’s head. The ant’s shell developed shallow cracks.
But One did not let go.
Lian activated Thunder Step. Blue lightning ran on the ground, and he appeared right in front of the Alpha.
Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his hand.
The Alpha raised its free claw. Several light reflections were created along with it.
Echo Adaptation had now seen enough of the species’ movement patterns.
"Your tricks won’t work anymore."
Lian identified the real point before the attack was complete. He lowered his body, and the Alpha’s claw passed over his head.
He sank Glacial Reaper Claw directly into the monster’s transparent chest. The cold spread through its body.
The light inside its organs went out. The ice spread from its chest to its neck and legs.
The Alpha tried to pull back, but One was still holding its leg.
It had no chance to escape!
A crack formed in the center of the monster’s chest, then a second crack, and then dozens of cracks ran through its entire transparent body.
Lian turned the claw. The Prismfang Alpha’s body collapsed from the inside.
The crystalline pieces fell on the ground. The reflected lights in the entire forest went out.
The remaining Stalkers remained motionless for a few moments upon seeing the Alpha’s death, then scattered among the trees without trying to continue the battle.
Lian did not chase them. Their goal was hunting, but entering a deeper ambush for a few Level 17 or 18 creatures was not worth it.
System notifications appeared.
[You have slain Prismfang Stalker Lv.17.]
[You have slain Prismfang Stalker Lv.18.]
[You have slain Prismfang Stalker Lv.18.]
[You have slain Prismfang Alpha Lv.21.]
[Bloodlust has absorbed 100% of the available exp.]
[Due to group kill, the EXP received is halved.]

The young Pendragon made no defensive move.
The image passed through her body and shattered on the trunk behind her... it was a reflection.
The real creature attacked from the left a moment later.
Seris, without fully turning her body, lowered her sword.
The blade passed through the transparent Stalker’s jaw and went up to its neck.
The monster fell on the ground with a sound like a glass goblet shattering.
"Did you know which one was real from the start?" Lian gave her a brief look.
"Reflections don’t have a smell." Seris shook the blue blood off her blade.
"When did you realize that?"
"Just now."
A deep roar echoed in the forest.
The reflections trembled for a moment.
All the remaining Stalkers stepped back.
Not to flee, but as if to open a path.
A faint light moved among the trunks.
Something larger was slowly approaching.
Its body was taller and more muscular than the other Stalkers.
Its skin was more transparent, so much so that from some angles, it almost completely disappeared.
Golden and purple veins flowed inside its body.
Its teeth were longer, and prismatic blades had grown along its spine.
Its panel appeared.
[Prismfang Alpha]
[Level: 21]
[Rank: Normal]
The Alpha lowered its head, and its reflection appeared on all the surrounding trees.
Dozens of identical bodies, some on the ground, some on the branches, and some even standing on the transparent trunks in a direction opposite to gravity.
This time, not only the creature’s body was reflected, but its movements were also repeated several times.
The Alpha raised its right claw.
At that same moment, dozens of glowing lines resembling claws moved toward them from different angles.
Lian kept Predator’s Instincts active.
Most of the attacks were only light reflections, but identifying the real claw among them was not easy.
"Be careful, this one knows even better how to use the environment." He then warned.
The other monsters could use the environment to some extent, but they had obvious weaknesses.
However, this Alpha knew much better how to use the environment.
Seris stepped back and held her sword in front of her body.
A few light lines passed by her.
One hit her armor and created a scratch on it.
Only one was real.
The Alpha changed its path at that same moment.
Instead of Lian or Seris, it moved toward One.
It had probably detected the remaining exhaustion in the ant’s body.
One opened its jaws, but still did not know which direction the attack would come from.
"You thought only you could do it?
Two can play that game!" Lian whispered mockingly and activated False Presence.
[False Presence]
A few meters away, a false presence of One formed.
The sound of six legs moving on the ground, the smell of the ant’s body, and a weak Mana Signature.
The Alpha turned its head toward the false presence for a fraction of a second.
Its body changed its path, but stopped before completing the attack.
Its prismatic eyes narrowed.
The false presence had no natural shadow.
Its weight pressure on the ground was not felt.
The Alpha had noticed the difference.
False Presence had not been able to completely fool it, but that fraction of a second was enough.
Seris raised her sword.
[Silver Requiem]
The blade’s movement disappeared from view.
Dozens of silver strikes appeared in the space around the Alpha, and each cut collided with one of the attack’s reflections.
The false lines broke, the deflected lights collapsed, and for a moment, only the Alpha’s real body remained.
Lian also did not miss the opportunity and moved.
[Iron Fortress Charge]
Force gathered in his legs and shoulder.
He hit the Alpha’s side at high speed.
The monster’s semi-transparent body was lifted off the ground and thrown through two trees into a more open space.
A few glass branches shattered under its weight.
Before falling completely, the Alpha spun its body and landed on four legs.
But One had already moved.
The ant lunged at it, and its jaws closed around the Alpha’s back leg.
The monster roared and brought its claws down on One’s head.
The ant’s shell developed shallow cracks.
But One did not let go.
Lian activated Thunder Step.
Blue lightning ran on the ground, and he appeared right in front of the Alpha.
Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his hand.
The Alpha raised its free claw.
Several light reflections were created along with it.
Echo Adaptation had now seen enough of the species’ movement patterns.
"Your tricks won’t work anymore."
Lian identified the real point before the attack was complete.
He lowered his body, and the Alpha’s claw passed over his head.
He sank Glacial Reaper Claw directly into the monster’s transparent chest.
The cold spread through its body.
The light inside its organs went out.
The ice spread from its chest to its neck and legs.
The Alpha tried to pull back, but One was still holding its leg.
It had no chance to escape!
A crack formed in the center of the monster’s chest, then a second crack, and then dozens of cracks ran through its entire transparent body.
Lian turned the claw.
The Prismfang Alpha’s body collapsed from the inside.
The crystalline pieces fell on the ground.
The reflected lights in the entire forest went out.
The remaining Stalkers remained motionless for a few moments upon seeing the Alpha’s death, then scattered among the trees without trying to continue the battle.
Lian did not chase them.
Their goal was hunting, but entering a deeper ambush for a few Level 17 or 18 creatures was not worth it.
System notifications appeared.
[You have slain Prismfang Stalker Lv.17.]
[You have slain Prismfang Stalker Lv.18.]
[You have slain Prismfang Stalker Lv.18.]
[You have slain Prismfang Alpha Lv.21.]
[Bloodlust has absorbed 100% of the available exp.]
[Due to group kill, the EXP received is halved.]

chapters.title: Chapter 253: A Friend in Danger!
paragraphs: Lian opened his level panel. The distance had become shorter, very close, but Level-Up had not occurred yet.
Seris also checked her panel for a moment. From her expression, it was clear she had progressed, but she had not yet reached Level 18.
’My progress speed is very good considering I only became an awakened one a month or two ago, and especially considering that I need a huge amount of EXP for each level up.’
’My current stats have passed 3000. I thought I had reached my limit, but it seems it’s a little higher. I can feel I’m getting close to the maximum.’
’At this rate, 4000 stats is probably the maximum I can have, twice the maximum of a five-star class... that’s really a lot.’ He thought to himself.
He knew his limits were very different from other awakened ones, but still, every time he thought about it, it was amazing.
His class was beyond an anomaly. It was an outlier that simply shouldn’t exist.
This made him curious about the level limit. Is it like awakened ones, where the maximum level one can reach is 100?
Or can he go beyond that?
There was no need to think about it right now. By waiting, sooner or later, he would find out one day.
Lian then looked at the corpses. The Prismfang bodies had high value even after death, especially their financial value.
Their transparent skin could be used for making stealth equipment or Mana-resistant armor.
Their prismatic teeth had the ability to penetrate Armor, and the crystalline veins inside their bodies might be useful in making weapons or Arrays.
Lian collected all the carcasses. He left no part behind. The Alpha’s body had the most value.
He gathered all the corpses. He could sell them for a very large sum!
Of course, he asked Seris if she wanted her share, and her answer was no. It didn’t matter, that meant more profit for him.
Then he looked at the stats he had obtained. Because of the monsters’ low levels, it wasn’t much, only 47 stats, of course, the reason was also the group kill, which had halved the amount obtained.
After a short rest and checking One’s wounds, they set off again.

They advanced for hours into the depth of Glassthorn Forest. The further they went, the stranger the forest became, while at first they thought this forest was not going to be as amazing as the other two forests, they realized how wrong they were.
Inside some transparent trunks, small creatures lived.
Their bodies resembled fish, but they swam in Mana and would hide in the tree’s depth when Lian and Seris got close.
Flowers with glass petals had grown along the path.
Every time One got close to them, the petals would close with a sharp sound, and the light inside them would go out.
They passed by a narrow river. It was neither water nor pure Mana. Every drop reflected the surrounding light and made a musical sound when hitting the rocks.
Lian did not allow One to drink from it. As long as the liquid’s nature was unknown, touching it was also dangerous.
In another part of the path, they found the skeleton of a massive monster, but its bones had not decayed.
They had gradually turned into crystal and merged with the tree roots. One of the creature’s horns was now part of a transparent trunk, and Mana was flowing through it.
"Apart from how annoying they are, they are also beautiful."
A few hours later, Seris saw marks on three trees. Deep and regular lines.
"Are these writings?"
Lian went closer. The writings did not belong to anywhere they recognized. It was another language.
"While they are familiar, I don’t recognize them. I guess they are significantly similar to one of the languages of the Ruined Realm, like the map."
They had understood from the marks and some of the writings on the map that it was made by a native of the Ruined Realm who had come here in some way.
And now the carvings here were exactly the same, as if they belonged to the Ruined Realm.
He could not understand their meaning, but the location of the signs exactly matched the path on the map. The signs were also carved with power.
"I think the map’s creator carved these."

This proved that the map’s creator had really passed through this path. The map was not an estimate or an old story. Someone had walked this path step by step and recorded the real signs of the environment.
"That means the destination was that important to him? Apart from the map, he also left signs along the way." Seris thought.
"It seems so, and this shows we are going the right way."
However, the main mark was still a few days away.
The forest’s sky could hardly be seen.
The canopy of crystal trees was so dense that only small gaps remained between them.
The light of this world passed through those gaps and spread on the ground like a permanent twilight.
The exact time could only be determined by the change in light intensity and the system’s internal clock.
After a day of travel, they stopped in a relatively open part of the forest. Three massive trees surrounded the area, and their roots had created a natural wall.
One sat on the ground.
Seris placed her sword beside her hand and looked at the map that Lian had opened.
"How far are we from the mark?"
"At our current speed, two more days." Lian compared their position with the map’s lines.
The silver-haired girl looked at her sword and then at the surrounding forest.
"So until then, we need to gain a few Levels. I need three levels, of course, I’m not far from Level 18, I’ll probably reach it tomorrow."
"What about you?"
Lian opened the Experience bar.
[Level: 18]
"I’m also not far from nineteen." He could reach Level 19 tomorrow too, but the distance to 20 was significant and required a lot of hunting.
"That’s what makes something bad happen."
"Why?" Seris raised an eyebrow.
"Because usually when something is very close, we don’t reach it easily."
The young Pendragon looked at him for a few moments, probably wanting to say this logic wasn’t real.
But before she could say anything, One suddenly raised its head.
Its antennae straightened completely. A strong wave of warning reached Lian’s mind through Hive Link.
The danger was not close.
One had sensed something in the sky.
Lian and Seris looked up at the same time. At first, nothing could be seen except the dense glass branches.
Then a red light passed through them. At first, like a thin line.
But in a fraction of a second, a massive column of red energy was shot from a distant point in the forest toward the sky.
The light turned the branches red, broke inside the transparent trunks, and scattered in hundreds of directions.
For a moment, the entire Glassthorn Forest turned blood red.
The energy column passed through the treetops and exploded at a high altitude.
A large red circle formed in the sky. In its center, a familiar symbol appeared.
The symbol for a distress signal!
HELP
"This... is our language!" Seris whispered in surprise.
"Does that mean? It’s him?" Lian frowned, he realized what this was.
Emergency Beacon.
This was the item he had given to his group members before entering, to activate if they were in danger.
If the other group members were nearby, they could find each other and go to help.
The system panel immediately opened before Lian’s view.
[Emergency Beacon Detected.]
[Origin: Registered Party Member.]
[Distance: 37.4 Kilometers.]
[Status: Critical.]
[Beacon Integrity: 82%]
Lian stood up.
"What happened?" Seris also picked up her sword at that same moment. She didn’t know what was going on, but she knew this boy did.
The number before Lian’s eyes changed.
[Beacon Integrity: 81%]
Then again.
[Beacon Integrity: 80%]
The Beacon was not a simple message.
The sender created an emergency column using equipment or their own Mana.
Integrity showed how much longer its structure could hold. The continuous decrease in the number meant the sender or the Beacon’s source was still under pressure.
Maybe the equipment was being destroyed, maybe the person who activated it didn’t have enough Mana to maintain it.
Or maybe the enemy was directly trying to turn off the Beacon.
Lian opened the map again. He had to find out where that point was located, and with one look, he realized it was coming from the northeastern part of Glassthorn Forest.
The signal was not on their main path.
To reach it, they would have to leave the marked route and deviate dozens of kilometers to the north.
But Lian did not even think for a moment about his choice.
[Beacon Integrity: 77%]
The red column pulsed in the sky again. This time, its light was slightly weaker.
He gave the command to get ready through Hive Link. The ant put aside its exhaustion and immediately lowered its body.
Seris looked at One’s back.
"Aren’t you going to tell me what’s going on?"
"That red signal means one of my friends is in danger." Lian answered in the simplest way he could and then closed the map and jumped on One’s back.
Seris also mounted behind him.
The Vorhelm fixed his gaze on the red column that was trembling through the crystal trees.
"I don’t know which one, but whoever it is, they are in danger."
The number dropped again.
[Beacon Integrity: 74%]
Then.
[Beacon Integrity: 71%]
Lian sent the command to move. One lunged forward with all its power.
Its six legs hit the ground at the same time. The dark soil and crystal roots cracked under the pressure of its feet.
The trees on both sides turned into stretched lines of blue and purple light.
Seris lowered her body and gripped her sword’s hilt firmly.
The red column in the distance split the sky again. This time with a weaker wave. Whatever it was, it was slowly fading.
Lian recognized only one feeling within that wave.
Fear... not a simple fear... the fear of someone who was no longer fighting to win... someone who was only trying to stay alive for a few more minutes.
The situation was truly urgent!
He placed his hand on One’s body.
"Faster."
The ant increased its speed. The cold wind hit their faces.
The glass branches around them trembled, and the sound of thousands of bells echoed throughout the forest.
The panel remained before his view.
[Beacon Integrity: 68%]
They still did not know which member of the group was trapped at that point.
They did not know what monster they had faced or why they had been forced to activate the Emergency Beacon.
But one thing was clear.
At the speed the Beacon was collapsing, not much time remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 254: Friends In Danger!
paragraphs: [Beacon Integrity: 48%]
One was running with all its might among the crystal trees.
Its six massive legs cracked the dark soil of Glassthorn Forest with every step and crushed the thin glass roots under its weight.
The cold wind hit Lian and Seris’s faces with force, and the transparent branches on both sides of the path had turned into stretched lines of blue and purple light.
In the distance, the red column of the Emergency Beacon was still rising through the dense treetops toward the sky.
But its glow was not like before. The light was getting weaker each time, it was clear that the user’s condition was getting worse and worse.
[Beacon Integrity: 43%]
The reflection of the red column had fallen on hundreds of glass trunks. For this reason, it sometimes seemed like dozens of Beacons had been activated in different parts of the forest.
However, Lian was not fooled by the reflections. He was not looking at the light, he was following the main flow of Mana.
A thin trace of emergency energy remained among the trees; like a red vein that separated its path from the forest’s natural lights.
A distance of thirty-seven kilometers for a normal person meant hours of travel, but One was running at a speed that many monsters in this forest could not match.
However, they could not move directly toward the Beacon.
The massive roots of some trees extended for dozens of meters on the ground.
Walls of crystal appeared on their path, and sometimes deep gaps separated different parts of the forest from each other.
Lian was forced to change One’s direction several times. Every deviation meant losing time.
And time was something their friend did not have.
[Beacon Integrity: 39%]
Seris was leaning over One’s back, holding one hand on the ant’s armor to keep her balance.
Her gaze did not separate from the red column.
"How long at this speed?"
Lian checked the distance again.
"If we don’t have to change course, a few minutes."
Seris looked at the crystal wall that was approaching ahead.
"Then we will have to."
Lian commanded One to turn right before reaching the wall.
The ant, without reducing its speed much, turned its heavy body. Its left legs dragged on the ground and left a deep mark.
A few glass branches shattered in their path. At that same moment, a sound echoed from a distance in the forest.
It was neither a roar nor a scream, but a multi-layered and coordinated sound that had risen from dozens of sources at the same time.
Its vibration passed through the air and reached the transparent trunks around them.
The trees began to tremble. The lights inside them became irregular for a moment.
Even One’s natural armor developed a slight vibration. Lian placed his hand on the ant’s back.
Hive Link transmitted the tremor more clearly to his mind.
This was not only sound, there was a structured wave of Mana within the vibration.
Something in the distance was using sound to attack a Barrier or defensive structure.
At that same moment, the red column of the Beacon became weaker.
[Beacon Integrity: 34%]
"I guess they used a defensive layer or a disposable shield, and the monsters are trying to break it." Lian said.
Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
"How many?"
"From the sound? A lot."
"Good."
Lian gave her a brief look.
Seris did not explain. There was no need. For her, a large number of enemies was usually not a problem.
The coordinated sound shook the forest again, this time closer.
The crystal leaves separated from the branches and fell on the ground like a rain of glass.
One passed through them, and the transparent pieces shattered on its black shell.
Lian stood up on his feet.
"We’re here."
The trees ahead parted, and a relatively large clearing appeared.
A massive Glassthorn tree was in its center.
The tree’s trunk was hollow, and a dark crack could be seen in its lower part.
But the area around it was filled with monsters. Six-legged creatures with black and elongated bodies.
Thin and transparent plates had grown from their spines, extending like a row of crystal blades to their tails.
Their jaws were large and multi-segmented. Every time they opened their mouths, the transparent jaw bones would open in four directions.
Their eyes were white and pupil-less.
None of them were very large individually, but their numbers had completely covered the clearing.
The panel for one of them appeared.
[Resonant Glassmaw]
[Level: 17]
[Rank: Normal]
Similar panels were seen on the rest of the creatures.
Their levels ranged from sixteen to nineteen, as expected, the monster levels in this forest were not that high, and monsters above level 20 were rare.
In the center of the colony, a larger monster stood.
The crystal plates on its back were thicker and taller. Its tail ended in a multi-layered mace, and every time it struck the ground, all the Glassmaws would move their heads in a specific rhythm.
[Glassmaw Chorus Alpha]
[Level: 22]
[Rank: Normal]
Inside the tree’s crack, a large blue and purple Barrier had formed.
The Barrier’s surface was full of cracks. Behind it, two people could be seen. Two people Lian immediately recognized upon seeing their faces.
Seraphina was holding her sword with both hands, its tip sank into the ground.
Three large Magic Circles were rotating around her sword, and strands of Mana were connected from them to the Barrier.
Her hair was stuck to her face, parts of her armor were broken, and her breaths were heavy.
A few steps behind her, Liana was kneeling on one knee.
Her clothes were torn from the side, and dried blood could be seen on her skin and armor. Her left shoulder was also wounded, and her face looked pale from exhaustion.

In front of both girls, a black wolf was standing.
Its body, unlike normal wolves, was not made of flesh but of shadows!
The shadows moved like thick smoke in its body structure. Two red eyes shone from its dark face, and its claws left a black trail in the air with every movement.

But it was still standing in front of its summoner. Of course, that wolf was Liana’s summon.
The Glassmaw Alpha raised its tail.
All the surrounding monsters lowered their heads. The crystal plates on their backs began to tremble.

[Resonant Chorus]
A collective wave whose power was greater than the simple sum of the sounds.

Blue and white light exploded among the colony. Lian entered the field before One.
[Thunder Step]
He appeared in the center of the Glassmaw circle.
A few monsters had not even had time to turn their heads toward him when Lian’s palm hit the ground.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
A compressed wave of Mana entered the soil. The ground did not explode widely.
He had controlled the force.
The wave passed under the Glassmaws’ feet and hit them exactly at the moment their crystal plates reached a unified rhythm.
The ground trembled, the feet of some monsters shifted from their places, and a few crystal plates cracked.
The collective rhythm was disrupted for a fraction of a second, but the stored Mana within the Resonant Chorus could no longer be contained.
The incomplete wave exploded among the colony itself. A screeching sound split the space.
A few Glassmaws were thrown back by the pressure of their own attack. One of them hit the tree’s trunk, and the plates on its back shattered. Another’s jaw was split from one side.
The blue and purple Barrier also trembled, but the main attack did not reach it.

Mana spread around the blade.

Her hand’s movement disappeared from view for a moment, then dozens of silver lines appeared among the Glassmaws.
One of the monsters was still getting up when all six of its legs were severed at the same time.
Another monster’s transparent jaw was split from both sides.
The plates on the backs of three Glassmaws were shattered in an instant, and black blood splashed on the soil.
Seris landed among them and took the next step without stopping.
One entered the clearing with a muffled roar.
Its massive body collided with two Glassmaws and dragged them under its feet. Its jaws closed around the third monster’s body and crushed its black armor and crystal plates with pressure.
The Glassmaw Alpha struck its tail to the ground. This time, it was not a collective Resonant Chorus.
"AAAAAAAGH" The monster’s roar covered the area.
It was enraged that outsiders had dared to interfere in its hunt!
And it was sure they would pay the price

sentences.text: [Beacon Integrity: 48%]
One was running with all its might among the crystal trees.
Its six massive legs cracked the dark soil of Glassthorn Forest with every step and crushed the thin glass roots under its weight.
The cold wind hit Lian and Seris’s faces with force, and the transparent branches on both sides of the path had turned into stretched lines of blue and purple light.
In the distance, the red column of the Emergency Beacon was still rising through the dense treetops toward the sky.
But its glow was not like before.
The light was getting weaker each time, it was clear that the user’s condition was getting worse and worse.
[Beacon Integrity: 43%]
The reflection of the red column had fallen on hundreds of glass trunks.
For this reason, it sometimes seemed like dozens of Beacons had been activated in different parts of the forest.
However, Lian was not fooled by the reflections.
He was not looking at the light, he was following the main flow of Mana.
A thin trace of emergency energy remained among the trees; like a red vein that separated its path from the forest’s natural lights.
A distance of thirty-seven kilometers for a normal person meant hours of travel, but One was running at a speed that many monsters in this forest could not match.
However, they could not move directly toward the Beacon.
The massive roots of some trees extended for dozens of meters on the ground.
Walls of crystal appeared on their path, and sometimes deep gaps separated different parts of the forest from each other.
Lian was forced to change One’s direction several times.
Every deviation meant losing time.
And time was something their friend did not have.
[Beacon Integrity: 39%]
Seris was leaning over One’s back, holding one hand on the ant’s armor to keep her balance.
Her gaze did not separate from the red column.
"How long at this speed?"
Lian checked the distance again.
"If we don’t have to change course, a few minutes."
Seris looked at the crystal wall that was approaching ahead.
"Then we will have to."
Lian commanded One to turn right before reaching the wall.
The ant, without reducing its speed much, turned its heavy body.
Its left legs dragged on the ground and left a deep mark.
A few glass branches shattered in their path.
At that same moment, a sound echoed from a distance in the forest.
It was neither a roar nor a scream, but a multi-layered and coordinated sound that had risen from dozens of sources at the same time.
Its vibration passed through the air and reached the transparent trunks around them.
The trees began to tremble.
The lights inside them became irregular for a moment.
Even One’s natural armor developed a slight vibration.
Lian placed his hand on the ant’s back.
Hive Link transmitted the tremor more clearly to his mind.
This was not only sound, there was a structured wave of Mana within the vibration.
Something in the distance was using sound to attack a Barrier or defensive structure.
At that same moment, the red column of the Beacon became weaker.
[Beacon Integrity: 34%]
"I guess they used a defensive layer or a disposable shield, and the monsters are trying to break it." Lian said.
Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
"How many?"
"From the sound?
A lot."
"Good."
Lian gave her a brief look.
Seris did not explain.
There was no need.
For her, a large number of enemies was usually not a problem.
The coordinated sound shook the forest again, this time closer.
The crystal leaves separated from the branches and fell on the ground like a rain of glass.
One passed through them, and the transparent pieces shattered on its black shell.
Lian stood up on his feet.

chapters.title: Chapter 255: Friends Are Now Safe
paragraphs: A focused and direct wave was released from the plates on its back. The air rippled in the attack’s path, and the sound went toward Lian like an invisible blade.
He saw the Mana movement. Instead of directly defending, he activated Thunder Step again... lightning exploded at his previous location.
The Resonance wave passed through the remaining image and knocked a few Glassmaws behind him to the ground.
"You roar at me, bastard?" Lian appeared behind the Alpha.
[Iron Fortress Charge]
Force gathered in his legs, waist, and shoulder. His shoulder hit the Glassmaw Alpha’s side with full power.
The black plates of the creature’s body sank in. The massive monster was lifted off the ground and thrown several meters into the air.
Directly toward Seris.
That girl had already seen its path. She stepped forward, and heavy pressure formed on her blade.
[King’s Breaker]
The sword hit the center of the Alpha’s chest. The sound of crystal breaking echoed throughout the clearing.
The defensive plates on the creature’s chest cracked from the impact point. The cracks quickly spread across the entire armor.
The Alpha fell on the ground, but before it could pull back, Lian reached it.
Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his hand. Transparent blue claws came out from his fingers.
He sank his hand directly into the gap created by King’s Breaker.
[Glacial Reaper Claw — Divine]
The cold rushed into the monster’s ribcage. The black veins froze in an instant, and the crystal plates on the Alpha’s back turned blue one after another.
Seris raised her sword.
[King’s Edge]
Her precise strike passed through the chest gap. The blade directly split the frozen center of the monster’s body.
The Glassmaw Alpha remained motionless for a moment.
Then all the plates on its back shattered at the same time. Its large body fell on the ground.
From the moment Lian entered until the Alpha’s death, not even a minute had passed.
A monster that thought it was among the strongest in this forest had been easily butchered. It didn’t even have a chance to fight back or resist.
With the leader’s destruction, the colony’s shared rhythm was lost. Some of the Glassmaws immediately retreated.
A few other creatures attacked One chaotically, but the ant’s jaws and legs crushed them.
Seris moved among the remaining monsters. Every strike took down a Glassmaw.
The last two creatures fled into the forest.
Lian did not chase them. The main goal was to save his friends, not to destroy the entire colony.
Sudden silence fell over the clearing.
Seraphina was still holding her sword.
Liana was sitting next to Shadow Wolf, and both were staring at the field in front of them.
Liana had fought alongside Lian before.
She knew Lian as a smart, calculating, and dangerous person; someone who used the environment and the enemy’s weak points to compensate for power gaps.
But what she had just seen was not the same Lian from before. The analysis and precision were still there, but they were no longer being used to compensate for weakness.
Now, raw power, speed, and massive Mana were behind that analysis.
The Lian she saw now bore no resemblance to the Lian she had fought in the border city or earlier in the academy during practice.
This man was a monster! What kind of power was that? They were the same age!
So how had he managed to reach such power? What was his damn secret?
She was so stunned and amazed that she didn’t even know what to say.
Seraphina’s Barrier turned off.
The Magic Circles around her sword collapsed one after another.
She took a deep breath and pulled the blade out of the ground, but her body could no longer handle it after maintaining the Barrier for several hours.
Her right leg bent for a moment.
Lian moved toward them. Before he could say anything, Seraphina closed the distance.
She wrapped her arms around him and hugged him tightly. The movement was so sudden that even Lian remained motionless for a moment.
Seraphina was usually too proud and controlled to show her feelings like this.
But now, all that cold exterior had crumbled for a few seconds.
"You came..." Her voice was weaker than usual, and she tightened her arms.
"Our signal really reached you. I thought no one was around here."
"Relax. It’s over." Lian placed his hand gently on her shoulder.
Seraphina took a deep breath. She probably hadn’t believed they were truly saved until she saw Lian.
"I’m so glad you received our distress call."
Lian gave a brief look at her wounds and preferred not to answer.
Liana, who was sitting next to Shadow Wolf, smiled tiredly.
"I’m also glad our savior was you." Her gaze moved over him with weak mischief.
"Of course, I also wanted to hug you, but the glorious vice head of the student council attacked without permission as usual."
"Shut up." Seraphina moved away from Lian and frowned at her.
Liana placed her hand on her chest.
"Even after being saved, you treat me like this? You’re really cruel."
"First, treatment."
Lian’s tone left no room for argument. He couldn’t believe that even in this state, these two still didn’t want to put aside their hostility toward each other.
He didn’t know if all girls were like this, or just these two. He felt his second guess was more accurate.
For example, he looked at Seris. What a calm and quiet girl she is? Of course, apart from the times when she recklessly and stubbornly does something stupid.
Both girls looked at their own condition.
Seraphina took out two bottles from her storage space. One contained a blue liquid, and the other red.
She first drank the Mana potion.
The blue color slowly returned to her face, and her mana was refilled. Then she drank the Healing potion.
Strands of green light passed under her skin, and the smaller scratches and wounds began to close.
Liana also took out a healing potion. She drank half of it and poured the rest into her palm.
She placed her hand on Shadow Wolf’s head. A small summoning circle formed under the wolf.
Instead of falling on the ground, the red liquid turned into strands of Mana and entered the shadowy creature’s body.
Red and purple veins moved through its black body for a few seconds. The faint parts of its body became dense again.
Shadow Wolf brought its head close to Liana’s hand.
She gave a short smile and stroked behind its shadowy ear.
After making sure their condition was somewhat stable, Lian asked.
"How did you get trapped in this situation? What happened from the start?"
Liana looked at Seraphina. The latter sat on a broken root and placed her sword beside her.
"From the moment we entered the Special Area, everything fell apart."
She paused for a few moments, recalling the events of the past few days.
"When I opened my eyes, I was alone. There was no trace of any of you or the others. I didn’t even know where I was in this forest."
"In the first few hours, I thought the reflections were just because of the trees. Then I realized some monsters use them to hunt."
She talked about encountering a few small Prism Beetles.
Insects whose bodies reflected light and attacked in groups from under the soil.

Then she talked about the Glassthorn Lynx; a Level 18 cat-like creature that could become almost invisible, and Seraphina had been forced to use a combination of fire and sword to pull it out from among the reflections.
"Then I found an abandoned shelter. It was very old. Inside, there were two Mana Crystals and a few potions left."
"Were there any writings or signs inside?" Lian asked.
"A few marks on the walls, but I didn’t recognize their language."
Lian thought for a moment. Since it was old, it didn’t belong to an awakened one like them.
It could belong to a native of this world, or maybe to one of the Ruined Realm’s natives who had come here in the past.
There were many possibilities, but in the end, it didn’t matter.
If he saw those signs, he could identify them, but it wasn’t necessary. It wasn’t something he would deviate from the path or delay for.
Seraphina continued that a little further from the shelter, she had found a small pool of compressed Mana.
The water in the pool was not water. It was a thick blue liquid that could increase Mana!
She had trained next to it for a few hours and had been able to slightly increase her Mana control.
In the following days, she had also hunted a few groups of monsters.
"Eventually, I reached Level 19."
"Not bad, it seems you had some good opportunities."
"Yeah... but well, that idiot almost got me killed." Seraphina’s cold gaze fell on Liana.
Liana gave a quiet laugh and clearly didn’t care.
Lian turned his gaze to her this time.
"What about you?"
"I was running away almost from the first day."
Liana said she had appeared at a point much farther from Seraphina.
Only her summons were with her, and from the first hours, she had encountered a group of hunting monsters.
Unlike Seraphina, her class was not built for direct confrontation.
Every Stat Point she had gained in the past few months had been spent on increasing Mana capacity, resistance, and her summons’ power instead of strengthening her own body.
Her personal power without her Summons was even lower than many awakened ones at the same level.
"I barely managed to kill a few monsters." Her smile slowly faded.
Her gaze remained on Shadow Wolf.
"And I lost one of my summons." Her voice lowered in the next sentence.
"It was my first summon." She tried to hide it well, but the sadness in her eyes was clear.
Lian wanted to say something to comfort her, but no sentence seemed appropriate.
For most people, a Summon is only a Skill or a tool for battle.
But for a real Summoner, the first summon is something much more.
They grow together from the first Levels.
Their Mana, minds, and part of their emotions are connected through the contract.
The Summoner feels the Summon’s pain.
The Summon also understands its owner’s fear, anger, and commands.
Losing the first summon is more like losing an old companion than destroying a weapon.
"I’m sorry for your loss." Lian only said.
Liana lowered her gaze.
Shadow Wolf placed its head on her leg. She moved her fingers through the dense shadows of its neck.
"Yesterday, this idiot found me." Seraphina also felt a little and changed the subject and atmosphere.
"The way you say it is very unfair." Liana raised her head.
Seraphina continued without paying attention.
"She found me while a whole army of monsters was chasing her."

Then she talked about the Glassthorn Lynx; a Level 18 cat-like creature that could become almost invisible, and Seraphina had been forced to use a combination of fire and sword to pull it out from among the reflections.
"Then I found an abandoned shelter.
It was very old.
Inside, there were two Mana Crystals and a few potions left."
"Were there any writings or signs inside?" Lian asked.
"A few marks on the walls, but I didn’t recognize their language."
Lian thought for a moment.
Since it was old, it didn’t belong to an awakened one like them.
It could belong to a native of this world, or maybe to one of the Ruined Realm’s natives who had come here in the past.
There were many possibilities, but in the end, it didn’t matter.
If he saw those signs, he could identify them, but it wasn’t necessary.
It wasn’t something he would deviate from the path or delay for.
Seraphina continued that a little further from the shelter, she had found a small pool of compressed Mana.
The water in the pool was not water.
It was a thick blue liquid that could increase Mana!
She had trained next to it for a few hours and had been able to slightly increase her Mana control.
In the following days, she had also hunted a few groups of monsters.
"Eventually, I reached Level 19."
"Not bad, it seems you had some good opportunities."
"Yeah... but well, that idiot almost got me killed." Seraphina’s cold gaze fell on Liana.
Liana gave a quiet laugh and clearly didn’t care.
Lian turned his gaze to her this time.
"What about you?"
"I was running away almost from the first day."
Liana said she had appeared at a point much farther from Seraphina.
Only her summons were with her, and from the first hours, she had encountered a group of hunting monsters.
Unlike Seraphina, her class was not built for direct confrontation.
Every Stat Point she had gained in the past few months had been spent on increasing Mana capacity, resistance, and her summons’ power instead of strengthening her own body.
Her personal power without her Summons was even lower than many awakened ones at the same level.
"I barely managed to kill a few monsters." Her smile slowly faded.
Her gaze remained on Shadow Wolf.
"And I lost one of my summons." Her voice lowered in the next sentence.
"It was my first summon." She tried to hide it well, but the sadness in her eyes was clear.
Lian wanted to say something to comfort her, but no sentence seemed appropriate.
For most people, a Summon is only a Skill or a tool for battle.
But for a real Summoner, the first summon is something much more.
They grow together from the first Levels.
Their Mana, minds, and part of their emotions are connected through the contract.
The Summoner feels the Summon’s pain.
The Summon also understands its owner’s fear, anger, and commands.
Losing the first summon is more like losing an old companion than destroying a weapon.
"I’m sorry for your loss." Lian only said.
Liana lowered her gaze.
Shadow Wolf placed its head on her leg.
She moved her fingers through the dense shadows of its neck.
"Yesterday, this idiot found me." Seraphina also felt a little and changed the subject and atmosphere.
"The way you say it is very unfair." Liana raised her head.
Seraphina continued without paying attention.
"She found me while a whole army of monsters was chasing her."

chapters.title: Chapter 256: A Moment of Rest
paragraphs: "A whole army is a huge exaggeration, it was more like a small herd..." Liana objected. She felt like this bitch was trying to ruin her credibility in front of Lian.
She never puts others in danger, okay? Maybe she would be willing to put their glorious vice head of the student council in danger though...
Seraphina pointed at the Glassmaw corpses with her hand.
"These were only part of that same group."
"Well, maybe a small army." Liana said in a very low voice, like a mosquito’s buzz.
Seraphina explained that when Liana had reached her shelter, the Glassmaws had also seen her.
The chase quickly spread to both of them. They had fought for a while, but the enemies’ numbers did not end.
In the end, they had taken refuge in the hollow tree.
Seraphina had blocked the entrance with a Barrier, and Liana had sent Shadow Wolf to create false trails.
For a few hours, they had imagined they had escaped the pursuit.
But the Glassmaws were sensitive to sound and Mana. They had found the Barrier’s trace and started the siege.
"From then until now, you saw what happened."
Seraphina pointed at the remaining cracks on the trunk.
"Every time they attacked, the Barrier got weaker. When we realized the next attack would probably break it, we activated the Beacon."
"And fortunately, our favorite hero was nearby." Liana gave a faint smile.
Seraphina looked at her with displeasure, but before she could answer, her attention was drawn to Seris.
Until that moment, the danger, exhaustion, and conversation about past events hadn’t given her a chance to examine the silver-haired girl closely.
Seris was standing a little further away, had cleaned her sword, and no sign of exhaustion could be seen in her posture.
The Mana pressure around her was calm, but Seraphina, as a Mage, could clearly feel its unusual density.
Every movement of Seris was controlled. No energy was wasted from her body.
"Who is she?"
"Seris Pendragon. From the Pendragon clan."
The clan name made both girls’ expressions change slightly.
The Pendragon clan was not one that could be easily ignored.
Even among the great clans, their name was completely known.
Lian then pointed at the two girls.
"Seraphina and Liana. Members of my group."
Seris gave them a brief look.
"Seris."
Seraphina answered with a more formal tone.
"Seraphina."
Liana raised her hand slightly, and her mischievous smile returned.
"Liana. Pleased to meet the girl who appeared out of nowhere with Lian."
Seris showed no reaction to her emphasis on the words, only nodded.
Her complete indifference made Seraphina’s frown deepen slightly. She had seen Seris’s power, appearance, and calmness.
And without wanting to, she felt she had found a new rival.
Liana saw her change in expression. Her smile widened a little, but this time she said nothing.
"Have you found any trace of the other group members?" Lian asked.
"No. At least we haven’t seen any of them so far."
Liana looked at the forest with dissatisfaction.
"We didn’t even know where we were. Whatever this damn forest is, it’s very annoying."
She pointed at the multiple reflections on the trunks.
"Neither the right path is clear, nor are the sounds reliable, nor do we know where to go or what to look for." She then added with a frown.
"No one said this Special Area was going to be this stupid."
Lian involuntarily laughed.
Now he just remembered that these two had almost no information about this world.
They had only appeared in a part of Glassthorn Forest and had been fighting to survive from the start.
Seraphina looked at him suspiciously.
"Why are you laughing?"
"Nothing."
"That laugh was not a ’nothing’ laugh." Liana narrowed her eyes.
Lian decided to explain.
"We are currently in the northeastern part of Glassthorn Forest."
Liana looked at the transparent trees around.
"Glassthorn? The name suits it."
"How do you know?" Seraphina immediately asked.
He gave a short smile and nodded toward Seris.
"Because she and I didn’t appear here. We just entered this forest."
Then he briefly explained the events.
He talked about the Forest of Giants, the massive monsters of that area, the Giants’ Graveyard, and the deadly path between the two forests.
About the three main parts of this world.
The Forest of Giants.
Glassthorn Forest.
And Emberroot Forest.
Lian explained that according to the map and information, the largest remaining civilization in this world should be in Emberroot.
A large city or a collection of settlements, and there they should be able to find many interesting things.
Seraphina and Liana listened without interrupting. Both were clearly surprised. They had barely managed to advance a few kilometers in this forest.
But Lian and Seris had passed through several areas, found a map, and understood the world’s overall structure.
"I think I’ve found the key’s location." Lian continued.
Seraphina became more serious. The key was their way out of this world, and it was very important.
"Where?"
"The deepest point of this world. A place called the Forgotten Tree."
"You understood everything in this short time? What exactly were you doing?" Liana asked in disbelief, feeling a little embarrassed.
While those two had been running from monsters all this time, their classmate had already gathered years’ worth of information.
"I’ll explain later. For now, we have more important things to do."
He took out the map and spread it on the ground. He placed his finger on their approximate location and then moved it southeast.
"Tomorrow, we move toward the border between Glassthorn and Emberroot."
"You want to leave this forest?" Seraphina asked.
"Yeah. It doesn’t seem like there’s anything here worth staying long for."
Then he placed his finger on the mark that was just before the border.
"But before that, there’s something I want to check. It’s exactly on our path. Whoever made this map marked this place without explanation. Maybe there’s a good opportunity inside."
Liana and Seraphina looked at the mark for a few moments and then nodded.
"Okay." Their goal was also to become stronger, and they had no problem with exploring.
Now that Lian was with them, they no longer needed to worry about the monsters.
They spent the night in that same hollow tree.
Lian naturally took all the monster corpses for himself, and none of them had any problem with it.
Seraphina and Seris didn’t need the money, and Liana felt she hadn’t made any effort to deserve a share.
After that, they checked the area around the tree.
The two girls needed more rest due to their injuries and exhaustion.
Shadow Wolf lay down next to Liana, but even when its summoner closed her eyes, its red eyes remained open.
One also stationed itself at the tree’s entrance.
Its massive body blocked almost half of the crack.

In the middle of the night, Seraphina woke up for a moment to drink some water. It was a nightly habit she had since childhood. She saw Lian standing outside the tree, looking into the forest’s darkness.
Seris was at a distance, on one of the roots.
Neither was talking to the other, but every time Lian changed his gaze’s direction, Seris would check the opposite side.
Both had covered the entire environment without needing orders or explanation.
Their coordination was not just the result of a few hours together. They knew each other’s rhythm.
Seraphina watched for a few more seconds and then closed her eyes again with a slight frown... it was unclear what she had been thinking about before falling asleep.
With the arrival of daylight, Lian woke everyone up.
After a light meal and checking their wounds, they decided to ride on One to increase their speed.
For the first time, the two girls examined the ant’s body up close.
But Liana’s reaction was stronger. As a Summoner, she was not only looking at One’s appearance.
She felt the flow of Mana between the creature and Lian. She circled One several times.
"Where did you get this?"
"I found it."
"That’s not an answer."
She placed her hand on One’s head, and her eyes became serious for a moment.
"It doesn’t have a summoning contract. There’s no enslavement mark on its body either. Even your Mana bond is not like normal Taming."
This time even Seris looked at Lian. She too had never asked how this man had managed to tame and control such a monster.
"It’s a secret." Lian said briefly.
He naturally had no intention of explaining where he had obtained the S-rank Link Talent.
Liana pursed her lips.
"Is it that hard to say?"
"Yeah."
She let out her breath with feigned dissatisfaction, but stroked One again.
The ant remained still at first, then moved its antennae toward her and pressed its head slightly into Liana’s palm.
Through Hive Link, a wave of calm and satisfaction reached Lian’s mind.
One had liked her touch.
"At least it likes me." Liana gave a triumphant smile.
"It’s an ant." Seraphina said mockingly.
"And it has good taste." Liana answered without being upset.
All four sat on One’s back, and the journey began.
The first few hours passed without any major conflict.
But near noon, a strange change was detected in the ground’s vibration. The transparent roots around the path were too calm.
Dark spots were moving inside some of them.
Lian had not yet given the stop command when several roots came out of the ground.
Like glass snakes, they wrapped around One’s legs.
The panels appeared.
[Glassvine Hunter]
[Level: 18]
[Rank: Normal]
Seraphina placed her hand on her sword. Liana also prepared to form Shadow Wolf’s summoning circle.
But before either of them could enter the battle, Lian disappeared from One’s back. He didn’t need help to deal with such weaklings...
