chapters.title: Chapter 257: Only One Day ...
paragraphs: [Thunder Step]
Lightning exploded in three different points on the path. Glacial Reaper Claw moved.
The second one turned into a pillar of ice before wrapping around One’s leg.
The third tried to return underground, but the blue cold spread along its body.
Seris jumped down from One’s back.
King’s Edge appeared on her blade.
Three strikes, short, precise, and without extra movement, and all three were split almost simultaneously.
The roots fell on the ground.
The snake-like bodies inside the glass shells were revealed and trembled for a few moments, then remained motionless.
Liana was still holding her hand up for summoning and looked at the corpses.
"I didn’t even have time to summon it."
Seraphina said nothing, but took her hand off her sword’s hilt.
This was the first time both girls felt the real difference in power.
Liana had seen Lian’s speed before, but back then she could follow his movement.
Now Thunder Step had turned him into nothing but an explosion of light.
Seraphina also felt the remaining Mana density in the air.
Whatever Lian’s level was, his Mana and Skill quality did not match a normal awakened one at the same level.
In the late afternoon of the first day, they entered a denser part of the forest.
The treetops had covered almost the entire sky. Little light passed through the crystal leaves.
A deep buzzing sound was heard from above.
One stopped. A few hundred bright points separated from the branches.
At first, they looked like pieces of light, but as they got closer, their insect bodies became clear.
Wings made of transparent plates, armored bodies, multi-faceted eyes, and limbs ending in thin blades.
[Shardwing Drone]
[Level: 16]
[Rank: Normal]
Among the group, larger specimens were also moving.
[Shardwing Hunter]
[Level: 19]
[Rank: Normal]
Their number reached dozens of creatures.
Then the upper branches bent, and the group’s leader came down.
Thick, multi-layered armor was on its chest and head. Four larger wings came out from its back, and its two front arms resembled crystal spears.
[Shardwing Hive Knight]
[Level: 22]
[Rank: Normal]
The Hive Knight produced a sharp sound.
All the Shardwings turned their wings. Hundreds of small crystal blades rained down from the sky toward the group.
Seris drew her sword.
Lian prepared Cataclysm Pulse.
But the number of attacks was such that even with their defense, some blades passed by.
It could be said that this was the first time they were facing a flying race, but fortunately, the enemy was not very powerful, and apart from their wings, they had no other advantage.
This time, Seraphina and Liana also found a chance to enter.
Seraphina jumped down from One’s back and held her sword in front of her body.
Blue, red, and purple mana formed around her at the same time.
Lian glanced at her. His childhood friend’s class was one of the rarest. It wasn’t outside the norm of the six basic classes.
But it was a combination of two classes.
Dual Class
Warrior / Mage
Dual Class was one of the rarest awakening structures.
Most people only had one main path.
Their bodies were not built to support two classes simultaneously.
But Seraphina had both the physical ability of a swordsman and the Mana structure of a Mage.
Having such a class was a one-in-a-million phenomenon. A person could be both a healer and a swordsman, or any other combination.
Of course, there are only a few known examples of dual classes, and for this reason, they are not considered categories, and this is not a random or chance phenomenon.
It is mostly a form of intervention and manipulation. There is a specific Artifact that, if used, can create such a thing.
And Seraphina was lucky enough that her family used such an item, which they had kept for generations, for her.
Although Lian didn’t know why Seraphina. Was there a specific reason? Was there a secret behind it? Or was she just chosen by chance?
She raised her blade.
[Arcane Edge]
Mana gathered on the sword’s edge. Three Magic Circles formed behind her.
The first circle was blue, the second was red, and the third was purple.
Seraphina sent a horizontal strike. A line of fire moved with the blade through the air and burned a few Shardwing Drones.
The second strike went upward.
A wave of ice was released from the blue Magic Circle and froze the wings of several insects.
The frozen creatures fell from the sky. Seraphina took her sword toward another group.
Several Arcane Lances were shot from the purple circle. The Mana spears pierced the insects’ armor.
She didn’t need to distance herself from the battle to Cast. Her sword was both a weapon and a Magic Focus.
Every physical strike could release another Spell.
While fighting, Lian evaluated her for a moment. As always, nothing was perfect, and even Dual Classes had weaknesses.
The weakness of most Dual Classes was that the person wouldn’t reach the peak in either of the two paths.
But Seraphina had high talent in both areas. Her sword power was real, and her Spells were also not weak or incomplete.
Maybe this girl could make history.
Liana also raised her hand. A black circle formed under her feet.
"Go."
Shadow Wolf entered One’s shadow and disappeared.
A moment later, it jumped out from the shadow of a tree at a high altitude. Its body stretched through the air like black smoke, and its red eyes shone among the Shardwings.
Its claws moved, leaving dark lines in the air, and the wings of three insects were cut simultaneously.
Shadow Wolf disappeared into a shadow again.
It came out from another Shardwing’s shadow and closed its jaws around its neck.
Liana did not have high direct offensive power, but her control over her summon was precise.
Every finger movement changed Shadow Wolf’s path. With a wrist turn, she sent a retreat command.
By closing two fingers, she marked the next target. By changing her Mana, she controlled the exit time from the shadow.
Her playful and carefree appearance had completely changed at that moment. Her eyes were moving across the entire field.
She was monitoring every shadow and every enemy.
As long as Shadow Wolf was alive, Liana could attack from angles that most enemies didn’t expect.
But if she lost this summon too, she would be left almost defenseless.
’That wolf is much stronger than when I last saw it. It’s Level 19, and for its level, it has high power.’ Lian could see this girl’s progress with just one look.
’It’s a pity she lost her other summon. With two Level 19 summons, she could be a nightmare for her enemies.’
Seris looked at the sky, and her mana spread around her.
[Silver Requiem]
Dozens of sword lines formed among the Shardwing group. More than ten insects fell from the sky almost simultaneously.
Lian raised his palm. Cataclysm Pulse was sent toward the sky this time.
The Mana wave spread through the colony like an invisible explosion.
The insects’ flight formation was disrupted. Some collided with each other.
The Shardwing Hive Knight came down from among the group. Its four wings compressed Mana and increased its speed.
The multi-layered armor on its chest protected it against direct attacks, and Seraphina built three new Magic Circles behind her.
A lot of Mana was gathered for a larger Spell, but Seris moved sooner, and her body jumped from a broken branch.
[King’s Breaker]
The sword hit the center of the Hive Knight’s armor. A sound like several glass plates breaking was heard.
The creature’s defensive structure collapsed from the center. The cracks spread through the entire armor.
Lian activated Thunder Step and appeared on the Hive Knight’s back in an explosion of lightning.
He sank Glacial Reaper Claw into its body through the armor crack. The cold spread through the insect.
Its four wings froze in an instant, and the Hive Knight fell.
But Lian sank his claw deeper, and he closed his fingers, completely crushing and destroying the entire inside of the monster’s body.
[You have slain Shardwing Hive Knight Lv.22.]
[Bloodlust has absorbed 100% of the available Experience.]
[Due to group kill, the EXP received is halved.]
[Experience threshold reached.]
[Level increased.]
[You have reached Level 19.]
A wave of power spread through Lian’s body. His exhaustion completely disappeared, but since there were no wounds, his body was not healed either.
The invisible pressure around him increased. The remaining Shardwings scattered with the death of their leader.
Liana looked up at Lian from below.
The last time she had fought alongside him, his power was considerable, but still within a understandable range. Now everything had changed.
Speed, physical power, Mana volume, and the variety of Skills.
Lian had grown in this short time like someone who had been in continuous battles for months or even years.
A brief thought crossed Liana’s mind.
Was this really the same person as before?
Seraphina also felt the difference. She herself was Level 19, but after Lian reached the same level, the pressure of their power did not seem equal.
Fighting him would be unpredictable for any enemy.
Seris only cleaned her sword.
Seraphina and Liana’s reactions didn’t matter to her.
As long as they didn’t slow the group down, their presence didn’t cause any problem.
This time, the corpses were divided among all three of them, except for the silver-haired girl who again wanted nothing, and they immediately moved on.
With nightfall, they camped again beside a tree to rest both themselves and One.
"How much longer until we arrive?" Seraphina asked Lian, who was leaning against One.
"At this speed, only one more day."
They themselves didn’t know at that time... but only one day remained until they faced this world’s secret...

sentences.text: [Thunder Step]
Lightning exploded in three different points on the path.
Glacial Reaper Claw moved.
The second one turned into a pillar of ice before wrapping around One’s leg.
The third tried to return underground, but the blue cold spread along its body.
Seris jumped down from One’s back.
King’s Edge appeared on her blade.
Three strikes, short, precise, and without extra movement, and all three were split almost simultaneously.
The roots fell on the ground.
The snake-like bodies inside the glass shells were revealed and trembled for a few moments, then remained motionless.
Liana was still holding her hand up for summoning and looked at the corpses.
"I didn’t even have time to summon it."
Seraphina said nothing, but took her hand off her sword’s hilt.
This was the first time both girls felt the real difference in power.
Liana had seen Lian’s speed before, but back then she could follow his movement.
Now Thunder Step had turned him into nothing but an explosion of light.
Seraphina also felt the remaining Mana density in the air.
Whatever Lian’s level was, his Mana and Skill quality did not match a normal awakened one at the same level.
In the late afternoon of the first day, they entered a denser part of the forest.
The treetops had covered almost the entire sky.
Little light passed through the crystal leaves.
A deep buzzing sound was heard from above.
One stopped.
A few hundred bright points separated from the branches.
At first, they looked like pieces of light, but as they got closer, their insect bodies became clear.
Wings made of transparent plates, armored bodies, multi-faceted eyes, and limbs ending in thin blades.
[Shardwing Drone]
[Level: 16]
[Rank: Normal]
Among the group, larger specimens were also moving.
[Shardwing Hunter]
[Level: 19]
[Rank: Normal]
Their number reached dozens of creatures.
Then the upper branches bent, and the group’s leader came down.
Thick, multi-layered armor was on its chest and head.
Four larger wings came out from its back, and its two front arms resembled crystal spears.
[Shardwing Hive Knight]
[Level: 22]
[Rank: Normal]
The Hive Knight produced a sharp sound.
All the Shardwings turned their wings.
Hundreds of small crystal blades rained down from the sky toward the group.
Seris drew her sword.
Lian prepared Cataclysm Pulse.
But the number of attacks was such that even with their defense, some blades passed by.
It could be said that this was the first time they were facing a flying race, but fortunately, the enemy was not very powerful, and apart from their wings, they had no other advantage.
This time, Seraphina and Liana also found a chance to enter.
Seraphina jumped down from One’s back and held her sword in front of her body.
Blue, red, and purple mana formed around her at the same time.
Lian glanced at her.
His childhood friend’s class was one of the rarest.
It wasn’t outside the norm of the six basic classes.
But it was a combination of two classes.
Dual Class
Warrior / Mage
Dual Class was one of the rarest awakening structures.
Most people only had one main path.
Their bodies were not built to support two classes simultaneously.
But Seraphina had both the physical ability of a swordsman and the Mana structure of a Mage.
Having such a class was a one-in-a-million phenomenon.
A person could be both a healer and a swordsman, or any other combination.
Of course, there are only a few known examples of dual classes, and for this reason, they are not considered categories, and this is not a random or chance phenomenon.
It is mostly a form of intervention and manipulation.
There is a specific Artifact that, if used, can create such a thing.
And Seraphina was lucky enough that her family used such an item, which they had kept for generations, for her.
Although Lian didn’t know why Seraphina.
Was there a specific reason?
Was there a secret behind it?
Or was she just chosen by chance?
She raised her blade.
[Arcane Edge]
Mana gathered on the sword’s edge.
Three Magic Circles formed behind her.
The first circle was blue, the second was red, and the third was purple.
Seraphina sent a horizontal strike.
A line of fire moved with the blade through the air and burned a few Shardwing Drones.
The second strike went upward.
A wave of ice was released from the blue Magic Circle and froze the wings of several insects.
The frozen creatures fell from the sky.
Seraphina took her sword toward another group.
Several Arcane Lances were shot from the purple circle.
The Mana spears pierced the insects’ armor.
She didn’t need to distance herself from the battle to Cast.
Her sword was both a weapon and a Magic Focus.
Every physical strike could release another Spell.
While fighting, Lian evaluated her for a moment.
As always, nothing was perfect, and even Dual Classes had weaknesses.
The weakness of most Dual Classes was that the person wouldn’t reach the peak in either of the two paths.
But Seraphina had high talent in both areas.
Her sword power was real, and her Spells were also not weak or incomplete.
Maybe this girl could make history.
Liana also raised her hand.
A black circle formed under her feet.
"Go."
Shadow Wolf entered One’s shadow and disappeared.
A moment later, it jumped out from the shadow of a tree at a high altitude.
Its body stretched through the air like black smoke, and its red eyes shone among the Shardwings.
Its claws moved, leaving dark lines in the air, and the wings of three insects were cut simultaneously.
Shadow Wolf disappeared into a shadow again.
It came out from another Shardwing’s shadow and closed its jaws around its neck.
Liana did not have high direct offensive power, but her control over her summon was precise.
Every finger movement changed Shadow Wolf’s path.
With a wrist turn, she sent a retreat command.
By closing two fingers, she marked the next target.
By changing her Mana, she controlled the exit time from the shadow.
Her playful and carefree appearance had completely changed at that moment.
Her eyes were moving across the entire field.
She was monitoring every shadow and every enemy.
As long as Shadow Wolf was alive, Liana could attack from angles that most enemies didn’t expect.
But if she lost this summon too, she would be left almost defenseless.
’That wolf is much stronger than when I last saw it.
It’s Level 19, and for its level, it has high power.’ Lian could see this girl’s progress with just one look.
’It’s a pity she lost her other summon.
With two Level 19 summons, she could be a nightmare for her enemies.’
Seris looked at the sky, and her mana spread around her.
[Silver Requiem]
Dozens of sword lines formed among the Shardwing group.
More than ten insects fell from the sky almost simultaneously.
Lian raised his palm.
Cataclysm Pulse was sent toward the sky this time.
The Mana wave spread through the colony like an invisible explosion.
The insects’ flight formation was disrupted.
Some collided with each other.
The Shardwing Hive Knight came down from among the group.
Its four wings compressed Mana and increased its speed.
The multi-layered armor on its chest protected it against direct attacks, and Seraphina built three new Magic Circles behind her.
A lot of Mana was gathered for a larger Spell, but Seris moved sooner, and her body jumped from a broken branch.
[King’s Breaker]
The sword hit the center of the Hive Knight’s armor.
A sound like several glass plates breaking was heard.
The creature’s defensive structure collapsed from the center.
The cracks spread through the entire armor.
Lian activated Thunder Step and appeared on the Hive Knight’s back in an explosion of lightning.
He sank Glacial Reaper Claw into its body through the armor crack.
The cold spread through the insect.
Its four wings froze in an instant, and the Hive Knight fell.
But Lian sank his claw deeper, and he closed his fingers, completely crushing and destroying the entire inside of the monster’s body.
[You have slain Shardwing Hive Knight Lv.22.]
[Bloodlust has absorbed 100% of the available Experience.]
[Due to group kill, the EXP received is halved.]
[Experience threshold reached.]
[Level increased.]
[You have reached Level 19.]
A wave of power spread through Lian’s body.
His exhaustion completely disappeared, but since there were no wounds, his body was not healed either.
The invisible pressure around him increased.
The remaining Shardwings scattered with the death of their leader.
Liana looked up at Lian from below.
The last time she had fought alongside him, his power was considerable, but still within a understandable range.
Now everything had changed.
Speed, physical power, Mana volume, and the variety of Skills.
Lian had grown in this short time like someone who had been in continuous battles for months or even years.
A brief thought crossed Liana’s mind.
Was this really the same person as before?
Seraphina also felt the difference.
She herself was Level 19, but after Lian reached the same level, the pressure of their power did not seem equal.
Fighting him would be unpredictable for any enemy.
Seris only cleaned her sword.
Seraphina and Liana’s reactions didn’t matter to her.
As long as they didn’t slow the group down, their presence didn’t cause any problem.
This time, the corpses were divided among all three of them, except for the silver-haired girl who again wanted nothing, and they immediately moved on.
With nightfall, they camped again beside a tree to rest both themselves and One.
"How much longer until we arrive?" Seraphina asked Lian, who was leaning against One.
"At this speed, only one more day."
They themselves didn’t know at that time... but only one day remained until they faced this world’s secret...

chapters.title: Chapter 258: Hidden Dungeon!
paragraphs: On the second day, shortly after the forest’s faint light rose, they faced another threat.
Unfortunately, they realized that last night’s campsite was actually a monster’s lair, and apparently the owner was not happy that they had settled there.
A massive snake was moving inside the trunk of one of the transparent trees.
From the outside, its body was almost invisible because the color of its scales blended with the Mana inside the tree.
The monster had engaged with One, and after realizing it couldn’t match them, it wanted to escape.
Too bad that escape was not going to be possible.
"Right side." Lian said.
Seris drew her sword without asking.
King’s Edge appeared on the blade.
A precise strike hit the trunk. She did not completely cut the tree, only the outer shell and the snake’s body inside it.
The Crystalcoil Serpent fell out of the trunk with a sharp scream.
Lian activated Iron Fortress Charge. His shoulder hit the snake’s head and slammed it to the ground.
Before the creature could coil its body, Lian’s claw crushed under its neck.
Seraphina had not even completed her first Magic Circle and said with dissatisfaction.
"At least leave one for us."
"Too slow." Seris answered without looking at her.
The Magic Circle behind Seraphina went out. Her eyes narrowed slightly.
Liana laughed quietly. The silent rivalry that had formed earlier intensified with that one word.
In the end, she snorted, and all four mounted One again and set off.
Today was finally the last day they were traveling, and they were going to arrive soon.
A few hours later, a tree-like creature rose from among the roots.
[Mirrorbark Sentinel]
[Level: 23]
[Rank: Normal]
Its body’s shell was made of Mana-reflecting plates.
Any direct Spell could be returned to the user.
Seraphina thought this time she should enter the field with her sword, but before she could move, Seris reached the Sentinel’s leg.
[King’s Breaker]
The strike collapsed the creature’s defensive structure on the leg. The reflective armor cracked from the center.
Lian placed his palm on the ground. Cataclysm Pulse entered the roots, and the Mana wave continued its path underground.
The explosion occurred from inside the Sentinel. The lights on its shell went out, and the giant creature fell to the ground in less than a few seconds.
"I guess our role is to be beautiful spectators." Liana looked at the corpse.
Lian preferred not to answer.
During the journey, each of them gained a new image of the others.
Seraphina now knew that Lian was no longer just a fighter who compensated for power gaps with intelligence and traps.
He now had enough raw power to execute any plan. His speed could compete with Assassins at the same level.
His body could withstand heavy blows, he had massive Mana, and his Skills did not follow any predictable path.
Practically an all-round warrior.
Liana already knew Lian was dangerous.
But the origin of One and the variety of his Skills, even with a Summoner’s knowledge, she could not explain.
The bond between the two was not natural, but it didn’t seem forced either.
One obeyed Lian but was not afraid of him.
Lian had also evaluated Seraphina more precisely. Her Dual Class truly deserved its rarity.
The ability to switch seamlessly between swordsmanship and magic made her a dangerous enemy at both close and long range.
If she had time to grow, she would probably become one of the strongest.
Liana’s value was not in direct power. She was a field controller.
Shadow Wolf could chase enemies, disrupt their focus, and attack from shadows that usually seemed safe.
But losing her first Summon had severely reduced her power.
If she found a chance to obtain a new summon in Emberroot, her abilities would multiply.
Seris showed almost no particular evaluation of the two.
Neither Seraphina’s power had impressed her, nor Liana’s control. As long as they didn’t slow them down, they didn’t matter.
And this indifference annoyed Seraphina more than any hostile behavior.
At the end of the second day, the map reacted for the first time. The black mark on its surface glowed with a faint light.
Lian stopped One and opened the map.
"We’re close."
They changed the path to the south. The further they went, the less dense the trees became.
The bell-like sound of the leaves gradually faded. The small creatures inside the trunks disappeared.
No insects or monsters could be seen on the path. Even the Mana inside the trees flowed more slowly.
As if the entire forest was distancing itself from the point they were approaching.
Of course, aside from that, they were slowly reaching the forest’s edge.
A few minutes later, the trees completely parted, and a circular clearing appeared before them.
All the surrounding trees were bent outward.
In the center of the circle, a dead tree stood. Unlike other Glassthorn trees, its trunk was completely black.
No blue or purple light moved inside it.
Its massive dry roots were wrapped around a stone structure. Among the roots, a door of black glass could be seen.
Its surface did not reflect light. Any light that reached the door disappeared into its darkness.
In the center of the door, the same symbol from the map was carved.
A shape between a closed eye and a broken star. Four hand-shaped indentations were on the four sides of the symbol.
One stopped at the clearing’s edge.
Through Hive Link, Lian felt its instinctive resistance.
The ant did not want to enter the circle.
Lian got down from its back.
Seris, Seraphina, and Liana also got on the ground.
The moment all four stepped into the clearing, silver lines lit up beneath their feet.
The lines moved from four directions and reached the black door.
A system panel appeared before everyone’s view.
[Hidden Dungeon Discovered.]
[Mirror Vault]
[Required Participants: 4]
[Participants Detected: 4/4]
[Entry Condition Satisfied.]
"This was the point on the map? A dungeon?" Seraphina looked at the notification.
"Yeah." Lian did not take his eyes off the black door.
"And coincidentally, it needs four people." Liana looked at the four hand indentations and then added.
"But I didn’t expect it to be a dungeon. A dungeon in the middle of nowhere gives a bad feeling."
"Dungeons are always in the middle of nowhere." Seraphina looked at her as if she was looking at an idiot.
"Don’t argue. For now, this dungeon is more important. Focus on it. We need to figure out exactly what it is." Lian said quietly but with a serious tone.
"So we open it?" Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
"I guess. We came all this way for this." He nodded. Besides, whatever was inside, his intuition was screaming that he had to go inside.
His intuition had not been wrong so far... so it was clear that this time too, he would trust his intuition.
Before any of them could get close to the door, a deep sound rose from underground.
The clearing’s soil trembled. The black roots of the dead tree began to move.
Years of dust fell from the door. The broken symbol in its center slowly lit up white.
Like an eye opening after centuries, a thin line appeared in the center of the black glass.
The door split into two sections. Cold, old air came out from the darkness behind it.
The smell of stone, metal, and a place that had been closed for a very long time spread through the clearing.
The final notification appeared before their view.
[The Trial of Reflections has recognized its challengers.]
The black glass door began to open for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Chapter 259: A Legacy Dungeon!
paragraphs: The black glass door finally opened completely.
Its two massive halves sank into the dry black roots of the dead tree without any sound of scraping or mechanical movement.
The narrow gap that had initially formed between them slowly widened, revealing the darkness behind it.
Cold air came out from inside the structure. Its coldness was not like the natural cold of Glassthorn Forest.
It had no smell of soil, moisture, or plants.
It was dry and lifeless; like air that had remained in a closed space for hundreds or perhaps thousands of years.
Lian stood at the entrance for a few moments. Because of his innate skill, he still did not feel the cold.
But after a long time, he finally felt the cold. This cold was not the kind that makes the body shiver... but a cold that targeted the soul.
He tried to look inside.
His vision passed through the black glass’s surface, but he could not determine the real depth of the space behind the door.
The flows of Mana moved like thin and countless strands in the darkness, and every time he tried to follow their path, they would break on invisible walls.
The interior space did not match the outer structure.
The structure placed among the roots was only a few dozen meters wide from the outside.
But what Lian saw behind the door was much larger.
Seraphina looked at her panel.
[The Trial of Reflections has recognized its challengers.]
"I think it’s too late to turn back now." Liana leaned slightly toward the darkness, but did not cross the threshold.
"It was clear from when the door opened." Seris added coldly.
Liana gave her a brief look.
"Do you always speak this encouragingly?"
Seris did not answer.
Lian commanded One through Hive Link to stay outside the clearing. A wave of dissatisfaction from the ant immediately reached his mind.

One did not want Lian to enter an unknown place without it. Since the Hive Link had formed between them, this was not the first time Lian felt such resistance from it, but this time One’s reaction was stronger.
It was not fear, but a kind of instinctive distrust toward what lay behind the door.
"Stay here and wait." He placed his hand on One’s black shell.
The ant lowered its antennae, and Lian continued.
"If the door closes and we don’t return within a day, move away from this area. Enter Glassthorn Forest and hide yourself."
A wave of opposition was transmitted through the link. It was clear One was not happy with what it had heard.
"This is not an order to abandon us. It’s an order to stay alive."
One remained motionless for a few seconds.
Then it slowly lowered its head, accepting the command, although it was not satisfied with it.
"You sound like you’re saying goodbye." Liana, who could not directly see the communication between the two, but had noticed the subtle changes in One’s behavior, said.
"It’s just caution. We don’t know what we’re going to enter, and I don’t want it to be in danger either."
"Are we going in?" Seraphina gripped her sword tighter.
"We’re going, but anyone who wants to can stay outside. I’m not forcing anyone into an unknown dungeon." Lian examined the dark space once more.
No one said anything. Everyone wanted to enter. No matter how big the threat was, this was not an opportunity they wanted to miss.
The path to becoming stronger and reaching the peak was not going to be calm and safe. In fact, only those who accept risks and dangers can become the future pillars of the world.
The four crossed the threshold.
The moment the last person, Liana, entered, the glass door behind them closed.
The two black halves silently came out from among the roots and joined together.
The outside light was cut off, but the hall did not remain dark. White strands lit up on the floor.
Light spread from beneath their feet and traced thin lines on the ground. The lines went to the surrounding pillars and lit them up one after another.
The interior space gradually became clear. A vast hall lay before them.
So vast that the walls on both sides could be seen at a great distance, and its ceiling disappeared into the darkness.
Pillars of white glass extended in two rows to the end of the hall.
Each pillar had a smooth and flawless surface, but vague shadows moved inside them; like memories trapped behind a thick layer of ice.
The walls were made of black glass.
Their surface reflected the group’s image, but the reflections were blurry and multi-layered.
Sometimes Lian’s image was seen a step behind. Sometimes Seris’s reflection looked in a different direction, and sometimes the faces would change for a moment and turn into unknown faces.
Panels appeared before all four of them.
[Hidden → Legacy Dungeon Discovered.]
[Name: Mirror Vault]
[Type: Succession / Archive]
[Origin: Unknown Ancient Civilization]
[Primary Objective: Search for a Worthy Heir]
Liana kept her gaze on the first phrase.
"Legacy Dungeon?"
"Do you know what that means?" Seraphina also looked at Lian.
There were many types of dungeons, and they didn’t know all of them, especially those who didn’t pay attention in class.
But if anyone here was going to know what a Legacy Dungeon meant... that one person was the young Vorhelm.
Lian examined the panel for a few seconds.
The information he had read in the academy, Vorhelm clan reports, and old documents returned to his mind.
"I think I know. Not every cave or place where a few monsters gather is a dungeon." His voice echoed in the vast hall and returned several times with irregular delays from the walls.
"A dungeon is a space that has its own core, rules, and structure. Its internal environment can differ from the outside world. Sometimes time, distance, or even the rules inside a dungeon change.
Like how this place looked much smaller from the outside.
Some dungeons form naturally. When Mana gathers in one place for a long time, it changes the environment.
Monsters are born inside, rare resources form, and eventually, the dungeon’s core is created."
"But this one is not a natural dungeon." Seraphina added.
"No." Lian turned his gaze back to the panel.
"This is a Legacy Dungeon. That means a civilization or a powerful individual deliberately built it."
"For what?" Liana asked.
"Isn’t it clear from the name? To preserve something after their death or destruction."
"It could be a Skill, a civilization’s knowledge, a weapon, a Bloodline, even memories."
His gaze stopped on the word Succession.
"The Mirror Vault is of the succession type. Its main goal is not to keep treasure or kill intruders. It’s looking for someone who can carry its creator’s legacy."
"So its main goal is not to kill us." Liana smiled for a moment.
That meant they didn’t need to worry about their lives, right? It made her breathe a sigh of relief.
But Lian’s next words were like a hard slap on her face.
"Of course, just because its main goal is not to kill us doesn’t mean we won’t die inside."
"Very encouraging." Liana’s smile faded. She looked at the dark walls.
"What do we need to do to open the next path?" Seris, who had been only examining the environment since the explanation began, said.
Before Lian could answer, a sound was heard from the end of the hall.
It was not the sound of footsteps, but like the very quiet collision of glass with the ground.
Once.
Then again.
A white light appeared among the distant pillars. A creature was coming toward them from the end of the hall.
It had a human-like body, but it bore no resemblance to a living creature. Its entire body was made of white and semi-transparent glass.
Inside its chest, arms, and head, silver strands were moving. Those strands would sometimes intertwine and form a shape like a network of nerves or veins.
Its face was completely flat. It had no eyes.
No mouth, no nose, nothing could be seen on the glass surface of its head.
A panel appeared before their view.

[Level: 10]
From its level, it was clear that it was not a threat at all. It seemed like just a creature entrusted with this legacy dungeon.
The creature stopped a few meters away. Its faceless head first turned to Lian.
Then Seris, Seraphina, and finally Liana.
"Four applicants have been registered." Its voice did not come from a specific place. It was heard simultaneously from all the walls, pillars, and even the floor.
"Memories will be examined, identity will be measured, false bonds will be removed."

"What happens if we fail?" Seraphina stepped forward.
The Mirror Curator turned its head toward her.
"What cannot maintain its own identity is not worthy of carrying the memories of the dead."
The answer was neither a direct threat nor a clear explanation.
"That was not an answer to my question." Seraphina frowned.
The Curator showed no reaction. It was clear that it was not here to answer questions.
It was here to explain the instructions.

Four sections of the black walls separated and moved toward the center.
Each section turned into a tall standing mirror. The mirrors surrounded the group from four directions.
Their surfaces were initially completely black, then reflections appeared.

The version inside the mirror continued to look straight at him.
Seris’s reflection, instead of imitating its owner’s movement, had turned its head toward Lian.
In Seraphina’s mirror, a young girl with similar hair stood, but not the current Seraphina, a child version.
Her clothes were dirty, and blood could be seen on her cheek.
In Liana’s mirror, her own reflection could be seen, but behind her stood the shadow of another girl.
A girl whose hand was placed on the shoulder of Liana’s child version.
A new panel appeared.
[First Trial: The Wound You Carry]
[Enter your reflection.]

Its two massive halves sank into the dry black roots of the dead tree without any sound of scraping or mechanical movement.
The narrow gap that had initially formed between them slowly widened, revealing the darkness behind it.
Cold air came out from inside the structure.
Its coldness was not like the natural cold of Glassthorn Forest.
It had no smell of soil, moisture, or plants.
It was dry and lifeless; like air that had remained in a closed space for hundreds or perhaps thousands of years.
Lian stood at the entrance for a few moments.
Because of his innate skill, he still did not feel the cold.
But after a long time, he finally felt the cold.
This cold was not the kind that makes the body shiver... but a cold that targeted the soul.
He tried to look inside.
His vision passed through the black glass’s surface, but he could not determine the real depth of the space behind the door.
The flows of Mana moved like thin and countless strands in the darkness, and every time he tried to follow their path, they would break on invisible walls.
The interior space did not match the outer structure.
The structure placed among the roots was only a few dozen meters wide from the outside.
But what Lian saw behind the door was much larger.
Seraphina looked at her panel.

"I think it’s too late to turn back now." Liana leaned slightly toward the darkness, but did not cross the threshold.
"It was clear from when the door opened." Seris added coldly.
Liana gave her a brief look.
"Do you always speak this encouragingly?"
Seris did not answer.
Lian commanded One through Hive Link to stay outside the clearing.
A wave of dissatisfaction from the ant immediately reached his mind.
One did not want Lian to enter an unknown place without it.
Since the Hive Link had formed between them, this was not the first time Lian felt such resistance from it, but this time One’s reaction was stronger.
It was not fear, but a kind of instinctive distrust toward what lay behind the door.
"Stay here and wait." He placed his hand on One’s black shell.
The ant lowered its antennae, and Lian continued.
"If the door closes and we don’t return within a day, move away from this area.
Enter Glassthorn Forest and hide yourself."
A wave of opposition was transmitted through the link.
It was clear One was not happy with what it had heard.
"This is not an order to abandon us.
It’s an order to stay alive."
One remained motionless for a few seconds.
Then it slowly lowered its head, accepting the command, although it was not satisfied with it.

"It’s just caution.
We don’t know what we’re going to enter, and I don’t want it to be in danger either."
"Are we going in?" Seraphina gripped her sword tighter.
"We’re going, but anyone who wants to can stay outside.
I’m not forcing anyone into an unknown dungeon." Lian examined the dark space once more.
No one said anything.
Everyone wanted to enter.
No matter how big the threat was, this was not an opportunity they wanted to miss.
The path to becoming stronger and reaching the peak was not going to be calm and safe.

The moment the last person, Liana, entered, the glass door behind them closed.
The two black halves silently came out from among the roots and joined together.
The outside light was cut off, but the hall did not remain dark.
White strands lit up on the floor.
Light spread from beneath their feet and traced thin lines on the ground.
The lines went to the surrounding pillars and lit them up one after another.
The interior space gradually became clear.
A vast hall lay before them.

Pillars of white glass extended in two rows to the end of the hall.
Each pillar had a smooth and flawless surface, but vague shadows moved inside them; like memories trapped behind a thick layer of ice.
The walls were made of black glass.

chapters.title: Chapter 260: The First Trial I
paragraphs: Before any of them could decide what to do, what was happening, or what situation they were in, the mirrors’ surfaces rippled.
An invisible force came out from within them.
Lian tried to pull his foot back, but the hall’s floor locked around his feet like a sticky substance.
Seris placed her hand on her sword.
Seraphina flowed Mana through her body.
Liana prepared her summoning circle.
But none of them found a chance to use their abilities.
Darkness swallowed them from four directions, and the hall disappeared.
Lian smelled old wood before opening his eyes.
A familiar smell, of course not from Glassthorn Forest, but the smell of wooden walls, protective oil, and heavy fabrics of the Vorhelm clan’s main mansion.
He opened his eyes. He was standing in one of the eastern corridors of the mansion.
The orange light of evening was coming through the tall windows and creating drawn lines on the polished floor.
"Here? How is this possible?"
The sound of servants’ footsteps could be heard in the corridor. The curtains moved with a gentle breeze.
Everything was real... too real.
Lian placed his hand on the wall. The texture of the wood could be felt under his fingers.
Even the thin scratch that had been made years ago when moving a training armor on the wall was still in that same spot.
He was sure... this was the Vorhelm clan’s mansion, but how was he here?
An illusion? What other possibility could there be besides an illusion?
He looked at his body. He had his current body.
His armor, Skills, and stats were all in place... but no one saw his presence.
Two servants passed by him without even turning their heads.
At the end of the corridor, a boy was standing.
A younger Lian, from a few years ago, before awakening talents and before leaving the clan... at a time when his awakening failure had destroyed all the future they had imagined for him.
The boy standing at the end of the corridor was thinner, wearing simple training clothes.
In his hand was a sheet of paper with several names written on it.
His gaze was stopped on one of the lines. His own name was not there.
The clan’s instructor came out of the training door.
The younger Lian stepped forward.
"Instructor, my name is not on the list."
"There is no mistake." The instructor did not even take the sheet from his hand.
"But today’s tactical training was for all members of the same age." The young Lian was sure a mistake had been made. Why was his name not on the training list?
The instructor gave him a brief look. Not with hatred or anger, but with a kind of indifference that was heavier than any direct humiliation.
"The clan’s resources are used for those who have a future." He said calmly, as if explaining an obvious truth.
Then he passed by the boy.
The current Lian watched the scene. He remembered this memory, but not with this clarity. In his mind, only a short sentence had remained.
This was a normal scene he experienced for a while after turning 16.
The Mirror Vault had restored all the forgotten details.
The scene changed. Only a blink was enough, as if the world had suddenly shifted.
Lian found himself in the clan’s dining hall. The long table was prepared for dinner.
Various family members and a few guests were seated around it.
The younger Lian was standing next to his usual seat, but one of the servants collected his plate and utensils.
A young guest with a four-star class was supposed to sit there.
"Your place has been prepared at the end of the table." The servant who had called him "Young Master Lian" for years said this time without looking.
Only "Lian", not young master, not a member of the clan. Just a name that had to be sent to a corner so as not to disturb the important guests.
Near him, two clan members were talking about him.
Of course, not secretly or even in a low voice, as if his presence didn’t matter.
"Without a Talent, there’s no place for him even in the secondary branches."
"He’ll probably be given a clerical job later."
"If it wasn’t for his father, they would have kicked him out of the mansion by now."
No one directly targeted him. No one needed to. All the behaviors had one message.
He was no longer part of the clan’s future.
The scene changed again.
Lian’s small training room. The weapon racks were empty. His training armor had been removed.
Even his notes table had been moved to someone else’s room.
"They said you no longer need this room." one of the servants said.
The younger Lian stood in the center of the empty space.
"Then where am I supposed to train?"
The servant shrugged.
"I don’t know."
And left.
Again, no violence, no shouting, no direct insults. Only the gradual removal of everything that proved he had a place in that house.
The current Lian watched in silence.
Once, he had thought he could leave the clan.
But where would he go? His family name was his entire identity.
He had no money, no connections outside the clan, no school or organization would accept an awakening failure without support.
Even if he left, no future awaited him.
He lived in a house that no longer wanted him, but the outside world also had no place for him.
The scene changed to the library.
It was night. Most of the lights were off.
The younger Lian was sitting at a table in a far corner. Combat reports, maps, and analysis of other people’s Skills were spread around him.
His eyes were red from exhaustion, but he was still reading.
Not just because he loved studying. Analysis was the only thing no one had been able to take from him.
If he couldn’t obtain the power of Skills, he could understand their structure.
If he couldn’t participate in training, he could see others’ mistakes.
If he wasn’t allowed to enter the field, he could reconstruct the entire field on paper.
Those nights built the foundation of the person who had now survived the Graveyard and the Forest of Giants, and had the ability to fight Fallen ones and colonies.
The sound of footsteps was heard from behind.
Lian turned around.
A mature version of himself was standing among the shelves. The face was the same, but he wore the Vorhelm clan’s formal attire.
The heir’s insignia was on his chest, and his gaze was calm and confident.
"All you ever wanted was their acceptance."
Lian did not answer.
"You didn’t want power for power’s sake." The Reflection approached the table.
It placed its finger on one of the reports.
"You wanted to force them to look at you."
Lian looked at his younger version. The boy was still leaning over the report, as if he didn’t see either of them.
The difference between him and the younger version was only two years.
Did he really want to be admired by his family at that time? Maybe.
"You wanted to walk into that same hall one day and make everyone who ignored you stand up." The Reflection continued.
"You wanted the instructor who removed your name from the list to beg to teach you."
"You wanted to prove to everyone they were wrong."
"Back then? Yeah." Lian finally said. He didn’t want to listen to this nonsense anymore.
The Reflection paused for a moment, perhaps expecting denial.
"I thought about it every day." The admission was not difficult for Lian. This was a truth that had existed inside him for years.
He really did want power to force others to accept him.
Not out of nobility, not out of a grand ideal, but out of anger, humiliation, and the need to be seen.
"Now you have power." The Reflection gave a faint smile.
The library hall faded. The clan’s main hall took its place.
Dozens of Vorhelm members were kneeling on both sides of the path, and at the end of the hall, the heir’s seat was placed.
"Don’t you want to go back and force them to kneel?"
Lian looked at the scene. Once, this image was a dream for him.
Maybe even now, part of him would enjoy seeing it. But that desire was no longer the center of his decisions.
If he had wanted to stay in the Vorhelm clan, he would have just said yes to his uncle’s proposal when he returned for the birthday ceremony... but
"No."
"Why?" The Reflection raised an eyebrow.
Lian took his gaze off the kneeling figures and fixed it on his teenage self standing in the corner of the hall.
"Because if I still make all my decisions based on their opinion, it means I never really left that house."
"I don’t have to forgive them." His gaze turned cold.
"I don’t have to pretend those years didn’t matter." Then he approached the teenager. The young boy finally raised his head.
Lian stood in front of him.
"But what they did to us is not going to be everything we are."
The young boy said nothing, and Lian placed his hand on his shoulder.
"You were weak, but you were not worthless."
The environment cracked. The hall... the kneeling figures... the heir Reflection.
"So there is no wound or regret." The young Lian suddenly said with a smile.
All turned into pieces of glass.
The teenage version of Lian also slowly faded, but this time his face was not empty or broken.
A panel appeared before Lian’s view.
[First Trial Cleared.]
[Trial Boon Acquired: Mirror Anchor]
[Your sense of identity has been strengthened.]
A calm feeling formed in the depth of his mind. Not an increase in physical power or anything like that.
More like a fixed point in the center of his consciousness; something that told him who he was, even if all his memories and senses around him changed.
This was his identity, this was his character, and he had proven that there was no regret about his past.
The days that were expected to be the darkest days of his life... had been buried by himself.

He no longer needed his family’s admiration. He just wanted to be the strongest, to stand at the top of the world, to be above everyone, so that this world would seek his approval... not him seeking the world’s approval.
Before he could find a chance to examine further, the darkness swallowed him again...

"Because if I still make all my decisions based on their opinion, it means I never really left that house."
"I don’t have to forgive them." His gaze turned cold.
"I don’t have to pretend those years didn’t matter." Then he approached the teenager.
The young boy finally raised his head.
Lian stood in front of him.
"But what they did to us is not going to be everything we are."
The young boy said nothing, and Lian placed his hand on his shoulder.
"You were weak, but you were not worthless."
The environment cracked.
The hall... the kneeling figures... the heir Reflection.
"So there is no wound or regret." The young Lian suddenly said with a smile.
All turned into pieces of glass.
The teenage version of Lian also slowly faded, but this time his face was not empty or broken.
A panel appeared before Lian’s view.
[First Trial Cleared.]
[Trial Boon Acquired: Mirror Anchor]
[Your sense of identity has been strengthened.]
A calm feeling formed in the depth of his mind.
Not an increase in physical power or anything like that.
More like a fixed point in the center of his consciousness; something that told him who he was, even if all his memories and senses around him changed.
This was his identity, this was his character, and he had proven that there was no regret about his past.
The days that were expected to be the darkest days of his life... had been buried by himself.
He no longer needed his family’s admiration.
He just wanted to be the strongest, to stand at the top of the world, to be above everyone, so that this world would seek his approval... not him seeking the world’s approval.
Before he could find a chance to examine further, the darkness swallowed him again...

chapters.title: Chapter 261: The First Trial II
paragraphs: Seraphina opened her eyes to the sound of an alarm, a loud and continuous sound echoing throughout the city.
People were running in the streets, someone was holding a child in their arms.
A bloody man was lying on the ground, soldiers at the end of the street were trying to guide the crowd toward a shelter.
The sky had split into purple and black.
A massive crack was among the clouds, and the shadows of monsters were coming out of it one after another.
Even before seeing the half-destroyed house, Seraphina recognized the place.
Her breath caught for a moment. She had not forgotten this day.
She never could... the day her mother died.
She was in her current body, her sword in her hand, her Skills available.
But a few meters away, her child version was trapped under a section of collapsed wall.
The little girl was not crying, perhaps from the intensity of fear, she couldn’t even cry.
A few steps ahead, her mother was standing in front of a monster.
A woman with long hair and simple clothes, she had no real weapon, only a metal rod in her hand to keep the creature away from her child.
"Get back!" Seraphina involuntarily shouted.
No one heard her voice.
The monster attacked the mother.
Seraphina moved, her body passed through the street, her sword covered with red Mana, and the blade passed through the creature’s neck.
The monster’s head was severed, and for a moment, everything was silent.
Seraphina looked at her mother... she had saved her.
But a shadow came out from behind the wall... the second monster sank its claw into the woman’s chest.
Seraphina turned around.
It was too late. Blood splashed on the ground.
"Nooooo" Her eyes filled with tears... a scene that tore her heart into a thousand pieces.
But before she could do anything, the world suddenly rewound.
The alarm sound started from the beginning again... people ran in the same direction.
The wall was collapsed the same way... her mother was standing in front of the monster.
This time, Seraphina went straight for the second monster. A blue Magic Circle formed behind her.
A wall of Mana was built in front of her mother.
The first monster hit the Barrier, the second was killed before it could attack.
Seraphina let out her breath. This time, she had been able to save her mother... even if it wasn’t real... even if it was just a dream, illusion, or whatever... she had succeeded.
But the building’s roof above them collapsed. Rubble fell on her mother.
The child’s scream echoed in the street.
"Motherrrrrrr!" Seraphina’s eyes filled with tears again!
The world rewound again.
The third time, Seraphina was faster... she used sword and magic simultaneously.
The monsters were killed before they could get close.
A Barrier was built around the mother and child, even the roof was deflected before falling by a wave of Mana.
But the crack in the sky widened.
A wave of purple energy covered the city, and her mother’s body was torn apart under the Mana pressure.
Rewind.
Fourth time.
Fifth.
Sixth.
Each time, Seraphina acted stronger, faster, and angrier. Each time, she used a different combination.
Fire.
Barrier.
Sword.
Arcane Lance.
But the result did not change. If the monsters died, the rubble would fall. If the rubble was controlled, the Mana wave would arrive.
If the wave was deflected, the child version would die under the wall, and the mother would sacrifice herself to save her.
The Mirror Vault found a different path to the same end every time.
Seraphina’s breaths became heavy. Her hands were trembling, from anger.
"Again."
The world obeyed.
Rewind.
She fought again.
And failed again.
"Again."
Once more.
Again, she was too late.
"Again!"
Her voice broke in the street.
But this time, before the scene could begin, everything stopped.
The people froze mid-run... the monster remained motionless in the air... her mother was still standing in front of the child.
Seraphina was breathing in the center of the street, her hand around her sword’s hilt clenched so tightly that blood flowed from her palm.
"If the sword wasn’t enough, magic was chosen." A voice came from nowhere.
An image of Seraphina with a sword appeared, then a version in Mage robes.
"If magic was too slow, the sword was chosen."
"If one failed, the other was created."
Two versions stood in front of her.
"But neither changed the past."
Seraphina closed her eyes. Her entire life, she had tried to never be helpless again.
That’s why she had developed her Dual Class with pressure and training beyond normal limits.
If the enemy was close, she had a sword. If far, magic. If attack wasn’t enough, defense.
There was always another tool, always another way.
But in the deepest part of her being, she was still the same child who believed that if she had more power, her mother would have survived.
This had happened when she was two or three years old. Her family lived in one of the country’s large cities.
Her father was an important figure in that city and was even known at the national level.
Their house was in a safe area, or at least it should have been!
But in the face of a massive and widespread surge of monsters, nowhere is safe.

In the current era, monster rifts are not a great danger. Guilds, governments, and alliances have many ways to deal with them, and people’s safety is not as threatened as in the old days when entire cities were massacred.
But occasionally, just occasionally, a very large rift opens and a huge surge of monsters occurs, so many that dealing with them is not easy.
This was what happened when she was two years old. When her father had gone to the capital... at that time, a large rift opened and a great number of monsters came out.
The city was massacred, and her mother was killed... she almost died too but was saved at the last moment.
She didn’t understand why... why had the support teams arrived so late? Why? Why? Why?
If they had arrived just a few minutes earlier, her mother would have been saved too... if her father had never left the city, her mother would have survived.
Nevertheless, her father had never once expressed regret!
After that and her mother’s death, she returned with her father to his family’s city, to the city of Medes, where the Vorhelm clan was located, and she met Lian.
Sixteen years had passed since that incident, but she could never and would never forget that day...
The pain of that day followed her like a curse. She always tried to hide it, and many people are not aware of the truth about her mother.
But she knew she either had to understand that no matter what she did... the past cannot be changed... or she had to try to make sure this didn’t happen to another child.
The scene moved again.
But this time, Seraphina did not go toward the monsters. She lowered her sword and walked toward her child version.
She knelt beside the rubble.
The child looked at her, her eyes full of fear and questions.
"Why can’t you save her?"
For a few seconds, Seraphina could not answer. Her throat was dry, and her gaze fell on her mother.
She knew what was about to happen in a few moments.
But this time, she did not stand up. Instead, she took the child’s hand.
"Because this already happened."
The sentence was simple, but saying it was harder than any battle.
"Then why did we come back?" The child fixed her gaze on her mother.
Seraphina held her small fingers tighter.
"To understand that surviving was not a betrayal." Her voice became quieter.
"We survived."
Her mother looked at them for the last time.
Not with anger, not with blame, not with expectation, but only calmness in her gaze.
"Now we have to make sure her death wasn’t meaningless." Seraphina continued.
The scene began to collapse.
But before it disappeared completely, two flows of Mana inside Seraphina changed.
The Warrior’s physical path and the Mage’s magical flow had always moved like two separate rivers in her body. She had learned to switch quickly between them, but they had never truly become one.
Now, for the first time, their rhythm became synchronized. As if a great pain had been lifted from her soul... that wound was still not healed, but it no longer hurt.
A panel appeared.
[First Trial Cleared.]
[Trial Boon Acquired: Twin-Core Resonance]
[Compatibility between Swordswoman and Mage has increased.]
Seraphina placed her hand on her chest.
She felt the beat of the two power paths. For the first time, there was no wall between them.
Perhaps on that day, the greatest Dual awakened one was born...
Before she could examine the change further, the street, the sky, and her mother’s image turned to light.

chapters.title: Chapter 262: The First Trial ( Final )
paragraphs: Liana opened her eyes and saw a cracked ceiling. Cold air was coming in through the broken window.
A few metal beds were on both sides of the room. Some had no mattresses, and some were covered with thin, old blankets.
The smell of thin soup and moisture was in the air.
The orphanage.
Liana recognized it immediately, not because of a sign or specific mark, but because of the feeling that formed in her chest.
An old feeling of hunger, cold, and waiting for someone to call her name.
In the corner of the room, a small girl was sitting.
Her hair was messy, her clothes looked slightly too big for her body.
A child version of Liana, and next to her, a girl of the same age but with a slightly larger build was sitting.
Selina.
Selina divided her food bowl between herself and Liana.
She took a smaller portion for herself and, without saying anything, placed the larger portion in front of the younger girl.
"An illusion?" The current Liana watched from a distance. Memories appeared one after another.
"Even if it’s an illusion, what should I do? Just watch?" She didn’t understand what this trial wanted from her.
There was no explanation, and she had been thrown here without her consent. Was this trial stupid?
Anyway, since she couldn’t do anything else, she continued watching.
An older boy had taken Liana’s toy.
Selina stood in front of him and took it back.
Nights when thunder and lightning came and Liana would wake up from sleep.
Selina would sit on the bed next to her without mocking her.
Time passed like this.
One day, when one of the orphanage officials angrily asked about a broken dish, Liana smiled and distracted his attention with a joke.
The first time she succeeded, the man’s anger subsided.
That day, she understood something. A smile could be a weapon. A joke could change dangerous questions.
Playfulness could make others not ask how she really felt.
Years passed.
The childish smile turned into a seductive tone. Simple jokes turned into wordplay.
Liana learned to always have something to say, always keep the answer light, and always change the atmosphere before anyone could get close to her fear.
Not because nothing mattered to her.
But because if everything was a joke, no one could see how much she feared being alone.
The scene suddenly changed.
The warmth of the orphanage, however little and insufficient, disappeared.
Liana found herself in Glassthorn Forest, but the forest was darker, the trees were broken, and blood could be seen on the glass roots.
In the distance, Selina was lying on the ground.
Her adult version, her armor was torn, blood was flowing from her mouth.
A few monsters were approaching her from among the trees.
Upon seeing that scene, even though she knew it was an illusion, her heartbeat suddenly increased. She panicked and became scared, and Liana ran.
But with every step, the distance grew.
"Selina!"
Her voice echoed in the forest.
Selina raised her head. Her gaze was cold, not the gaze Liana knew.
"You always laugh."
"Just hold on a little!" Liana increased her speed.
"Even when others die because of you."
The words entered her chest like blades. Liana tried to smile.
"Well, if that’s going to be your last words, you could have chosen something better."
But the sound did not come from her throat. Her lips moved, but no sound was made.
As if she was only condemned to listen.
"Your summon died." Selina continued.
An image of Liana’s lost first Summon appeared on the ground.
"The rest will die too."
Shadow Wolf lay wounded at another distance.
"Then me.
The monsters came closer.
"And you will still laugh."
Liana’s smile disappeared. For the first time, she had no sentence to change the atmosphere.
No joke, no game... only fear remained, the fear she had hidden behind a smile her entire life.
"I laugh because..." Her voice broke.
The forest fell silent, even the monsters stopped. The girl took a deep breath.
She had never said this confession out loud. Perhaps she had never even fully expressed it to herself.
"Because if I don’t, I might ask everyone not to leave me alone." Tears gathered in her eyes, but she didn’t let them fall.
She looked at the fake Selina.
"I might have to admit that I’m scared."
Selina said nothing.
Liana stepped forward. This time, the distance became shorter.
"But you are not Selina." The reflection’s face trembled for a moment.
"She would never use my fear against me."
The shadow beneath Liana’s feet expanded. Shadow Wolf came out of it.
Its body was not wounded. Its red eyes shone in the darkness. This time, Liana did not stand behind the Summon, but beside it.
She placed her hand on the shadowy wolf’s neck.
"Together."
Shadow Wolf leaped forward, and she moved with it.
The dark claws passed through Selina’s image. The reflection shattered like glass.
But before it completely collapsed, its cold face turned into the same calm smile of the real Selina.
Then it disappeared, and a panel appeared.
[First Trial Cleared.]
[Trial Boon Acquired: Familiar Soul Anchor]
[Your spiritual connection with contracted creatures has been stabilized.]
A warm flow moved through the contract toward Shadow Wolf.
Liana not only felt the Summon’s presence, but also its spiritual pulse.
Fear, loyalty, and its desire to protect her. A smile formed on her face.
But this time, it was not to hide.
At the same time... Seris appeared in the Pendragon clan’s hall.
The space was cold, massive, and flawless.
Black and silver flags hung from the walls. Ancestral swords were in glass cases, and the clan’s emblem was seen above the hall.
Pendragon members were standing on both sides of the path.
None of them moved. All their gazes were fixed on the end of the hall.
Seris first looked at them. With one look, she could tell that this trial had trapped her in an illusion.
But an illusion? Did this dungeon really think such a cliché thing would work on her?
She had no regrets, fears, or weaknesses that could be used against her.
Then she stared at the end of the hall, where everyone was staring.
Lian was standing there, wearing the Vorhelm clan’s formal attire, and the black insignia of the clan was on his chest.
"These Vorhelms never approach without a purpose." A voice said from among the Pendragon members.
"You simple girl! We told you not to trust a Vorhelm!"
"Vorhelms are all cunning foxes! They use everything for their own benefit!"
"Because of your simplicity, all our family’s secrets are now in the hands of the Vorhelms! This is the end of the Pendragon clan! You are a traitor!"
An image appeared in the air.
Lian asking about King’s Edge.
The second image.
He was examining Seris’s sword movements during training.
The third image.
A conversation about the Pendragon clan’s structure.
The fourth image.
Lian looking at the family insignia on her weapon.
The memories seemed real.
Every normal question looked like information gathering, every analytical look like target assessment.
The fake version of Lian stepped forward a few steps.
"Our families were enemies." His tone was calm, not villainous or exaggerated.
Exactly like the real Lian when explaining an unpleasant truth.
"Did you really think I became friends with you for no reason?"
Seris said nothing. Her hand was on her sword’s hilt.
"You were useful." The fake Lian continued.
The images around them changed.
Pendragon Skills.
The paths to enter the mansion, the clan’s important people.
"You had access to Pendragon Skills."
"To the clan’s information." Then he looked directly into her eyes.
"And most importantly, you trusted me."
For Seris, Seraphina and Liana did not matter much. She had just met them.
If their paths separated tomorrow, perhaps the only practical effect would be reducing the group’s number of fighters.
Even in her entire life, she had never truly connected with anyone... everyone, at best, had only been an instructor or a training target for her.
She had been raised as the family’s treasure from childhood, and her parents’ behavior with her was different and special, which had caused her to have no special feelings even toward them.
But Lian was different.
He was the only person Seris truly considered her friend.
Someone who knew her combat rhythm, someone who understood her decisions without long explanations.
Someone who had accepted her presence not because of her clan, power, or duty, but as an independent person. And Lian was the only person who had been able to defeat her... a goal she could pursue.
That is why this illusion was more dangerous than any physical enemy.
The enmity between the clans was real. Vorhelm and Pendragon had stood against each other many times in politics, resources, and influence.
It was possible that one day Lian would use his connection with Seris.
She knew that Lian had separated from the Vorhelms... but what if it was all just a plan to get close to her? It was not impossible, right?
Logically, it was not impossible.
Seris’s fingers tightened around the hilt.
"Finally, you understand." The fake Lian gave a short smile.
Seris did not attack immediately.
Instead of the face in front of her, she remembered Lian’s real actions. Times when he could have left her and didn’t.
Moments when he hadn’t hidden information from her, even when hiding it would have been easier.
And more importantly, her knowledge of his mind.
Seris drew her sword.
"So you understand?" Lian’s reflection said.
"Yeah."
"What?"
Seris held the blade beside her body.
"If Lian wanted to use me, he would have done it much better than this."
The fake version’s smile faded.
Seris took a step, and her sword moved only once. Lian’s image was split from the center.
The Pendragon hall also cracked with it.
But just before collapsing, Seris’s fingers were still slightly tighter around the hilt than usual.
The illusion was a lie.
But it had touched a real point.
Seris might not care about many people, but now she knew that losing Lian’s trust really mattered to her.
This was a truth she had never even thought about until now... but now she had realized it.
She didn’t want to lose her friendship with Lian.
[First Trial Cleared.]
[Trial Boon Acquired: Unclouded Edge]
[Mental interference will have less influence on your Sword Intent.]
Her sword’s Mana became clearer for a moment.
Every doubt that could have diverted the blade’s path was gone.
The hall shattered, and the darkness returned.
All four returned to the main hall almost simultaneously, and only a few seconds of real time had passed.
The first trial was over!
