Liana learned to always have something to say, always keep the answer light, and always change the atmosphere before anyone could get close to her fear.
Not because nothing mattered to her.
But because if everything was a joke, no one could see how much she feared being alone.
The scene suddenly changed.
The warmth of the orphanage, however little and insufficient, disappeared.
Liana found herself in Glassthorn Forest, but the forest was darker, the trees were broken, and blood could be seen on the glass roots.
In the distance, Selina was lying on the ground.
Her adult version, her armor was torn, blood was flowing from her mouth.
A few monsters were approaching her from among the trees.
Upon seeing that scene, even though she knew it was an illusion, her heartbeat suddenly increased.
She panicked and became scared, and Liana ran.
But with every step, the distance grew.
"Selina!"
Her voice echoed in the forest.
Selina raised her head.
Her gaze was cold, not the gaze Liana knew.
"You always laugh."
"Just hold on a little!" Liana increased her speed.
"Even when others die because of you."
The words entered her chest like blades.
Liana tried to smile.
"Well, if that’s going to be your last words, you could have chosen something better."
But the sound did not come from her throat.
Her lips moved, but no sound was made.
As if she was only condemned to listen.
"Your summon died." Selina continued.
An image of Liana’s lost first Summon appeared on the ground.
"The rest will die too."
Shadow Wolf lay wounded at another distance.
"Then me.
The monsters came closer.
"And you will still laugh."
Liana’s smile disappeared.
For the first time, she had no sentence to change the atmosphere.
No joke, no game... only fear remained, the fear she had hidden behind a smile her entire life.
"I laugh because..." Her voice broke.
The forest fell silent, even the monsters stopped.
The girl took a deep breath.
She had never said this confession out loud.
Perhaps she had never even fully expressed it to herself.
"Because if I don’t, I might ask everyone not to leave me alone." Tears gathered in her eyes, but she didn’t let them fall.
She looked at the fake Selina.
"I might have to admit that I’m scared."
Selina said nothing.
Liana stepped forward.
This time, the distance became shorter.
"But you are not Selina." The reflection’s face trembled for a moment.
"She would never use my fear against me."
The shadow beneath Liana’s feet expanded.
Shadow Wolf came out of it.
Its body was not wounded.
Its red eyes shone in the darkness.
This time, Liana did not stand behind the Summon, but beside it.
She placed her hand on the shadowy wolf’s neck.
"Together."
Shadow Wolf leaped forward, and she moved with it.
The dark claws passed through Selina’s image.
The reflection shattered like glass.
But before it completely collapsed, its cold face turned into the same calm smile of the real Selina.
Then it disappeared, and a panel appeared.
[First Trial Cleared.]
[Trial Boon Acquired: Familiar Soul Anchor]
[Your spiritual connection with contracted creatures has been stabilized.]
A warm flow moved through the contract toward Shadow Wolf.
Liana not only felt the Summon’s presence, but also its spiritual pulse.
Fear, loyalty, and its desire to protect her.
A smile formed on her face.
But this time, it was not to hide.
At the same time...
Seris appeared in the Pendragon clan’s hall.
The space was cold, massive, and flawless.
Black and silver flags hung from the walls.
Ancestral swords were in glass cases, and the clan’s emblem was seen above the hall.
Pendragon members were standing on both sides of the path.
None of them moved.
All their gazes were fixed on the end of the hall.
Seris first looked at them.
With one look, she could tell that this trial had trapped her in an illusion.
But an illusion?
Did this dungeon really think such a cliché thing would work on her?
She had no regrets, fears, or weaknesses that could be used against her.
Then she stared at the end of the hall, where everyone was staring.
Lian was standing there, wearing the Vorhelm clan’s formal attire, and the black insignia of the clan was on his chest.
"These Vorhelms never approach without a purpose." A voice said from among the Pendragon members.
"You simple girl!
We told you not to trust a Vorhelm!"
"Vorhelms are all cunning foxes!
They use everything for their own benefit!"
"Because of your simplicity, all our family’s secrets are now in the hands of the Vorhelms!
This is the end of the Pendragon clan!
You are a traitor!"
An image appeared in the air.
Lian asking about King’s Edge.
The second image.
He was examining Seris’s sword movements during training.
The third image.
A conversation about the Pendragon clan’s structure.
The fourth image.
Lian looking at the family insignia on her weapon.
The memories seemed real.
Every normal question looked like information gathering, every analytical look like target assessment.
The fake version of Lian stepped forward a few steps.
"Our families were enemies." His tone was calm, not villainous or exaggerated.
Exactly like the real Lian when explaining an unpleasant truth.
"Did you really think I became friends with you for no reason?"
Seris said nothing.
Her hand was on her sword’s hilt.
"You were useful." The fake Lian continued.
The images around them changed.
Pendragon Skills.
The paths to enter the mansion, the clan’s important people.
"You had access to Pendragon Skills."
"To the clan’s information." Then he looked directly into her eyes.
"And most importantly, you trusted me."
For Seris, Seraphina and Liana did not matter much.
She had just met them.
If their paths separated tomorrow, perhaps the only practical effect would be reducing the group’s number of fighters.
Even in her entire life, she had never truly connected with anyone... everyone, at best, had only been an instructor or a training target for her.
She had been raised as the family’s treasure from childhood, and her parents’ behavior with her was different and special, which had caused her to have no special feelings even toward them.
But Lian was different.
He was the only person Seris truly considered her friend.
Someone who knew her combat rhythm, someone who understood her decisions without long explanations.
Someone who had accepted her presence not because of her clan, power, or duty, but as an independent person.
And Lian was the only person who had been able to defeat her... a goal she could pursue.
That is why this illusion was more dangerous than any physical enemy.
The enmity between the clans was real.
Vorhelm and Pendragon had stood against each other many times in politics, resources, and influence.
It was possible that one day Lian would use his connection with Seris.
She knew that Lian had separated from the Vorhelms... but what if it was all just a plan to get close to her?
It was not impossible, right?
Logically, it was not impossible.
Seris’s fingers tightened around the hilt.
"Finally, you understand." The fake Lian gave a short smile.
Seris did not attack immediately.
Instead of the face in front of her, she remembered Lian’s real actions.
Times when he could have left her and didn’t.
Moments when he hadn’t hidden information from her, even when hiding it would have been easier.
And more importantly, her knowledge of his mind.
Seris drew her sword.
"So you understand?" Lian’s reflection said.
"Yeah."
"What?"
Seris held the blade beside her body.
"If Lian wanted to use me, he would have done it much better than this."
The fake version’s smile faded.
Seris took a step, and her sword moved only once.
Lian’s image was split from the center.
The Pendragon hall also cracked with it.
But just before collapsing, Seris’s fingers were still slightly tighter around the hilt than usual.
The illusion was a lie.
But it had touched a real point.
Seris might not care about many people, but now she knew that losing Lian’s trust really mattered to her.
This was a truth she had never even thought about until now... but now she had realized it.
She didn’t want to lose her friendship with Lian.
[First Trial Cleared.]
[Trial Boon Acquired: Unclouded Edge]
[Mental interference will have less influence on your Sword Intent.]
Her sword’s Mana became clearer for a moment.
Every doubt that could have diverted the blade’s path was gone.
The hall shattered, and the darkness returned.
All four returned to the main hall almost simultaneously, and only a few seconds of real time had passed.
The first trial was over!

chapters.title: Chapter 263: The Second Trial
paragraphs: Even though only a few seconds had passed, for each of them, hours or even days had gone by.
No one spoke immediately.
Liana brought her usual smile back to her face, but this time it was calmer, less like a shield.
Shadow Wolf appeared beside her foot and pressed its body against her leg.
Seraphina had placed her hand on her chest.
She felt the two flows of Mana moving inside her for the first time without collision or delay.
Seris gave a brief look at Lian, only a moment.
Lian saw that look, but asked nothing. He felt that each of them had seen something they currently had no desire to explain.
He could understand. He himself had seen something he hadn’t expected, but he had moved past that stage long ago, and it really didn’t affect him.
But he couldn’t say the same for the rest of them.
"Are you all okay?" As soon as he said this, the Mirror Curator, still standing in the center of the hall, suddenly opened its mouth.
"The wounds have been identified."
"No identity has collapsed."
A panel appeared.
[First Trial Cleared.]
The floor beneath their feet began to move. White lines spread in a circular pattern.
Before they could step back, the ground surface disappeared, but they did not fall. Their bodies were suspended in a column of light and transferred to another space.
The second hall was circular.
Smaller than the first, but the Mana pressure there was much stronger.
Four people appeared on four sides of the circle. A massive mirror extended from floor to ceiling between them, its surface liquid-like, with unclear images moving inside it.
Before anyone could take a step, silver chains rose from the floor.
Each chain wrapped around one of their wrists, and the other end connected to the central mirror.
Seris drew her sword and tried to cut the chain. The blade passed through it without leaving a trace.
The chain was not physical, but connected to the soul and consciousness.
The Mirror Curator appeared at the hall’s edge.
"The past builds the person."
"But the bonds determine the future path."
"One betrayal is enough to break an entire group."
A panel appeared before their view.
[Second Trial: The Bond You Distrust]
[Four challengers entered.]
[All four must refuse the offered lie.]
"If one fails?"
"All will fail."
"This dungeon really has a thing for trust." Liana said with annoyance.
Seris gave her a brief look. For some reason, she agreed.
Then all four looked at each other. There was no need to speak. With just a look, they could understand each other’s meaning.
Don’t do anything foolish!
The mirror’s surface rippled. Images inside it lit up. All four were still physically in the same hall.
But their eyes and minds saw something else.
Seris saw Lian in front of her.
The hall had disappeared.
Only an endless white surface remained.
Lian looked real. No evil smile, no obvious sign of being fake... but was he real?
Even his posture, breathing rhythm, and gaze were exact.
A panel appeared between them.
[Pendragon Bloodline detected.]
[Required Sacrifice for Vault Activation.]
"The Vorhelm clan knew about this place from the beginning." The fake Lian held a sword in his hand and said calmly with a real tone.
Seris looked at him.
"We knew we needed four people to open it." The version continued.
Short images appeared. The map, the travel paths, the moment Seris joined him.
"That’s why I let you come with me."
He raised the sword.
"The final condition is to sacrifice a Pendragon member.
"It’s not personal." His tone remained calm as the blade pointed at Seris.
"It’s the most logical choice."
This sentence was dangerous. The real Lian either did or didn’t make emotional and uncalculated decisions. His mentality couldn’t be understood, and all his actions depended on the moment.
Seris didn’t know if the person in front of her was real or not, but her mind was still occupied by the previous trial, occupied with betrayal!
What if this Lian was real? Or what if this was also the trial’s game?
Seris drew her sword and took a defensive stance for a moment.
But she didn’t attack. She looked at the panel and then at the fake Lian.
"Lian sometimes makes cold decisions."
The version in front of her gave a very faint smile. But Seris suddenly lowered her sword.
"But he never makes a stupid decision."
The fake version’s face changed slightly, and a frown appeared on it.
"Sacrificing the strongest ally to open an unknown dungeon is not logical."
"You don’t even know how to think like him."
Lian’s image cracked, and the fake panel faded. The silver chain on Seris’s wrist changed color from gray to white.
Seraphina found herself in a collapsing hall.
The pillars were falling, stone and glass were falling from the ceiling.
Lian was trapped under a pile of rubble. Blood was flowing from the side of his forehead and mouth.
On the other side, Seris was fighting a dark and unknown creature.
The enemy was getting closer to the exit every moment. Two paths lit up before Seraphina.
One toward Lian, the other toward the enemy.
Panels appeared in the air.
[Remain and attempt rescue.]
[Probability of Trial Failure: 81%.]
[Chase the target and obtain the inheritance.]
[Future probability of saving more lives: Increased.]
"Go after it." Lian’s voice was heard from under the rubble.
"You’re bleeding." Seraphina looked at him.
"It doesn’t matter."
The enemy was moving away.
"If you get the inheritance, you can become stronger later."
The scene directly hit Seraphina’s oldest fear. Once again, someone she cared about was dying in front of her.
And again, there was power at a distance that might prevent future disasters.
Should she abandon the person she could save now to protect more people one day?
"Go." The fake Lian said again.
But this repetition made Seraphina pause.
The real Lian, in a critical situation, would never give such an order without examining the path, the enemy, and the possibilities.
Even if he wanted to sacrifice himself, he would first transmit the necessary information.
This image only used his appearance and tone.
Not his mind.
Seraphina looked at the two paths and then sank her sword into the ground.
"I don’t have to accept a choice you made for me."
A large Magic Circle formed beneath her feet.
But this time, unlike before, the Spell was not built first to be released after a strike.
The blade itself became part of the magical structure.
The Swordswoman and Mage flows activated simultaneously.
[Twin-Core Resonance]
Fire and ice did not spin around the blade. They entered the metal’s structure, and Seraphina pressed the sword into the ground.
A large Barrier spread from the point of contact.
Not only Lian, but all four real group members in the main hall were covered. For a moment, the silver chains of all four stabilized.
The Mirror Vault reacted.
[Exceptional Compatibility Detected.]
[Succession Parameters Updated.]
Seraphina looked at the message, but had no time to examine it further.
The fake scene collapsed, and the chain on her wrist turned white.
Liana stood in front of a glass door.
Behind the door, Selina could be seen, wounded and bloody, and dark monsters were moving in the corridor behind her.
"Liana!" Selina was hitting the glass with both hands.
And Liana immediately went to the door and placed her hand on its surface.
"Step back. I’ll open it."
A panel appeared.
[Lock requires spiritual power.]
[Available source: Familiar Contract.]
[Destroy the contract and sacrifice the familiar.]
Shadow Wolf’s contract circle appeared before her. If she broke it, the released spiritual energy would open the lock.
Shadow Wolf was her last remaining summon.
But behind the door was Selina, who was worth more to her than any power, Skill, or Summon.
Without initial hesitation, Liana reached her hand toward the circle.
Shadow Wolf appeared beside her.
She looked at it. It was neither sad nor scared. Acceptance could be seen in its eyes.
The creature was willing to die for its summoner’s decision... in the end, for a summon, the greatest achievement is sacrifice for its master.
Liana’s fingers approached the circle.
"Faster!" Selina shouted from behind the glass.
The monsters came closer.
"It doesn’t matter if that wolf dies!"
Liana’s hand stopped. Her gaze moved from the circle to Selina.
The sentence was wrong. Not in logic, but in personality.
The real Selina would never call another creature’s life so meaningless.
Even to save herself.
Liana lowered her hand.
"You are not her."
"You’re letting me die." Selina’s image started crying.
The monsters were a few steps away from her.
"I’m your only family."
Liana closed her eyes for a moment. When she opened them again, there was no smile on her face.
"Even if you were real, you wouldn’t use my fear against me."
Shadow Wolf lowered its body, and Liana placed her hand on its neck.
"Break the door."
The wolf sank into the shadow. A moment later, it came out from the shadow behind the door.
Its claws landed on Selina’s image. The illusion and the glass door shattered at the same time.
Liana’s chain turned white.
"Again? Does this trial not know any other place?" Lian once again saw the Vorhelm clan’s hall.
But this time, no one ignored him.
All the clan members were standing on both sides of the hall. When he entered, everyone lowered their heads.
His uncle and the other elders were at the end of the path, holding the heir’s insignia with both hands, ready to hand it over to him.
"Your power has been proven." The voice echoed in the hall.
"The Vorhelm clan accepts you as heir."
The teenage version of Lian was standing next to the insignia, his eyes fixed on it.
The Mirror Vault opened a panel before Lian.
[Exclusive Succession Available.]
[Eliminate the remaining challengers.]
[All inheritance will be transferred to a single host.]
Beneath it, the benefits appeared one after another.
[Unholy Monster Bloodline.]
[Demon-Rank Monster Structure.]
[10000 stats points]
[Dragon Soul]
[10 level ups]
It was a tempting offer...

chapters.title: Chapter 264: The Second Trial ( Final )
paragraphs: Lian looked at the rewards. They were so insane that even he couldn’t take his eyes off them.
"Are these real?" The rewards were so crazy that he doubted a dungeon could give even one of them.
But the way to obtain them was equally insane. He would have to kill all his friends!
"You were made to be alone from the beginning." A voice said from behind.
The mature Reflection of Lian appeared in the hall.
"Allies only slow you down." The trial had no way to challenge his trust.
So they decided to tempt him instead!
Images of Seraphina, Seris, and Liana formed around the insignia.
Each one was like a source of power.
Skill.
Bloodline.
Spiritual structure and physical structure!
"By eliminating three people, you can become something no awakened one has ever been."
"We finally became strong?" The teenage version of Lian looked at him.
Lian was silent for a few moments. He looked at the heir’s insignia. Once, it was everything he wanted.
Not necessarily the position itself, but the meaning behind it.
Acceptance, proving his worth, and the clan’s admission that he was not a mistake.
"We became strong." Lian answered the teenage version.
"Then why don’t you take it?" The boy turned his gaze back to the insignia.
"Because we don’t need it anymore."
The space trembled for a moment.
"You’re lying." The mature Reflection said.
Lian fixed his gaze on the clan members.
"Acceptance that only comes after power is worthless." Then he looked at the images of his three companions.
"And three powerful allies are more useful than a bloodline and these things." At least he hoped so.
The fake version began to crack, but the illusion had not completely collapsed yet.
Mirror Anchor activated in the depth of Lian’s mind. He felt the fixed point of his identity.
Behind the hall’s sound, he heard other sounds. Real breaths, Mana flow, the vibration of chains.
Seris.
Seraphina.
Liana.
All were still present in the second hall.
Lian understood the Trial’s structure.
If he attacked the illusion’s center with Cataclysm Pulse, the pressure might be transferred to the other chains.

Then he called their names, just to create a real sound among the lies.
"Seris."
His voice passed through the other illusions.
"Seraphina."
The second chain trembled.
"Liana."
Three breaths synchronized for a moment.
The Vorhelm hall collapsed. The heir’s insignia turned to ash.
Lian’s chain also turned white.

The circular hall had returned. All the chains were white, but the trial was not over.
The central mirror rippled more intensely. Four hands came out from its liquid-like surface.
Then bodies.
Complete Reflections of Lian, Seris, Seraphina, and Liana entered the hall.
Each moved toward their original owner. Seris’s version made a sword of black glass.
Liana’s version spread fake shadows on the ground.
Lian’s Reflection gathered Mana in its hand.
And Seraphina’s version formed two Magic Circles behind it.
The Curator’s voice was heard from the walls.
"The lie has been rejected."
"Now the substitutes will be eliminated."
Seris’s Reflection made the first attack.
The real Seris drew her sword. The two blades collided.
But Unclouded Edge did not allow the Trial’s disturbance to affect her Sword Intent.
Her movement was simple and direct. The real blade passed through the fake version’s defense path and split it from shoulder to side.
The Reflection turned into pieces of glass.
The fake shadows moved toward Liana.
Shadow Wolf entered the ground and moved among them.
Familiar Soul Anchor kept their bond stable.
Liana felt the real Mana path.
"Left side."
Shadow Wolf came out of the Reflection’s shadow and closed its jaws around its neck.
The fake version collapsed in the darkness.
Lian lazily looked at them. The four Reflections seemed independent, but very thin threads from behind their bodies connected to the mirror’s center.
"What’s controlling them is in the mirror’s center."
Seraphina fixed her gaze on the center. Her fake version and Lian’s Reflection attacked at the same time.
Lian activated Thunder Step and blocked his own version’s path.
The two strikes collided, and Mana pressure spread through the hall.
Seris also moved toward Seraphina’s Reflection and deflected its magical strike.
Seraphina placed both her hands on the hilt.
Twin-Core Resonance activated, and the sword and magic flows moved simultaneously in her body.
[Arcane Edge]
But the Skill was not like before this time. Both elements entered the sword’s structure.
The metal turned transparent white. Cold vapor and intense heat, instead of destroying each other, stood together in a precise balance.
The Curator turned its faceless head toward Seraphina.
Seraphina took a step.
Lian’s Reflection tried to block her path, and the real Lian pushed it aside with Iron Fortress Charge.
Seraphina’s fake version released a large Spell.
Seris split the strike with King’s Edge.
The path opened.
Seraphina sank her sword into the mirror’s center, and at that same moment, the physical strike and the Spell reached the core.
Not one before the other, exactly simultaneously, and the entire mirror surface turned white.
A massive crack spread from its center.
The remaining Reflections stopped, then collapsed into thousands of pieces along with the mirror.
None of the pieces hit the four. Before reaching them, they turned into light.
System panels appeared.
[Second Trial Cleared.]
[All Bonds Preserved.]
[An Heir-Compatible Soul has been detected.]
[Final Compatibility Evaluation Pending.]
Seraphina stared at the notification. The white light on her blade slowly faded.
"Which one does it mean?" Liana looked around.
No answer came. The Mirror Curator stood completely still toward Seraphina for a few seconds.
Despite having no eyes or face, everyone felt its gaze on her.
But then it turned its head. The wall behind it began to split open, and this time, behind the wall, there was no dark hall or stone corridor.
An endless space was revealed.
Thousands of crystals were suspended in the darkness. Some the size of a fist, some larger than a human.
Inside each one, images, faces, and unknown scenes moved.
Memories.
Not illusions made to test them, but real memories of the civilization that had built the Mirror Vault.
Those crystals were memory crystals, a special magical artifact that could record memories.
In the center of the space, the image of a massive tree could be seen. Its trunk was so large that cities were built on its roots.
Its branches covered the entire sky.
Lian understood with one look. These images must show this world, and also the civilization that built this dungeon and the trials.
But something was strange. In the images, the three forests did not exist.
The entire world was unified.
The Mirror Curator turned toward the memory space.
"The first trial asked what made you."
Its voice this time was less like a system, slightly more human, and slightly more tired.
"The second trial asked who you would betray to save yourself."
"The third trial will not test your power." The memory crystals lit up one after another.
"It will show a truth buried deep within this world."
A panel appeared before them.
[Third Trial: The Forgotten World]
[This trial contains True Memories.]
"Only the chosen one can go to the third trial... but all three of you have been successful so far."
Mirror Anchor reacted in the depth of Lian’s mind. The fixed point of his identity became brighter.
At the same time, Seraphina felt warmth on her palm.
A white mark had formed on her skin, the same closed eye and broken star symbol.
Its light was synchronized with her pulse.
The four looked at each other, thinking about what to do. They had come this far, so they would continue too... They stepped into the memory space.
All the crystals activated at the same time... White light covered the world.
The last image they saw before the hall collapsed was the sitting giant of the Giants’ Graveyard.
But this time, it was not a skeleton, it was alive.
It had gray skin and armor of ancient metal. Its height seemed taller than mountains, and its golden eyes were full of awareness.
The giant was kneeling before the first tree. Its head was lowered, and its massive hands were placed on the ground.
And an ancient voice echoed through the entire memory space.
"Before the world was broken into three forests, one root ruled over everything."

chapters.title: Chapter 265: The Primordial Root
paragraphs: "Before the world was broken into three forests, one root ruled over everything."
The ancient voice was still echoing in the memory space when the white light around the four slowly faded.
The Mirror Vault’s hall had disappeared.
The black glass walls, white pillars, and thousands of suspended crystals were no longer visible around them.
There was not even a clear ground beneath their feet, yet none of them fell.
They were standing like invisible spirits in the heart of a massive memory.
Lian raised his hand.
His fingers were not transparent, and his body had its usual appearance, but when he tried to gather Mana in his palm, no reaction occurred.
His Skills were still present. He could feel them.
But this space would not allow interaction with the memory.
Not he, not Seris, not Seraphina or Liana. They were only observers of something that had happened thousands of years ago.
’Interesting, this is the first time I’m seeing something like this. Does it only relate to the crystals, or do skills or arrays also play a role in forming such a thing?’

What they were experiencing was like a cinema with very high reality simulation, so much so that it had no flaws, and this made him even more curious about the civilization behind building such a thing.
In his world too, such technology exists. His surprise comes from the fact that such a civilization with such technology once existed in this small world.
’What happened that caused such a civilization to fall? I guess I’ll find out soon.’
A vast world was spread before them.
The sky was different from what they had seen in Glassthorn Forest.
There was no mist or broken light among the clouds. A golden sun shone in a blue sky, and its light fell without distortion on green lands and wide rivers.
There was no trace of Glassthorn Forest, nor the giant trees and unnatural monsters of the Forest of Giants.
And there were no burning roots and hot air of Emberroot.
All those areas were parts of a unified land.
But none of those scenes caught Lian’s attention as much as what was in the world’s center.
A massive tree had risen from the ground. Even the word "massive" could not describe its size.
Its trunk was like a pillar connecting the earth and sky. The mountains around it, compared to its exposed roots, were only small protrusions.
Its branches extended hundreds of kilometers in the sky.
The tree’s canopy kept a large part of the world under its shade, and its leaves, the size of buildings, had a quiet glow of green and gold Mana.
Its roots did not only remain around the trunk. They extended across the entire land.
Some passed under cities, some split mountains.
And some continued into the depths of the seas.
[The Primordial Root]
Seraphina stared at the tree for a few moments.
Even her usually controlled face could not completely hide her surprise.
"Is this the Forgotten Tree?"
The Mirror Curator appeared beside them.
Its white, faceless body was more transparent in this space than before. The lines inside its body moved in a slow rhythm, as if it too had become part of the memory.
"What is today called the Forgotten Tree is only the remains of what you see."
Lian remained an observer in silence. Mirror Anchor had reacted in his mind.
Since receiving this Boon, a cold, fixed point had existed in the depth of his consciousness.
Now that point became brighter with every change in the memory, allowing him to understand something beyond the images’ appearance.
He was not only seeing the tree. He also felt the order of Mana movement.
Massive energy flows entered the trunk from the Primordial Root’s canopy. Then they divided into three main paths and were distributed through the roots to the entire world.
The first flow was heavy and dense. It penetrated the ground, bones, muscles, and the physical structure of creatures.
The second flow was more delicate.
Like millions of strands of light, it moved among the minds of living creatures, and upon death, it would return part of their memories to the Primordial Root.
The third flow was warm and full of life.
It circulated Mana, kept the earth alive, and allowed new generations to grow.
Three functions.
Body.
Memory.
And heart.
The entire world was connected to the tree through these three flows.
"So the three forests were not separate from the beginning." Lian said under his breath. This was a truth that had not even been recorded in the ancient documents of the Lacerian tribe.
The Mirror Curator turned its faceless head toward him.
"The three forests are the three remaining parts of a single entity."
The scene slowly changed.
Without the Primordial Root disappearing, the land around it moved forward; as if time were moving thousands of years before their eyes.
A large city formed around the tree’s roots.
First a few small buildings, then towers and bridges, and finally a massive civilization.
People moved in the air on paths of light without using flying devices.
In large squares, crystals displayed images of past events.
Children gathered around them and watched historical scenes, while guards and researchers added new information to the archives.
The city’s inhabitants looked like humans from a distance, but when the memory came closer, the differences became clear.
Veins were visible inside their skin, their eyes shone like mirrors when using Mana.
And some of them had marks similar to the Mirror Vault symbol on their foreheads or palms.
Another panel appeared.
[Mirrath Civilization]
"The Mirrath were not the world’s greatest army." The Mirror Curator said.
An image of a few Mirrath soldiers was seen, but most of the city’s people carried no weapons.
Archivists, researchers, builders, and memory keepers were active throughout the city.
"They were not the rulers of the world either."
The memory showed a hall where representatives of several races had gathered.
The Mirrath were not seated in the highest position. They were only in the center of the hall, next to an archive of white glass.
"However, they were the keepers of something that the rulers feared."
"Memories?" Liana looked at the surrounding images. Considering how good they were at recording memories, this was a logical guess.
"Truth."
The scene changed to an ancient war recorded inside a crystal.
A commander tried to change his defeat report, but the Mirrath archivist kept the real version of the event inside the glass.
A king declared his enemy attacked first, while a stored memory showed otherwise.
A clan tried to remove one of its members’ names from history, but that person’s face and actions remained in the archive.
The Curator continued.
"The Mirrath knew that civilizations, before being destroyed, first change the truth."
The archive towers lit up, and thousands of memories moved like stars inside the glass.
"That is why they did not entrust memories to writing. They preserved them as they occurred."
"So everything we see here is real?" Liana asked.
"The memory is not complete, but it is not a lie." The Curator answered.
Lian kept his gaze on the images. The answer was precise. A memory might only preserve one person’s perspective.
Parts of the event might not have been recorded, and the person who owned the memory might not have understood some things.
But the Mirror Vault had not deliberately fabricated anything. What it showed had truly been seen or experienced by someone.
The images of the Mirrath city gradually darkened, and the golden light of the Primordial Root weakened.
At first, the change was so small that only Lian noticed it. One of the deep roots underground turned black for a moment.
A thin vein, like a hair strand compared to the tree’s greatness, but Mirror Anchor detected the change in Mana order.
The energy flow had not passed through that point. Something had consumed it.
The memory went deep into the ground, passing through layers of soil and rock, to where the Primordial Root’s roots disappeared into absolute darkness.
There was a crack in the lowest part of the world. Not a natural crack in the rock, but a shapeless space, a darkness into which lights entered but did not return.
A dark strand came out of the crack and attached to one of the roots.
This was a disaster, a disaster that engulfed the world and was the beginning of the end for a world that the civilizations of this world once knew.
A panel appeared.
[The Black Silence]
The contamination first moved slowly, turning a small part of the root black.
Then it spread through the underground network. Wherever it passed, the light went out.
As if that part of the world had never been alive.
But the destruction of light was not the only danger.
Another memory appeared. An archivist in the Mirrath tower was recording a report.
He placed a scene of black creatures attacking a village inside a crystal. A few hours later, when he checked the crystal again, the image had changed.
In the new version, the villagers had attacked first.
The archivist checked his own personal memory in terror. He too was no longer sure what had happened.
At first glance, this was not a threat... but in depth, this was the greatest threat to the entire race... because the truth was changing!
The next scenes appeared faster.
A commander believed his deputy had betrayed him and killed him before the battle began.
Two clans that had been allies for generations suddenly believed the other was responsible for their ancestors’ deaths.
A mother did not recognize her own child.
Soldiers in a city fired on support forces because their memories showed them as enemies.
Even the Mirrath archives began to change. The memory crystals turned black from the inside.
Faces changed, the order of events shifted.
The disaster was changing the shape of truth in a way that resulted only in bloodshed, destruction, and enmity!

Not a natural crack in the rock, but a shapeless space, a darkness into which lights entered but did not return.
A dark strand came out of the crack and attached to one of the roots.
This was a disaster, a disaster that engulfed the world and was the beginning of the end for a world that the civilizations of this world once knew.
A panel appeared.
[The Black Silence]
The contamination first moved slowly, turning a small part of the root black.
Then it spread through the underground network.
Wherever it passed, the light went out.
As if that part of the world had never been alive.
But the destruction of light was not the only danger.
Another memory appeared.
An archivist in the Mirrath tower was recording a report.
He placed a scene of black creatures attacking a village inside a crystal.
A few hours later, when he checked the crystal again, the image had changed.
In the new version, the villagers had attacked first.
The archivist checked his own personal memory in terror.
He too was no longer sure what had happened.
At first glance, this was not a threat... but in depth, this was the greatest threat to the entire race... because the truth was changing!
The next scenes appeared faster.
A commander believed his deputy had betrayed him and killed him before the battle began.
Two clans that had been allies for generations suddenly believed the other was responsible for their ancestors’ deaths.
A mother did not recognize her own child.
Soldiers in a city fired on support forces because their memories showed them as enemies.
Even the Mirrath archives began to change.
The memory crystals turned black from the inside.
Faces changed, the order of events shifted.
The disaster was changing the shape of truth in a way that resulted only in bloodshed, destruction, and enmity!

chapters.title: Chapter 266: The Black Silence I
paragraphs: People were removed from history, and creatures that had never existed appeared in memories.
That strange contamination did not only spread to intelligent creatures... it also spread to other living beings of this world that played the role of animals and beasts.
And by spreading to them, it drove them mad and made them bloodthirsty, creatures that had no purpose other than killing and domination.
And this led to the formation of monsters in this world...
Lian finally understood the reason for the design of the first two trials.
The Mirror Vault was not looking for someone who could only withstand the power of the inheritance.
The heir had to maintain their identity against distorted memories.
They had to be able to distinguish between what they truly knew and what their fear showed them.
And more importantly, when all the surface evidence pointed to their companions’ betrayal, they had to not act against them without sufficient reason.
Someone who collapsed in the first trial would lose themselves with the first change in their memories.
And someone who betrayed in the second trial would become a tool for spreading the Black Silence.

’This legacy dungeon is looking for an heir who can resist identity distortion. But this makes me wonder, a disaster that targets identity and memories? Where did such a thing even come from?’ Lian reflected.
Until now, the Ruined Realms, each of which is a world, fell due to monster invasions. But this world had experienced a different disaster.
This surprised him greatly. This meant that not all worlds fell in the same way, and in fact, there could be different disasters.
And more importantly, in this world, monsters were not invaders entering through rifts and destroying everything; they were actually created right here.
But what is the reason for these disasters? Why do worlds fall and get destroyed? What is behind them?
And this gave him an idea.
What if their own world was also facing a different model of disaster? Different from this world and the Ruined Realms?
What if there were different models of disaster?
But how many? How did they work? How was each world chosen? And why did these disasters even exist in the first place...?
The images grew larger. War spread across the entire world.
But civilizations were not only fighting against the contamination, they were also fighting each other, each remembering a different version of the disaster’s beginning.
Some blamed the Mirrath, some imagined the Primordial Root as the enemy.
One group wanted to destroy the tree, and another group was willing to eliminate all contaminated races.
The world had collapsed from within before it was physically destroyed.
A meeting appeared in a massive hall. Representatives of the remaining civilizations had gathered around a white root.
Many were wounded, some were not even looking at each other, and in the center of the hall, a woman with white hair stood.
Her silver eyes were dark from exhaustion, but her voice did not tremble when she spoke.
Then the trial showed them more information about her.
[Aurelia Mirrath / Magic Warrior]
Next to her, an armored giant knelt, a very massive giant that was the protector of the Primordial Root.
But upon seeing that giant, Lian immediately recognized it. At first he had some doubt, but he was sure.
It was the same creature he had seen in the Giants’ Graveyard, but not as a skeleton, but alive and aware and full of power.
Even from within the memory, Lian could feel its unusual physical pressure.
The meeting was about finding a way to stop the Black Silence.
Destroying the Primordial Root was impossible. Its roots were connected to the entire world. Its complete death meant the death of the world and all living creatures.
Cleansing the contamination was also no longer possible.
The Black Silence had infiltrated all three of the tree’s main functions.
The only way was to separate those functions from each other.
If the contamination could not move freely between body, memory, and heart, perhaps its spread could be stopped.
But this was not enough. A creature needed to be large enough to absorb all the contamination and seal it within its body.
The ritual began.
Thousands of Mages, Warriors, Priests, and creatures of different races were placed in various points of the world.
Massive strands of Mana connected from cities and towers to the Primordial Root.
This was not cutting a tree. It was an operation similar to splitting the soul of a living creature.
The three main flows were separated from each other. The physical force and growth were pushed to the western part of the world.
The ground trembled, and the trees grew at an unnatural speed.
The animals changed, their bones became thicker, and their blood and muscles were saturated with physical energy.
Some creatures multiplied several times in a few minutes, and their roars shook the mountains.
A panel showed the region’s name.
[Forest of Giants]
In the middle section, the memories and perception of the Primordial Root were separated from the main flow.
The tree’s sap came out from the roots, but instead of flowing on the ground, it froze in the air and turned into a transparent substance.
New trees grew with glass trunks. Light, sound, and Mana broke among them.
Images of people kilometers away appeared on the trunks.
The memories of the dead passed through the branches like brief shadows.
[Glassthorn Forest]
In the east, the heart and warmth of life were concentrated.
The roots turned red, the ground split, and warm light emerged from its depths. Trees grew with fiery leaves, but did not burn.
The Mana flow in that region multiplied several times.
The cities were moved to the east, and the survivors took refuge around the burning roots.
[Emberroot]
The center of the Primordial Root remained.
Not as a complete tree, but a large part of the trunk had been destroyed.
The roots reached from three directions to a massive wound in the world’s center, and there, without connecting to each other, they stopped.
[Forgotten Tree]
Lian saw the underground network. All the roots, despite being separated, still returned to that point.
The Forgotten Tree was not the complete heart of the Primordial Root but the...

chapters.title: Chapter 267: The Black Silence II
paragraphs: Forgotten tree was only the point of separation, where the three parts of the world were separated from each other, a central wound that had still not fully healed.
If the exit or the control core of this Special Area was located at any point, that was the most logical choice.
His previous guess was no longer just a possibility. The Forgotten Tree was their final goal, and he now understood why it was called the Forgotten Tree.
That tree was a piece of something completely forgotten by the current era.
But the images were not finished yet. The western part of the world was shown.
During the separation of the Primordial Root’s body, a massive wave of the Black Silence had entered that region.
If the contamination had remained free, the entire Forest of Giants would have been destroyed at that same moment.
The armored giant stepped forward.
A panel appeared above it.
[Orrakas]
[The Armed Titan]
Orrakas was one of the Primordial Root’s main guardians. He stood in the center of the physical flow and pulled all the released contamination into his own body.
The blackness rose from the ground, entered his legs, passed through his armor, and spread through his veins, bones, and flesh.
The giant did not scream. He only knelt and continued absorbing the contamination. His body turned black, and his golden eyes went dark for a moment.
But he still remained alive. The giant, by absorbing that contamination, had become the new nightmare and disaster of the world!
The giant who was the guardian of the Primordial Root had, with his sacrifice, absorbed all the contamination and become the main source of the disaster.
All the survivors realized one truth. If they wanted to save their world, they had to destroy this giant!
A great conflict occurred, but the armored titan was the strongest giant in this world. A creature that still seemed impossible to defeat.
A great battle took place. Many of the leaders and representatives of the civilizations were killed. Almost no one survived that massive battle.
And in the end, the most powerful figure of this world, Aurelia, by sacrificing herself and her civilization, defeated the giant.
At the end of that battle, only one representative of a civilization survived. The images showed that killing Orrakas was possible, but no one did such a thing.
His death would release all the contamination stored inside his body.
For this reason, massive chains were bound to his body.
A bone region formed around him. The creatures that had died during the separation were buried there.
Over time, that place became the Giants’ Graveyard.
"He is not a prisoner of that graveyard." The Mirror Curator said.
It showed an image of Orrakas sitting among the chains with his eyes closed.
"He is the lid of a wound that has still not healed."
Lian put all the pieces together.
The increase in Awakening after bloodshed, the Giants’ Graveyard’s reaction to the death of creatures, and the Ossuary Warden.
Everything now made sense.
The blood and remaining energy from death could feed the physical part of the Primordial Root.
But at the same time, the contamination inside Orrakas also used that energy. Every killing in the sensitive area brought the giant one step closer to awakening.
The Warden was not built to protect Orrakas.
Its job was to prevent bloodshed and clean up anything that could feed the giant.
Their goal, by keeping this monster asleep, was to prevent the disaster from returning to the world.

And finally, Lian understood the secret of how the Forest of Giants came to be. It was a massive mutation that had occurred in the genetics of the creatures in that region, causing gigantism among them.
However, a question remained. If the contamination was eventually eliminated and the disaster was stopped, then why do monsters still exist?
The reason for the monsters’ existence was that contamination. If it was stopped, shouldn’t the monsters gradually return to their original state and become normal animals and creatures again?
And another thing he realized was that if his guess was correct,
all the remaining civilizations were only branches that had barely managed to survive after the fall of the main civilizations, and yet they had forgotten their origins and history...
"What happens if he fully awakens?" Seraphina looked at the giant’s image.
The Curator did not answer for a few moments. Orrakas’s image became darker.
Black veins moved under his skin.
"The body will release what it has held inside, and the disaster will return."
No further explanation was needed.
If the Black Silence stored inside Orrakas’s body was released, the Forest of Giants would be the first region to fall.
Then the contamination could reach other parts through the roots still connected to the Forgotten Tree.
The memory returned to the Mirrath city, to before the final battle.
But the city was no longer like before. The transparent towers were broken.
The archives were turning black one after another. People in the streets were fighting each other, while each had a different memory of the reason for the war.
Aurelia was standing in the highest archive hall.
A few intact crystals still remained around her, and she was deep in thought. The memories did not show what she was thinking, but her occasional murmurs gave some signs.
"My guess was correct... the disaster was allowed..."
"Why? Why did you do this?"
"Ambition? Madness?"
"The world is being destroyed..."
"It must be punished... but I will not succeed."
"We will not win... but neither will you."
She gathered the last group of archivists.
The Mirror Vault was built at that same time.
Not as a shelter for escape, not as a tomb for treasures, but to preserve the truth and find someone who could carry it in the future.
The images showed the dungeon’s construction. The black glass walls, the Trial halls, the memory crystals, and the Mirror Curator, which was created from a part of Aurelia’s mind and memories.

Perhaps that woman knew that she and her civilization were going to be destroyed in the final battle, and she wanted to do everything she could to leave a legacy so that an heir could rebuild their civilization.
Or she had a deeper reason... an heir who would again stop the disaster... but the disaster should have been stopped, right?
Then the images of the first trial appeared.
"The heir had to maintain their identity against distorted memories."
The second trial.
"They did not betray those who trusted them for power."
Then an image of Seraphina was seen, sinking her sword into the ground and, instead of accepting two forced choices, creating a third option.
"And they could balance two different flows without destroying one of them."
Lian gave a brief look at Seraphina. The white mark on her palm had become brighter.
Now the reason for the Mirror Vault’s reaction was clear.
Seraphina, like Aurelia, was a Magic Warrior. But this was not the only reason for her selection. The real choice depended on her decisions in the Trials.
The memory ended.
The light of the unified world went out, and the four were again in the dark space among the suspended crystals.
For a few seconds, no one spoke.
The information they had seen was heavier than what they could immediately talk about.

chapters.title: Chapter 268: The Succession I
paragraphs: The memories they had seen had answered many of Lian’s questions about this world, but at the same time, they had created even more questions, both about this world and beyond.
And it was clear that he was not going to find more answers here.
But there was something that bothered him the most.
’How did the map’s creator know about this place? And what happened to them? Did they die? Were they killed? Did they manage to reach here?’ The map he had was too complete.
It had even marked the location of this dungeon, and that could only mean one thing: the map’s creator knew about this dungeon. But then why hadn’t they entered it?
Or had they entered and failed to obtain the inheritance? Or maybe they had been killed on the way here?
But if they were killed, how did they manage to create a complete map of this world? How exactly was that possible? Did they have a special skill or artifact for this?
Or is there another reason behind it?
’I guess I first need to find out how old this map is. That might help me reason more information.’
Anyway, for now, there were more pressing matters to deal with.
This place was the remains of a living, wounded entity, and The Black Silence, whatever it was, might not have been completely destroyed yet.
Seraphina raised her palm, and the white mark was shining inside her skin.
"So this dungeon was looking for someone with a Dual Class from the beginning?"
The Mirror Curator appeared in front of her.
"A Dual Class is not a sufficient condition."
"What is the main condition?" Seris asked.
"Carrying two truths without destroying one of them." The Mirror Curator raised its hand.
Four pillars of light formed before them.
"The final evaluation begins."
The first pillar moved toward Seris. The light scanned her body from head to toe.
A panel appeared before everyone.
[Candidate Evaluation: Seris Pendragon]
[Identity Stability: Exceptional]
[Sword Intent: Exceptional]
[Archive Compatibility: Low]
[Succession Compatibility: Rejected]
Seris only looked at the panel for a few seconds.
"Natural." There was no discomfort or objection in her tone.
She had not entered the Mirror Vault to obtain the inheritance. The rejection was only a result that did not align with her power structure.
The second pillar covered Liana.
Shadow Wolf stood beside her foot, carefully looking at the light.
[Candidate Evaluation: Liana]
[Spiritual Bond Compatibility: Exceptional]
[Identity Stability: High]
[Archive Capacity: Insufficient]
[Succession Compatibility: Rejected]
"At least I got Exceptional." Liana pointed at the first phrase, even though she didn’t even know what it meant.
"In a part that had nothing to do with the inheritance." Seraphina said.
"It’s still Exceptional."
The third light came toward Lian.
Mirror Anchor reacted in his mind.
For a moment, he felt that the Mirror Vault was not only examining his Mana or Class level.
Something deeper inside him was being touched.
The white light turned gray for a moment.
Then a panel appeared.
[Candidate Evaluation: Lian Vorhelm]
[Identity Stability: Exceptional]
[Memory Interpretation: Exceptional]
[Host Adaptability: Abnormal]
[Warning: Predatory Assimilation Detected.]
[Archive Preservation Probability: 17%]
[Archive Consumption Probability: 83%]
[Succession Compatibility: Rejected]
Lian was not surprised by the result. His body and soul were too adaptable for accepting external powers.
But this adaptability differed from the Mirror Vault’s purpose. The dungeon was not looking for a vessel that could turn the inheritance into personal power.
It was looking for someone who would preserve the memories as they were and rebuild the destroyed civilization.
It wanted someone who would act in line with this purpose and dedicate themselves to it.
Lian was not such a person. If there was no benefit for him, he would not waste his time, let alone the fact that this could be very difficult and time-consuming.
Liana stared at the panel.
"Archive Consumption means what?"
"It means it doesn’t trust me." Lian answered.
The last pillar focused on Seraphina.
The white light activated the mark on her palm. The suspended crystals around them turned toward her one after another.
[Candidate Evaluation: Seraphina]
[Identity Stability: High]
[Dual-Path Compatibility: Exceptional]
[Memory and Combat Synchronization: Exceptional]
[Emotional Fracture: Stabilized]
[Succession Compatibility: 96%]
[Worthy Heir Detected.]
No one was surprised. Everyone had understood to some extent that she had already been chosen as the heir.
Thousands of strands came out from the crystals, but none had yet entered Seraphina’s body.
The Mirror Curator stood in front of her.
"Do you accept the inheritance?"
Seraphina looked at the mark on her palm and, instead of answering immediately, asked.
"What is the cost?"
"The memories of the dead will remain within you." Vague images of thousands of Mirrath appeared inside the crystals.
"If your identity weakens, they will replace your voice with their own."
The strands wrapped around her hand, but did not reach her skin.
"The inheritance gives power; but power is the smallest part of it." This meant she would gain the identity of thousands of people, including their memories.
Seraphina was silent for a few moments. Lian looked at her face. He did not know her thoughts, but he could see the weight of the decision in her pause and the pressure of her fingers.
This was not a normal Skill that could be discarded if unsuitable. When the Archive entered her soul, a part of her being would change forever.
The act she was about to perform was so great that it could cause her soul to collapse.
"If you’re only accepting it for power, don’t."
Seraphina turned her head toward Lian, and he continued.

"We don’t yet know exactly what effect carrying this Archive will have on your mind and soul. Whatever decision you make, you should think about it carefully. If you can’t handle it, your soul might shatter."
His gaze moved over the surrounding crystals for a moment.
"This is not a decision that can be taken back later." Liana was not joking this time. Her smile had faded, and she was silently looking at Seraphina.
Seris didn’t care enough to offer any advice.
Seraphina looked at the mark on her hand again. A few seconds passed, then she closed her fingers.
"My mother died because of a rift that no one was prepared to stop."
Her voice neither trembled nor rose.
"If this inheritance can really help prevent something similar from happening again, I will accept it."
"Even knowing that your own memories might one day be lost among the memories of the dead?" The Mirror Curator asked.
"Then I have to stay strong enough not to get lost."
A panel opened before her.
[Succession Accepted.]
At that same moment, the entire Archive space lit up. The memory crystals began to move.
At first slowly, then faster.
Thousands of crystals rotated in complex orbits around Seraphina. Each orbit formed part of a very large Magic Circle.
A white mark appeared beneath her feet. Her sword came out of its sheath without being touched and floated in front of her body.
Two flows of Mana left her body. The first flow was in the form of a silver blade, compressed, sharp, and direct.
The Swordswoman path.
The second flow made a ring of multi-colored Mana, with fire and ice moving inside it.
The Mage path.
Until now, those two flows had only been synchronized within Seraphina’s body.
But the Mirror Vault now pulled them out and placed their structures against each other.
The silver blade entered the Mana ring. For a moment, both flows resisted.
The lights were thrown around, and the suspended sword trembled.
But then Twin-Core Resonance activated. The rhythm of the two powers became one. The Mana ring compressed around the blade and penetrated its structure.
The inheritance panels appeared one after another.
[Heir Selected: Seraphina]
[Legacy: The Last Mirror Archivist]
[Succession Authority Granted.]
[Evolution Path Unlocked.]
She would still remain a Warrior and Mage, but upon reaching Evolution, a new path would become available to her.
A path that would probably turn the two Classes into something unified.
[Twin-Core Resonance has evolved.]
[Twin-Core Convergence — Incomplete]
[Legacy Skill Acquired: Prismatic Spellblade]
[Authority Acquired: Mirror Archive — First Layer]
[Title Acquired: Heir of the Last Reflection]
The white mark moved from Seraphina’s palm to her arm and then to her chest, but just before reaching her heart, a few crystals in the farthest part of the Archive turned black.
Their blackness did not resemble The Black Silence, but it conveyed the same feeling of loss and void.
The Mirror Curator suddenly turned toward them. For the first time, its movement was outside its usual calm.
A frown appeared on its flat face, so clearly that it was obvious.
[Archive Contamination Detected.]
[Rejected Reflections Awakening.]
The black crystals cracked. Dark smoke came out from within them and gathered at one point.
First a hand... then a shoulder, torso, and head.
A human-like body formed from the darkness, but it had no fixed face.
For a moment, it was Lian’s face, then Seris’s, Seraphina’s, Liana’s.
And then unknown faces, probably belonging to people who, over the years, had found this dungeon and challenged its trials, faces of people whose memories existed in the archive.
The same archive that Seraphina was about to obtain, along with all its memories and information.
A panel appeared.
[The Nameless Fifth]
"The reflections of rejected challengers were preserved over the centuries." The Mirror Curator said.
"They were not supposed to gain awareness, but memories are like that. If they become too obsessive, they can take shape and will."
"It seems that because someone has obtained the inheritance, the anger that had accumulated in them over all this time over their failures has erupted and caused the formation of what you see."
The Nameless Fifth’s body stretched. Several mouths opened on its different faces, and multiple voices came out of them simultaneously.
"Heir..."
"Body..."
"Escape..."
The creature moved toward Seraphina. The inheritance transfer process had not yet been completed.
Seraphina was standing in the center of the Magic Circle and could not leave it.
If she was attacked, she might lose everything!

Did they die?
Were they killed?
Did they manage to reach here?’ The map he had was too complete.

chapters.title: Chapter 269: The Succession ( Final )
paragraphs: Every time the monster’s face or limb changed, the Mana path also changed.
Its hand turned into a blade, then a claw, and then into an arm belonging to an unknown creature.
Seris positioned herself between it and Seraphina.
The Nameless Fifth brought out several glass blades from its body.
Each blade reflected a face.
Lian, dozens of versions of his face appeared around Seris.
Some were wounded, some were screaming, and a few images were asking for help from behind Seris. But her Sword Intent did not waver even for a moment.
[Unclouded Edge]
Seris’s sword moved. The first memory blade shattered from the middle.
Then the second and third. She cut all the fake faces without pausing.
Not because she could distinguish the original among them, but because she saw the real Lian a few steps away.
The Nameless Fifth made another arm.
From the shadows on the Archive floor, creatures emerged.
Black wolves, faceless birds, and Summons whose bodies were made of pieces of memories.
Liana raised her hand. A summoning circle formed beneath her feet.
"Shadow Wolf."
The black wolf came out of her shadow. Its red eyes moved over the fake creatures.
The reflections attacked it with shapes similar to the real summon.
[Familiar Soul Anchor]
The bond between Liana and Shadow Wolf lit up. There was a real strand of emotion between them.
The fake versions had similar appearances, but there was no spiritual connection inside them.
"They’re not real."
Shadow Wolf entered the ground, came out of the first fake Summon’s shadow, and split its body with dark claws.
Then it sank into the next shadow. The creatures collapsed one after another.
However, The Nameless Fifth was still approaching Seraphina.
Seris was blocking its path, Liana was holding the Summons.
But every time a part of the creature’s body was split, another face would take its place.
Lian did not focus on its appearance. He kept Mirror Anchor active. In the previous Trials, this Boon had allowed him to maintain his real identity among fake memories.
Now it revealed another change. Every face of The Nameless Fifth belonged to a different time.
Some of the Reflections had been created centuries ago.
Some were newer, but all of them returned to one fixed point, a core that existed in the current moment.
Lian gave an annoyed look at it. This monster, like the Doppelgängers, was a headache, and more importantly, its source of creation was also annoying.
It was formed from will and obsession, and as long as its source was not found, it could not be destroyed, the source that gives life to this thing.
’So these bastards were so full of spite and jealousy that they turned into a living grudge?’
He activated Predator’s Instincts, and the flows appeared before his eyes.
Very thin strands came out from behind each Reflection.
They passed through the space and connected to a black crystal behind Seraphina, on the left side of the Magic Circle.
"Its body doesn’t matter." Lian said.
Seris deflected a strike. Liana pulled Shadow Wolf out from among three Summons.
Lian pointed his finger behind Seraphina.
"The source is behind Seraphina, on the left."
Seris, without looking at the point, increased the pressure of her attacks. King’s Edge formed on her blade.
A horizontal strike opened the path in front of Lian.
Liana closed her hand. Shadow Wolf came out from the shadow of one of the crystals and placed its claw on the core’s shadow.
The crystal’s body remained still for a moment.
Lian activated Thunder Step. Blue lightning exploded in the space. He appeared next to the black crystal.
He prepared Glacial Reaper Claw, but stopped before the strike.
Night Eyes showed that white strands were also connected from that same crystal to Seraphina’s Magic Circle.
The source was part of the main Archive structure. If he destroyed it, the inheritance transfer might stop.
Or worse, all the memories that had entered Seraphina’s soul would remain without structure.
Direct destruction was not the solution.
The Nameless Fifth sensed the danger. It moved its body through Seris’s strikes and sent several long arms toward Lian.
Lian placed his hand on the crystal, prepared Cataclysm Pulse, but minimized its force.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
A very small wave entered the crystal, not to break the structure, but to create disorder in its rhythm.
He guided the Pulse’s path, and the wave avoided the white strands and only moved in the black channels that connected the Reflections to the source.
The Nameless Fifth stopped in the middle of its attack.
Its faces trembled at the same time. Hundreds of different voices came out of its mouths, and the black strands were revealed for a moment.
"Now!"
Seris sent a vertical strike. The memory blades moved aside, and Liana issued a short command.
Shadow Wolf turned its entire body into a large shadow and locked around the core.
And at that same moment, finally, the inheritance transfer was completed.
[Succession Process Completed.]
Seraphina’s eyes opened. White and multi-colored light moved in her pupils, and the suspended sword landed directly in her hand.
The blade no longer had its previous appearance. A transparent layer had formed on the metal, changing color with every change in angle.
[Prismatic Spellblade]
Seraphina did not leave the Magic Circle. She only gently moved her sword to one side.
Compressed Mana was stored inside the blade. The two elements of fire and ice, instead of being released, turned into a white prismatic light.
Then she sent the strike. A sword line came out of the blade but did not go directly toward the source.
It hit one of the floating glass pieces, and its path changed.
Then to the second surface.
Third.
Fourth.
In less than a second, dozens of reflections of that same strike formed around the source, each approaching from a different angle.
The Nameless Fifth tried to place its body among the strikes.
But the attack came from all directions. The connecting strands were cut one after another. First, Lian’s face separated from the creature’s body.
Then Seris, Liana, Seraphina, and then hundreds of unknown faces appeared on its surface.
All of them opened their mouths at the same time, but before they could make a sound, the final strike reached the source’s center.
The white light exploded.
The Nameless Fifth cracked like a glass statue.
The cracks spread from the chest to the head and limbs. For a moment, thousands of faces were seen in different pieces.
Then they all collapsed, of course, only pieces of black glass that turned into particles of light before reaching the ground.
The source crystal did not remain black. Its color changed from darkness to white, and the Archive flow stabilized again.
Seraphina lowered her sword. Her breathing had become heavy.
The first use of the new Skill had been done with the temporary power of the Mirror Vault, and it was clear that in normal circumstances, she could not repeat that same power without cost.
But the result was clear. She had landed the final strike. However, without Seris, the path to the source would not have opened.
Without Liana and Shadow Wolf, the core would not have remained still.
And without Lian’s analysis, they would have only fought a body that never truly existed for an unknown amount of time.
The Mirror Curator appeared in the Archive’s center.
White light returned to it from the surrounding crystals.
"The Archive contamination has been cleansed."
"The heir has been accepted."
"The heir’s companions have been registered as Archive witnesses."
Panels appeared before the other three.
First, Lian’s panel.
[Mirror Anchor has evolved.]
[True Sequence Anchor]
[Effects:
[Artificially created, removed, or displaced memories may be identified.]
[You can see through all illusions and control them in any way you wish.]
[The power of all mental attacks below the third evolution is reduced by 40%.]
The change in Lian’s mind was felt immediately. Of course, this was a new innate skill.
Mirror Anchor had only maintained his identity before.
But True Sequence Anchor was something more.
This Skill was not offensive.
It did not increase his Stats.
The second panel appeared.
[You have obtained an A-rank Artifact.]
[World Memory Acquired.]
He looked at the crystal that had appeared in his hand. According to its information, by combining it with the map he already had, he could create a living map.
Not in the sense of a truly living map, but practically, the map would become more advanced and would update locations in real-time like satellite maps.
The interesting thing about this artifact was that it was not a one-time use. He could combine it with any map he wanted, and that map would practically act like a living map.
’I remembered the Celestial Book of Treasure. Because of the circumstances, I had completely forgotten to use it. I guess I should take a look at it.’
But this also made him somewhat curious. What would happen if he combined this thing with the Celestial Book of Treasure? Because that book already acts like a satellite treasure map.
If this artifact is combined with it, what ability will be added to it?
He then looked at the three other girls. He could tell that each of them had also received their own rewards.
And finally, their work here was done...
