[Mirror Anchor has evolved.]
[True Sequence Anchor]
[Effects:
[Artificially created, removed, or displaced memories may be identified.]
[You can see through all illusions and control them in any way you wish.]
[The power of all mental attacks below the third evolution is reduced by 40%.]
The change in Lian’s mind was felt immediately.
Of course, this was a new innate skill.
Mirror Anchor had only maintained his identity before.
But True Sequence Anchor was something more.
This Skill was not offensive.
It did not increase his Stats.
The second panel appeared.
[You have obtained an A-rank Artifact.]
[World Memory Acquired.]
He looked at the crystal that had appeared in his hand.
According to its information, by combining it with the map he already had, he could create a living map.
Not in the sense of a truly living map, but practically, the map would become more advanced and would update locations in real-time like satellite maps.
The interesting thing about this artifact was that it was not a one-time use.
He could combine it with any map he wanted, and that map would practically act like a living map.
’I remembered the Celestial Book of Treasure.
Because of the circumstances, I had completely forgotten to use it.
I guess I should take a look at it.’
But this also made him somewhat curious.
What would happen if he combined this thing with the Celestial Book of Treasure?
Because that book already acts like a satellite treasure map.
If this artifact is combined with it, what ability will be added to it?
He then looked at the three other girls.
He could tell that each of them had also received their own rewards.
And finally, their work here was done...

chapters.title: Chapter 270: The End Of Legacy Dungeon
paragraphs: After all the decisions, in the end, Lian decided to use the new artifact he had obtained for the map for now.
Lian reached his hand into his storage space and took out the map.
The lines on it still showed the locations of the three forests, the Giants’ Graveyard, and a few side paths, but part of the information was probably years or decades old.
The crystal in his other hand immediately reacted.
[Compatible Cartographic Medium Detected.]
[Would you like to synchronize World Memory?]
Lian confirmed.
Contrary to his expectation, the crystal did not melt.
Its white surface began to open, and hundreds of very thin strands of light came out from within it.
The strands spread across the map’s surface like delicate roots. First, they followed the old lines.
They passed through the Forest of Giants, curved around the Giants’ Graveyard, then entered Glassthorn, and illuminated all the paths that Lian and Seris had traveled in the past few days.
The light penetrated the ink and the map’s skin. For a moment, all the signs disappeared, and only the dark, empty surface of the skin remained.
Then a white wave spread from the map’s center. The world’s image appeared again, but it was no longer a flat image.
The trees, roots, and terrain height gained depth on the map’s surface. Small valleys went lower, and rock walls slightly rose from the surface.
Four small points lit up at the group’s current location.
A fifth point, larger and blacker, was outside the Mirror Vault.
One.
A root they had passed by two days ago slowly shifted on the map. The old path turned gray, and a new route formed around it.
[Artifact Synchronization Completed.]
[World Memory Map]
[Rank: A]
[Functions Unlocked:]
[Live Positioning]
[Terrain Reconstruction]
[Route Recalculation]
[Recorded-World Synchronization]
Lian examined the map for a few moments.
The group’s live positions changed with every small movement, but other creatures, monsters, or hidden resources did not appear on the map.
The sections they had never recorded remained as dark spots.
World Memory could not generate information from nothing.
It only reconstructed what had already been recorded in its own memory, the map, or the owner’s direct observation.
This limitation was logical.
If the Artifact could reveal all the details of an area without being present there, its rank A would be too low for it.
Nevertheless, even this ability was very valuable. From now on, Lian no longer had to trust paths that might have collapsed or been blocked years ago.
If a bridge was broken, a root had shifted, or a new crack had formed in the ground, the map could recalculate the route.
He did not fold the map.
He changed its angle several times and tested its reaction. At the same time, from the corner of his eye, he noticed the three girls.
Each was standing a short distance from the others, apparently examining their own rewards.
Seraphina sometimes looked at her palm.
The white heir mark was no longer shining as intensely as before, but it still had a gentle movement under her skin.
Then she placed her hand on her sword’s hilt, as if comparing something between that mark and her weapon.

Liana placed a small object, whose shape Lian did not have time to identify, immediately into her storage space. Then she summoned Shadow Wolf beside herself and stared at its red eyes for a few moments.
Seris stood still.
Her sword was still in its sheath, but her gaze was fixed on an empty point; a state that showed she was reviewing a memory or experience in her mind.
Lian asked nothing.
Just as he himself needed to examine his new Artifact’s abilities, they also had the right to first understand their rewards.
The Mirror Curator appeared in the Archive’s center. Its semi-transparent body was fainter than before.
"I apologize for the sudden appearance of that living grudge. It should not have been part of this trial and was an unexpected variable."
"The succession process has been completed."
"The Archive will enter its sleep cycle."
In the distance, a white door opened.
Cold air entered the silent dungeon space through it.
Lian folded the World Memory Map and placed it into his storage space.
"It’s time to go."
No one objected. The four moved toward the door.
Seraphina was the last one, glancing back at the silent crystals for a moment.
Lian did not ask anything from her expression. The inheritance she had obtained was not just a collection of Skills.
Thousands of memories, duties, and truths of a dead civilization had entered her soul along with it.
It would probably take a long time for her to understand the full meaning of what she had accepted.
The group passed through the door. The white light covered their vision for a moment.
Then the cold and dark forest space replaced the Archive.
Night had completely fallen.
Only black gaps could be seen in the sky. Blue and purple lights flowed inside the glass trunks, covering the clearing with a dim and unnatural glow.
Behind them, the black glass door was still visible among the dead tree’s roots.
But the light on its central symbol had gone out.
Lian had not even taken his second step when a strong wave of emotions entered his mind through Hive Link.
Relief.
Excitement.
Protest.
And a kind of simple, raw joy that One made no effort to hide.
The massive ant raised its head at the clearing’s edge. Its antennae moved quickly.
Then, without paying attention to Seraphina, Liana, or Seris, it ran straight toward Lian.
At first, Lian thought One wanted to bring its head close to him, so he raised his hand to touch its black shell.
But One stuck out its rough, warm tongue and licked Lian from his chin to the side of his face all at once.
Lian remained completely motionless for a moment. The warm moisture remained on his face.
Liana first looked at the scene with wide eyes, then her laughter echoed throughout the clearing.
One pushed its head forward again. Lian placed both his hands on the front part of the ant’s head and held it back.
"I’m alive. That’s enough."
One tried to move its head through his hands. A new wave of relief and dissatisfaction was transmitted through Hive Link.
During the entire time the group was inside the Mirror Vault, One had sensed the possibility of Lian not returning.
The dungeon had not cut off their direct connection, but the link had become very weak and vague. One knew Lian was alive, but it could not determine his real condition.
Now, upon seeing him, all the accumulated anxiety was pouring out directly.
"I think it really missed you." Liana said, still laughing.
"Or it’s hungry." Seris said with her usual dry tone.
One immediately pulled its head out from between Lian’s hands and turned toward Seris.
Its antennae went up, and a clear wave of dissatisfaction entered Lian’s mind.
"It’s not hungry." Lian wiped his wet face with his hand and then was silent for a few moments, glancing at his storage space.
"Of course, it needs to eat."

chapters.title: Chapter 271: The Cindervein Passage I
paragraphs: This time, One brought its head close to Lian’s shoulder, but it did not try to lick him again.
Lian touched the shell on top of its head, and a few fresh scratches could be seen on it.
Also, the corpses of a few creatures were lying around the clearing.
Two Glassvine Hunters were crushed under One’s massive legs, and a cat-like monster lay a little further away next to a root.
Apparently, One had not only waited; it had also protected the entrance.
"Good work."
A calm satisfaction was transmitted through the link.
"It’s gotten very dark." Seraphina looked around.
Lian raised his head. Moving through Glassthorn Forest at night was more dangerous than during the day.
The reflections increased, distances were harder to judge, and some monsters were exactly more active in the darkness.
Besides, all four of them were mentally exhausted.
The Mirror Vault might not have wounded their bodies, but a few hours of intense experience, distorted memories, and the battle with The Nameless Fifth was not something that could be easily ignored.
At least for Seraphina and Liana, that was the case.
"We’re staying here tonight."
Seris looked at the dungeon’s extinguished door.
"The Vault’s remaining pressure will keep most monsters away."
"And One has also cleared the area, so this is a good place to rest."
"So the hero tonight is him." Liana placed her hand on the ant’s head.
One moved its antennae toward her.
They prepared the area for camping.
Lian and Seris moved in opposite directions to make sure no monster was hiding nearby.
The World Memory Map proved useful for the first time in a practical way.
With the map open, Lian and Seris’s positions moved apart on its surface. The terrain’s unevenness and surrounding roots also became clearer with their movement.
Lian circled the camp area.
The map recorded every observed section and compared it with the old information at the same time.
A narrow crack that was not on the map was added to the image.
A root that had blocked the northern path also turned gray. No large monster was in the area.
After returning, Lian and Seris moved a few corpses further away so the smell of blood wouldn’t attract more creatures.
Then they lit a small fire between a few stones. The orange flame reflected on the surrounding glass trunks.
Instead of one fire, dozens of its images could be seen among the trees. Some reflections were larger. Some moved with a few seconds’ delay, and some even burned in a different direction.
Lian looked at the numerous flames for a moment.
After the Mirror Vault, seeing reflections that did not completely follow the original no longer seemed like just a beautiful feature of the forest.
Each member of the group sat a little further from the others. Everyone needed some time alone with what they had gained.
Seraphina placed her sword on her knee.
She put the tip of her finger on the blade’s flat part and infused a very small amount of Mana into it.
For a moment, the sword’s edge was covered with prismatic light, and colors shifted on the metal’s surface.
Red.
Blue.
White.
But before the Skill could fully form, Seraphina cut the Mana flow.
The light went out. She put the sword back in its sheath without explanation.
Lian had seen the scene from a short distance. The Mana structure was different from Seraphina’s previous Arcane Edge.
In the past, Mana had been placed on the blade like a separate layer. The sword would deliver the strike, and the Spell would be released almost simultaneously, but still as a second part.
This time, Mana had entered the blade’s very structure. There was no clear boundary between the sword and the magic.
The Skill was not complete, but even this change was enough for Lian to understand what path Aurelia’s inheritance had opened for Seraphina.
The two Classes no longer had to act in turns. They could become one unified movement.
Liana was sitting next to Shadow Wolf, her hand on the shadowy wolf’s head, silent for a while.
This silence was unusual for her, but the bond between them had clearly changed.
Before the Mirror Vault, Liana’s spiritual power had entered Shadow Wolf in the form of a commanding thread.
Their relationship was deep, but still, the energy path flowed more from the summoner to the Summon.
Now the movement had become more two-way.
When Liana placed her hand on the wolf’s head, the shadows of its body changed with her breathing rhythm.
Lian did not know the name or details of her reward, but it was clear that the Mirror Vault had strengthened their spiritual bond.
Seris was sitting at another distance. She had taken her sword out of its sheath and was holding it in front of herself.
Several times she moved her finger along the blade’s edge.
She did not activate any Skill, but a very subtle and invisible pressure formed around the weapon.
Lian already knew her Sword Intent. In fact, he had seen her use it in the dungeon. He didn’t know if she had it before and had been hiding it, or if she had obtained it in the dungeon.
Sword Intent is an advanced form of swordsmanship, a skill that professional swordsmen can acquire through practice and experience.
Sword Intent greatly strengthens the power and precision of attacks and is divided into three ranks: Basic, Professional, and Great.
Even the best swordsmen rarely achieve Sword Intent before their first evolution, but Seris had been able to attain it.
And this showed her terrifying talent.
Previously, the few times Lian had seen it in the dungeon, even under full control, her Sword Intent had been slightly fueled by anger and a desire to dominate. Now that layer had almost disappeared.
Only the decision to cut remained.
Lian took his gaze off them and opened the World Memory Map in front of himself.
But his mind did not stay fixed on tomorrow’s path. The images of the Mirror Vault were still moving in his mind.
Where had The Black Silence come from?
The memories had shown that the contamination had entered the world through a crack in the roots’ depths.
But where did that crack connect? Was it a door to another world?
A damaged part of the Special Area itself?
Another question related to the Forgotten Tree.
If The Black Silence was not completely destroyed, when might it awaken again? And could it spread to their world too?
If that happened, their world would face a disaster that could end them, and that was something he did not want under any circumstances.
Lian folded the map. He did not have enough information to conclude. Building hypotheses without more data would only fill his mind with useless possibilities.
His gaze fell on Seraphina. That girl was now the heir of the Mirror Vault.
He had no unpleasant feelings about the dungeon’s choice. The inheritance Seraphina had received was not a simple, cost-free reward.
Thousands of memories were inside her soul. The duty of preserving the truth of a dead civilization was also on her shoulders.
Besides, according to Lian’s reasoning and Aurelia’s final words, there might be a great secret that they were unaware of.

’In her final words, she mentioned that the Black Silence disaster was allowed into this world and that there was a betrayal by someone. What did she mean? Does that mean someone is responsible for that disaster?’
’But who?’ According to what they understood, one person had survived the final battle.
But who was that one person?
’If I had to bet, it probably has to do with the remaining civilization in Emberroot.’ He had a feeling that the answers to the rest of the questions should be in that forest.
In any case, this was not a responsibility Lian was interested in carrying.
On the other hand, Seraphina truly deserved it... and in the end, her becoming stronger was directly beneficial for Lian.
They were members of one group.
The stronger his companions became, the higher the chances of survival, overcoming dangers, and reaching their goal.
Having an ally with an evolved Dual Class was more valuable than another Skill that would only be added to his own complex set of abilities.
Lian had enough Skills. What he needed more were people he didn’t have to constantly protect on the battlefield.
After a while, the three girls also finished their initial examination of their rewards and came closer to the fire.
One sat a little further away, crushing a large piece of stored meat between its jaws.
Lian opened the World Memory Map again. The map showed their location as bright points.
"Is this the same map from before?" Liana came a little closer.
"It has been upgraded."
"Can it show everything live?" She looked at the map with more interest.
"Only the environment, not monsters, not treasures, and not things it has no information about."
"Tomorrow’s path?" Seris looked at the map.
Lian placed his finger on the border crossing.
The border between Glassthorn and Emberroot was marked with a curved line. There was only one passable path near them.
"From here to the border is less than half a day’s journey." He placed his finger on a name next to the narrow gap.
"Then we enter the Cindervein Passage. That’s the passage between the two forests."
Seraphina repeated the name under her breath.
"Cindervein Passage... Is it natural or built?"
"I don’t know."
Unlike the Giants’ Graveyard, they had no information about this passage.

What he needed more were people he didn’t have to constantly protect on the battlefield.
After a while, the three girls also finished their initial examination of their rewards and came closer to the fire.
One sat a little further away, crushing a large piece of stored meat between its jaws.
Lian opened the World Memory Map again.
The map showed their location as bright points.
"Is this the same map from before?" Liana came a little closer.
"It has been upgraded."
"Can it show everything live?" She looked at the map with more interest.
"Only the environment, not monsters, not treasures, and not things it has no information about."
"Tomorrow’s path?" Seris looked at the map.
Lian placed his finger on the border crossing.
The border between Glassthorn and Emberroot was marked with a curved line.
There was only one passable path near them.
"From here to the border is less than half a day’s journey." He placed his finger on a name next to the narrow gap.
"Then we enter the Cindervein Passage.
That’s the passage between the two forests."
Seraphina repeated the name under her breath.
"Cindervein Passage...
Is it natural or built?"
"I don’t know."
Unlike the Giants’ Graveyard, they had no information about this passage.

chapters.title: Chapter 272: The Cindervein Passage II
paragraphs: In the documents Lian had read in the tribe, there was barely any information about the Giants’ Graveyard, let alone the border passage between Glassthorn and Emberroot.
It could be a natural passage, and since there was a significant civilization in that forest, it might also be a constructed one.
They wouldn’t know until they entered.
"Maybe it’s just a simple path between the two forests." Liana added.
"It’s not." Seris said without changing her expression.
"How do you know?"
Seris took a piece of meat from beside the fire.
"Because we haven’t had a single simple path so far."
Liana looked at her for a few seconds.
"I can’t argue with that logic, but I still don’t like it."
Seraphina looked at the border line on the map.
"Glassthorn was the memory part of the Primordial Root, and Emberroot was the heart and Mana part."
She followed the passage path with her finger.
"If this path was formed exactly between the two regions, the Mana flows of both forests might collide inside it."
"Reflections and heat, and maybe monsters that have adapted to both environments." Lian considered the possibility. It was not impossible.
Seraphina nodded.
"There’s another possibility too. If the Emberroot civilization is really as large as the map showed, they might be monitoring the region’s entrances."
"So there might be food, beds, and real baths on the other side?" Liana immediately said.
"They might arrest us first." Seris answered.
"You really have a special talent for crushing other people’s hopes." Liana looked at her with annoyance.
Seris started eating without paying attention to her objection.

Seraphina and Lian did not continue this discussion either, but the entire group had to be prepared for any possibility. It was true that a civilization existed, but there was also the possibility of conflict with that civilization.
For a while, the conversation returned to the Mirror Vault. None of them told the complete details of what they had seen in the trials.
Perhaps some memories were too personal, perhaps they were not yet ready to talk about them.
Liana kept her gaze on the fire’s flames.
"Did all of you see things from your past?"
"Yeah." Seraphina said after a short pause.
Seris only nodded.
"Things the dungeon knew would have the most impact on us." Lian answered.
Liana threw a small piece of wood into the fire. Sparks rose into the air and multiplied on the glass trunks.
"At least now I know a mirror can be crueler than most people."
"The mirror didn’t create anything by itself." Seraphina said.
"That’s the worse part."
For a few moments, silence fell.
Lian looked at all three. Their changes were not large or dramatic, but they were there.
Liana still smiled and joked, but she no longer immediately spoke to cover every silence. Sometimes she would let the space between sentences remain empty.

Seraphina was still proud and serious, but the constant pressure to control everything was less in her movements. Even when they talked about the path’s unknowns, she didn’t try to find a definitive answer for every possibility immediately.
Seris appeared to remain the same person as before.
The same cold demeanor, the same short sentences, but several times her gaze turned toward Lian without any obvious reason.
Every time Lian noticed, Seris would either look at the fire or ask another question about the path.
Lian said nothing. He was probably the only one who had remained unchanged because he had simply already come to terms with the greatest grudge and wound of his life.
The rest of the night passed more calmly. They ate.
One consumed a large part of the meat supply.
Liana placed more pieces in front of it several times, and Lian stopped her on the third time.
"Enough."
"It still looks hungry."
"It’s about to burst from hunger!"
"From its antennae movement, it’s clear it wants more." Liana looked at One’s head.
One moved its antennae toward her.
Lian received a wave of hope for more food.
"It’s taking advantage of you."
"At least someone here appreciates my affection."
One took another piece from her hand, then they divided the watch.
Seraphina and Liana rested first due to their greater exhaustion.
Lian and Seris monitored the environment.
In the second half of the night, they switched places with them. No major attack occurred until morning.
The remaining pressure of the Mirror Vault and One’s presence kept most nearby monsters away.
Before full dawn, Lian opened his eyes.
The sky was still dark, but the lights inside the trees had dimmed slightly; a sign that day was beginning.
Seris was a little further away, packing her equipment.
Seraphina was examining her armor by the extinguished fire.
Liana was also trying to secretly give the last piece of meat to One.
Lian said nothing. He got up and walked a few steps away from the camp. He positioned himself behind a set of transparent roots, out of the girls’ direct sight.
Then he took out the Celestial Book of Treasure from his storage space.
The book’s cover lit up with a golden light. The patterns on its surface moved like constellations.
The pages began to turn without Lian touching them and stopped a few seconds later on a blank page.
[Current Detection Radius: 10 Kilometers.]
A golden line formed in the center of the page.
Lian’s position appeared as a white point, then three other marks lit up around it.
One was near the border entrance, the second was deeper in the path, and the third was near a point that was probably the Emberroot exit.
No name or rank was visible next to them. To identify their nature, he would have to get closer.
Lian opened the World Memory Map in his other hand.
He compared the three marks’ positions with the passage path. The first point was only a few hundred meters from the main path.
The second was almost inside the passage itself, and the third was just before the exit. None of them required a large detour.
Lian closed the book. The golden light immediately went out. He placed the Celestial Book of Treasure back into his storage space.
Using the World Memory Map, he set a path that would pass by all three marks, but outwardly, it only looked like the safest and shortest possible route.
When he returned to the camp, Liana had given the last piece of meat to One.
"I thought you said you wouldn’t give it any more food. Besides, how are you going to survive hunger yourself?" Lian looked at her empty hand.
"It took it itself, and don’t worry about me, I’m sure we can get more food along the way." Liana answered calmly.
One lowered its antennae.
Lian decided not to argue.
Less than half an hour later, the group was ready to move.
All four mounted One’s back. The ant took the path.
The World Memory Map was open in front of Lian, recording new parts of the forest with every step.
The first few hours passed without any serious incident, but Glassthorn’s appearance gradually changed.
The transparent trunks were no longer as clear as before. Some had darkened from the center, and black veins moved inside them.
The blue and purple lights were replaced by orange and red colors.
The forest’s cold air became warmer. At first, only a few degrees, and then the heat increased so much that faint steam rose from the surface of some roots.
The soft and gray ground also changed.
A layer of black glass had formed on the soil, and beneath it, red and burning roots flowed.
Every time One stepped on the surface, red light spread beneath its feet.
A few hours later, the trees parted. A massive gap appeared before them.
Two walls of black and red roots rose to an unknown height, and the space between them resembled the mouth of an ancient creature.
A warm wind came out from inside the gap. The sound of a slow beat was also heard from its depths.
The World Memory Map reacted.
[Cindervein Passage]
"At least its name is honest." Liana looked at the dark entrance.
They could feel the sound of beats that resembled the pulsing of veins at any moment, and it was guessed that this was probably why this place was called Cindervein.
"The heat can be felt from here." Seris said.
"Yeah, God knows how hot it is inside that forest."
Lian commanded One to reduce its speed. The passage was formed between the dead and living roots of the Primordial Root.
Parts of the wall still had Glassthorn’s characteristics. Black and glassy surfaces reflected light.
But from beneath them, Emberroot’s red roots had penetrated, creating burning cracks on the walls and floor.
The heat wave made all the reflections appear curved and stretched, making the real distance of the walls hard to determine.
The World Memory Map began recording the environment.
The passage’s dark line slowly lit up. Branches, heights, and unstable sections appeared on the map’s surface one after another.
The first treasure point was nearby. Lian continued on the main path for a few minutes.
Then he saw a narrow crack in the right wall. The passage was so tight that One could not enter.
"Wait here. I’ll check the path ahead for stability." Lian said.
"Alone? Do you want me to come with you?" Seraphina looked at the crack.
"If a root collapses, one person can get out more easily."
The group didn’t object. The reasoning seemed logical.
Lian jumped down from One’s back, took a few steps into the crack, and when he was out of their direct sight, he activated Thunder Step.
Blue lightning lit up the narrow space for a moment. He appeared in the crack’s depth.
The book of treasure’s mark was exactly in front of him...

chapters.title: Chapter 273: The Cindervein Passage III
paragraphs: Lian looked ahead. The first treasure was there.
A mass of transparent red material had formed between two roots.
Its appearance resembled thick sap that had turned into glass mid-flow.
Small lights moved inside it, and every time Lian got closer, gentle heat emanated from its surface.
A panel appeared.
[Emberglass Resin]
[Rank: B]
[Description: A rare material formed from the fusion of Glassthorn memory sap and Emberroot heart-heat.]
[Primary Uses: Fire-resistant equipment, mental-resistance reinforcement, and advanced alchemy.]
He placed his hand on the material. The heat passed through his skin but was not harmful.
The amount of Emberglass Resin was more than he had expected, enough to make at least one full armor or a few small tools.
Lian placed the entire mass into his storage space. There was no reason to leave any part of it behind.
The crack became darker after the material disappeared.
Lian returned along the path, and when he reached the group, Seraphina asked.
"Was there anything?"
"The path seems stable."
He hadn’t told a direct lie. The path was indeed stable. It wasn’t that he wanted to hide something from them, but explaining how he found treasures would be troublesome.
Under no circumstances did he want to talk about the Celestial Book of Treasure. The truth about that book was a red line.
He trusted the girls, but if they accidentally said something somewhere, it could lead to disaster.
Instead, if he found anything useful for them, he would definitely give it to them.
Lian mounted One and the journey continued. The deeper they went into the passage, the narrower and hotter it became.
In some sections, only a natural bridge of black glass continued the path over a deep gap.
Below the bridge, molten roots moved.
Red and orange materials flowed among them, sending waves of heat upward.
One slowed its steps, carefully placing all six feet on the thick parts of the bridge.
"Hmm?" Lian suddenly felt an unpleasant sensation at the back of his neck.
[Predator’s Instincts]
Danger was from above. He raised his head.
Reflections could be seen on the ceiling, images of winged creatures moving among the black glass.
But Predator’s Instincts warned that the real bodies were not at the reflections’ location.
"Be careful!"
The heat waves had hidden their shape.
"Above!" He suddenly shouted.
At that same moment, the creatures detached from the ceiling. Winged reptiles with transparent, elongated bodies.
Their skin was like glass, but molten veins moved inside it. Their thin wings resembled blades, and when diving, their bodies almost merged with the heat wave.
[Ashglass Ripper]
[Level: 20]
[Rank: Normal]
More than ten creatures dove toward One from several directions. Lian disappeared before the first Ripper arrived.
[Thunder Step]
Lightning exploded in mid-air, and he appeared in front of the creature. Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his hand.
The ice claw hit the Ripper’s glass wing. The cold spread over the wing’s surface instantly.
The molten veins inside it were still hot. The sudden temperature difference caused the entire wing to explode with a sharp sound.
Glass fragments scattered in the air, and the Ripper lost its balance and fell toward the gap below the bridge.
Lian returned to One’s back with a second Thunder Step.
At the same time, Seris jumped off the ant’s armor. Three Ashglass Rippers were approaching from the left.
[King’s Edge]
Compressed pressure formed on her sword.
This was not the first time Lian had seen King’s Edge, but after the Mirror Vault, the Skill’s execution had undergone a subtle change.
Previously, Seris’s Sword Intent would reach the enemy like an aggressive blade before the strike.
This time, there was no leakage. All intent, Mana, and pressure were locked within the blade’s edge. Its movement was harder to detect, but the final cut was more precise.
Seris sent only one strike. A silver line passed through all three Rippers.
For a moment, their bodies remained intact, but then they split in half from the middle.
The bodies fell toward the molten roots below and began to burn before reaching the surface.
A few more Rippers came out from under the bridge. They had been hidden in the dark shadow of the bridge’s surface.
Liana raised her hand.
"Shadow Wolf."
The black wolf appeared next to One. The moment its claws touched the bridge’s surface, its entire body sank into the shadow.
Lian followed the Mana flow.

Before the Mirror Vault, Shadow Wolf had to temporarily break down its body structure to pass through shadows and reform at another point. Although this process was fast, it created a very brief interruption in the bond.
Now that interruption had almost disappeared. Liana’s bond acted like a spiritual container, keeping the wolf’s structure stable even during movement.
Shadow Wolf came out from the shadow beneath the first Ripper.
Its dark claws sank into the creature’s glass abdomen. The molten veins tore, and the wolf grabbed the Ripper’s body and pulled it down.
Seraphina also drew her sword.
One of the creatures had passed from an angle that Seris could not attack without harming One.
[Arcane Slash]
Seraphina’s blade moved.
Lian immediately noticed the difference. In the past, the sword’s cut would go forward, and the Arcane wave would form slightly after it.
This time, the magical wave was born from the exact point where the blade touched the air.
The sword and Spell were not two attacks, but one unified structure. A white and blue line hit the Ripper.
The front part of its body was split, and the remaining Arcane wave pushed it off One’s path. The creature hit the wall and got stuck among the glass cracks.
One opened its jaws and caught another Ashglass Ripper that had gotten too close between them.
The sound of shattering glass echoed in the passage.
In less than half a minute, the attack was over.
The last Ripper tried to return to the ceiling, and Seris did not throw her sword at it.
Lian activated Thunder Step, appeared at a higher altitude, and slammed the creature’s body into the wall with an Iron Fortress Charge strike.
The Ripper’s glass shell shattered, then fell along with the broken pieces.
Silence returned to the passage, only the sound of the molten roots flowing beneath the bridge could be heard.
Liana summoned Shadow Wolf onto the bridge.
"These creatures really attack from every direction."
Lian looked at the ceiling.
"They were using the reflections to hide their real path."
Seraphina put her sword back in its sheath.
"And the heat disrupts Mana vision too."
Lian nodded. The Cindervein Passage was exactly what they had predicted.
A combination of both forests’ features: Glassthorn’s reflections and Emberroot’s heat and life.
This was a bit troublesome, but because of the monsters’ low levels, they were not a threat to them, and they could easily deal with them.
After crossing the bridge, the path widened for a while.
The second treasure mark slowly approached. The World Memory Map showed that the main path ahead was blocked by a massive root.
The only passable route went beside that same root.
Lian commanded One to stop. The root covered almost the entire width of the passage.
A hole could be seen in its middle section.
"There’s a side path inside. I’ll check it."
"Should I come with you?" This time Seris asked.
Lian looked at the hole’s opening. The treasure mark was only a few dozen meters inside it.
"No, the entrance is narrow. If something wakes up, keep One ready."
Seris held her gaze on him for a few moments, then nodded.
Lian entered the hole. The air inside the root was much hotter. The walls pulsed every few seconds.
Not like living tissue, but because of the Mana waves passing through from Emberroot’s depths.
He passed a few bends. At the end of the hole was a small space.
A fruit was hanging in its center from root strands. Its surface was red and gold, and every time the light inside it rose, the entire fruit pulsed like a heart.
A panel appeared.
[Cinderheart Fruit]
[Rank: B+]
[Effects: Permanently increases heat resistance and improves internal Mana circulation.]
Lian approached the fruit. Its heat could be felt on his skin even without touching it.
Its effect was permanent, although the increase was probably not very large, but any permanent reward had high value.
Especially for entering Emberroot.
Lian grabbed the fruit’s stem and separated it with one movement. At that same moment, the entire root trembled, and dust and glass pieces fell from the ceiling.
There were a few other fruits around. He took them too. He could give them to his group members one by one.
The pulse that had been regular until then suddenly stopped, and then a deep sound rose from beneath Lian’s feet.
The book of treasure had shown the treasure, not its guardian.
Lian immediately placed the Cinderheart Fruit into his storage space.
The hole’s floor split open.
Black glass plates came out from beneath the root. A worm-like creature pulled its body up through the root’s structure.
Its head alone was almost the size of One.
Its body was covered with thick black plates, and from the cracks in its armor, red molten veins could be seen.
Several rows of teeth moved inside its massive circular mouth.
[Cindervein Devourer]
[Level: 24]
[Rank: Normal]
"Damn it."
The creature opened its mouth. A wave of heat gathered inside the hole.
Predator’s Instincts reacted so strongly that all of Lian’s muscles contracted.
He activated Thunder Step.
A moment later, an explosion of fire and molten glass filled the entire hole. Blue lightning appeared at the root’s opening, and Lian emerged.
"Move!"

"Above!" He suddenly shouted.
At that same moment, the creatures detached from the ceiling.
Winged reptiles with transparent, elongated bodies.
Their skin was like glass, but molten veins moved inside it.
Their thin wings resembled blades, and when diving, their bodies almost merged with the heat wave.
[Ashglass Ripper]
[Level: 20]
[Rank: Normal]
More than ten creatures dove toward One from several directions.
Lian disappeared before the first Ripper arrived.
[Thunder Step]
Lightning exploded in mid-air, and he appeared in front of the creature.
Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his hand.
The ice claw hit the Ripper’s glass wing.
The cold spread over the wing’s surface instantly.
The molten veins inside it were still hot.
The sudden temperature difference caused the entire wing to explode with a sharp sound.
Glass fragments scattered in the air, and the Ripper lost its balance and fell toward the gap below the bridge.
Lian returned to One’s back with a second Thunder Step.
At the same time, Seris jumped off the ant’s armor.
Three Ashglass Rippers were approaching from the left.
[King’s Edge]
Compressed pressure formed on her sword.
This was not the first time Lian had seen King’s Edge, but after the Mirror Vault, the Skill’s execution had undergone a subtle change.
Previously, Seris’s Sword Intent would reach the enemy like an aggressive blade before the strike.
This time, there was no leakage.
All intent, Mana, and pressure were locked within the blade’s edge.
Its movement was harder to detect, but the final cut was more precise.
Seris sent only one strike.
A silver line passed through all three Rippers.
For a moment, their bodies remained intact, but then they split in half from the middle.
The bodies fell toward the molten roots below and began to burn before reaching the surface.
A few more Rippers came out from under the bridge.
They had been hidden in the dark shadow of the bridge’s surface.
Liana raised her hand.
"Shadow Wolf."
The black wolf appeared next to One.
The moment its claws touched the bridge’s surface, its entire body sank into the shadow.
Lian followed the Mana flow.
Before the Mirror Vault, Shadow Wolf had to temporarily break down its body structure to pass through shadows and reform at another point.
Although this process was fast, it created a very brief interruption in the bond.
Now that interruption had almost disappeared.
Liana’s bond acted like a spiritual container, keeping the wolf’s structure stable even during movement.
Shadow Wolf came out from the shadow beneath the first Ripper.
Its dark claws sank into the creature’s glass abdomen.
The molten veins tore, and the wolf grabbed the Ripper’s body and pulled it down.
Seraphina also drew her sword.
One of the creatures had passed from an angle that Seris could not attack without harming One.
[Arcane Slash]
Seraphina’s blade moved.
Lian immediately noticed the difference.
In the past, the sword’s cut would go forward, and the Arcane wave would form slightly after it.
This time, the magical wave was born from the exact point where the blade touched the air.
The sword and Spell were not two attacks, but one unified structure.
A white and blue line hit the Ripper.
The front part of its body was split, and the remaining Arcane wave pushed it off One’s path.
The creature hit the wall and got stuck among the glass cracks.
One opened its jaws and caught another Ashglass Ripper that had gotten too close between them.
The sound of shattering glass echoed in the passage.
In less than half a minute, the attack was over.
The last Ripper tried to return to the ceiling, and Seris did not throw her sword at it.
Lian activated Thunder Step, appeared at a higher altitude, and slammed the creature’s body into the wall with an Iron Fortress Charge strike.
The Ripper’s glass shell shattered, then fell along with the broken pieces.
Silence returned to the passage, only the sound of the molten roots flowing beneath the bridge could be heard.
Liana summoned Shadow Wolf onto the bridge.
"These creatures really attack from every direction."
Lian looked at the ceiling.
"They were using the reflections to hide their real path."
Seraphina put her sword back in its sheath.
"And the heat disrupts Mana vision too."
Lian nodded.
The Cindervein Passage was exactly what they had predicted.
A combination of both forests’ features: Glassthorn’s reflections and Emberroot’s heat and life.
This was a bit troublesome, but because of the monsters’ low levels, they were not a threat to them, and they could easily deal with them.
After crossing the bridge, the path widened for a while.
The second treasure mark slowly approached.
The World Memory Map showed that the main path ahead was blocked by a massive root.
The only passable route went beside that same root.
Lian commanded One to stop.
The root covered almost the entire width of the passage.
A hole could be seen in its middle section.
"There’s a side path inside.
I’ll check it."
"Should I come with you?" This time Seris asked.
Lian looked at the hole’s opening.
The treasure mark was only a few dozen meters inside it.
"No, the entrance is narrow.
If something wakes up, keep One ready."
Seris held her gaze on him for a few moments, then nodded.
Lian entered the hole.
The air inside the root was much hotter.
The walls pulsed every few seconds.
Not like living tissue, but because of the Mana waves passing through from Emberroot’s depths.
He passed a few bends.
At the end of the hole was a small space.
A fruit was hanging in its center from root strands.
Its surface was red and gold, and every time the light inside it rose, the entire fruit pulsed like a heart.
A panel appeared.
[Cinderheart Fruit]
[Rank: B+]
[Effects: Permanently increases heat resistance and improves internal Mana circulation.]
Lian approached the fruit.
Its heat could be felt on his skin even without touching it.
Its effect was permanent, although the increase was probably not very large, but any permanent reward had high value.
Especially for entering Emberroot.
Lian grabbed the fruit’s stem and separated it with one movement.
At that same moment, the entire root trembled, and dust and glass pieces fell from the ceiling.
There were a few other fruits around.
He took them too.
He could give them to his group members one by one.
The pulse that had been regular until then suddenly stopped, and then a deep sound rose from beneath Lian’s feet.
The book of treasure had shown the treasure, not its guardian.
Lian immediately placed the Cinderheart Fruit into his storage space.
The hole’s floor split open.
Black glass plates came out from beneath the root.
A worm-like creature pulled its body up through the root’s structure.
Its head alone was almost the size of One.
Its body was covered with thick black plates, and from the cracks in its armor, red molten veins could be seen.
Several rows of teeth moved inside its massive circular mouth.
[Cindervein Devourer]
[Level: 24]
[Rank: Normal]
"Damn it."
The creature opened its mouth.
A wave of heat gathered inside the hole.
Predator’s Instincts reacted so strongly that all of Lian’s muscles contracted.
He activated Thunder Step.
A moment later, an explosion of fire and molten glass filled the entire hole.
Blue lightning appeared at the root’s opening, and Lian emerged.
"Move!"

chapters.title: Chapter 274: The Cindervein Passage ( Final )
paragraphs: "Move!"
One had already received the command through Hive Link before the sentence was complete.
The ant turned its body and moved away from the root at full speed.
Seris, Seraphina, and Liana maintained their balance on its back. The massive root exploded from the center.
The Cindervein Devourer pulled its body out, and the glass plates around it shattered the passage’s path.
Part of the ceiling collapsed, and a wave of soil, stone, and glass scattered in the space.
The creature roared.
Hot air came out of its mouth and turned the opposite wall red.
Lian landed on One’s back with Thunder Step.
"This thing was inside there?" Seraphina asked.
"Yeah."
"Did you go to check the path or to wake up a monster?"
"Both happened." Lian said without changing his expression. He hadn’t expected the inside to be a monster’s lair.
He had even checked, but this worm lived deep underground, and detecting it was practically impossible, which is why he hadn’t noticed it.
The Devourer dragged its body on the ground.
With every movement, the plates under its abdomen shattered the glass surface. A few images of its body appeared in the heat waves.
Five identical Devourers moved toward the group from different directions.
But Predator’s Instincts only sensed real danger from one of them.
The main body was slightly further back and to the right.
"Right side. The rest are heat reflections." Lian said immediately after figuring out which one was real.
One carried the group to a wider part of the passage.
Seris jumped down before the ant fully stopped.
The Devourer slammed its heavy tail on the ground. A wave of glass plates moved toward her.
Seris walked among them, her sword held low.
When the first plate reached a few meters away, heavy pressure formed on the blade.
[King’s Breaker]
The strike hit one of the defensive plates beside the creature’s head.
King’s Breaker was not made for cutting.
The Skill collapsed the defensive structure through concentrated force transfer.
A heavy explosion sound echoed in the passage. The black plate sank from the center.
Cracks spread across the surrounding layers.
The Devourer shook its head, and then the cracks in its body opened.
The accumulated heat burst out. Hundreds of molten glass pieces, like a red rain, were thrown toward the group.
Seraphina and Liana prepared to attack, but Lian moved forward.
[Diamond Skin]
His skin’s surface hardened.
[Iron Fortress]
Compressed defensive pressure formed around his body. He found the wave’s weakest part with Predator’s Instincts and passed directly through it.
A few molten pieces hit his armor and arm.
Diamond Skin prevented deep penetration, but the heat still burned his skin.
Lian reached close range.
Instead of attacking the Devourer’s body, he slammed his palm on the root beneath the creature.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
The wave entered the root’s structure, passed through the broken plates, and exploded exactly beneath the Devourer’s heavy body.
The root cracked from below. The creature’s balance was disrupted for a moment, and its massive head tilted to one side.
The false bodies trembled in the heat wave. The Devourer opened its mouth, and red light gathered in the depths of its throat.
This time, it intended to release all its stored heat in one direction.
Lian activated Thunder Step, and blue lightning remained on the ground. He appeared directly on the creature’s head.
The crack created by King’s Breaker was in front of him.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
The ice claw sank into the cracked armor. The cold entered the Devourer’s body.
The molten veins around the crack changed from red to orange and then gray in an instant. The temperature difference widened the cracks.
The Devourer roared and shook its body violently.
Lian sank his claws deeper into the armor to avoid being thrown off. The creature’s tail hit the wall, and a large part of the black glass collapsed.
Seraphina and Liana jumped down from One’s back.
But before they could enter the battle, Seris ran on one of the Devourer’s body plates. Her movement was synchronized with the creature’s shakes.
Every time the plate went up, she would place her next step on a lower part.
Lian only saw her path for a moment, and then King’s Edge lit up.
Seris sank the blade into the same crack. Her cut moved along the cold of Glacial Reaper Claw.
The defensive plates separated from the inside.
Lian released more cold. The molten veins froze one after another.
The Devourer tried to release the heat in its throat, but the internal Mana path was blocked.
The energy built up inside its body. The cracks on its armor lit up with red light.
"Back!" Lian sensed the danger and warned immediately.
Seris pulled her sword out without asking and jumped off the monster’s body.
The young Vorhelm activated Thunder Step, appearing on the ground a moment before the explosion.
The Cindervein Devourer’s body exploded from the inside, and red light burst through hundreds of cracks.
The glass plates were thrown in all directions.
Lian activated Iron Fortress again. A few pieces hit his defense and were deflected.
Seris spun her sword in the air and cut the nearby plates.
One positioned its body in front of Seraphina and Liana. The glass pieces shattered on its black shell.
The explosion subsided after a few seconds. The front part of the Devourer was completely destroyed.
The molten veins went out. The creature’s massive body fell to the ground with a heavy sound.
A panel appeared.
[You have slain Cindervein Devourer Lv.24.]
[Bloodlust has absorbed 100% of the available exp.]
A significant amount of EXP entered Lian’s body, but it was not enough to reach Level 20.
He looked at the corpse. The coordination between him and Seris had been done almost without words.
He had opened the weak point, the young Pendragon had broken the defense, and then both had concentrated their attacks on the same path.
"You really don’t leave any chance for us." Seraphina lowered her sword, a little dissatisfaction could be heard in her voice.
She also wanted to test her new skills and abilities. Since last night, instead of sleeping, she had only been examining the inheritance she had obtained.
She had understood many things and was even sure that her power had still increased.
But these two gave her no opportunity to test her skills, and as long as she was in a group with them, this situation would probably continue.
"I was even ready to be useful this time." Liana stood beside One.
Seris cleaned her sword.
"Be faster."
Seraphina gave her a sharp look, and Liana sighed.
Lian turned his attention back to the broken root. The others probably assumed the Devourer had awakened because of his entry into the hole.
This assumption was not entirely wrong, but none of them knew about the Cinderheart Fruit.
"How about this? From now on, you two take the weak monsters, and we’ll take the strong ones." After a moment of thought, he suggested.
"Great." Seraphina smiled and accepted the suggestion.
She knew Lian meant monsters between levels 15 and 22 by "weak," and for her, those monsters were actually considered strong.
After making sure the creature was dead, the group stopped for a few minutes to recover energy.
One had taken a few fresh scratches, but none of them were deep.
Liana sat next to the ant and wiped the glass pieces off its shell with a thick cloth.
Lian first looked at the notifications. Aside from the stats points he had obtained, he had also finally acquired a new skill.
Then he opened the World Memory Map.
The explosion had blocked part of the main path. After a few seconds, the map calculated an alternative route beside the gap.
The new path was slightly longer but passed through stable root sections.
They continued moving. The further they went, the less Glassthorn’s features became.
The black glass on the walls receded, red and brown roots took its place, and the passage’s air was no longer just hot.
The smell of wood, soil, and smoke was in it. The sound of insects could be heard from a distance.
Signs of natural life, after a few days among reflections and glass trees, seemed almost strange.
The third book of treasure mark was getting closer.
In a wide part of the passage, the skeleton of a massive creature lay among the roots.
Its bones were partially burned and blackened. The World Memory Map showed the main path passing beside that same skeleton.
One needed a short stop because of the scratches on its legs.
"We’ll rest for a few minutes." Lian said.

chapters.title: Chapter 275: The Emberroot Forest
paragraphs: Seraphina and Seris went ahead to check the path. Liana stayed with One. It was a good opportunity.
Lian, apparently to examine the bones, moved away from the group. The book’s mark was exactly under the skeleton’s ribcage.
He pushed one of the heavy bones aside. A dark stone was visible beneath it.
Golden lines moved on the stone’s surface like veins, and a deep but controlled heat came out from within it.
[Rootfire Marrow]
[Rank: B]
[Description: Condensed heart-Mana formed inside ancient Emberroot creatures.]
[Uses: Equipment core enhancement, creature strengthening, and advanced medicinal refinement.]
Lian picked up the stone.
Its weight was unusual for its size. It could later be used for equipment enhancement or making medicine.
Without pausing, he placed it into his storage space, then returned the bone to almost its previous position.
When he returned to the group, no one asked any specific questions.
With the Rootfire Marrow obtained, all the treasures the Celestial Book of Treasure had shown had been collected.
Three B-rank or higher treasures in one day. The book had once again proven its real value. He also checked it again to see if there were any special treasures nearby.
The answer was no. There were some treasures, but all of them were below B-rank, and in his eyes, such treasures were no different from trash.
But it didn’t matter. Even so, he had gained a lot of profit from this Special Area. He had a lot of monster corpses in his storage space.
He was slowly getting closer to Level 20 and felt he should finally reach it within the next few days.
After One recovered its energy, they resumed moving. While moving, Lian also glanced at the map.
"We’re not far from the exit."
"That’s it? We’re arriving that soon?" Liana said with surprise and relief.
"Yeah, the passage was shorter than I expected. Compared to the Giants’ Graveyard, this was like a kindergarten."
"Isn’t that good? We faced no danger and are leaving safely." Seraphina added.
Lian nodded. At least they had been able to cross this place quickly and there was no great danger.
"I have a bad feeling. Everything has been too calm." But Seris disagreed.
"Please be quiet and don’t jinx it!" Liana glared at her.
"Look!" Seraphina pointed.
An orange light could be seen at the passage’s end. Fresh air was coming from that side. The sound of birds became clearer.
One increased its speed. The last glass walls remained behind them.
The red roots on both sides of the path parted. The group emerged from the Cindervein Passage’s opening.
Emberroot Forest spread before them.
For a few moments, no one could immediately say anything. The forest was different from all the areas they had seen so far.
Massive trees with dark brown trunks rose to heights of dozens of meters.
Red veins moved inside their bark, and every time Mana reached from the roots to the branches, the golden and orange leaves would light up.
The leaves looked like fire but did not burn.
Narrow rivers of fire flowed among the roots. Their surfaces were red and gold, and bright steam rose from them.
Unlike the Forest of Giants and Glassthorn, clear signs of civilization could be seen everywhere.
Wooden and stone bridges were built between the large roots.
A wide path lay on the ground, with traces of wheels, feet, and pack creatures on it.
Lamps with red glass were placed on posts at regular intervals. Even in the distance, part of a stone wall could be seen among the trees.
"Finally." Liana let out her breath upon seeing the path and lamps.
But Lian had a bad feeling. According to the map’s information, the civilization should not be next to the border passage. So what were all these constructions?
Could they have built a base and structures here to control and protect the border? It wasn’t unlikely. That’s what an intelligent civilization would do.
"We better be careful. We might encounter intelligent creatures at any moment."
"There’s no need to worry. I doubt—" But before Liana could complete her sentence... something happened.
One only took a few steps into the forest, and then the sound of dozens of weapons being drawn simultaneously echoed around them.
Lian immediately activated Predator’s Instincts.
Danger warnings came from all directions. Soldiers appeared from behind the trees, among the roots, and above the wooden platforms.
Not a few scattered guards, but a complete and trained unit!
More than thirty people took positions around the group in less than a few seconds.
Their armors were uniform: black metal with red lines, and rectangular shields with a flaming root emblem.
Half of them held long spears with red tips.
The rest carried bows whose strings were made of Mana strands instead of normal string.
A few archers were positioned on high platforms among the trees. All arrows were aimed directly at One and the people on its back.
Three soldiers blocked the return path to the Cindervein Passage.
Another group covered the eastern path. Even the roots above were controlled by archers.
This encirclement had not formed in an instant. They had been prepared for something to exit the passage.
One lowered its body, its jaws opened.
A wave of anger and the desire to protect entered Lian’s mind through Hive Link.
Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
Seraphina also adjusted her feet to jump down.
Shadow Wolf came out of Liana’s shadow.
"No one attack." Lian immediately said calmly, trying to calm his group members.
One still let out a muffled growl.
Lian sent another direct command through Hive Link. The ant did not fully close its jaws, but it did not attack.
Lian examined the soldiers’ formation. The distances were precise. The spearmen were in the first line, and the shields were ready to block the path.
The archers were at height, and two reserve groups were behind the roots. These were not hunters or mercenaries.
They were a real army, and it was clear their goal was to control and protect the border.
A commander came forward from the front line. His armor was thicker than the rest.
Black plates with red veins covered his chest, and a dark cloak with the flaming root emblem was on his shoulder.
He held a long spear in his hand, its tip shining with dense Mana. He stopped at a safe distance and pointed the spear directly at Lian.
"Get down from the creature."
His voice was loud and commanding. There was no sign of fear or hurry in it.
His gaze moved over One, then Lian, Seris, Seraphina, and Liana.
"Place your weapons on the ground and declare your identities."
The first line of soldiers brought their shields forward. The archers pulled their Mana strings tighter.
Lian did not get down from One, but he did not reach for any weapon either.
The commander took his gaze off them and fixed it on the Cindervein Passage’s opening.
For the first time, his cold expression changed slightly. Something between doubt and disbelief.
"No traveler comes out of that passage."
The warm wind of Emberroot moved his cloak, and the tips of all the arrows became brighter. The commander looked at Lian again.
"So explain how you four crossed a border that has been closed for years, or you will be executed!"

Lian picked up the stone.

It could later be used for equipment enhancement or making medicine.
Without pausing, he placed it into his storage space, then returned the bone to almost its previous position.
When he returned to the group, no one asked any specific questions.
With the Rootfire Marrow obtained, all the treasures the Celestial Book of Treasure had shown had been collected.
Three B-rank or higher treasures in one day.
The book had once again proven its real value.
He also checked it again to see if there were any special treasures nearby.
The answer was no.
There were some treasures, but all of them were below B-rank, and in his eyes, such treasures were no different from trash.
But it didn’t matter.
Even so, he had gained a lot of profit from this Special Area.
He had a lot of monster corpses in his storage space.
He was slowly getting closer to Level 20 and felt he should finally reach it within the next few days.
After One recovered its energy, they resumed moving.
While moving, Lian also glanced at the map.
"We’re not far from the exit."
"That’s it?
We’re arriving that soon?" Liana said with surprise and relief.
"Yeah, the passage was shorter than I expected.
Compared to the Giants’ Graveyard, this was like a kindergarten."
"Isn’t that good?
We faced no danger and are leaving safely." Seraphina added.
Lian nodded.
At least they had been able to cross this place quickly and there was no great danger.
"I have a bad feeling.
Everything has been too calm." But Seris disagreed.
"Please be quiet and don’t jinx it!" Liana glared at her.
"Look!" Seraphina pointed.
An orange light could be seen at the passage’s end.
Fresh air was coming from that side.
The sound of birds became clearer.
One increased its speed.
The last glass walls remained behind them.
The red roots on both sides of the path parted.
The group emerged from the Cindervein Passage’s opening.
Emberroot Forest spread before them.
For a few moments, no one could immediately say anything.
The forest was different from all the areas they had seen so far.
Massive trees with dark brown trunks rose to heights of dozens of meters.
Red veins moved inside their bark, and every time Mana reached from the roots to the branches, the golden and orange leaves would light up.
The leaves looked like fire but did not burn.
Narrow rivers of fire flowed among the roots.
Their surfaces were red and gold, and bright steam rose from them.
Unlike the Forest of Giants and Glassthorn, clear signs of civilization could be seen everywhere.
Wooden and stone bridges were built between the large roots.
A wide path lay on the ground, with traces of wheels, feet, and pack creatures on it.
Lamps with red glass were placed on posts at regular intervals.
Even in the distance, part of a stone wall could be seen among the trees.
"Finally." Liana let out her breath upon seeing the path and lamps.
But Lian had a bad feeling.
According to the map’s information, the civilization should not be next to the border passage.
So what were all these constructions?
Could they have built a base and structures here to control and protect the border?
It wasn’t unlikely.
That’s what an intelligent civilization would do.
"We better be careful.
We might encounter intelligent creatures at any moment."
"There’s no need to worry.
I doubt—" But before Liana could complete her sentence... something happened.
One only took a few steps into the forest, and then the sound of dozens of weapons being drawn simultaneously echoed around them.
Lian immediately activated Predator’s Instincts.
Danger warnings came from all directions.
Soldiers appeared from behind the trees, among the roots, and above the wooden platforms.
Not a few scattered guards, but a complete and trained unit!
More than thirty people took positions around the group in less than a few seconds.
Their armors were uniform: black metal with red lines, and rectangular shields with a flaming root emblem.
Half of them held long spears with red tips.
The rest carried bows whose strings were made of Mana strands instead of normal string.
A few archers were positioned on high platforms among the trees.
All arrows were aimed directly at One and the people on its back.
Three soldiers blocked the return path to the Cindervein Passage.
Another group covered the eastern path.
Even the roots above were controlled by archers.
This encirclement had not formed in an instant.
They had been prepared for something to exit the passage.
One lowered its body, its jaws opened.
A wave of anger and the desire to protect entered Lian’s mind through Hive Link.
Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt.
Seraphina also adjusted her feet to jump down.
Shadow Wolf came out of Liana’s shadow.
"No one attack." Lian immediately said calmly, trying to calm his group members.
One still let out a muffled growl.
Lian sent another direct command through Hive Link.
The ant did not fully close its jaws, but it did not attack.
Lian examined the soldiers’ formation.
The distances were precise.
The spearmen were in the first line, and the shields were ready to block the path.
The archers were at height, and two reserve groups were behind the roots.
These were not hunters or mercenaries.
They were a real army, and it was clear their goal was to control and protect the border.
A commander came forward from the front line.
His armor was thicker than the rest.
Black plates with red veins covered his chest, and a dark cloak with the flaming root emblem was on his shoulder.
He held a long spear in his hand, its tip shining with dense Mana.
He stopped at a safe distance and pointed the spear directly at Lian.
"Get down from the creature."
His voice was loud and commanding.
There was no sign of fear or hurry in it.
His gaze moved over One, then Lian, Seris, Seraphina, and Liana.
"Place your weapons on the ground and declare your identities."
The first line of soldiers brought their shields forward.
The archers pulled their Mana strings tighter.
Lian did not get down from One, but he did not reach for any weapon either.
The commander took his gaze off them and fixed it on the Cindervein Passage’s opening.
For the first time, his cold expression changed slightly.
Something between doubt and disbelief.
"No traveler comes out of that passage."
The warm wind of Emberroot moved his cloak, and the tips of all the arrows became brighter.
The commander looked at Lian again.
"So explain how you four crossed a border that has been closed for years, or you will be executed!"

chapters.title: Chapter 276: The Emberroot Forest II
paragraphs: "So explain how you four crossed a border that has been closed for years."
The commander’s voice echoed in Emberroot’s hot air.
No one answered immediately.

More than thirty soldiers had taken positions around the group. The spearmen with heavy shields formed the first ring of the encirclement, and the archers from platforms built among the massive tree trunks had them aimed.
The red lines on the soldiers’ armor flickered with Mana flow.
One had lowered its massive body.
Its six legs were placed on the ground at a proper distance, and its jaws were half-open. Only one command was needed for it to attack the first line of soldiers.
But Lian had not yet given such a command.
Through Hive Link, he clearly felt One’s anger and distrust.
The ant did not count the number of enemies, analyze the towers’ positions, or the archers’ angles. It only saw that a group of unknown creatures had aimed their weapons at Lian.
And for One, that was reason enough to attack.
"Don’t move." Lian sent a calm wave through the link. Although the situation seemed bad, he currently saw no need for conflict.
One’s jaws closed slightly, but its body remained ready.
Lian took his attention off the soldiers and focused on the commander.
A tall man stood in the center of the encirclement. His skin was dark bronze, and veins of red light extended from under his neck to the side of his face.
The veins were not constant.
With every pulse, their light would intensify and then fade; like molten flow moving beneath a layer of black stone.
His black hair was tied behind his head.
His ears were slightly more elongated than human ears, and their tips curved backward, but the difference was not so great that it made him resemble races like elves.
His eyes caught Lian’s attention more than anything else.
The center of his eye was black, but the iris surrounding it shone in dark red. The pupil was not visible in the usual shape, and the light inside the eye moved like glowing coal.
His armor was also different from human equipment.
Black metal, but not entirely metal.
In some sections, a texture like compressed wood could be seen, and red veins flowed between its plates. When the commander transferred Mana to his spear, those veins lit up.
[Race: Cindari]
[Level: 25]
[Rank: Mutated]
Lian kept his gaze on his Level for a moment. A border unit commander was Level 25.
Not a city leader, not one of the civilization’s most powerful warriors, only the commander of an outpost protecting one of the western entrances.
That number alone was enough for Lian to decide to avoid direct conflict with the Emberroot civilization for now.
Of course, there was the possibility that they only placed powerful individuals to guard the borders, but in any case, caution was necessary in such conditions.
On the other hand, the soldiers were also examining them carefully.
For the Cindari, four humans with skin without red veins, normal eyes, and round ears were probably just as strange as they were to Lian.
A few soldiers kept their gazes on Seris’s and Seraphina’s hair.
Others examined One.
A creature that size, with a black shell and jaws that could crush an armored soldier in half, could not be ignored.
Kael still held his spear pointed at Lian.
But before Lian could give an explanation, the commander narrowed his eyes slightly.
"You look like the outsiders we have found recently."
"There are other people like us here?" Lian’s mind immediately moved away from the passage issue.
The border commander, or Kael, examined him for a few seconds.
Perhaps he had expected Lian to first explain about his own safety.
"Many."
Only one word, but it was enough to make all four of them focus completely on him.
Seraphina leaned forward slightly.
Lian, without turning his head toward her, lowered his hand slightly; a small gesture asking her not to say anything for now.
Seraphina understood and remained silent.
"But we found all of them inside Emberroot." The commander continued.
His gaze moved among the four humans.
"Some appeared near the rivers. Some among the southern roots. We found a few groups inside the eastern ruins, and some near the hunting paths."
Then he turned his head toward the dark opening of the Cindervein Passage.
"None of them came out of Glassthorn." His spear rose slightly higher, and the light at its tip intensified.
"So I ask again. How did you cross a passage that has been closed for years?"
Lian could either tell the truth or come up with various excuses.
"Before I explain about the path, I want to know the condition of the outsiders you found." He answered.
"That race that calls itself human? Well... why should I tell you? I’m the one asking questions here!"
Lian nodded. Upon hearing the word "human," he was sure that other humans were really there.
This strengthened a few possibilities. Some of the main group members might be among them.
Even if none of their acquaintances were there, the humans present would have valuable information about Emberroot, its cities, and the events after the transfer.
"Now answer." Kael said with a colder voice.
"We found an old map that showed the path."
"A map from who?"
"An old group that had passed through different areas."
"Their name?"
"The Varkesh." Lian thought for a moment and decided to just randomly say one of the tribes’ names.
A few soldiers looked at each other upon hearing the name.
Kael hid his reaction, but the veins on his neck became brighter for a moment.
So they knew the name Varkesh, or at least had read about them in old documents.
"Where are they?"
"Dead."
"So you took the map from their corpses?"
"Yeah."
Lian was not lying. They had indeed obtained a piece of the map from the Varkesh tribe, right? He just didn’t need to give all the details.
Kael was silent for a short moment and then added.
"The passage should be unsafe. How did you manage to cross it without trouble? The other humans we found shouldn’t have such ability.
"Well, we are a bit stronger than them."
"Where are you from?"
"We are not from around here." Lian said with a blank face. Normally, he wouldn’t say such a thing.
But unfortunately, it was possible that the humans had already told the truth. In fact, he was sure some of them had told the truth.
But he still decided to give an ambiguous answer.
This time, the soldiers’ reaction was more obvious.
A few Cindari whispered something in their own language. Some spears went lower, some higher. An archer on the left platform adjusted his arrow’s angle directly at Lian’s head.
Kael did not seem surprised. He had probably heard the same answer from the other humans too.
"How did you enter this world?"
"Through a rift." Lian said. His guess was correct. This bastard knew they were not from this world, and he then realized something.
This guy was only asking formal questions that had probably been asked of all humans.
"How many?"
"There were many groups. We got separated after entering."
"Did all of you enter together?" Kael looked at Seris and then at the other two girls.
"Yes."
"What is your goal in Emberroot?"
"Finding the rest of our group members, and finding a way out of this world." He added the last part only as a relatively false excuse.
"Did you kill anyone from Emberroot’s people to get here?" The commander asked seriously.
"No."
"Did you attack an outpost or caravan?"
"No."
"Did you steal anything from our borders?"
"No." Lian said without changing his expression.
The three treasures he had found in the Cindervein Passage were not within the Cindari’s defined territory, and even if they were, it didn’t matter. They were his now.
Kael took his gaze off Lian and looked at his three companions, as if trying to examine them to see if there was any problem with them.
The commander was silent for a while.
Then he lowered his spear, but none of the soldiers put down their weapons.
"You must come with us."
"Where?" Seraphina asked.
"Vhalaris."
Kael pointed toward the eastern path with his spear’s tip.
"The largest western border city of Emberroot."
Then he kept his gaze directly on Seraphina.
"The Rootwarden will see you and personally conduct the interrogation. He will decide whether you are allowed to stay, imprisoned, or expelled from our territory."
Seris’s frown deepened. Her hand was still on her sword’s hilt. She didn’t like being told what to do.
"And if we don’t want to come with you?" Seraphina also said.
