chapters.title: Chapter 277: The Emberroot Forest ( Final )
paragraphs: The sound of several bowstrings being drawn simultaneously echoed in the air. The archers applied more pressure, and the veins on the first line of soldiers’ armor became brighter.
Tension increased in an instant.
It was clear that Seraphina’s words had not been well received by the natives of this forest!
One opened its jaws wider, but Lian sent a stronger wave through Hive Link.
"Not yet."
And then, before Seraphina or Seris could say another word, he said.
"It’s fine. We’ll come with you."
Seraphina turned toward him. Seris also gave him a brief look.
Neither of them was satisfied. They didn’t understand why Lian was behaving this way. The Lian they knew should have acted ruthlessly and dominantly in such a situation.
But why was he cooperating with these wild creatures?
In the end, they said nothing and did not object.
Kael examined Lian’s face for a few seconds, perhaps trying to understand if this acceptance came from fear or calculation.
"Then move."
The commander placed his spear beside his body.
"But if you try any tricks, escape, or do anything foolish, all four of you and that monster will be executed on the spot."
One let out a threatening sound from its jaws.
The veins on several soldiers’ armor immediately lit up.
Lian, without taking his gaze off Kael, placed his hand on One’s shell.
"Understood."
Kael commanded his soldiers. Most of the forces remained at the outpost.
Twelve soldiers changed their formation and positioned themselves around One. Four in front, four on the sides, and four behind.
Kael himself moved at the front.
Lian noticed that the commander did not want to hand over responsibility for them to someone else.
Four humans crossing the Cindervein Passage was too unusual for him.
One moved with Lian’s command. The Cindari soldiers synchronized their steps with it.
None of them had to run.
Their bodies were completely adapted to the heat and uneven ground of Emberroot.
The path ahead was different from all the roads they had seen in the previous two forests.
A wide road was built among the massive roots.
The road’s surface consisted of compacted soil, red stone pieces, and bands of Heartwood. Every few hundred meters, pillars with amber lamps were placed.
In some sections, narrow Mana rivers crossed the path.
Bridges of Heartwood Steel were built over them; a material that had both the texture of wood and the strength of metal.
When One stepped onto the first bridge, the red veins beneath its surface lit up and distributed its weight pressure across the entire structure.
Lian carefully examined the bridge’s structure.
The Cindari civilization did not only use the forest’s natural resources. They had learned to directly channel the roots’ Mana flow into their structures.
Every few kilometers, a large watchtower was built on a tree trunk. The platforms were connected by narrow bridges, and soldiers monitored the forest from above.
Some towers had large weapons on them.
A combination of Ballista and Mana tools that fired massive metal bolts.
If the Cindari really intended to kill the group, escaping from this path would not be simple, at least that’s what they thought.
From Lian’s view, fighting the natives of this forest was not that hard. Their only advantage was environmental superiority, which has no use against absolute power.
After a while, the first caravan appeared from the front.
Six four-legged creatures with gray skin and stone plates on their backs were moving. Large chests, bags of resources, and barrels full of glowing liquid were tied to their bodies.
The caravan guards stopped upon seeing One and four humans on its back.
A young Cindari child stuck his head out from inside one of the wagons.
His golden eyes were wide with curiosity. His mother immediately pulled him back and closed the curtain.
The hunters accompanying the caravan gave cautious looks at the humans.
Some reached for their weapons but, upon seeing Kael and the border soldiers, did not intervene.
Lian allowed a distance to form between One and the front soldiers. The sound of the ant’s feet on the road prevented their quiet conversation from reaching Kael’s ears.
"Couldn’t we just kill all of them?" Seris asked without introduction.
Her tone was so serious that even Liana stared at her for a moment.
"We could." Lian answered.
Seris raised her eyebrow slightly.
"Then why didn’t we?"
Lian looked at the watchtower on the right. Three soldiers were standing on it, one behind a Ballista.
"Because we don’t know if after those thirty, three hundred would come, or thirty thousand." Then he looked at Kael, who was moving ahead.
"A border outpost commander was Level 25."
Seraphina turned her head toward him, and Liana’s ears perked up.
"We don’t know what Level the strongest person in this civilization is, how many cities they have, how large their army is, or what Artifacts they use."
Seris gave a brief look at the towers.
"Killing that group might not have been hard. But afterward, we would have to fight an entire civilization we know nothing about." Lian said.
"And if it becomes necessary?" Seris said.
"Let us first get familiar with the civilization as an enemy, and then if necessary, we’ll proceed with your method."
The young Pendragon nodded. That answer was enough for her.
"Do you think the rest of our group members are inside Vhalaris?" Seraphina said after a few moments.
Lian looked at the path ahead.
"Kael said they found many people like us."
"How many?"
"We don’t know yet." Lian paused briefly.
"If we’re lucky, maybe one or two of our group will be among them."
Seraphina nodded. Her gaze fell on her sword for a moment and then returned to the path.
"I hope Selina is there too." Liana, who had been silent until then, said.
Her usual playful tone was weaker.
"I haven’t heard anything about her since we entered the Special Area."
Seraphina gave her a brief look.
"She’s usually the one who should be worried about me." Liana sighed.
A very small smile formed on her face, but quickly faded.
"This situation is reversed, and I don’t like it at all."
Lian could not promise that Selina was safe. He didn’t know where she had appeared or what danger she had faced, so he only said what he could truly do.
"First, we find the humans inside the city. If she’s not there, we’ll ask about all the groups seen in other areas."
Liana was silent for a few seconds and then nodded.
"Okay."
The path continued. The deeper they went into Emberroot, the more intense the heat became.
At first, only their skin had become warm, but a few hours later, the air entered their lungs like hot steam.
The trees were larger, the red veins inside their trunks shone more intensely, and the rivers that were narrow near the border had now become wide and powerful currents.
Golden steam rose from the rivers’ surfaces.
Some stones along the path had turned dark red due to the constant heat.
The Cindari showed no signs of discomfort. Even their heavy armor did not hinder their movement.
But the humans gradually felt the effects. Sweat ran down Seraphina’s face.
Liana pushed her hair away from her neck several times.
Even Seris, who usually showed no discomfort, adjusted her armor’s collar and took a deeper breath once.
Lian also felt the heat. He had resistance to cold, not to heat.
He reached into his storage space.
He took out four fruits from inside. Each was about the size of a large apple, perhaps even slightly larger.
Their skin was red and gold, and the light inside them pulsed in a slow rhythm. He kept one for himself and handed the other three fruits to the girls.
Liana was the first to take one.
"What is this?"
Seraphina and Seris also took their fruits, and the information panel appeared before them.
[Cinderheart Fruit]
[Rank: B]
[Effect: Permanently increases heat resistance and improves Mana circulation.]
All three stared at the panel for a moment. Seraphina moved her gaze from the fruit to Lian.
"You’re just giving us three B-rank consumable items like that?"
"There were four." Lian examined his own fruit.
"Where did you get them?" Liana immediately asked.
"In the passage."
"When did you manage to find them?"
"When I went to check the path."
"We were also inside that same passage." Liana narrowed her eyes.
"I know."
"So why didn’t I see them?"
Lian took a small bite of the fruit. The initial taste was sweet.
But a moment later, compressed heat was released inside his mouth; like drinking molten metal, without burning his tongue or throat.
"You’re not supposed to see everything." He answered.
Liana opened her mouth to object, but Seris ate her fruit without asking any further questions.
Seraphina did the same after a few seconds.
Liana looked at the two, then bit into the fruit. Red and golden strands appeared under all four of their skins for a moment.
The heat went down from the throat and gathered in the center of the chest.
Then it quickly spread throughout the body. Lian felt his Mana channels open wider.
Emberroot’s heat, which had been heavy and suffocating moments before, suddenly became more natural.
Not that the temperature had dropped, but his body had adjusted itself to the environment.
The sweat on their skin evaporated. Seraphina’s breathing became calmer, and Seris returned her armor’s collar to its previous state.
Liana opened and closed her fingers a few times.
[Heat resistance increased.]
[Heat resistance increased.]
"How did you get such a treasure?" Liana whispered in disbelief. All that hellish heat was gone, and she stared at Lian with wide eyes.
She doubted such a thing could be found by chance!

sentences.text: The sound of several bowstrings being drawn simultaneously echoed in the air.
The archers applied more pressure, and the veins on the first line of soldiers’ armor became brighter.
Tension increased in an instant.
It was clear that Seraphina’s words had not been well received by the natives of this forest!
One opened its jaws wider, but Lian sent a stronger wave through Hive Link.
"Not yet."
And then, before Seraphina or Seris could say another word, he said.
"It’s fine.
We’ll come with you."
Seraphina turned toward him.
Seris also gave him a brief look.
Neither of them was satisfied.
They didn’t understand why Lian was behaving this way.
The Lian they knew should have acted ruthlessly and dominantly in such a situation.
But why was he cooperating with these wild creatures?
In the end, they said nothing and did not object.
Kael examined Lian’s face for a few seconds, perhaps trying to understand if this acceptance came from fear or calculation.
"Then move."
The commander placed his spear beside his body.
"But if you try any tricks, escape, or do anything foolish, all four of you and that monster will be executed on the spot."
One let out a threatening sound from its jaws.
The veins on several soldiers’ armor immediately lit up.
Lian, without taking his gaze off Kael, placed his hand on One’s shell.
"Understood."
Kael commanded his soldiers.
Most of the forces remained at the outpost.
Twelve soldiers changed their formation and positioned themselves around One.
Four in front, four on the sides, and four behind.
Kael himself moved at the front.
Lian noticed that the commander did not want to hand over responsibility for them to someone else.
Four humans crossing the Cindervein Passage was too unusual for him.
One moved with Lian’s command.
The Cindari soldiers synchronized their steps with it.
None of them had to run.
Their bodies were completely adapted to the heat and uneven ground of Emberroot.
The path ahead was different from all the roads they had seen in the previous two forests.
A wide road was built among the massive roots.
The road’s surface consisted of compacted soil, red stone pieces, and bands of Heartwood.
Every few hundred meters, pillars with amber lamps were placed.
In some sections, narrow Mana rivers crossed the path.
Bridges of Heartwood Steel were built over them; a material that had both the texture of wood and the strength of metal.
When One stepped onto the first bridge, the red veins beneath its surface lit up and distributed its weight pressure across the entire structure.
Lian carefully examined the bridge’s structure.
The Cindari civilization did not only use the forest’s natural resources.
They had learned to directly channel the roots’ Mana flow into their structures.
Every few kilometers, a large watchtower was built on a tree trunk.
The platforms were connected by narrow bridges, and soldiers monitored the forest from above.
Some towers had large weapons on them.
A combination of Ballista and Mana tools that fired massive metal bolts.
If the Cindari really intended to kill the group, escaping from this path would not be simple, at least that’s what they thought.
From Lian’s view, fighting the natives of this forest was not that hard.
Their only advantage was environmental superiority, which has no use against absolute power.
After a while, the first caravan appeared from the front.
Six four-legged creatures with gray skin and stone plates on their backs were moving.
Large chests, bags of resources, and barrels full of glowing liquid were tied to their bodies.
The caravan guards stopped upon seeing One and four humans on its back.
A young Cindari child stuck his head out from inside one of the wagons.
His golden eyes were wide with curiosity.
His mother immediately pulled him back and closed the curtain.
The hunters accompanying the caravan gave cautious looks at the humans.
Some reached for their weapons but, upon seeing Kael and the border soldiers, did not intervene.
Lian allowed a distance to form between One and the front soldiers.
The sound of the ant’s feet on the road prevented their quiet conversation from reaching Kael’s ears.
"Couldn’t we just kill all of them?" Seris asked without introduction.
Her tone was so serious that even Liana stared at her for a moment.
"We could." Lian answered.
Seris raised her eyebrow slightly.
"Then why didn’t we?"
Lian looked at the watchtower on the right.
Three soldiers were standing on it, one behind a Ballista.
"Because we don’t know if after those thirty, three hundred would come, or thirty thousand." Then he looked at Kael, who was moving ahead.
"A border outpost commander was Level 25."
Seraphina turned her head toward him, and Liana’s ears perked up.
"We don’t know what Level the strongest person in this civilization is, how many cities they have, how large their army is, or what Artifacts they use."
Seris gave a brief look at the towers.
"Killing that group might not have been hard.
But afterward, we would have to fight an entire civilization we know nothing about." Lian said.
"And if it becomes necessary?" Seris said.
"Let us first get familiar with the civilization as an enemy, and then if necessary, we’ll proceed with your method."
The young Pendragon nodded.
That answer was enough for her.
"Do you think the rest of our group members are inside Vhalaris?" Seraphina said after a few moments.
Lian looked at the path ahead.
"Kael said they found many people like us."
"How many?"
"We don’t know yet." Lian paused briefly.
"If we’re lucky, maybe one or two of our group will be among them."
Seraphina nodded.
Her gaze fell on her sword for a moment and then returned to the path.
"I hope Selina is there too." Liana, who had been silent until then, said.
Her usual playful tone was weaker.
"I haven’t heard anything about her since we entered the Special Area."
Seraphina gave her a brief look.
"She’s usually the one who should be worried about me." Liana sighed.
A very small smile formed on her face, but quickly faded.
"This situation is reversed, and I don’t like it at all."
Lian could not promise that Selina was safe.
He didn’t know where she had appeared or what danger she had faced, so he only said what he could truly do.
"First, we find the humans inside the city.
If she’s not there, we’ll ask about all the groups seen in other areas."
Liana was silent for a few seconds and then nodded.
"Okay."
The path continued.
The deeper they went into Emberroot, the more intense the heat became.
At first, only their skin had become warm, but a few hours later, the air entered their lungs like hot steam.
The trees were larger, the red veins inside their trunks shone more intensely, and the rivers that were narrow near the border had now become wide and powerful currents.
Golden steam rose from the rivers’ surfaces.
Some stones along the path had turned dark red due to the constant heat.
The Cindari showed no signs of discomfort.
Even their heavy armor did not hinder their movement.
But the humans gradually felt the effects.
Sweat ran down Seraphina’s face.
Liana pushed her hair away from her neck several times.
Even Seris, who usually showed no discomfort, adjusted her armor’s collar and took a deeper breath once.
Lian also felt the heat.
He had resistance to cold, not to heat.
He reached into his storage space.
He took out four fruits from inside.
Each was about the size of a large apple, perhaps even slightly larger.
Their skin was red and gold, and the light inside them pulsed in a slow rhythm.
He kept one for himself and handed the other three fruits to the girls.
Liana was the first to take one.
"What is this?"

[Cinderheart Fruit]
[Rank: B]
[Effect: Permanently increases heat resistance and improves Mana circulation.]

"There were four." Lian examined his own fruit.
"Where did you get them?" Liana immediately asked.
"In the passage."
"When did you manage to find them?"
"When I went to check the path."
"We were also inside that same passage." Liana narrowed her eyes.
"I know."

chapters.title: Chapter 278: The City Of Vhalaris
paragraphs: After eating the fruits and solving the heat problem, before the conversation could continue, Kael looked back from the front of the line.
His red eyes fixed for a moment on their newly brightened skin.
He had probably recognized the effect of the Cinderheart Fruit, but he asked nothing.
Near dusk, the first signs of the city appeared among the trees.
At first, only a few tall towers, then bridges stretched between massive trunks, and finally, all of Vhalaris was revealed from behind the red roots.
The city was not built on flat ground.
It was spread around several giant trees and roots, with buildings at different heights.
Some houses were built on platforms of living roots.
Some were directly inside hollow trunks, their amber windows protruding from the tree’s bark.
Massive wooden and metal bridges connected the city’s different levels.
Some bridges were so wide that several caravans could pass through them at the same time.
Red rivers flowed through transparent channels between the streets, their energy entering the buildings, workshops, and the city’s lamps.
Whenever a wave passed through the channel, hundreds of windows would become brighter for a moment.
The houses were made of black wood, red stones, and amber glass.
Their roofs did not have a usual shape.
Some curved outward like large leaves, and some merged with the natural growth of the roots.
In the center of the entire city, a massive trunk had risen.
Larger than all the surrounding trees, platforms, bridges, and government buildings were built inside and around it.
The upper part of the trunk disappeared among the golden leaves and orange smoke.
The center of Vhalaris’s government.
The city walls were also not built in a normal way.
Massive roots were woven together, and Heartwood Steel plates were placed between them. Defensive towers had emerged from those same roots.
Large Ballistas were installed on high platforms, and Mana waves from the city’s channels entered them directly.
If a war occurred, the entire wall could react like a living creature, and the path reached the first gate.
Two massive roots formed the two sides of the entrance, and metal plates were raised between them.
Several guard lines were stationed around the gate. With One’s approach, the gate’s activity stopped.
A fully armored guard came forward, and his gaze moved over the massive ant.
"The creature cannot enter the city."
"It’s not a creature. Its name is One." Liana immediately answered.
The guard gave her a brief look.
"Whatever it is, without a seal, a registered contract, or a War Beast permit, it is not allowed to enter."
Seraphina frowned. Seris placed her hand on her sword’s hilt again.
"Then issue a permit for it."
"Registering a creature of this size takes several days. Until then, it must be kept in the Beastward." The guard added.
He pointed to a military area outside the wall.
Several large enclosures could be seen there. Stone pack creatures, armored beasts, and a few War Beasts were kept in separate sections.
"We won’t leave it with a few pack animals." Liana said.
"That is the law."
"I don’t care."
A few guards stepped closer and placed their hands on their weapons. Seraphina got down from One’s back.
Seris also calmly did the same, and tension rose again.
Lian was the last to get down. His movement was calm, but when his feet touched the ground, his gaze changed.
His eyes became cold and emotionless.
A very small part of his aura leaked from his body.
Not enough to be considered an attack, but for someone standing directly in front of him, it was enough.
The guard felt something deadly staring at him from the darkness.
Not a young human, not a tired traveler, not a prisoner, but something that, if it decided to attack, would not stop with killing just one person.
The veins on the guard’s face suddenly lit up, an instinctive reaction to danger.
"Who will be responsible for its safety?" Lian asked.
The guard unconsciously stepped back. Enduring the pressure was not easy for him, and before he could answer, Kael stepped forward.
"I will."
Lian moved his gaze to the commander. Kael did not step back.
"He will be kept in the military section of the Beastward."
He pointed at one of the officers by the gate.
"He will receive enough food, and no one will approach him without permission."
"And if something happens to him?" Lian asked.
Kael was silent for a few moments.
"If when I return, I see even a fresh scratch on his body, I won’t look for the person responsible." Lian continued with the same calm tone.
His gaze passed over the guards and fixed on the massive city behind the gate.
"I will hold your entire civilization responsible."
He did not shout the threat. His voice was not even loud, but this calmness made it seem heavier.
A few soldiers lit up the veins on their armor.
Seraphina and Seris said nothing, but neither showed any objection to Lian’s words.
Liana was standing beside One, her hand on its shell.
"I will put my name and rank as guarantee." Kael still looked directly at Lian.
"Your name and rank mean nothing to me."
"Then I will guarantee something that has value to me."
The commander looked at the city behind him.
"If that creature is harmed under my soldiers’ care, the responsibility is mine."
Lian examined his face for a few seconds. The commander was not lying, at least he himself had no intention of harming One.
Lian communicated with the ant through Hive Link.
He transmitted images of waiting, food, and their return.
One immediately showed dissatisfaction. Its antennae moved toward the gate.
"You can’t enter."
One lowered its head.
Liana stroked the front part of its head.
"We’ll be back soon."
The ant fixed its gaze on Lian. A wave of opposition and worry entered his mind, and he placed his hand on its shell.
"Wait for me."
After a few seconds, One accepted the command.
Kael assigned four experienced soldiers to accompany him to the military section of the Beastward.
Lian looked at each of them. None dared to reach their hand toward One.
The four humans moved toward the gate.
One did not take its gaze off Lian until the last moment.
Even after they passed through the gate, its dissatisfied presence was felt through Hive Link.
Inside Vhalaris was even busier than outside. The streets extended on several levels.
Markets were built on root platforms. Sellers sold flame-like fruits, warm stones, bottles full of red liquid, and pieces of Heartwood equipment.
In the workshops beside the streets, craftsmen melted black metal in furnaces without fire. Red mana waves directly entered the furnaces from the underground channels and softened the metal.
Hammers fell on anvils, each strike scattering golden sparks in the air.
Small Emberroot creatures moved among the crowd.
Some resembled lizards with fiery tails, some were small birds with copper feathers that sat on the edges of bridges.
Elevators made of living roots went up and down in different parts of the city. Wooden platforms moved between levels with the contraction of the roots.
But with the arrival of four humans, the activity around them quieted down. A seller stopped in the middle of a sentence.
A few hunters turned their heads. A mother pulled her child closer.
A group of young Cindari, without hiding their curiosity, looked at the veinless skin and normal eyes of the humans.
Some looks were only curious, some cautious, and some openly hostile.
"New Outsiders."
Lian heard the word. Apparently, the Cindari had chosen a specific name for humans.
"They don’t seem very hospitable." Liana said quietly.
Lian looked at the hunters who were examining their weapons.
"If a few dozen people from an unknown race suddenly appeared in the middle of our city, we probably wouldn’t behave much better."
"At least they haven’t attacked us yet. That itself is a positive point." Seraphina said.
"Yet, but they will soon." Seris snorted. She had a bad feeling and remembered the village of the Dreadmaw mutants.
Liana sighed.
"One of you two needs to learn to say hopeful things."
Kael led them from the main street toward the city center.
The closer they got to the center, the more formal the buildings became, and the security increased.
More soldiers were on the bridges. Some of them wore armors with golden veins instead of red.
The entrance to the Rootspire, or the city’s command center, was located in a natural crack in the massive trunk.
Two doors of white wood opened before them. Inside the tower, unlike the busy streets of the city, was very quiet.
The walls were alive. Energy veins passed through the wood tissue like blood, and every few seconds, a calm orange light spread through the hall.
The corridors were covered with black and red carpets. The patterns on the walls showed the city’s history, battles with monsters, and the construction of Vhalaris.
Kael led them through several corridors and a root elevator.
Finally, they reached a large hall. The hall was built inside the hollow part of the trunk... its ceiling was so high that it disappeared into the orange darkness.

chapters.title: Chapter 279: Another Friend !
paragraphs: Wooden pillars extended from floor to ceiling, and strands of Mana floated between them.
At the end of the hall, a middle-aged man was sitting on a simple chair.
Contrary to Lian’s expectations, there was no massive throne or exaggerated decorations around him. The man had dark bronze skin.
His hair was gray, but the tips of it glowed with a faint red light.
The veins on his face formed a pattern resembling branches rising from his neck to his temples; a shape like a natural crown.
He wore formal robes of black and red. A simple sword was placed beside the chair.
The weapon’s appearance was ordinary, but Predator’s Instincts gave Lian a faint warning. Both the man and that sword were much more dangerous than they appeared.
[Cindari]
[Level: 30]

’Level 30, huh? I guess it’s not bad.’ This was not the highest level he had seen in this forest, but overall, while it might be considered dangerous for others, for him and his group, a level 30 was not a threat.
Kael stepped forward and knelt on one knee.
"Rootwarden."
Maelor raised his hand.
"Rise, Captain."
Then he moved his gaze to the four humans. His eyes were amber, but unlike Kael, they did not have an aggressive intensity.
"Welcome to Vhalaris." His voice was calm and controlled.
"I am Maelor Veyn. The Rootwarden of this city and the guardian of Emberroot’s western paths." He pointed at the four chairs in front of him.
"Sit down. You have traveled a long way."
A few servants brought bowls of cool water and simple food. This treatment was very different from the border encounter.
Maelor had neither chained them nor interrogated them like prisoners.
But Lian was not fooled by his apparent calmness.
All the details of the room, the placement of the soldiers, and the distance to Maelor’s weapon were arranged in a way that kept control of the hall always in his hands.
The four sat down.
Kael remained by the entrance.
"Captain Varun’s report says you crossed the Cindervein Passage."
"That’s right." Lian answered.
"A passage that has been considered closed from our side for years."
"From your side, perhaps."
"So it is still passable, as dangerous as it is." A very small smile appeared on Maelor’s face.
Lian said nothing. The passage was certainly dangerous for normal awakened ones, but its danger level was not even close to the Giants’ Graveyard.
Maelor placed his hands on the chair’s arms.
"Let’s start from the beginning."
His gaze moved over all four of them.
"You are not the first humans we have seen. We are somewhat familiar with your race, but the ones we saw all awakened in this same forest. But you are different."
"What is your goal in entering Emberroot?"
"Finding our group members, gathering information, and finding a way out."
"And why did you cross Glassthorn? You could have found information there too."
"We obtained information about the civilization here and thought we might find more answers here." Lian answered.
Maelor looked at him for a few seconds. He probably knew the answer was not complete, but he did not try to force out all the details.
"We have not had news from that forest for a long time. Did you find anything in Glassthorn that could be a threat to Emberroot?"
"Many monsters." Lian said without pausing. He could tell the other was trying to get information about the other forest through them.
"I didn’t only mean monsters."
"Nothing that would intend to act against your civilization, no."
Maelor asked a few more questions about the path, the number of travel days, and the creatures seen.
Lian gave precise but limited answers.
He said nothing about the Mirror Vault. He also did not speak about the Primordial Root, The Black Silence, or the truth of Orrakas.
Seraphina remained silent about her inheritance.
This was not information to share with outsiders.
"We have no problem with you being guests, but there are rules here. Do you intend to follow Vhalaris’s laws?" Maelor asked in the end.
"As long as your laws are not used against us, naturally, we will be good guests." Lian said.
Kael frowned from the side of the door, but Maelor only nodded.
"That is an honest answer." He leaned forward slightly.
"As long as you are in Vhalaris, conflict with citizens, entering military areas, attacking city forces, and leaving the gates without registration will be considered crimes.
"Will you take our weapons?"
"No."
"A city where armed people live cannot ask its guests to be defenseless." He then added.
"But using weapons inside the city limits without acceptable reason will have consequences." He pointed at Kael.
"Issue Guest Sigils for all four."
The commander bowed his head, and Maelor continued.
"This mark proves you are not prisoners and have temporary residence permission. It also records your entry and exit."
"You mean you’ll monitor us." Lian said.
"Yes."
Maelor answered without trying to hide the truth.
"You are from an unknown race, you have crossed a closed border, and your power seems greater than other members of your race. If I don’t monitor you, I would not be worthy of my position."
Lian did not dislike his direct answer. At least Maelor did not intend to hide the monitoring with respectful words.
"As long as you follow the rules, you are allowed to stay in the city. Vhalaris gives shelter to travelers who are not a threat."
Seraphina relaxed slightly. Seris also lowered her guard a little. They felt this man was not a bad person.
"You said other people like us have been found, right?" Lian changed the subject after nodding.
Maelor nodded.
"That’s correct."
"How many?"
"At least several dozen."
Lian kept his gaze on his face.
"Maybe more. Some northern and eastern routes have not yet sent full reports. Some groups have also left the city without registration and not returned."

"Take them to the Ashfall Ward."
Captain Varun bowed his head.

Four Guest Sigils were issued for them on the way out.
The marks were small pieces of black Heartwood with a red line shaped like a root on them. When Lian touched it, his name and race appeared on the surface.

"Because it was empty."
"What a kind reason." Liana said.

If dozens of armed humans had suddenly appeared in Vhalaris, placing them in a separate district would both protect the Cindari’s security and prevent constant conflict.
After crossing an old bridge, Ashfall Ward was revealed.
The area had been abandoned in the past.
This was still evident from the broken walls, burned roots, and buildings whose roofs were partly destroyed.
But humans had changed the district in a short time. Broken windows were covered with wood and metal plates.
New doors were installed on the buildings. The entrance street was reinforced with defensive barriers, filled bags, and metal plates.
Guards were standing on several rooftops.
One of the larger buildings had been turned into a medical center. A white cloth with a red symbol was on its entrance, and a few wounded people could be seen inside.
Another building was a warehouse.
Monster parts, weapons, and food packages were being moved inside it.
In the central square, several maps were installed on large boards.
People had gathered around them, marking hunting routes, dangerous points, and monster sighting locations.
Almost all the humans were wearing armor.
Even those sitting on chairs or eating kept their weapons within reach.
People moved in groups of four to ten.
A group had just returned from hunting, dragging the corpse of a horned creature on a wooden cart.
Another group was dividing potions and equipment.
A few people were standing in front of the mission building, discussing the next day’s path.
Ashfall Ward looked more like a temporary military base without a single commander than a residential area.
"The Outsiders reside in this section."

"Some leave the city to hunt. Some trade, and some only wait to find their companions."

Rindo.

chapters.title: Chapter 280: The Missing Members
paragraphs: "Seraphina? Lian?"
The names of Seraphina and Lian passed through the murmur of Ashfall Ward.
The young man’s voice was not loud, but the familiarity in it made Seraphina freeze at that moment.
Lian also recognized the owner before turning toward the sound.
The crowd that had formed around the four newcomers parted slightly. A young man passed through two armored groups and came toward them.
Rindo had changed since the last time Lian had seen him.
His neat and controlled demeanor was still there. His back was straight, his steps were not hurried, and his gaze examined the condition of all four before approaching.
But he no longer only resembled the student council president.
His main armor was burned and broken in several places. Replaced plates of Heartwood Steel were on his left shoulder and part of his chest, and their red veins lit up with every Mana movement.
A scratch extended from his eyebrow to above his cheek.
Fatigue could be seen on his face; not the fatigue of a sleepless night, but the pressure that had accumulated over several days without a real chance to stop.
Nevertheless, the moment he was sure the people in front of him were real, his shoulders relaxed slightly.
"It’s really you."
"Did you think we were dead?" Seraphina stepped forward.
They hadn’t expected to be lucky enough to find the student council president here.
Rindo looked at her damaged armor and the battle marks on her sword for a moment.
"After seeing what this forest has, it was hard not to think about it."
His gaze moved from Seraphina to Liana.
Liana gave a faint smile, but the anxiety that had been visible on her face moments before while searching for Selina had not completely faded.
Then Rindo looked at Seris. His brief pause showed he did not recognize her.
Seris also silently examined the young man from head to toe. Her gaze remained more on his weapon, stance, and the wounds on Rindo’s armor than on his face.
Seraphina noticed and said.
"Rindo, this is Seris Pendragon. She was with Lian in the Forest of Giants, and they came together from there."
Then she pointed at Seris.
"Seris, this is Rindo. The head of the academy’s student council."
Rindo raised his eyebrow slightly upon hearing the Pendragon name.
"Seris Pendragon?"
Seris nodded.
"Nice to meet you, young Pendragon." Then his gaze fixed on Lian.
Rindo and Lian had never been close friends.
In the academy, they both knew each other, but their paths and positions were different. Rindo was the head of the student council; someone who dealt with professors, rules, and official structures.
And Lian, since entering the academy, had not spent much time there. They knew each other but were not close, but being in the same group and seeing that both were safe was good news.
Rindo extended his hand.
"I’m glad you arrived safely."
Lian shook his hand.
The pressure of Rindo’s grip was stronger than before. His palm was rougher, and a few fresh cuts could be seen on his fingers.
Before anyone could ask the next question, an armored man approached from the crowd.
"President."
Rindo immediately turned his head toward him.
"The third group still hasn’t returned. They were supposed to send a signal before sunset. Should we send a search team?" The man continued.
The student council president looked at the orange light above the city.
In Vhalaris, seeing the real sky was almost impossible, but the intensity of the central roots’ light decreased with nightfall.
"Wait an hour. If they haven’t sent a signal by then, the second support group will move."
"The second group still hasn’t fully recovered."
"Then add two people from the fifth group to them. But no one leaves the gate without a registered map."
The man nodded and immediately left.
Then a young woman in a gray cloak approached from the other side.
"Council Head, the western medical center’s potions are almost gone. The hunting groups have kept most of the low-rank potions for themselves."
"Transfer half of the central warehouse’s reserve to the medical center." Rindo said without hesitation.
The woman frowned.
"That reserve is for emergencies."
"Seven wounded without treatment is an emergency."
"The hunting groups will complain."
"Let them complain. Tomorrow, each group will receive its share based on the resources they deliver, not what they hide in their room."
The woman looked at him for a few moments and then nodded.
"Understood."
Another teenager arrived and gave a report about a dispute between two groups over dividing monster corpses.
Rindo asked him to bring both leaders to the council building within half an hour and to keep the corpses in the shared warehouse until review.
His orders were short and precise. He did not shout or humiliate others to show power.
But people executed his orders without serious argument.
Lian looked around. People still called Rindo "President," a title that had come with him from Earth.
Some also used the title "Council Head."
But it was clear these names had not remained only because of his old position. Besides, none of the awakened ones present were from their academy.
So it was not logical for them to care about his position in their country’s academy. This showed that the student council president had not been idle during this time.
Rindo had organized the chaos of the humans.
People who had appeared in an unknown world had no unified structure. Most of them were talented novice awakened ones experiencing their first Special Area and didn’t know what to do.
Rindo had formed hunting groups.
He had built a shared warehouse, organized missions, guard duty, a medical center, and the registration of missing people.
These actions had probably made the Cindari accept the humans of Ashfall Ward as a controllable population, not a group of armed invaders.
On Earth, the title of student council president might have seemed more administrative.
Here, the experience of managing people was more valuable than many offensive Skills.
Rindo raised his hand and said to the crowd still standing around the group.
"You can ask your questions later. First, I need to talk to them."
A few people stepped back with dissatisfaction, but no one objected.
Rindo gestured to the four.
"Come. This is not a good place to talk."
He led them through the central square of Ashfall Ward.
Along the way, several people stopped him to greet him or give a brief report. Rindo answered most of them by name.
Lian noticed these details. Real trust was not built only by giving orders.
Rindo knew the names of the wounded, the warehouse managers, and even the groups that had not yet returned.
’He has practically taken control of all the awakened ones who appeared in this forest. That’s admirable.’ It wasn’t just about organizing.
It was about how he had managed to convince the others to listen to him.
Lian could also do such a thing, but he would go the Vorhelm clan’s way... using force to organize everyone.
The temporary council building was in the center of the district’s reconstructed section.

The two-story building had probably been an administrative office or commercial center of Ashfall Ward in the past. Part of the right wall was burned, but it had been repaired with wood and Steel plates.
Two human guards stood at the entrance and stepped aside upon seeing Rindo.
The inside of the building was more organized than the outside.
A large table was in the central section, and several maps were installed on the walls.
The main Emberroot map still had many dark areas, but around Vhalaris, the hunting routes and a few nearby ruins were marked with more detail.
On another wall, the registered hunting groups were listed.
Member names, approximate Levels, departure times, and expected return times.
A separate table showed the amounts of rations, Potions, Arrows, and usable equipment.
In a corner of the room was a list of those who had died or not returned from missions.
But the left wall caught Liana’s attention the most. A large board with English writing at the top was installed.
[Missing Outsiders]
Dozens of names were recorded on small pieces of paper. Next to some names, the last sighting location was written.
Next to some, only the group name or academy was listed, and a few names were marked with red lines; those whose bodies had been found.
Liana silently walked toward the board. Her finger moved over the list.
Once.
Then again from the beginning.
Lian knew which name she was looking for.
Selina.
But her name was not among the list.
"We don’t have the names of all missing people." Rindo said behind them.
Liana turned toward him.
"What do you mean?"
"Only the names of those whose companions entered the city and reported them are registered."
Rindo pointed at the board.
"If Selina is with a group that hasn’t reached Vhalaris yet, her name won’t be here."
"So is her absence good or bad?" Liana looked at the list again.
Rindo was silent for a few moments.
"Neither. It just means we don’t have information yet."
The answer was not encouraging, but it was honest.
Liana said nothing. Her gaze only remained on the missing names for a few more seconds, and then she stepped away from the board.
Rindo took them to a room at the end of the building.
The room had a large window facing the district, and a rectangular table was in its center.
Several chairs of different shapes were around the table; apparently collected from different buildings.
Rindo asked someone outside the room to bring water and simple food, and then closed the door.
"Now, explain."

In Vhalaris, seeing the real sky was almost impossible, but the intensity of the central roots’ light decreased with nightfall.
"Wait an hour.
If they haven’t sent a signal by then, the second support group will move."
"The second group still hasn’t fully recovered."
"Then add two people from the fifth group to them.
But no one leaves the gate without a registered map."
The man nodded and immediately left.
Then a young woman in a gray cloak approached from the other side.
"Council Head, the western medical center’s potions are almost gone.
The hunting groups have kept most of the low-rank potions for themselves."
"Transfer half of the central warehouse’s reserve to the medical center." Rindo said without hesitation.
The woman frowned.
"That reserve is for emergencies."
"Seven wounded without treatment is an emergency."
"The hunting groups will complain."
"Let them complain.
Tomorrow, each group will receive its share based on the resources they deliver, not what they hide in their room."
The woman looked at him for a few moments and then nodded.
"Understood."
Another teenager arrived and gave a report about a dispute between two groups over dividing monster corpses.
Rindo asked him to bring both leaders to the council building within half an hour and to keep the corpses in the shared warehouse until review.
His orders were short and precise.
He did not shout or humiliate others to show power.
But people executed his orders without serious argument.
Lian looked around.
People still called Rindo "President," a title that had come with him from Earth.
Some also used the title "Council Head."
But it was clear these names had not remained only because of his old position.
Besides, none of the awakened ones present were from their academy.
So it was not logical for them to care about his position in their country’s academy.
This showed that the student council president had not been idle during this time.
Rindo had organized the chaos of the humans.
People who had appeared in an unknown world had no unified structure.
Most of them were talented novice awakened ones experiencing their first Special Area and didn’t know what to do.
Rindo had formed hunting groups.
He had built a shared warehouse, organized missions, guard duty, a medical center, and the registration of missing people.
These actions had probably made the Cindari accept the humans of Ashfall Ward as a controllable population, not a group of armed invaders.
On Earth, the title of student council president might have seemed more administrative.
Here, the experience of managing people was more valuable than many offensive Skills.
Rindo raised his hand and said to the crowd still standing around the group.
"You can ask your questions later.
First, I need to talk to them."
A few people stepped back with dissatisfaction, but no one objected.
Rindo gestured to the four.
"Come.
This is not a good place to talk."
He led them through the central square of Ashfall Ward.
Along the way, several people stopped him to greet him or give a brief report.
Rindo answered most of them by name.
Lian noticed these details.
Real trust was not built only by giving orders.
Rindo knew the names of the wounded, the warehouse managers, and even the groups that had not yet returned.
’He has practically taken control of all the awakened ones who appeared in this forest.
That’s admirable.’ It wasn’t just about organizing.
It was about how he had managed to convince the others to listen to him.
Lian could also do such a thing, but he would go the Vorhelm clan’s way... using force to organize everyone.
The temporary council building was in the center of the district’s reconstructed section.
The two-story building had probably been an administrative office or commercial center of Ashfall Ward in the past.
Part of the right wall was burned, but it had been repaired with wood and Steel plates.
Two human guards stood at the entrance and stepped aside upon seeing Rindo.
The inside of the building was more organized than the outside.
A large table was in the central section, and several maps were installed on the walls.
The main Emberroot map still had many dark areas, but around Vhalaris, the hunting routes and a few nearby ruins were marked with more detail.
On another wall, the registered hunting groups were listed.
Member names, approximate Levels, departure times, and expected return times.
A separate table showed the amounts of rations, Potions, Arrows, and usable equipment.
In a corner of the room was a list of those who had died or not returned from missions.
But the left wall caught Liana’s attention the most.
A large board with English writing at the top was installed.
[Missing Outsiders]
Dozens of names were recorded on small pieces of paper.
Next to some names, the last sighting location was written.
Next to some, only the group name or academy was listed, and a few names were marked with red lines; those whose bodies had been found.
Liana silently walked toward the board.
Her finger moved over the list.
Once.
Then again from the beginning.
Lian knew which name she was looking for.
Selina.
But her name was not among the list.
"We don’t have the names of all missing people." Rindo said behind them.
Liana turned toward him.
"What do you mean?"
"Only the names of those whose companions entered the city and reported them are registered."
Rindo pointed at the board.
"If Selina is with a group that hasn’t reached Vhalaris yet, her name won’t be here."
"So is her absence good or bad?" Liana looked at the list again.
Rindo was silent for a few moments.
"Neither.
It just means we don’t have information yet."
The answer was not encouraging, but it was honest.
Liana said nothing.
Her gaze only remained on the missing names for a few more seconds, and then she stepped away from the board.
Rindo took them to a room at the end of the building.
The room had a large window facing the district, and a rectangular table was in its center.
Several chairs of different shapes were around the table; apparently collected from different buildings.
Rindo asked someone outside the room to bring water and simple food, and then closed the door.
"Now, explain."

chapters.title: Chapter 281: the Jailed Members
paragraphs: "Now, explain."
All the group members sat down.
"Exactly which part?" Seraphina asked quietly.
"The guards said you came out of the Cindervein Passage."
The student council president sat across from them.
"None of the humans found so far have come from that side."
"First the Forest of Giants, then we entered Glassthorn, and then we came here." Seraphina answered.
"You crossed two forests?" Rindo stared at her for a few moments.
"Three forests, if we count Emberroot too." Lian added.
Rindo turned his gaze to Seraphina.
Not because he didn’t believe Lian’s words.
He knew well that if parts of the story needed a detailed explanation, Seraphina would probably provide the more organized version.
"I and Seris appeared inside the Forest of Giants." Although it was Lian who answered, he explained parts of the path.
The first hours after the transfer, passing through different sections of the Forest of Giants, reaching the Giants’ Graveyard.
Finding the path, moving to Glassthorn, and then finding Seraphina and Liana.
But his explanations were calculated. He said nothing about the true nature of the Giants’ Graveyard. He spoke nothing of Orrakas.
He omitted the Mirror Vault.
He also did not mention the Primordial Root, The Black Silence, or Seraphina’s inheritance.
Rindo remained silent throughout.
Sometimes he would ask a brief question about the distance, the monsters’ Levels, or the duration of the journey.
When the story reached the crossing of the Cindervein Passage, his gaze fixed on Lian for a moment.
"That’s it? You found a map and crossed the passage?"
"In short, yes." Lian answered.
"And the full version?"
"It’s longer."
Rindo examined him for a few seconds. He knew parts had been omitted, but he didn’t seem to consider it important, so he didn’t continue the question.
"I appeared directly inside Emberroot." This time it was his turn to explain.
"The first few hours I was alone. Then I found two second-year students from another academy and an independent Awakener who had obtained a special entry quota from the federation."
He pointed at the map on the wall.
"We appeared near one of the rivers. Before we knew where we were, a group of monsters attacked us."
The four had managed to survive, but one of the students was severely wounded.
After a while, a Cindari patrol found them and brought them to Vhalaris.
In the following days, more humans were found from different parts of Emberroot.
Some had come without resistance alongside the soldiers, some had assumed the Cindari were enemies and had caused conflict.
A few had been killed during the first encounter, and some groups had found Ashfall Ward themselves before being found by the city’s patrols.
"At first, everyone was working for themselves." Rindo said.
His gaze fell on the room’s maps.
"Food was being stolen. Groups were fighting each other. People were trying to take each other’s equipment through threats."
"And you organized everyone?" Liana asked.
"Organized is too strong a word. At least now no one kills each other for a piece of meat."
"That’s good progress."
The door opened, and two people placed bowls of water and food on the table.
After they left, Rindo closed the door again. Seraphina this time directly addressed the topic she had been waiting for since the start of the meeting.
"Do you have any news about the others?
Rindo placed his hand around his water glass, but did not raise it.
"Have you seen Selina?" Liana asked sooner.
Rindo turned his gaze to her.
"No."
The faint smile Liana was trying to keep on her face faded.
"I didn’t see her name among the registered people either." He added before the silence could become heavier.
"But that doesn’t mean she’s dead. Not all humans in Emberroot have reached Vhalaris yet. New groups are found every day."
Liana lowered her gaze. Her fingers tightened around the edge of the glass.
"Okay."
"What about Marcus and Ethan?" Lian added.
Rindo did not answer immediately this time. His pause was only a few seconds, but it was enough for Lian to understand something had gone wrong.
The young man’s fingers pressed on the table’s edge. His gaze moved away from them for a moment and fixed on the wall map.
"What happened?" Lian asked without changing his expression.
Rindo let out a quiet breath.
"Marcus and Ethan are alive."
Seraphina relaxed slightly.
"Cassian is also alive."
This name made Lian pay more attention.
"All three are here?"
"Yes, they are inside Vhalaris." Rindo paused briefly again and then sighed and added.
"But they are imprisoned."
The room’s atmosphere immediately changed. Seris, who had been more of a listener until then, asked.
"By the Cindari?"
"Yes."
Tension rose in the room for a moment. The student council president could see that the people present were not happy to hear that their friends had been imprisoned by outsiders.
"It’s complicated."
"Simplify it." Lian said with a cold tone.
Rindo was silent for a few seconds, then leaned forward and sat up straight.
"According to the city’s official report, Marcus and Ethan entered one of the restricted sections beneath the Rootspire without permission."
"The Cindari say they intended to steal from the military Archive."
"And Cassian? They say he was the one who prepared the entry route."
"How?" Seraphina asked in disbelief. With what she knew of all three of them, it was impossible for them to want to do such a thing.
Lian’s face was calm, but surprise could be seen in his eyes. For him too, it was hard to believe that Cassian would do something foolish.
Now, if it was Marcus, such stupidity could be expected, and he didn’t know Ethan well enough.
"By forging a Guest Sigil, stealing a seal from one of the Archive officials, and opening two checkpoints."
This accusation was not impossible with Cassian’s abilities.
He was a precise and intelligent person. If anyone in the group could find a way into a protected area without triggering an alarm, Cassian was one of the most likely options.
But Rindo’s expression showed the more important part had not yet been said.
"What are you hiding? Just tell everything?" Lian frowned.
"The city guard says Cassian killed one of the Cindari archivists inside the Archive."
For the first time, Lian, Seraphina, and Liana reacted almost simultaneously.
"Impossible."
All three voices overlapped.
Rindo said nothing.
"Cassian would never kill an unarmed person.
Lian kept his gaze on Rindo.
"Even if his goal was to enter the Archive, killing an archivist would have no benefit for him."
Cassian was cautious. More than that, he would examine the consequences of every action and would never endanger the entire group.
He might break a law. He might enter a forbidden area to save a group member.
But killing an unarmed person in an unknown city, in a way that would incite an entire civilization against humans, was not consistent with his character and methods.
"If he had to fight a guard, maybe. But an archivist? No." Seraphina said.
"I didn’t believe it either." Rindo nodded.
"The body was found next to him?"
"Yes."
"The weapon?"
"Cassian’s sword was inside the archivist’s body."
"They definitely framed him." Liana clenched her fist. She didn’t know why they would do such a thing, but she had no doubt.
"Cassian says when he entered the room, the archivist was already dead." Rindo said.
"Was the time of death checked?" Lian asked.
"The official report says he was killed at that same time."
"And what does Cassian say?"
"He says the body was colder than it should have been. That means the death happened earlier."
This was important.

The Cindari naturally have a higher body temperature than humans. If Cassian had been able to detect the cooling of the body even in Emberroot’s warm environment, there was probably a significant time gap.
"Before he could examine the room, the guards arrived." Rindo continued.
"Were Marcus and Ethan there too?" Lian asked.
"No. They were in the lower corridor. When the alarm was activated, the guards blocked their path. A conflict started."
According to the official account, Marcus and Ethan had attacked the city guard.
Several guards were wounded, and one Cindari soldier had died during the conflict.
"Which one killed the soldier?"
"Ethan. And he has been sentenced to execution."
"But why did they go down there at all? Just for an Archive?" Liana asked in disbelief.
She couldn’t understand why they would do something so foolish in an unknown civilization.
Rindo looked at the room’s closed door, and his voice lowered as he answered.
"Because they thought there were humans being held down there."
"Thought, or saw?" Lian immediately asked.
"Marcus had seen a night caravan."
He explained that a few nights before the incident, Marcus had returned to the city later than the others from a hunting mission.
Near the Rootspire, a military caravan had passed through one of the side entrances. The wagons were covered.
The guards had blocked the path to keep anyone from getting close. But for a few seconds, one wagon’s curtain had moved aside.
"Marcus said there were several people inside. Their hands were tied, and they wore prisoner clothes."
"Most of them were Cindari, but Marcus swore at least one of them was Human."
For a moment, silence filled the entire room.
Because if what they were hearing was true, contrary to their initial belief, they were not dealing with a hospitable and honest race.
On the contrary, they might have unknowingly walked into a large trap...
Lian leaned back slightly. He had guessed that a foreign civilization was not going to treat them well.
But now he was worried about One... could these bastards harm it?

chapters.title: Chapter 282: The Jailed Members II
paragraphs: "The Cindari denied this."
Rindo said that according to the city’s official response, that caravan was only transporting local criminals, and no Human was present in it.
They had claimed Marcus had been mistaken due to the darkness and distance.
But Marcus was sure. Ethan had also believed him.
Cassian had initially opposed direct entry, but after checking the caravan’s route and the city’s public documents, he had realized there was no official record of prisoner transfers on that night.
"So Cassian helped to find the path and forge the Sigil." Lian asked.
"Yes, they were only supposed to enter the underground section, check it out, and return without conflict." Rindo answered.
"It wasn’t a good plan." Seris said mockingly.
"I told them the same thing myself."
"But you didn’t stop them."
Rindo said nothing. This silence was enough to show that he had not known all the details before the incident.
If he had known, he would have stopped them by any means, even if he had to beat them until they listened.
"Where are they being held now?" Lian asked.
"The prison beneath the Rootspire."
"Then we’ll go get them out." Liana said without hesitation.
"No." Rindo immediately answered.
"No?"
"Why?" Seraphina also asked.
The student council president was silent for a few seconds.
Lian realized that saying the next part was harder for him than explaining the accusations.
"Because I handed them over myself."
The room fell into silence.
Even the sounds of Ashfall Ward coming from behind the window seemed more distant for a moment.
Liana stared at Rindo.
"What?"
Seraphina stood up. The chair’s legs scraped on the floor, making a harsh sound.
"You handed them over?" Anger was clear in her voice.
Rindo did not stand up, did not step back, and only sighed.
"Yes."
"You are the student council president, not a guard or informant for the Cindari." Seraphina said with clear anger in her voice.
She herself never thought she would shout at her superior like this... but so what?
Now the situation was not such that it mattered!
"Exactly because I was responsible for the others, I did this." Rindo’s voice became firmer this time.
"By handing over three of our own members?"
"By preventing more than forty people from being killed."
Seraphina fell silent, but did not sit down.
"After the conflict, Vhalaris’s forces surrounded all of Ashfall Ward." Rindo pointed at the window.
"Hundreds of soldiers. Archers on the rooftops, armored forces at all entrances, and two Ballistas on the main bridge."
Lian reconstructed the district’s image in his mind. Ashfall Ward had defensive barriers.
The humans were also armed. But against Vhalaris’s organized army, inside the Cindari’s territory, long-term resistance was not possible.
Besides, this is the Cindari’s territory, so logically, it was logical to hand over those three to save the rest.
Escape was also not possible because the enemies knew this forest like their own home, while the awakened ones had no knowledge of this place.
"The news of their arrest spread. Several groups decided to attack the soldiers to free them." Rindo said.
"How many?" Liana asked.
"More than twenty people were ready to fight." The awakened ones also have their pride. They cannot accept that their own kind are handed over to a bunch of outsiders.
Besides, they don’t care at all if the Cindari are killed. What is it to them?
"And the rest?
"They were scared." Rindo placed his hand on the table.
"That night, more than forty Humans were inside Ashfall Ward. Half of them weren’t even Level 18."
"You could have escaped the city." Seraphina said.
"All paths were blocked."
"You could have fought."
"And we would have lost." His tone was neither scared nor apologetic, only stating the truth.
"Maybe we would have killed ten or twenty soldiers. Maybe even more. Then the city’s main forces would have entered, and everyone here would have been killed or arrested."
"What did Maelor offer?" Lian asked.
"Two choices." He raised his first finger.
"Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian would be handed over and tried in the city court."
His second finger.
"Or all of Ashfall Ward would be disarmed and arrested as a hostile group."
"So there was no real choice." Lian nodded. Both options were surrender, one voluntary and one forced.
Rindo lowered his gaze for a moment.
"Marcus himself agreed to surrender. Cassian did too." The student council president gave a bitter and very short laugh.
"Cassian understood what would happen if we resisted sooner than anyone. He even asked me to stop the others."
Seraphina slowly sat down. Her anger had not faded, but it was no longer directed directly at Rindo.
"But Ethan didn’t agree." His voice lowered slightly.
"He said he would rather fight there than surrender himself to the Cindari."
"Then what happened?"
"We had to restrain him."
"Who do you mean by ’we’?" Liana asked.
"Me, Marcus, and three others."
Rindo closed his eyes for a moment and opened them again.
"Ethan has considered me a traitor since then."
No one immediately answered. Lian examined the situation in his mind. Handing over three people to save more than forty was a ruthless decision.
But being ruthless did not mean being wrong.
If Rindo had resisted, Ashfall Ward would probably have been destroyed that same night. If the three had escaped, the Cindari would have accused all humans of helping them escape.
And even if the group had managed to leave the city, dozens of weaker humans would have been left behind.
Unfortunately, the power of the Cindari and the awakened ones was in the same range, but the natives of this world also had their own advantages.
Rindo had chosen between loyalty to three people and responsibility for the lives of dozens.
There was no good choice, only a choice that sacrificed fewer people. He couldn’t really be blamed.
If Lian himself were in that position, he would definitely fight the Cindari, but he is different. The reason is that he has the power to force his way through.
And now that he is here, there is no need to worry.
"When is the trial?" He then asked.
"In three days." Rindo said.
"The possible sentence?"
"For Marcus, long-term imprisonment or forced labor at the borders."
"For Cassian?"
Rindo paused briefly.
"If the murder of the archivist is proven, execution."
Seraphina frowned again.
"Ethan?" Lian asked.
"Execution is almost certain."
"For the soldier he killed." Liana sighed quietly.
Rindo nodded.
"The city guard says Ethan struck directly into his heart while escaping."
"What does Ethan himself say?"
"He says the soldier was about to kill Marcus."
"He might be telling the truth."
"Maybe... there is something you need to see. Marcus found it and said it shows they really did arrest a human."
Rindo leaned forward from his chair and went to the small table by the wall. He opened its drawer.
Before taking anything out, he checked the door to make sure it was completely closed, then brought out a piece of black metal from inside a cloth.
He placed it on the main table. The metal was roughly the size of a palm.
It looked like part of a plate or the body of a larger object. The Cindari’s flaming root emblem was carved on one side.
But beneath the emblem, letters had been scratched into the metal with a sharp tool.
The letters were unknown, at least to them. Lian recognized them upon seeing them.
Liana leaned forward slightly.
"Who wrote this?"
"We don’t know." Rindo said.
Lian picked up the piece. The metal was not cold; natural heat was still flowing inside it.
But the grooves of the writing were not fresh. The edges of the scratches had smoothed out, and in some sections, they were covered with a thin layer of oxidation and grime.
This message had not been written in the past few days. Perhaps not even in the past few years. It could be much older.
"Where did Marcus find this?" Lian asked.
"Near one of the service entrances beneath the Rootspire."
Rindo explained that on the night after seeing the caravan, Marcus had examined its path. By backtracking and checking that route, he had been able to find this beside a tree.
It was unclear where the writing belonged, and they didn’t recognize it, but translating it could help.
"Maybe a newly found Human wrote it, in a coded language so no one would understand." Lian said.
"Cassian examined this possibility."
"The result?"
"He said the writing is old."
"That’s right." Lian turned the piece under the room’s orange light.
"How old?"
"Without tools, I can’t say exactly." Lian moved his finger over one of the grooves.
"But it’s not a few months old. Probably a few years or more."
"But we just entered this Special Area." Liana stared at the scratched letters.
"Exactly. This writing does not belong to our world or someone from our world at all."
Rindo pulled his chair forward.
"Marcus and Ethan didn’t enter the Rootspire to steal something."
"They were looking for a prisoner who wrote this message." Seraphina continued.
"Yes."
Lian placed the piece on the table. This writing was not part of any language from their world, but he was almost sure it belonged to a human.
How? Because he recognized the script. It was the same writing used on the map.
This script is one of the native languages of the Ruined Realm... its shape and form are very similar to the writing he had seen on the pillars of the Divine Of Light temple ruins.
That means whoever wrote this distress call was a native of the Ruined Realm who had probably been trapped here for years.
But the Cindari had eventually found and arrested him.
But many questions arise... what exactly did he do to get arrested? If his guess is correct, he had been in hiding all this time, but why? What reason could there be?
"I know where this writing belongs." He then said quietly.

sentences.text: "The Cindari denied this."
Rindo said that according to the city’s official response, that caravan was only transporting local criminals, and no Human was present in it.
They had claimed Marcus had been mistaken due to the darkness and distance.
But Marcus was sure.
Ethan had also believed him.
Cassian had initially opposed direct entry, but after checking the caravan’s route and the city’s public documents, he had realized there was no official record of prisoner transfers on that night.
"So Cassian helped to find the path and forge the Sigil." Lian asked.
"Yes, they were only supposed to enter the underground section, check it out, and return without conflict." Rindo answered.
"It wasn’t a good plan." Seris said mockingly.
"I told them the same thing myself."
"But you didn’t stop them."
Rindo said nothing.
This silence was enough to show that he had not known all the details before the incident.
If he had known, he would have stopped them by any means, even if he had to beat them until they listened.
"Where are they being held now?" Lian asked.
"The prison beneath the Rootspire."
"Then we’ll go get them out." Liana said without hesitation.
"No." Rindo immediately answered.
"No?"
"Why?" Seraphina also asked.
The student council president was silent for a few seconds.
Lian realized that saying the next part was harder for him than explaining the accusations.
"Because I handed them over myself."
The room fell into silence.
Even the sounds of Ashfall Ward coming from behind the window seemed more distant for a moment.
Liana stared at Rindo.
"What?"
Seraphina stood up.
The chair’s legs scraped on the floor, making a harsh sound.
"You handed them over?" Anger was clear in her voice.
Rindo did not stand up, did not step back, and only sighed.
"Yes."
"You are the student council president, not a guard or informant for the Cindari." Seraphina said with clear anger in her voice.
She herself never thought she would shout at her superior like this... but so what?
Now the situation was not such that it mattered!
"Exactly because I was responsible for the others, I did this." Rindo’s voice became firmer this time.
"By handing over three of our own members?"
"By preventing more than forty people from being killed."
Seraphina fell silent, but did not sit down.
"After the conflict, Vhalaris’s forces surrounded all of Ashfall Ward." Rindo pointed at the window.
"Hundreds of soldiers.
Archers on the rooftops, armored forces at all entrances, and two Ballistas on the main bridge."
Lian reconstructed the district’s image in his mind.
Ashfall Ward had defensive barriers.
The humans were also armed.
But against Vhalaris’s organized army, inside the Cindari’s territory, long-term resistance was not possible.
Besides, this is the Cindari’s territory, so logically, it was logical to hand over those three to save the rest.
Escape was also not possible because the enemies knew this forest like their own home, while the awakened ones had no knowledge of this place.
"The news of their arrest spread.
Several groups decided to attack the soldiers to free them." Rindo said.
"How many?" Liana asked.
"More than twenty people were ready to fight." The awakened ones also have their pride.
They cannot accept that their own kind are handed over to a bunch of outsiders.
Besides, they don’t care at all if the Cindari are killed.
What is it to them?
"And the rest?
"They were scared." Rindo placed his hand on the table.
"That night, more than forty Humans were inside Ashfall Ward.
Half of them weren’t even Level 18."
"You could have escaped the city." Seraphina said.
"All paths were blocked."
"You could have fought."
"And we would have lost." His tone was neither scared nor apologetic, only stating the truth.
"Maybe we would have killed ten or twenty soldiers.
Maybe even more.
Then the city’s main forces would have entered, and everyone here would have been killed or arrested."

"Two choices." He raised his first finger.
"Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian would be handed over and tried in the city court."
His second finger.
"Or all of Ashfall Ward would be disarmed and arrested as a hostile group."
"So there was no real choice." Lian nodded.
Both options were surrender, one voluntary and one forced.

"Cassian understood what would happen if we resisted sooner than anyone.

Seraphina slowly sat down.
Her anger had not faded, but it was no longer directed directly at Rindo.
"But Ethan didn’t agree." His voice lowered slightly.

"Me, Marcus, and three others."
