chapters.title: Chapter 283: The Jailed Members ( Final )
paragraphs: "I know where this writing belongs." Lian’s voice made all eyes in the room fix on him.
The black metal piece was still between his fingers.
"Oh? How? From where? What language is it?" Rindo leaned forward slightly.
Lian did not answer immediately. He held the piece at a different angle and examined the shape of the scratched letters once more.
There was only one word on the metal. No name was written, no sign that directly revealed the writer’s identity.
Only a short and simple request.
Help.
The writer probably did not know who would find that piece. Perhaps they did not have the chance to write a longer sentence, or they were afraid the guards would notice the message.
All they had left was that same word that anyone from their own people could recognize at a glance.
Lian moved his thumb over one of the worn grooves.

"I saw this language, not exactly this one, but the structure and shape are the same and close to it, on the pillars of the Temple of the Divine of Light ruins, a ruin I found when we were in the Ruined Realm."

"It is probably one of the native languages of the Ruined Realm. Perhaps it was shared among several ancient civilizations, or at least some groups used it." This language was not exactly the same as the one used in the ruin.
There were two possibilities. Either it belonged to one of the other seven human civilizations in the Ruined Realm, or it was a language belonging to a specific group in the Ruined Realm.
But in either case, he was sure this language belonged to the natives of the Ruined Realm.
For a moment, no one said anything.
The writing was a simple word, but its weight was different from any sentence that could have been written on metal.
"So the person who wrote this wasn’t Human? I mean, from the humans of our world." Seraphina asked quietly.
"No, not from Earth’s Humans." Lian returned his gaze to the lines on the piece.
"A native of the Ruined Realm wrote it. Probably hoping that one of his own people would find this piece one day."
"And come back to save him." Seraphina continued. This was probably what any poor helpless person would do, hoping to be rescued.
Lian nodded.
If his interpretation was correct, the Cindari had arrested someone from one of the other civilizations of the Ruined Realm some time ago.

The age of the scratches showed the matter had nothing to do with the recent arrival of humans, and since Marcus had said he saw a human, it was probably that same human who wrote this message and must be the Ruined Realm native trapped here. This is mostly certain, of course, it’s unclear how he got here and how long he has been here.
It was also possible he had been transferred to another location, or perhaps he was still being held somewhere beneath the Rootspire.
In any case, the mere presence of such a person could be very important.
He probably knew this world better than any transferred human.
Furthermore, he might have information about the collapse of the Ruined Realm civilizations and the remaining civilizations.

Perhaps he knew a truth about the Primordial Root, the separation of the three forests, or even The Black Silence, and of course, he might even know a greater secret that caused the Cindari to arrest him.
Nevertheless, something in the room made Lian’s attention separate from the metal piece.
A very faint and almost imperceptible feeling, a movement in the surrounding Mana.
Since entering the temporary council building, he had noticed the energy flows inside the walls.
All of Vhalaris’s structures used Mana channels. Even the old buildings of Ashfall Ward were connected to the living roots beneath the city.
For this reason, the presence of a strand of Mana inside the wall did not seem strange at first glance.
But this strand behaved differently.
The city’s normal flows were continuous. Energy would pass through the channel and enter the lamps, structures, or supporting roots.
This strand vibrated with the sounds inside the room. When someone spoke, the thin root would contract for a moment.
When silence returned, it would calm again.
Lian said nothing. At first, he had thought it was nothing special, but now he felt it was not.
How could the Cindari possibly trust them?
Lian slowly activated Predator’s Instincts. The room’s normal colors changed, and all the flows in the room appeared before his eyes.
The Mana flows were visible like bright veins in the walls.
Most of them were red and gold.
But among them, a very thin strand of dark red came out from the corner of the window frame. The strand would vibrate slightly with every word spoken in the room.
Something was hidden inside the wood.
’A listening device?’ Lian examined the point without moving his head. Whatever it was, it only vibrated when a sound was heard in the room.
It was clearly sensitive to sound.
’Not strange. I would have done the same thing... how foolish, why didn’t I realize sooner? No one trusts a group of armed outsiders. Of course, they’re monitoring us.’ He chuckled to himself.
The Cindari had probably started monitoring the humans’ council building after the arrest of Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian.
Perhaps the listening device had been active for a long time.
Rindo noticed his silence.
"What is it?"
Lian took his gaze off the window.
If he exposed the listening device at that moment, Seris would probably destroy it. Seraphina was also angry enough to react strongly.
But destroying the listening device would cut off the enemy’s surveillance, and they would react.
Lian could use that same path to test something... an insane idea... but so what? He needed to do it.
"I can translate the language of the person you imprisoned." He turned the metal piece between his fingers and said with a clear voice.
Rindo frowned.
"Who are you talking to?"

At that same moment, the strand inside the wall contracted. Not like a vibration caused by sound, but the Mana in the listening device gathered at one point, and then a short pulse passed through the wall.
The signal was sent out of Ashfall Ward at high speed.
Lian followed its movement until the strand disappeared among the city’s channels.
The reaction was immediate.
Someone behind that listening device was waiting to hear important information.
And Lian’s sentence was exactly what had caused an urgent report to be sent.
"So it really was a listening device." Lian said quietly.
Seraphina stood up.
"They were monitoring us?"
"Where is it?" Rindo immediately turned to the wall.
He took a step toward the window, but Lian raised his hand.
"It’s no use now."
"What do you mean?"
"The message was sent."
Rindo glared with anger at the point Lian was looking at.
"Why did you intentionally say that in front of the listening device?" He couldn’t believe this idiot had just said that.
What he said would definitely attract the Cindari’s attention! It wouldn’t even be surprising if they sent an army to arrest him right now!
Which fool would do such a thing?
Lian placed the metal piece on the table.

"To see if they would react or not. As long as we talked about the path, the prison, and the accusations, they only transmitted sound. When I said I understood the prisoner’s language, they sent a separate signal. Clearly, what I said was interesting to them." His tone was calm.
But at this moment, everyone present stared at him as if they were looking at a madman.
Why would he do such a thing? This put his life in definite danger!
"Where is the listening device?"
Lian pointed at the wall.
Rindo approached the wall. He pushed his fingers into the wood’s gap and, with pressure, separated part of the frame.
The listening device was hidden inside it. A small, oval object made of black wood, with a red vein moving in its center.
Rindo pulled it out, and the device’s light had gone out.
"Damn it."
"How long has this been here?" Liana looked at the Artifact.
"I don’t know." The student council president clenched his jaw.
"So they heard everything we said here?"
"Probably." He thought about all the words spoken in the past few days about this city and the ruling race, and his face paled.
Did they hear all those words?
"Then they tell me Ashfall Ward is under surveillance, not bugged."
"Now that they know what you know, what will happen?" Seraphina looked at Lian.
"Now they know I can read something they can’t."
Rindo looked at him for a few moments, then pulled back his chair and sat down again.

"No one is doing anything. We need to find a way out as soon as possible. They’ll definitely come after Lian. You need to escape right now." He couldn’t understand why this madman had said those last sentences.
But it didn’t matter. He had made the decision. He had to get everyone out of danger.
"Tomorrow, I need to find a way to see Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian and talk to them. We need to find a way to save them too." It could be done tonight.
But in his view, it was risky. Right now, getting Lian to escape was the most important thing.
"No." However, Lian himself disagreed.
"No?" Rindo thought he had misheard.
"We’re not waiting until morning."
"Why?"

"Because now they know we have information about the old prisoner, and since they’re coming after me anyway, they’ll probably guess we might attack or escape, and they might change the security structure."
Lian pointed at the general map of Vhalaris.
"They might move Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian to separate cells. They might destroy the evidence. They might even execute those three before the trial."
Rindo fell silent. In fact, not just him, but everyone fell silent. The words they were hearing were completely accurate and correct.
If they were being monitored, then the Cindari certainly knew they would not abandon their friends, and to prevent trouble, they might execute those three sooner.
So what could they do in this situation? Their friends could be killed at any moment.
Rindo felt the most pressure... how had he not noticed that damn listening device?
But even if he had, so what? If he had destroyed it, the Cindari might have caused trouble for him... but at least if he had known, he would have known what to say and what not to say.
But now what should they do...?
Everyone’s gaze fell on Lian... waiting to see if there was a way out of this predicament or not.

"Now they know I can read something they can’t."
Rindo looked at him for a few moments, then pulled back his chair and sat down again.
"No one is doing anything.
We need to find a way out as soon as possible.
They’ll definitely come after Lian.
You need to escape right now." He couldn’t understand why this madman had said those last sentences.
But it didn’t matter.
He had made the decision.
He had to get everyone out of danger.
"Tomorrow, I need to find a way to see Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian and talk to them.
We need to find a way to save them too." It could be done tonight.
But in his view, it was risky.
Right now, getting Lian to escape was the most important thing.
"No." However, Lian himself disagreed.
"No?" Rindo thought he had misheard.
"We’re not waiting until morning."
"Why?"

"Because now they know we have information about the old prisoner, and since they’re coming after me anyway, they’ll probably guess we might attack or escape, and they might change the security structure."
Lian pointed at the general map of Vhalaris.
"They might move Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian to separate cells.
They might destroy the evidence.
They might even execute those three before the trial."
Rindo fell silent.
In fact, not just him, but everyone fell silent.
The words they were hearing were completely accurate and correct.
If they were being monitored, then the Cindari certainly knew they would not abandon their friends, and to prevent trouble, they might execute those three sooner.
So what could they do in this situation?
Their friends could be killed at any moment.
Rindo felt the most pressure... how had he not noticed that damn listening device?
But even if he had, so what?
If he had destroyed it, the Cindari might have caused trouble for him... but at least if he had known, he would have known what to say and what not to say.
But now what should they do...?
Everyone’s gaze fell on Lian... waiting to see if there was a way out of this predicament or not.

chapters.title: Chapter 284: A Crazy Stupid Plan? I
paragraphs: "I didn’t want it to come to this, but the conflict has already started." Lian said quietly.
"Normally, it shouldn’t be a problem. We just found the listening device. If we act wisely, we could ask Maelor for an explanation, but do you really think he’ll give a real one?" He continued.

"If that prisoner or the documents related to him are still beneath the Rootspire, they’ll have enough time until morning to move everything. Besides, as I said, Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian’s lives are also in danger."
"So what’s your suggestion?" Seraphina said.
Lian looked at the city map mounted on the wall. The Rootspire was in Vhalaris’s center.
There were several security rings around it, and its military entrance was controlled through the central bridge.
"We don’t have time to waste. On the other hand, for now, you don’t need to get involved."
"So I’ll do something that makes them take me down there themselves."
It took a few seconds for the meaning of the sentence to become clear to the others.
"What do you mean by ’them taking me down there themselves’?" Liana asked in confusion.
Lian did not answer. He had explained enough, and the time for action had come. He moved toward the door.
Rindo stood up and blocked his path.
"Lian, what exactly are you thinking?" For some reason, he had a bad feeling. He could sense that this boy was about to execute an incredibly foolish idea!
"I’m not waiting for a visitation permit, and I won’t let them move the Ruined Realm native or our friends, or execute them."
Rindo stepped closer.
"You just arrived in Vhalaris. You don’t even know the city’s full structure. Don’t tell me you’re going to attack the prison? That’s complete madness!"
Upon hearing his words, the others suddenly understood what Lian’s idea was, and they all stared at him in disbelief, as if looking at a madman.
If this wasn’t suicide, it was definitely suicide!
Only Seris had excitement in her eyes, as if they were finally going to do things her way!
"Don’t worry." Lian placed his hand on the door handle.
"Whatever you’re going to do, explain it first." Rindo grabbed his arm.
He gave a brief look at Rindo’s hand, then at his eyes.
"If I explain, you’ll stop me."
"Because it’s a stupid idea! Get that foolish idea out of your head! You’re putting everyone in danger!"
"Probably."
The veins of anger on Rindo’s face became more prominent.
"I won’t allow it. You’re going to risk the safety of all of Ashfall Ward, and more importantly, your own safety and the group members’!"
"I know you want to save them, but this is not the way! We can find a way together. First, we get out of here, and then we come back to save them!"
Lian pulled his hand out from between his fingers without violence.
"Then it’s better if you don’t follow me."
"Lian, wait!" Seraphina stepped forward and tried to stop him.
It was impossible to let Lian execute such a foolish and suicidal idea!
Even though she was also worried about their other three members, Lian’s life was more important to her than all of them! It was impossible to let him harm himself!
But he opened the door.
The warm air of the district entered the room. The sound of coordinated footsteps could be heard from outside.
Before leaving, Lian noticed that the Cindari forces had reacted faster than he had expected.
More than twelve soldiers were approaching in the street in front of the council building.
Their black and red armor shone under the roots’ light. At the head of the group, Kael was moving.
His long spear was in his right hand, and his expression no longer held the calmness of the city’s entrance route.
When Lian came out of the building, Kael raised his hand. The soldiers behind him stopped and took positions in two rows.
"Outsider."
The commander’s voice echoed in the street.
The humans near the council building stopped moving, and a few reached for their weapons.
"Stay there." The commander continued, his gaze briefly falling on the people behind Lian.
Seraphina, Liana, Seris, and Rindo had also come out of the building.
"The Rootwarden has ordered you to come with us for questioning."
"At least they’re not planning to arrest you yet." Rindo sighed quietly. Maybe this would be enough to buy them time.
Lian looked at the soldiers. The official interrogation would probably be in one of the Rootspire’s rooms.
They wouldn’t take him to prison. Even if they asked about the native language, the entire conversation would be controlled.
He took out the World Memory Map. The map’s living texture opened.
His position in Ashfall Ward was marked with a bright point.
The Rootspire was in the city’s center. The direct path passed through the central square, three bridges, and two security rings.
Then he closed the map.
Kael lit up the Mana veins on his spear.
"Surrender and come with us without resistance. This way, your own safety and your friends’ safety will be preserved."
Lian stepped forward.
"Lian!" Seraphina said, warning in her voice. She knew her childhood friend well enough to know he wouldn’t surrender that easily.
"Damn it, how did everything come to this? Just a few hours ago, everything was calm!"
But Lian didn’t even look back.
"What is your decision?" Kael asked.
Lian activated Thunder Step. Blue lightning exploded in the street of Ashfall Ward, and the bright light turned everything white for a moment.
The sound of air breaking echoed among the buildings. Before the soldiers could fully react, Lian had disappeared from their view.
A trail of electricity remained on the ground and walls. He appeared on the roof of a building over thirty meters away.
"Stop him!" Kael immediately turned around.
The soldiers scattered. Two archers raised their arrows.
One of the Cindari officers placed his hand on a metal plate and sent a red signal into the sky.
An alarm sounded throughout Ashfall Ward.
Rindo stared at the point where Lian had disappeared for a few moments.
"Damn it, what is he doing?" He then shouted. The worst-case scenario was coming true!
Seraphina ran without hesitation. Liana lowered her hand, and a Summoning circle formed beneath her feet.
"Shadow Wolf!"
The black wolf came out of her shadow. Its red eyes fixed on the trail of lightning remaining on Lian’s path.
"When I catch him, I’ll kill him myself before the Cindari do!" Liana said angrily.
Seris watched the escape route for a few moments. Lian was not heading toward the exit walls or the city gate.
The trail of Thunder Step extended directly toward Vhalaris’s center.
"He’s not running away."
Rindo, who was ready to follow him, turned to Seris.
"What?"
Seris picked up her sword from the table by the door and moved toward the street.
"He’s heading toward the Rootspire." She didn’t care what decision Lian had made, but she intended to help him.
Liana and Seraphina felt the same. It didn’t matter to them what decision he had made; they supported him.
But so far, they were certain he intended to attack the prison and free their friends.
Lian moved across the rooftops of Ashfall Ward.
The buildings in this section were older than other parts of the city. Some roofs were reinforced with temporary plates, and some roots still carried traces of burns from years past.
He jumped between two buildings. His right foot landed on the wall’s edge.
Before falling, he activated Thunder Step again. Lightning crawled over the surface of a massive root.
Lian appeared on a higher level of the city.
The alarm sounded from within the trunks, a deep and vibrating sound that was not made of metal but produced by Vhalaris’s roots themselves.
With every beat of the alarm, the red lines inside the city’s channels became brighter.
The Cindari people stopped in the streets. Sellers left their goods, mothers pulled their children off the path, and hunters went for their weapons.
Lian crossed over a narrow bridge. On the other side, the first group of soldiers blocked his path.
Eight spearmen with rectangular shields took formation on the bridge. Two archers were behind them.
"Halt!" the group’s commander shouted.
Lian did not slow down. The spear tips lit up with red energy. He could easily see their movement paths.
Two spears from the center and three strikes from the sides. The archers would release their arrows a few moments later.
He activated Thunder Step at a short distance. Blue lightning appeared right in front of the shield line.
The distance was so close that the soldiers did not expect Lian to enter their formation directly instead of passing over them.
[Iron Fortress Charge]
Compressed defensive pressure formed around his shoulder and upper body.
Lian slammed his shoulder into the center of the first shield. A sound like a hammer hitting a wall passed through the bridge.
The central soldier was pushed back several meters. His back hit the spearman behind him, and the defensive line opened for a moment.
Lian passed through the gap, and a soldier from behind turned his spear.
He bent his body to one side, and the red tip of the weapon passed by his neck.
Then he grabbed the soldier’s wrist and, with a controlled spin, used his weight against him. The Cindari’s body was lifted off the ground and fell on the bridge’s surface.
Lian could have broken his arm, but only removed the weapon from his hand.
The archers released their arrows. One was coming toward his chest, and the other was aimed at his escape route.
Lian stepped onto the bridge’s edge and threw himself down. The arrows passed over his head and fell for a moment into the empty space between the city’s two levels.
The river glowed in the depth below him. Before the fall could gain speed, he activated Thunder Step.
Lightning passed through the tree’s wall.
Lian appeared on the roof of a building at a lower level and moved toward the Rootspire again.
The city’s alarm intensified. The gates closed one after another.
Soldiers appeared on the towers. Several Ballistas aimed at the main paths, though they were not yet preparing to fire inside the city.
Lian saw all these movements on the World Memory Map.
The map did not show living creatures, but with every gate closing and every bridge structure changing, it calculated a new path.
Behind him, Seraphina, Liana, Seris, and Rindo reached the first bridge.
The Ashfall Ward soldiers had blocked the path.
"Move aside!" Seraphina shouted angrily.
"An arrest order has been issued. No Outsider is allowed to leave the district." one of the soldiers said.
Seraphina placed her hand on her sword’s hilt. A very faint light formed on the blade.
Rindo grabbed her arm.
"If we attack here, it will be exactly what I was afraid of."

chapters.title: Chapter 285: A Crazy Stupid Plan? II
paragraphs: Seeing that Seraphina was about to explode from anger and worry at any moment, Liana looked at Shadow Wolf and said.
"Don’t worry, my little one can pass through shadows."
The black wolf sank into the wall’s shadow. The spiritual bond between him and Liana stretched for a few seconds.
Shadow Wolf came out from a farther shadow and followed Lian’s Mana trace.
But the distance grew with every Thunder Step.
"Even Shadow Wolf can’t reach him." Liana clenched her teeth.
"You said he’s not running away." Rindo looked at Seris.
"He’s not."
"He wants to get himself arrested." Seris watched the city’s central path.
"Why is he tearing up half the city to get arrested?" Rindo laughed in disbelief.
He felt he had heard a very funny sentence. What he was seeing was Lian charging toward the prison to attack it.
What kind of attempt to get arrested was this?
"Because if he surrenders here, they’ll take him to a regular detention center or an interrogation room." Seris did not take her gaze off the path.
Seraphina looked at her. She also saw this as foolishness and agreed with the student council president.
She felt Lian wanted to attack the prison and forcibly save those three along with the Ruined Realm native.
"But if he breaks into the Rootspire’s military zone, his crime will be directly registered under the tower’s security." Seris continued.
"And they’ll take him to that same prison." Liana whispered.
Seris nodded.
Rindo showed no reaction for a few seconds, then the veins of anger on his face became more prominent.
"I’m still sure his goal is to forcefully attack the prison. So much effort isn’t needed to get arrested, but regardless, that madman is insane!"
In the end, it was unclear whether his goal was to get arrested or to forcefully save his friends.
None of them could say with certainty what Lian’s insane goal was...
The soldiers still had the path blocked.
"I am the Council Head of this district. If we don’t go after him, he might kill your soldiers." Rindo raised his Guest Sigil.
"He hasn’t killed anyone so far." the group’s commander said.
"Then let us pass before he changes his mind."
The Cindari man hesitated. At that same moment, a new message was received through his communication equipment.
He looked at the four humans and then opened the path.
"Weapons stay in their sheaths."
"Only if necessary." Seris answered.
The four crossed the bridge quickly.
At the same time, Lian had reached the city’s second defensive ring.
A Heartwood Barrier had blocked his path.
A movable wall of black plates and compressed roots had risen between two buildings.
The red veins inside it were spinning rapidly, distributing any direct strike across the entire surface.
Behind the Barrier, more soldiers had gathered.
Hundreds of Mana lines were visible in the barrier’s structure, but all of them connected to one main junction on the left side of the gate.
He raised his right hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
An ice claw formed around his fingers. Instead of attacking the Barrier’s center, Lian sank the claw into the connection gap.
The cold moved quickly into the red veins.
For a moment, the Heartwood resisted the ice. The internal heat and the cold met.
White steam burst from the cracks with pressure. The sound of wood and metal cracking echoed on the path. The main joint could not withstand the temperature difference.
With an explosion of black chips and steam, the left side of the gate collapsed.
The barrier was not completely destroyed, but a gap large enough for one person to pass had formed in it.
Lian passed through the smoke. The soldiers behind the Barrier had lost their vision for a moment.
He pushed aside one of the shields with Iron Fortress, bent through two spears, and passed through the ring without delivering a fatal blow.
The people of Vhalaris watched the scene from higher levels. A murmur had risen from the bridges and platforms.
An Outsider who had entered the city only a few hours ago was now moving at full speed toward the Rootspire.
From their view, this behavior could only be a mad attack, and they became more certain that the outsiders were crazy and savage.
But Lian calculated every move. He did not strike any vital points, did not push any soldier from a height.
Even when an archer aimed directly at his heart, Lian only cut the bowstring with his ice claw and passed by.
If someone was killed, his crime would change from unauthorized entry to murdering city soldiers. Then the chance of being executed before reaching the prison would be much higher.
The Rootspire was now directly in front of him.
The massive trunk had risen through all of Vhalaris’s levels. The central bridge connected the city to the tower’s military entrance like a wide arm.
But with Lian’s approach, its defensive structure changed.
Golden veins lit up inside the bridge. Three layers of Barriers formed in front of the entrance.
The regular forces moved aside, and warriors with black and gold armor took their place.
[Rootbound Warden]
[Level: 26]
[Rootbound Warden]
[Level: 24]
[Rootbound Warden Captain]
[Level: 27]
Lian looked at their information for a moment. These were not ordinary city guards. Each of them could easily defeat most academy students without trouble.
Heavy bows were placed on platforms on both sides of the bridge. Golden strings formed inside them.
The World Memory Map recorded the structure of the three Barriers.
The first barrier distributed impact energy. The second disrupted movement Skills. The third was directly connected to the Rootspire and was powered by the tower’s Mana.
Destroying all three with raw power was possible, but it would probably collapse part of the bridge.
Lian looked for another path.
The first and second Barriers both drew from a single central junction for a brief moment.
He placed his palm on the bridge’s surface.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
A small and compressed wave entered. This time, its goal was not destruction. The Pulse followed the Mana paths.
It passed under the soldiers’ feet, directly entered the central junction, and the Barrier’s golden surface trembled.
"Stabilize the barrier!" the Warden commander shouted.
A few soldiers poured more Mana into the structure, but the Pulse had disrupted the junction’s rhythm before the new energy arrived.
But suddenly, a narrow gap opened in the center of the first two Barriers, and that was enough!
Lian activated Thunder Step. Blue lightning passed through the gap.
He appeared inside the Rootspire’s security ring, but before he could take the next step, something came down from above.
A long spear struck the bridge’s surface, and a ring of compressed fire spread around the impact point, closing the path behind Lian.
Kael stood in front of him. The commander’s cloak moved in the warm air.
The veins on his face and neck were now fully lit. The spear in his hand shone like a glowing rod.
"I gave you the chance to enter the city as a guest." Kael said with controlled anger.
"I’m still a guest, aren’t I?" Lian looked at the ring of fire around them with a smile.
The commander turned his head slightly and looked at the broken Barrier behind him.
"Guests don’t usually attack the center of government."
"Then your hospitality rules are strange."
Kael’s eyes narrowed for a moment, then he spun his spear.
Predator’s Instincts warned a moment before the attack.
Lian pulled his body back. The spear’s tip passed in front of his face.
But Kael did not stop the attack. He turned his wrist and struck the end of the spear into Lian’s side.
[Diamond Skin]
Lian’s skin and muscles hardened. The strike hit his side, but even with active defense, Kael’s force pushed him back several meters on the bridge.
The soles of his boots created grooves on the ground, and before he fully stopped, Kael had already advanced again.
The spear went directly toward Lian’s chest this time. Lian used a short Thunder Step.
Lightning exploded at a distance of less than two meters, and he shifted to Kael’s left.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
The ice claw struck the spear’s shaft. A layer of white ice spread on the ground, but the veins inside the weapon lit up with more intense light.
Heat burst from the shaft’s center. The ice cracked with a loud sound and turned to steam.
Kael attacked Lian’s face with his elbow, and Lian raised his forearm.
The impact made the bones in his hand vibrate.
The commander was not only dependent on spear Skills. His physical power and close-range experience were also high.
Lian stepped back. Kael raised his spear above his head and struck the bridge. Three lines of fire emerged from the surface.
Each covered a different path.
Lian jumped over the first line. The second one changed its path in the air.
Predator’s Instincts warned.
He spun his body, and the fire passed by his armor, burning part of his side’s cloth.
The third line reached his landing point directly.
Lian placed his arm against the wave. The fire explosion pushed him back, and smoke rose from his armor’s surface.
Kael immediately appeared from within the flames. The spear’s tip reached Lian’s side.
Diamond Skin prevented full penetration, but the heated blade cut the skin, and warm blood ran down from beside the armor.
Lian clenched his teeth and placed his hand on the spear’s shaft.
He released a very weak Cataclysm Pulse at close range. The wave did not enter Kael’s body, but entered the Mana path inside the weapon.
The spear trembled for a moment, and the fire veins became irregular. A small explosion formed between the two.
The commander was pushed back a few steps. Lian also distanced himself from the wave’s pressure.
For a few seconds, both examined each other without moving.
Kael looked at the blood on Lian’s side, then at the guards behind him who were wounded but alive.
"You’re holding yourself back."
Lian did not answer.
"You could have killed at least three of my men. Why didn’t you?" Kael continued.

"Don’t worry, my little one can pass through shadows."
The black wolf sank into the wall’s shadow.
The spiritual bond between him and Liana stretched for a few seconds.
Shadow Wolf came out from a farther shadow and followed Lian’s Mana trace.
But the distance grew with every Thunder Step.
"Even Shadow Wolf can’t reach him." Liana clenched her teeth.
"You said he’s not running away." Rindo looked at Seris.
"He’s not."
"He wants to get himself arrested." Seris watched the city’s central path.
"Why is he tearing up half the city to get arrested?" Rindo laughed in disbelief.
He felt he had heard a very funny sentence.
What he was seeing was Lian charging toward the prison to attack it.
What kind of attempt to get arrested was this?
"Because if he surrenders here, they’ll take him to a regular detention center or an interrogation room." Seris did not take her gaze off the path.
Seraphina looked at her.
She also saw this as foolishness and agreed with the student council president.
She felt Lian wanted to attack the prison and forcibly save those three along with the Ruined Realm native.
"But if he breaks into the Rootspire’s military zone, his crime will be directly registered under the tower’s security." Seris continued.
"And they’ll take him to that same prison." Liana whispered.
Seris nodded.
Rindo showed no reaction for a few seconds, then the veins of anger on his face became more prominent.
"I’m still sure his goal is to forcefully attack the prison.
So much effort isn’t needed to get arrested, but regardless, that madman is insane!"
In the end, it was unclear whether his goal was to get arrested or to forcefully save his friends.
None of them could say with certainty what Lian’s insane goal was...
The soldiers still had the path blocked.
"I am the Council Head of this district.
If we don’t go after him, he might kill your soldiers." Rindo raised his Guest Sigil.
"He hasn’t killed anyone so far." the group’s commander said.
"Then let us pass before he changes his mind."
The Cindari man hesitated.
At that same moment, a new message was received through his communication equipment.
He looked at the four humans and then opened the path.
"Weapons stay in their sheaths."
"Only if necessary." Seris answered.
The four crossed the bridge quickly.
At the same time, Lian had reached the city’s second defensive ring.
A Heartwood Barrier had blocked his path.
A movable wall of black plates and compressed roots had risen between two buildings.
The red veins inside it were spinning rapidly, distributing any direct strike across the entire surface.
Behind the Barrier, more soldiers had gathered.
Hundreds of Mana lines were visible in the barrier’s structure, but all of them connected to one main junction on the left side of the gate.
He raised his right hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
An ice claw formed around his fingers.
Instead of attacking the Barrier’s center, Lian sank the claw into the connection gap.
The cold moved quickly into the red veins.
For a moment, the Heartwood resisted the ice.
The internal heat and the cold met.
White steam burst from the cracks with pressure.
The sound of wood and metal cracking echoed on the path.
The main joint could not withstand the temperature difference.
With an explosion of black chips and steam, the left side of the gate collapsed.
The barrier was not completely destroyed, but a gap large enough for one person to pass had formed in it.
Lian passed through the smoke.
The soldiers behind the Barrier had lost their vision for a moment.
He pushed aside one of the shields with Iron Fortress, bent through two spears, and passed through the ring without delivering a fatal blow.
The people of Vhalaris watched the scene from higher levels.
A murmur had risen from the bridges and platforms.
An Outsider who had entered the city only a few hours ago was now moving at full speed toward the Rootspire.
From their view, this behavior could only be a mad attack, and they became more certain that the outsiders were crazy and savage.
But Lian calculated every move.
He did not strike any vital points, did not push any soldier from a height.
Even when an archer aimed directly at his heart, Lian only cut the bowstring with his ice claw and passed by.
If someone was killed, his crime would change from unauthorized entry to murdering city soldiers.
Then the chance of being executed before reaching the prison would be much higher.
The Rootspire was now directly in front of him.
The massive trunk had risen through all of Vhalaris’s levels.
The central bridge connected the city to the tower’s military entrance like a wide arm.
But with Lian’s approach, its defensive structure changed.
Golden veins lit up inside the bridge.
Three layers of Barriers formed in front of the entrance.
The regular forces moved aside, and warriors with black and gold armor took their place.
[Rootbound Warden]
[Level: 26]
[Rootbound Warden]
[Level: 24]
[Rootbound Warden Captain]
[Level: 27]
Lian looked at their information for a moment.
These were not ordinary city guards.
Each of them could easily defeat most academy students without trouble.
Heavy bows were placed on platforms on both sides of the bridge.
Golden strings formed inside them.
The World Memory Map recorded the structure of the three Barriers.
The first barrier distributed impact energy.
The second disrupted movement Skills.
The third was directly connected to the Rootspire and was powered by the tower’s Mana.
Destroying all three with raw power was possible, but it would probably collapse part of the bridge.
Lian looked for another path.
The first and second Barriers both drew from a single central junction for a brief moment.
He placed his palm on the bridge’s surface.

A small and compressed wave entered.
This time, its goal was not destruction.
The Pulse followed the Mana paths.
It passed under the soldiers’ feet, directly entered the central junction, and the Barrier’s golden surface trembled.
"Stabilize the barrier!" the Warden commander shouted.

Lian activated Thunder Step.
Blue lightning passed through the gap.
He appeared inside the Rootspire’s security ring, but before he could take the next step, something came down from above.
A long spear struck the bridge’s surface, and a ring of compressed fire spread around the impact point, closing the path behind Lian.
Kael stood in front of him.
The commander’s cloak moved in the warm air.
The veins on his face and neck were now fully lit.
The spear in his hand shone like a glowing rod.
"I gave you the chance to enter the city as a guest." Kael said with controlled anger.

chapters.title: Chapter 286: The Crazy Stupid Plan ( Final )
paragraphs: Lian looked around. His eyes were still indifferent, and it was unclear what was going on in his mind.
’Everyone probably thinks I’ve gone crazy now, huh?’ He almost laughed. From the outside, maybe all the things he had done really seemed insane.
But he himself knew that wasn’t the case, and behind every action he took, there was a purpose.
And right now, his purpose was to get into the prison.
Rootspire had reacted completely.
Rootbound Wardens came out from the side gates.
The towers around the bridge activated, and large bows aimed at Lian from several directions.
Further back, soldiers were dragging thick chains on the ground.
The golden veins inside the chains showed that these tools were not made for restraining ordinary people.
They were Mana suppression equipment. They knew they weren’t dealing with an ordinary enemy, so they had brought their best tools.
The Warden commander stepped forward. He was another commander, but almost equal in power to Kael.
His armor was covered in golden patterns, and a half-open helmet was on his face.
This gave Lian a general understanding of this city’s power. Contrary to his initial impression, this place was weaker than he had thought.
He doubted anyone above level 35 could be found here. Maybe not even that level existed.
"The encirclement is complete." His voice echoed across the entire bridge.
"Any further resistance will be recorded as a direct attack on Rootspire, and the punishment will be execution!"
Lian scanned his surroundings. More than forty soldiers, Kael in front of him.
Three Barriers behind him, archers on the towers, and probably more forces waiting inside Rootspire.
He could still fight. He could use a larger Cataclysm Pulse and destroy part of the bridge.
He could try Thunder Step to get past the first ring. Maybe even find a way to reach one of the side entrances.
And even if he pushed forward with all his power, defeating this army wasn’t impossible. By killing each of them, he would immediately receive stat points and add them to his stats.
In short, fighting and winning wasn’t impossible... but his goal wasn’t to get past these forces silently.
At that moment, the sound of footsteps was heard from behind the Barrier.
Seraphina, Liana, Seris, and Rindo finally reached the central bridge.
A few guards tried to stop them, but their Guest Sigils and Rindo’s presence allowed them to reach the edge of the security ring.
Seraphina was the first to see the dried blood on Lian’s side. Her expression changed in an instant.
Anger, worry, and disbelief appeared in her eyes simultaneously.
She drew her sword. A transparent layer formed on the blade, and prismatic light moved through it for a moment.
The Rootbound Wardens immediately turned some of the bows toward her.
"Sheath your sword!" Kael shouted angrily.
"First, move your spears away from him." Seraphina stepped forward.
Liana summoned the Shadow Wolf beside her.
The wolf’s body rose from the bridge’s shadow, and its red eyes moved over the soldiers.
"Lian, get back here! Right now!" Rindo looked angrier than both of them.
His face wasn’t red, and he wasn’t shouting aimlessly, but his clenched jaw and closed fists showed just how close he was to losing control.
"You haven’t even been in the city for an hour!" His voice echoed across the entire bridge.
"Do you understand what you’ve done to Ashfall Ward?"
Lian looked at them. He knew his decision had put them in danger without preparation.
If the Cindari decided to besiege Ashfall Ward again, Rindo would have to bear the consequences of Lian’s decision.
Seraphina and Liana were now also standing among dozens of weapons, simply because they didn’t want to leave him alone.
But if he had explained the plan from the start, none of them would have let him enter Rootspire alone.
Rindo would have definitely stopped him.
Seraphina would have come with him. Liana would have sent the Shadow Wolf ahead. And Seris, even if she thought the plan was logical, wouldn’t have let him move without support.
The presence of all four would have turned the plan from a deliberate infiltration by a prisoner into a war between humans and Vhalaris.
Seraphina stepped forward again.
"If you thought we’d let you get yourself killed alone—"
"No one attack." Lian cut her off.
"You’re saying this after what you did?" Seraphina stared at him in disbelief.
Her anger was no longer just directed at the Cindari soldiers. A large part of it was directly aimed at Lian.
"You crossed through the middle of the city without a word of explanation, attacked Rootspire, and now you’re telling us not to attack?"
"Couldn’t you have said something before doing something insane for once?" Liana also said in a sharp tone.
"They might execute you right here!" Rindo shouted.
Lian glanced briefly at Seris.
She was the only one who hadn’t drawn her sword.
Her hand was near the hilt, but her expression showed she understood Lian’s goal.
Still, her cold, narrowed gaze confirmed she wasn’t happy with his method... more like she was dissatisfied that she wasn’t part of the plan too.
"He wanted to throw himself into that prison. I said it before." Seris whispered quietly.
"Was there no better way to get arrested?" Liana whispered angrily.
"If he had surrendered in Ashfall Ward, they would have taken him to a regular holding cell." Rindo answered.
Now he too fully understood Lian’s goal, but this understanding didn’t reduce his anger in the slightest.
"This madman deliberately entered the military zone so they would be forced to take him to the prison under the tower."
The Warden commander had also heard part of the conversation, but that didn’t make him care. He probably felt this fool just wanted to enter the prison to see if his friends were safe or not.
A foolish and somewhat brave decision.
"Kneel and deactivate your Skills." Golden light spread across his armor.
"This is your final warning."
Lian assessed the situation again. Everything had reached the point he wanted, and there was no need to continue.
He raised his hands. The Glacial Reaper Claw disappeared from around his fingers.
The pressure of Iron Fortress subsided, and the remaining lightning from Thunder Step on his armor went out.
"You did all of this just to surrender now?" Kael looked at him as if he were facing an idiot.
"Tell Maelor that I can translate the language of the person you’ve imprisoned." Lian kept his gaze on Kael.
The expressions of several Cindari clearly changed.
Not the ordinary soldiers, but mostly the Rootbound Wardens and commanders standing near the tower’s entrance.
One of them glanced briefly at another.
Kael also lowered his spear slightly, but his eyes fixed on Lian more carefully.
"Who are you talking about?"
"If you don’t know, then you don’t need to worry." Lian smiled faintly, and then brought his hands forward.
"But until I see the prisoner myself, I won’t translate another word."
He wasn’t sure that native was still alive. He didn’t even know if the person who wrote the message was the same one who had transported the night caravan.
But the eavesdropping reaction and the change in the Rootspire commanders’ expressions showed that the matter was not unknown to the Cindari.
Kael was silent for a few seconds, then placed his fingers on the metal seal beside his neck.
A golden thread entered Rootspire from the seal.
He had probably sent an urgent report to someone inside the tower. A few seconds later, the seal’s light changed. He had received orders.
"Chains."
Four soldiers stepped forward, each holding part of the chains.
Lian didn’t resist. The first chain wrapped around his wrists.
The golden veins lit up and locked both hands in front of his body. The second chain wrapped around his right arm and shoulder.
Two more chains took hold of his chest, waist, and legs.
Mana pressure from the metal entered his body. His energy channels became heavy for a moment.
[External Mana Suppression Detected.]
[Skill Activation Efficiency Reduced by 46%.]
[High-output Mana Skills Temporarily Destabilized.]
Lian could have resisted the chains by releasing Cataclysm Pulse or the full power of Glacial Reaper Claw.
But he let all the locks be completed.
"Lian!" Seraphina stepped forward upon seeing the last chain locked.
Four spears blocked her path. The prismatic light on her sword grew more intense.
"Go see One." Lian looked at her without struggling.
This sentence only made Seraphina angrier.
"Your concern right now is One?"
"No. I’m not worried about anything."
"When you come out of there, you’ll answer to me before anyone else." She said with narrowed eyes.
"You should have let me come too." Seris looked at him without speaking for a few seconds, then said.
Lian nodded.
Seris was the only one who, instead of trying to stop the plan, was thinking about its next stage.
Still, she was even crazier and more illogical than Lian, and might do something stupid.
Besides, he didn’t plan to stay in the prison long and would be out soon.
"Move the prisoner. Temporary charges will be recorded." Then Kael said in a formal voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 287: Registered Prisoner
paragraphs: The military gate of the Rootspire closed behind Lian.
The sound of the massive plates colliding echoed in the narrow corridor, separating him from the last signs of the city.
The only thing still connecting Lian to the outside was One’s faint presence at the end of Hive Link.
The distance and dense layers between them had weakened the link, but it had not been severed. One’s dissatisfaction and worry remained like a vague pressure in the corner of his mind.
Lian, contrary to the situation, was completely calm.
Six Rootbound Wardens moved around him.
Two in front, two on the sides, and two behind.
Kael was also personally walking beside the group. He had placed his spear behind his back again, but his gaze turned toward Lian every few moments.
The commander still could not decide whether Lian was truly insane or if everything in the past few minutes had been planned from the start.
Probably the correct answer was a combination of both.
The military corridor had no obvious decorations, unlike the Rootspire’s main hall. The walls were made of compressed black roots, with wooden plates between them.
Red veins moved inside the root tissue, casting a faint light on the guards’ armor.
Heavy doors were placed at regular intervals on both sides of the corridor. Behind some, the sound of soldiers could be heard.
The Rootspire was not only Vhalaris’s center of government.
Part of it was a military fortress, a command center, and also a large underground prison.
Lian walked in silence.

The chains around his feet did not allow running, but they were not so short that he had to walk slowly. It seemed the Cindari had designed prisoner equipment so that transferring a dangerous individual was possible, without giving them freedom of movement.
After passing through two corridors, the group stopped in front of a circular door.
Two Rootbound Wardens placed their hands on the seals on both sides of the door.
The golden veins on their armor lit up.
Mana entered the metal plates, and the carved rings on the door began to rotate one after another.
The door opened with a heavy sound. A circular room was behind it.
Several metal rings hung from the ceiling, and golden roots had come out from the floor and connected to a transparent container in the room’s center.
Three Cindari were sitting behind semi-circular tables.
None of them wore full armor. They wore formal black and red clothes, and a special insignia was on their chests.
An older man in the center raised his gaze from a tablet in front of him.
His golden eyes first stopped on Kael and then on Lian’s chains.
"A new prisoner?"
"A High-Risk Outsider. Direct transfer order from Captain Thane." Kael answered.
The registration officer raised an eyebrow.
"The one who destroyed the central bridge?"
"Yes."
The man looked at Lian again. This time, more curiosity could be seen on his face.
"Guest Sigil."
One of the Wardens brought out Lian’s temporary insignia, which had been recorded earlier, and placed it inside the transparent container.
The container closed.
The golden roots around it began to move and touched the Guest Sigil from several directions.
For a moment, nothing happened.
Then a red light came out from inside the insignia and spread through the room.
The recorded images and information from the past few hours appeared one after another.
Entry through the First Root Gate, temporary registration at the Rootspire, receiving residence permission, moving to Ashfall Ward, and then the successive security alerts.
The registration officer placed his hand on a plate.
[Unauthorized Entry into Restricted Rootspire Territory.]
[Destruction of Civilian and Military Barriers.]
[Resisting Lawful Detainment.]
[Assault and Injury of Twenty-Seven Vhalaris Soldiers.]
[Direct Engagement with a Border Captain.]
[Threat Classification: High-Risk Outsider.]
[Additional Classification: Classified Intelligence Subject.]
The old man stared at the report for a few moments.
"Twenty-seven wounded." one of the younger officers beside him said under his breath and then pulled the screen up slightly.
"Not even one dead."
The room was silent for a moment.
The third officer examined the file.
"Three have fractures. Five have burns or damage. The rest have physical impact and superficial injuries."
"Was it accidental?" the old man looked at Kael.
"No." Kael answered without taking his eyes off Lian.
He was now sure. Lian could have killed at least a few soldiers the entire way.
On the first bridge, he could have thrown the soldier he had grabbed from a height.
In front of the second Barrier, he could have driven his fist directly into the guards’ bodies.
Even during the fight with Kael, there were several opportunities to deliver a fatal blow.
But he had chosen none of them. Everything had been done to reach the Rootspire and be registered as a dangerous prisoner, not to start a real war.
Of course, that was exactly the case. Lian had no plan to explain anything, but the reason for his actions was clear. If he had killed the soldiers, he might not have had any chance for negotiation.
The plan he had drawn up was based on negotiating with the Cindari, and he did not want to ruin all relations and cause enmity right now... not yet.
"No murder charges will be recorded." the registration officer said.
Kael nodded.
The old man did not take the Guest Sigil out of the container. The golden roots wrapped around it and sank the black insignia into their structure.
[Temporary Guest Status Revoked.]
[Prisoner Identity Registered.]
[Race: Call themselves Human.]
[Origin: Unknown.]
[Security Level: High.]
Then one of the officers brought out a small seal from a metal container.
The seal was hexagonal in shape, and golden lines moved on its surface.
He pointed at one of the Wardens.
"Keep the chains steady."
Two soldiers grabbed Lian’s shoulders. The officer came closer and placed the seal on the central lock of his chest chains.
Golden light quickly spread from the contact point, and new pressure entered Lian’s Mana channels.
[Secondary Suppression Seal Applied.]
[High-Output Skill Formation Further Destabilized.]
[Suppression Resistance Detected.]
[Seal Output Adjusted.]
Lian gave a brief look at the seal.
The previous chains had slowed his Skills, but this seal focused on the connection between his body and Mana.
The Cindari had considerable experience in restraining powerful individuals, and this made him curious about where that experience came from.
’It might have to do with the Ruined Realm natives. After all, they had entered this world in the past.’ He thought to himself.
There was probably certainty that conflicts had occurred between the natives of the two worlds, but if this was true, many questions would arise.
"The file is complete. Transfer responsibility for the interrogation section is with you." the registration officer said to Kael.
The circular door behind them closed.
This time, they headed toward an elevator at the end of a sloping corridor.
The elevator platform was made of metal rings and living roots. After the group entered, the roots gathered around it and formed a semi-open wall.
Kael touched the seal on the wall, and the platform began to descend.
The first level beneath the Rootspire still partially resembled the architecture of the upper sections. Orange lights, smooth walls, and doors with official insignias could be seen.
Ordinary prisoners were held on this level: thieves, city criminals, and those who had committed smaller crimes.
The sound of voices or movement could be heard from behind a few doors. The elevator passed without stopping.
On the second level, the light diminished.
The doors were thicker, and more veins moved on them. The guards on this level wore full armor, and their weapons were always ready.
This section was designed for Cindari warriors and criminals who had the ability to break ordinary prisons.
The third level was even heavier.
Black roots had replaced the smooth walls. Magical plates were placed in several layers between them, blocking Mana movement in the corridors.
The cells for military prisoners and dangerous individuals were probably located there.
But the elevator still did not stop.
The veins around the platform changed from orange to dark red.
The city’s orderly architecture gradually faded.
The roots became thicker, older, and more irregular. Some of them were so large that the elevator passed through their hollow tissue.
No floor name or official sign could be seen anywhere... as if they were heading to a part that officially did not exist...

chapters.title: Chapter 288: I’m Not Telling You Idiots Anything
paragraphs: The material of the walls deflected Mana, and various other protective layers became stronger the further they descended.
’I guess we’re going to a place where the most dangerous criminals are held... so does that mean I’m now considered a dangerous criminal too?’
’I guess my behavior was normal, though I don’t know if I should be proud of that or not.’ He quietly chuckled to himself.
He truly never thought he would end up in prison one day... and in a completely different world, by an unknown foreign race.
That was also a kind of honor...
"Why did you do such a thing?" Kael finally broke the silence.
"I just wanted to see my friends." Lian looked at the moving wall.
The commander stared at his face for a few seconds, expecting to see a sign of joking or mockery.
But this human’s expression was completely calm.
"You wounded twenty-seven soldiers and broke into the Rootspire for those three fugitives?"
Lian gave a small shrug, his chains making a short metallic sound.
"They’re good friends."
"One of them killed our soldier." Kael frowned.
Lian said nothing.
"Another murdered the city’s archivist."
Again, no answer came. He just turned his gaze back to the elevator wall.
Kael waited for a few moments. When he realized the conversation would not continue, he did not ask another question.
From his view, Lian had probably done such a crazy attack just to see his three companions.
This perception was useful for Lian’s plan.
The less Kael knew about his main goal, the less likely unwanted information would reach others.
The elevator finally stopped. The roots around the platform opened, and a short corridor was in front of them.
Of course, he didn’t know the truth, nor was he in a position to be told it.
Unlike the previous levels, no ordinary guards could be seen here. Only two Cindari in gray robes stood by a black door.
Their eyes glowed with a faint orange light.
Kael stepped forward, and one of the guards checked the seal on Lian’s chains.
Then he opened the door. The interrogation room was not large.
Its walls were made of polished black roots, and a few metal lines moved on their surface.
A heavy table was in the center, and two chairs were installed on both sides.
The chair facing the door was fixed to the floor, with rings for locking the chains on its arms.
A man was sitting behind the table. He was tall and thin.
His skin was grayer than most Cindari, and the veins on his face were dull orange instead of bright red.
His hair was short and black, with part of it turning gray on both sides of his head.
His right eye was amber.
But his left eye was behind a black lens. Very thin lines moved on the lens, and every time his gaze shifted, a small light lit up in its center.
It was clearly some kind of device.
This device could probably record changes in Mana, heart rate, body temperature, and involuntary reactions of the person in front of him.
The man was not wearing full armor.
He wore a long gray and black robe, and metal gloves covered both his hands.
Despite his unthreatening appearance, Predator’s Instincts gave a calm but continuous reaction.
His name was Tharos. He raised his gaze from a tablet in his hand, first examining Lian’s chains.
Then his eyes moved over the wound on his side and the battle marks on his armor.
"What is your name?"
"Lian."
"Lian?" He pronounced the name precisely.
"I am Tharos Keln. The head of all military and classified prisoners in the Rootspire."
"You may leave." Then he looked at Kael.
Kael did not move.
"The direct transfer order was for classified interrogation. I prefer to stay until—"
Tharos cut him off.
"From here on, the responsibility is with me."
His tone was not loud, but it left no room for argument.
The commander looked at Lian for a moment, probably still not trusting him and not wanting someone he had personally arrested to be interrogated without his presence.
Nevertheless, Tharos’s authority in this section of the prison was higher.
Kael finally signaled the guards to attach Lian’s chains to the chair.
The metal rings locked around the wrist and chest locks, then the commander turned to the door and, before leaving, looked at Lian one more time.
"Don’t do anything else foolish."
The door closed behind him.
The two guards also stayed outside.
Now only Lian and Tharos were in the room, and for a few seconds, neither spoke.
The black lens on the man’s eye adjusted with a very faint sound, and orange lines moved on it, fixing on Lian’s face.
"What do you know about that language?" He then asked directly.
"Don’t you want to interrogate me about my crimes?" Lian leaned back comfortably in his chair, not wanting to seem tense.
"Your crimes have been recorded."
"So I’m here for decoration?"
"Answer the question."
Lian examined him for a few seconds.
Tharos made no mention of the listening device. He did not ask where the metal piece was or how they had obtained it.
He had gone straight to the language.
So the matter of the native prisoner was more important to him than Lian’s infiltration of the Rootspire.
"We’re from the same world." Of course, that wasn’t entirely correct, but he didn’t have the patience and didn’t see the need to tell the truth.
A small change appeared on Tharos’s face. His eyebrow rose only a few millimeters. The black lens on his eye released a faint light.
"You and the prisoner?"
"Yes. My people’s language is different from his, but I know his language." Lian continued without pausing.
This claim was a calculated lie. He and the prisoner were not from the same world.
Earth and the Ruined Realm had no direct connection to each other.
But the Cindari had no way to verify this claim.
Unlike Earth’s Awakeners, they did not have a System that automatically translated unknown languages.
If the prisoner had refused to cooperate, the Cindari had probably been unable to understand his words.
Tharos tapped his metal fingers quietly on the table. The sound of the taps echoed in the room.
"Prove it."
"How?" Lian asked.
"You said you understand his language."
"I need to talk to him myself for you to understand."
Tharos said nothing. His eye lens flashed several times, as if examining Lian’s body reactions.
Then he stood up and left the room through a side door without explanation.
Lian was left alone.
Two listening devices were in the corners of the ceiling. This time, even without looking carefully, their presence was obvious.
Tharos did not want anything from the interrogation to remain unrecorded.
Lian also turned his head slightly, examining the chains attached to the chair.
Each was made of several links. The outer locks were opened with Mana from Tharos or the guards, but the center of the chains had a physical structure.
If he released all his physical strength and activated Iron Fortress for a moment, he could break the connections.
’This part of the prison definitely wasn’t built recently, but why was it built? For the Ruined Realm natives? Or for other creatures that belong here?’ He thought to himself.

Another thing that also seemed interesting to him now was that there were structures and units to protect the borders, as if the Cindari were worried that something might cross those borders and attack them.
Where did this worry come from?
A few minutes later, the door opened.
Tharos returned with a piece of gray stone.
The stone was different from the metal piece found. Its surface was smoother, and its edges showed it had been intentionally prepared for writing.
He placed it on the table in front of Lian. A few lines in that same old script were carved on the stone.
"Read it."
Lian fixed his gaze on the writing. The shape of the letters was familiar.
It was the same writing structure he expected, but this was the first time a complete sentence was placed before him.
At first glance, he only recognized a few words, and then the System reacted.
[Unknown Linguistic Structure Detected.]
[Translating...]
The letters shifted for a moment in his vision. Not that they really changed, but his mind received the concept behind them.
The sentence was short.
And its meaning made Lian stare at the stone for a few seconds. Then a sudden laugh escaped from his lips.
His laughter echoed in the cold interrogation room.
"What does it say?" Tharos frowned.
"It says: I’m not telling you idiots anything."
The prison head’s face turned cold. The orange veins on his face became slightly brighter.
"Are you sure?"
"Completely."
"Exactly that?"
"No threats, no requests. Just that he’s not telling you idiots anything."
Tharos picked up the stone and stared for a few seconds at the lines he had been unable to read for so long.
Apparently, the prisoner had written this sentence during one of the past interrogations, and the Cindari had imagined it contained important information, a location name, or even some kind of code.
But all this time, what they had carefully preserved was only a direct insult.
"It seems that bastard needs to learn a lesson." His tone was without shouting, but a cold violence was in it.
Lian moved his gaze from the stone to Tharos’s metal gloves.
This was probably not the first time the prison head had decided to "teach" a prisoner.
He still did not know the Ruined Realm native. He did not know what he had done, why he was arrested, or whether he was truly innocent.
But now he was almost sure the Cindari had spent years trying to extract information from him by force.
"From now on, you are our translator." Tharos put the stone aside.
"Excuse me?" Lian remained motionless for a few moments and then tilted his head slightly.
"You heard me." Tharos raised an eyebrow.
"I feel like I misheard." Lian continued with a calm tone and then added.
"Did you just speak to me in a commanding tone?"

And its meaning made Lian stare at the stone for a few seconds.
Then a sudden laugh escaped from his lips.
His laughter echoed in the cold interrogation room.
"What does it say?" Tharos frowned.
"It says: I’m not telling you idiots anything."
The prison head’s face turned cold.
The orange veins on his face became slightly brighter.
"Are you sure?"
"Completely."
"Exactly that?"
"No threats, no requests.
Just that he’s not telling you idiots anything."
Tharos picked up the stone and stared for a few seconds at the lines he had been unable to read for so long.
Apparently, the prisoner had written this sentence during one of the past interrogations, and the Cindari had imagined it contained important information, a location name, or even some kind of code.
But all this time, what they had carefully preserved was only a direct insult.
"It seems that bastard needs to learn a lesson." His tone was without shouting, but a cold violence was in it.
Lian moved his gaze from the stone to Tharos’s metal gloves.
This was probably not the first time the prison head had decided to "teach" a prisoner.
He still did not know the Ruined Realm native.
He did not know what he had done, why he was arrested, or whether he was truly innocent.
But now he was almost sure the Cindari had spent years trying to extract information from him by force.
"From now on, you are our translator." Tharos put the stone aside.
"Excuse me?" Lian remained motionless for a few moments and then tilted his head slightly.
"You heard me." Tharos raised an eyebrow.
"I feel like I misheard." Lian continued with a calm tone and then added.
"Did you just speak to me in a commanding tone?"

chapters.title: Chapter 289: A Translator’s Price
paragraphs: "You are a prisoner." The prison head said with anger.
"And?" Lian stood up despite the chains.
The rings attached to the chair were pulled. The golden veins on the chains became brighter, and the Suppression pressure increased in his body.
A heavy pain spread through his Mana channels, but his physical strength was not restricted.
The chair fixed to the floor trembled for a moment.
Tharos reached his hand toward the alert seal beside the table, but did not step back.
Lian looked at him with cold eyes.
"Even if there’s an army behind that door, before I die, I’ll make sure I take a lot of you bastards with me." He only allowed a small part of his presence’s pressure to leak out.
The room became heavy for a moment.
Since when did bastards who don’t even belong to the same world dare to speak to him in a commanding tone? And these stupid frogs?
The black lens on Tharos’s eye began to move faster.
Lian’s heartbeat was steady. His breathing had not changed. There was no sign of bluffing or trying to scare him.
He truly believed that if the Cindari tried to force him, he could kill a significant number of them before dying.
Of course, he had no doubt he could kill all of them.
"I don’t work for you. If translating doesn’t benefit me, I won’t open my mouth."
Tharos was silent for a few seconds. The light of his eye lens went out.
"You think you’re in a position to bargain?"
"I don’t think, I am bargaining." Lian answered.
"I can put you in a cell where you can’t even move your hand."
"You can."
"I can interrogate you every day."
"You can do that too, but you still don’t understand his language." Lian gave a faint smile.
A heavy silence formed between them. Tharos didn’t like being threatened.
More than that, he was dissatisfied that Lian actually had leverage.
But the matter of the prisoner was important enough that he couldn’t simply destroy a potential translator.
He finally took out a small device from his robe.
A black tool with an orange ring around its center. The prison head moved his finger over the device’s surface.
A thin strand came out of it and entered the wall. He sent a few short messages.
Lian sat down again. The chains loosened slightly, but their pressure remained.
A few minutes passed in silence.
Tharos sometimes received new messages. His expression became colder with each response.
Someone at a higher level was probably opposing giving concessions to a new prisoner, but the need for a translator ultimately overcame the opposition.
"What do you want?"
"I want to talk to my friends."
"Which ones?"
"The same three you arrested. Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian."
"Separately?" Tharos asked.
"Together."
"Gather four dangerous prisoners in one room?"
"If you’re not confident in your chains, that’s not my problem."
"Ten minutes." Tharos frowned.
"Twenty minutes."
"Ten.
"Then you have no translator." Lian leaned back in his chair.
The veins on Tharos’s face became brighter. Since when do prisoners even dare to negotiate, let alone bargain?
He wanted to explode with anger! But unfortunately, the circumstances didn’t allow it. They really needed a damn translator!
"Fifteen minutes."
"Accepted."
The prison head called the soldiers. The door opened, and two soldiers entered.
"Take him to meeting room three."
One of the guards unlocked the chains attached to the chair. Lian’s body chains remained, but he could move again.
"Every word you say will be recorded." Tharos said before leaving.

Lian looked at the ceiling listening devices. He didn’t care. These idiots don’t even know their language, and the only reason they understand what they’re saying is that the System translates for both sides.
If he tells the System not to translate, how are these idiots going to understand their language?
Lian was taken out of the room. The interrogation section corridor was completely silent, unlike the upper levels.
The doors had multiple seals, and the guards didn’t even speak when passing prisoners.
After two turns, they reached a rectangular door. The first guard placed his seal on it.
The door opened. The meeting room looked more like an empty cell.
Its walls were made of black anti-Mana plates. There were no windows.
Only a heavy metal table and four chairs were in the center. Each chair had rings for attaching chains.
Two visible listening devices were installed in the room’s corners. A small Artifact was also on the ceiling, probably recording images, sound, and Mana changes.
Lian sat on one of the chairs.
The guards did not attach his chains to the table’s rings.
After they left, the door closed.
A few minutes passed. During this time, Lian examined the room’s Mana flow.
The anti-Mana walls not only blocked Skills, but also weakened the World Memory Map’s connection to the environment.
Nevertheless, the Artifact had still recorded its entry path.
If he was forced to escape by force, at least he knew the way back to the elevator.
The sound of several locks opening was heard from behind the door.
Then the door opened. Four guards entered, and three prisoners moved among them.
Marcus was the first.
A dark bruise could be seen beside his jaw, and his left shoulder was wrapped with thick cloth. Despite the wounds, his gaze still moved over all the room’s details.
First the listening devices, then the guards’ positions, and finally Lian. His steps stopped at that same moment.
"Lian?"
Cassian entered behind him.
His face was paler than before. Bruise marks could be seen around his wrists and the lower part of his neck. He had probably endured a lot of pressure during interrogations or arrest.
But his expression was still calm. The moment he saw Lian, he lost control of his face for the first time.
His eyes widened slightly.
"What are you doing here?"
Ethan was the last.
His chains were thicker than the other two. An extra ring was around his neck, and three Suppression seals shone on his chest.
Anger could be seen in his entire posture.
When he saw Lian, he first looked at the two guards, and then at his chains.
"Don’t tell me Rindo sold you out too?"
Lian laughed.
Seeing all three alive, even in such a condition, was good news.
"I’m glad you’re safe." Then he gestured toward the chairs with a head movement.
"Sit down."
"That wasn’t an answer to my question." Ethan said.
"Sit first. Fight later." Marcus sat on a chair.
The guards attached all three of their chains to the table’s rings and then left the room. The door closed, and for a few seconds, the four just looked at each other.
"Where are Seraphina and the others?" Cassian was the first to ask.
"Outside the prison. Seraphina and Liana are fine."
"Thank God."
"How did you get to Vhalaris? Did you also appear in this forest?" Marcus asked curiously.
Lian first told them to turn off their translators and then gave a short and controlled version of their path.
"I appeared inside the Forest of Giants."
He talked about the first day and crossing the forest’s dangerous sections. He described the Giants’ Graveyard only as an area full of monsters.
Then he explained how they found the Glassthorn path and met Seraphina and Liana there.
Then they crossed the passage and encountered the Cindari at Emberroot’s border.
"You walked from the Forest of Giants to Glassthorn?" Marcus asked in disbelief.
"Not exactly. I found a good mount. Its name is One."
"Who is One?" Ethan frowned.
"An ant." Lian answered.
Ethan looked at him for a few moments.
"I think the chains have affected your brain." And Marcus added.
"If Liana and Seraphina made it safely, it doesn’t matter what they rode." Cassian said and then added.
"So almost the whole group is together, right?"
The room’s atmosphere became calmer for a moment, but Lian’s answer made it heavy again.
"Still no news of Selina."
None of them immediately said anything. Ethan took his gaze off the table. Marcus frowned. Cassian was silent for a few seconds and then said.
"I’m sure she’s fine."
There was no real certainty in the sentence.
No one could know where Selina had appeared or what creatures she had encountered.
But Cassian didn’t want the silence and worse possibilities to weigh on everyone’s minds.
"Now what do you want to do?" Ethan looked at Lian’s chains and gave a bitter laugh.
"You’re trapped here too, and it doesn’t seem like those bastards have any plan to free us."
"It doesn’t matter." Lian said calmly.
"What doesn’t matter?"
"A few hours from now, we’re getting out of here anyway."
All three looked at him at the same time.
"We?" Marcus asked.
"All four of us."
"How?" Cassian kept his gaze on Lian’s face.
"We’ll force our way out." Lian said very casually and randomly, as if talking about a normal topic.
Complete silence formed in the room.
"That’s your whole plan? A direct suicide? There are better and less painful ways to kill yourself." Ethan was the first to react.
