chapters.title: Chapter 290: Fifteen Minutes Is Done
paragraphs: "Getting out of here isn’t that hard." Lian shrugged. He didn’t understand why they were making it so difficult.
Of course, with a second thought, it was clear. They didn’t know his real power and didn’t know what he was capable of.
But he preferred not to say anything for now. He could show his power later through his actions.
"Our powers are limited." Marcus pointed at the black walls.
Then he raised his own chains.
"There are at least three seals on each of us. This level has dozens of guards, and we don’t even know which way the exit is."
"I do."
"How?" Cassian asked.
"Don’t worry. I have my own plan." Lian shrugged.
In truth, there was no precise multi-stage plan.
The World Memory Map had recorded the path.
The chains restricted his Skills, but his physical strength was still high enough to break one of the locks by finding the right point.
After freeing his hands, Glacial Reaper Claw or Cataclysm Pulse could destroy the rest of the seals.
Then he would have to free the other three, and then they would force their way out of the prison.
That was the extent of the plan.
Lian usually analyzed more details before entering danger, but this time, the simpler way was exactly what he had told Ethan.
Using power.
If Seris were here, she would love this plan. It’s exactly her style.
"You really don’t have any other plan, do you?" Marcus looked at his calm face.
"The result is what matters."
"It seems another madman has joined us." Ethan laughed with a laugh sadder than crying.
"Is there another reason you came here?" Cassian, unlike him, remained calm. He felt that seeing them was not the only reason this boy had come.
"If you only wanted to see us, you could have found a less risky way."
"You’re right. Before leaving, I need to see the person Marcus saw in the caravan." Lian said.
"That Human? We couldn’t find any information about him." He paused briefly and then added.
"Honestly, after everything that happened, I even thought maybe I was mistaken. It was dark, and the caravan was far away."
"You weren’t mistaken." Lian answered.
Then he explained about the metal piece.
He said there was only one word on it in the old Ruined Realm language.
Help.
The script was similar to the pillars of the Temple of the Divine of Light ruins.
The writer was not one of Earth’s Humans.
It was probably a native of the Ruined Realm who had been imprisoned and had hoped that one day his message would reach one of his own people.
All of them listened with focus. They didn’t expect to hear such things, especially that the person was probably a native of the Ruined Realm, which was beyond their expectations.
"So the person in the caravan was one of the Ruined Realm natives?"
"Most likely."
"Do you want to free him?"
"It depends." Lian answered.
"On what?"
"First, we need to talk to him."
"If these Cindari imprisoned him, that’s reason enough to free him." Ethan said.
Cassian gave him a brief look.
"He might actually be a criminal."
"It doesn’t matter."
"Maybe for you."
Ethan pointed at the guards behind the door.
"For me, anyone these bastards imprison is on our side for now."
Marcus frowned.
"God knows why they took one of the Ruined Realm natives."
Then he looked at Lian.
"What is he even doing here?"
"We’ll find out soon." Lian answered calmly and then turned his attention to Cassian.
"By the way, you didn’t kill that archivist, right?"
"Of course not." Cassian answered without the slightest pause.
"Tell me exactly what happened."
"We entered the Archive to find information about that same prisoner."
"No one was supposed to know we were there."
"I found the caravan’s route. Cassian also managed to find a way past two security checkpoints." Marcus said.
"Ethan was waiting outside the main path. I entered the archivist’s room to check the records of caravans and classified prisoners."
His face became colder.
"But when I arrived, the archivist was already on the ground."
"Dead?"
"Already." Cassian curled his fingers around the table’s edge.
"One of my daggers was inside his chest. One of the daggers I bought before entering the Special Area."
"The alarm was triggered right at that moment." Marcus said.
"The guards seemed to know exactly where to go. They didn’t check other paths or search for the real attacker. They went straight for us." Ethan continued with anger.
"So someone stole your dagger before you entered?" Lian said, but a question arose for him. How exactly?
Aren’t their weapons supposed to be in their Storage space? And as far as he knows, no one but themselves should have access to it.
"Well, during one of the battles in the first few days, its edge was damaged, so I gave it to Rindo to repair."
"Hmph, I say Rindo is a traitorous bastard, and you don’t believe me." Ethan said mockingly.
But everyone ignored him.
Someone had known about their plan. Someone had gained access to Cassian’s dagger.
They had killed the archivist before their entry and sent the guards exactly when Cassian was next to the body.
This plan would not have been possible without hearing those three’s decision, and Lian had a good understanding of how these fools had fallen into such a trap.
"Before you decided to secretly enter the Archive, where did you talk about it?" He then asked.
If his guess was correct, he had no doubt they had discussed the plan in the same office where he had found the listening device.
All three looked at each other for a moment.
Marcus frowned. Cassian’s expression changed.
He also immediately understood the connection between Lian’s question and the setup.
"We were inside—" Cassian opened his mouth.
But at that same moment, the door’s lock opened with a loud sound. The door moved to both sides.
Four soldiers entered.
Two went directly toward Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian.
"Meeting time is over." said the small officer standing in front.
Lian looked at the wall. Fifteen minutes were up. Time had passed sooner than he thought.
Of course, Lian was willing to bet that the prison head was extremely angry.
That fool had wanted to listen to their conversation to understand what they were talking about.
But he and the others, by turning off the translators, had made sure that none of their words were translated, and the Cindari couldn’t understand anything they said.
In fact, the prison head had shown good patience.
Lian had guessed that he might end the meeting time earlier than 15 minutes.
One of the soldiers grabbed the ring around his neck.
Cassian stood up.
Before the guards could take him out of the room, he gave a brief and meaningful look at Lian.
Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian were taken out of the room.
The door remained open for a few seconds, and the sound of their chains faded in the corridor. Then two soldiers stood beside Lian.
"Get up."
"Where?" Lian stood up without rushing.
"The prison head says it’s time for you to see that one." the first guard answered.

One of the daggers I bought before entering the Special Area."
"The alarm was triggered right at that moment." Marcus said.
"The guards seemed to know exactly where to go.
They didn’t check other paths or search for the real attacker.
They went straight for us." Ethan continued with anger.
"So someone stole your dagger before you entered?" Lian said, but a question arose for him.
How exactly?
Aren’t their weapons supposed to be in their Storage space?
And as far as he knows, no one but themselves should have access to it.
"Well, during one of the battles in the first few days, its edge was damaged, so I gave it to Rindo to repair."
"Hmph, I say Rindo is a traitorous bastard, and you don’t believe me." Ethan said mockingly.
But everyone ignored him.
Someone had known about their plan.
Someone had gained access to Cassian’s dagger.
They had killed the archivist before their entry and sent the guards exactly when Cassian was next to the body.
This plan would not have been possible without hearing those three’s decision, and Lian had a good understanding of how these fools had fallen into such a trap.
"Before you decided to secretly enter the Archive, where did you talk about it?" He then asked.
If his guess was correct, he had no doubt they had discussed the plan in the same office where he had found the listening device.
All three looked at each other for a moment.
Marcus frowned.
Cassian’s expression changed.
He also immediately understood the connection between Lian’s question and the setup.
"We were inside—" Cassian opened his mouth.
But at that same moment, the door’s lock opened with a loud sound.
The door moved to both sides.
Four soldiers entered.
Two went directly toward Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian.
"Meeting time is over." said the small officer standing in front.
Lian looked at the wall.
Fifteen minutes were up.
Time had passed sooner than he thought.
Of course, Lian was willing to bet that the prison head was extremely angry.
That fool had wanted to listen to their conversation to understand what they were talking about.
But he and the others, by turning off the translators, had made sure that none of their words were translated, and the Cindari couldn’t understand anything they said.
In fact, the prison head had shown good patience.
Lian had guessed that he might end the meeting time earlier than 15 minutes.
One of the soldiers grabbed the ring around his neck.
Cassian stood up.
Before the guards could take him out of the room, he gave a brief and meaningful look at Lian.
Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian were taken out of the room.
The door remained open for a few seconds, and the sound of their chains faded in the corridor.
Then two soldiers stood beside Lian.
"Get up."
"Where?" Lian stood up without rushing.
"The prison head says it’s time for you to see that one." the first guard answered.

chapters.title: Chapter 291: Human?
paragraphs: "Him?" Lian asked with a blank face.
"The prisoner you claimed to understand the language of."
The chains were checked again, and then he was taken out of the meeting room.
This time, the path was different from the route he had taken to enter.
Instead of returning to the main elevator, they passed through a narrow corridor behind an unmarked door.
Two other guards were waiting there, each wearing black armor with no Vhalaris insignia at all.
Neither the flaming root on their chests nor any military rank could be seen.
The first guard placed his hand seal on the door. A strand of orange energy entered it.
The door opened, and a smaller elevator was behind it.
Lian and the four guards entered, and the platform began to descend.
’So that person is so important to them that they’re protecting him in such a secure location? What did he do? Or... what does he know?’ He frowned.
A completely hidden elevator existed to take them even lower! This itself showed how strange the situation was.
The World Memory Map recorded a new line.
The path separated from the prison’s normal section and moved toward that same fourth line that extended from beneath the Rootspire into the roots’ depths.
They descended two more levels. At each level, the pressure increased.
The Suppression seals on Lian’s chains also reacted, becoming warmer.
The elevator stopped in front of the first gate. The guards had to activate three separate seals to pass through it.
After passing, the roots behind them twisted back together and closed the path.
The second gate required the Mana reaction of each guard. The third gate checked their heartbeat and blood flow.
The fourth gate only opened after sending a message to an unknown part of the Rootspire.
The fifth was made of pure metal and had no visible physical lock.
The lower they went, the more obvious the Cindari’s sensitivity became.
Multiple listening devices were on the walls.
Artifacts resembling black eyes were placed inside the roots, recording all movements.
Lian’s conversation with the prisoner would not only be heard, but probably every facial change, hand movement, and Mana fluctuation would also be stored.
This level did not exist on any public list.
Not even the prisoner’s name was recorded. Before the last checkpoint, one of the soldiers’ communication seals lit up.
Tharos’s voice came from it.
"You will not ask any questions about the prison’s location, the duration of detention, or the Rootspire’s structure."
"Then I’ll probably ask those questions first." Lian gave a faint smile.
The guard beside him placed his hand on his weapon, and Tharos’s voice became colder.
"You will translate every word."
"That wasn’t part of our agreement."
"If you don’t cooperate, the meeting ends."
"Then you’ll have to find another translator." Lian said lazily.
Tharos did not answer, and the seal went silent. The guards continued moving. The last gate was in front of them.
Unlike all the previous structures, this gate did not look new.
Behind the metal layers, dark stone with worn patterns could be seen. This stone did not belong to Vhalaris’s architecture.
It was even different from the Glassthorn ruins’ structure.
Perhaps the lower part of the Rootspire had existed long before the city was built.
The gate was closed with several separate locks.
Thick chains were stretched over its surface, and five Mana-suppression Artifacts were installed around it.
The guards stopped in front of it.
One activated the first seal. The sound of a metal lock opening echoed in the corridor.
The second seal went silent.
Then the third.
The chains on the door loosened one after another and fell to the ground.
The Suppression Artifacts released more intense light for a moment, and then their output decreased.
The thick door slowly moved aside. Cold, stagnant air came out of the cell. This cold contrasted with Emberroot’s natural heat.
The red light of the corridor entered the darkness behind the door.
Lian stood at the threshold. The cell was larger than he had expected, but it looked almost empty.
Chains from the ceiling and walls extended to its center, and someone was sitting among them.
His body could not be seen in the complete darkness, only the lines of chains on his arms and shoulders were visible.
After all the path Lian had traveled, he had finally reached the prisoner he was looking for: a native of the Ruined Realm who had lived here for years!
Four Cindari guards took positions around him. Two behind him and two at the cell’s entrance.
Their hands were near their weapons’ hilts, and their gazes did not separate from the darkness in front even for a moment.
The Mana Suppression chains were still around Lian’s wrists, arms, chest, and legs.
The golden seal installed on the central lock had weighed down his Mana channels and limited access to his storage space.
But the pressure of these restraints occupied only a small part of his attention at that moment.
Someone was sitting in the cell’s center. At first, only his silhouette could be seen.
Thick chains from the ceiling and walls were attached to his body. Some were wrapped around his wrists and ankles.
One of the chains was around his neck, and another from behind was directly connected to a metal seal on his spine.
As light entered, more details became clear.
A man who appeared to be in his thirties.
His long hair, a mixture of black and gray, had fallen to his shoulders and covered much of his face.
An unkempt beard had grown on his chin and cheeks. His body was extremely thin.
The bones of his shoulders and ribcage were visible under his skin, but even the weakness from years of imprisonment could not completely hide his past physical structure.
His arms were still muscular.
Old scars on his chest, neck, and stomach showed that before captivity, he had participated in real battles many times.
Several Suppression seals were carved directly into his skin.

Black and orange patterns extended from above his chest to his shoulders and the back of his neck. Every time the slightest Mana flow formed in his body, the seals would light up, and the chains would apply more pressure.
Nevertheless, something in him was still not broken. His head was down, but his posture did not resemble a defeated man.
More like a wounded animal that had been kept in a cage for years but had still not forgotten the first opportunity to tear the guards’ throats.
One of the Cindari struck the cell floor with the end of his spear.
"Raise your head."
The prisoner showed no reaction.
The guard raised his spear for the second time, but before he could strike, the man slowly raised his head.
His long hair moved away from his face. His eyes were dark gray.
Tired and worn, but still alive and alert.
His gaze first moved over the guards’ armor, then examined the chains bound around Lian’s body.
Finally, it fixed on his face. For a few seconds, he did not move. His expression gradually changed.
First doubt, then disbelief, and finally, a shock so deep that even years of imprisonment could not hide it.
His dry lips parted slightly.
"Human?"
The word was spoken in a language that for the Cindari guards was only a collection of unknown sounds.
But the moment it reached Lian’s ears, the System reacted. The concept of the word formed in his mind without the need for conscious translation.
[Ancient Ruined Realm Language Detected.]
[Contextual Translation Active.]
Lian said nothing. The chained man leaned forward slightly.
The ring around his neck stretched, and the seals on his chest glowed with orange light, but he didn’t even notice the pain.
His eyes remained fixed on Lian.
"I thought I was the only human left in this damn world." His voice was weak, but the tremor in it did not come from bodily weakness.
His chained hands moved slightly.
"How did you survive?"
"What did he say?" one of the guards turned to Lian.
Lian did not take his gaze off the prisoner. In those few sentences, he had understood something important.
This man did not imagine that Lian had come from another world. He had no knowledge of Earth.
For him, "human" only referred to the people of his own world. A world that, before being trapped in this Special Area, was probably the only home of the humans he knew.
This meant the Ruined Realm native thought Lian belonged to the Ruined Realm as well... and this was going to make things much easier for him.
An incomprehensible grin appeared on his face...

chapters.title: Chapter 292: The World is Dying?
paragraphs: And now, after years, the Ruined Realm native, upon seeing another human face, had naturally assumed that someone from his own people had finally entered the prison.
Lian could correct the misunderstanding.
He could explain about Earth, the Awakeners, and the arrival of a new generation of Outsiders.
But doing so would have no benefit... would he be foolish enough to do that?
This man had been under the Cindari’s interrogation. His trust in any creature that entered the cell with the guards must be almost zero.
But a human from his own world? Someone who had just come through the rift and understood his language?
That story could open closed doors that no torture had been able to unlock.
"I just arrived in this world." He answered after a few seconds of silence, in the same language.
The prisoner remained motionless for a moment, then slowly let out his breath, a long and heavy sigh that seemed to carry the weight of several years.
"The rift has opened again?"
Lian nodded. This answer was not a complete lie. The rift had indeed opened again.
The only difference was that the people who had passed through it were from a world he did not imagine.
"What did he say?" the guard asked again, with more seriousness in his tone.
"He’s asking who I am and how I entered this world." Lian answered without looking at him.
"And what did you tell him?"
"I told him I just arrived."
The guard exchanged a brief look with the soldier beside him.
The listening devices on the walls and the memory-recording Artifacts were recording the entire conversation, but none of the Cindari understood the meaning of the language.
As long as there was no other translator, they had to trust the translation that Lian chose to provide.
This was a major leverage point.
The prisoner examined Lian’s face more carefully, as if wanting to make sure he was really a human... not an illusion or any other trick the Cindari might have created.
"Which region are you from?" The man was still not completely convinced. "Region" was something only someone from his world would understand.
Lian paused for a moment, but chuckled inwardly. He had seen another native in the Ruined Realm before and had even interrogated him.
One of the names that remained in his memory was Third Region.
"Third Region." He answered without hesitation.
The change in the prisoner’s state was small but clear. His shoulders lowered slightly. His defensive gaze did not completely disappear, but part of the cynicism in it faded.
People from different regions probably shared a common language, but the way they expressed themselves, their words, and their tone were different.
"Third Region..."
The prisoner repeated these two words as if uttering the name of a place belonging to a very distant life.
Then a faint, worn smile formed on his face.
"So the regions haven’t fallen yet..."
Lian said nothing. In fact, what he heard was a little strange to him. This man must have been here for at most 25 years. Did he think that in 25 years, the seven regions might have fallen?
Of course, it wasn’t a wrong thought either. Given the state of the Ruined Realm, everything could turn upside down at any moment, and civilizations could fall.
"Don’t worry. If the rift has opened again, maybe the others will come to save us." The man continued, and something like hope could be heard in his voice.
Lian looked at his face. The man truly believed this possibility.
Despite all the years he had spent here and all the time he had spent in chains, part of his mind still expected that one day one of his people would find his messages and return to save him.
"Before I was captured, I scattered many stones throughout the forest."
"Many stones?" Lian’s eyebrows rose slightly.
"On each one, I wrote a request for help. Near old paths, ruins, rivers, and anywhere I thought one of our people might pass." His gaze went to the distance for a moment.
"Sooner or later, someone will find them."
Lian thought of the metal piece Marcus had found.
He had imagined that message was the only evidence the prisoner had been able to leave behind.
But apparently, more samples were hidden throughout the forest.
If other Awakeners found one of them, they might gain similar information.
Or maybe the Cindari had collected many of them over the years.
"My name is Aren."
"Lian."
Aren nodded.
"What did he say?" the guard by the door asked.
"He said his name."
"Anything else?"
"No."
The guard touched the communication seal by his neck. Tharos was probably watching the conversation from another room and waiting for a report.
Lian had to be careful. If his translations were too short or suspicious, they might end the meeting.
"Why did they imprison you?" He asked Aren.
Aren gave a brief look at the four Cindari around the cell and then lowered his voice.
"Because they think I know a way to open the rift."
"The rift to our own world?"
"Yes."
"They want to escape this world and enter ours." Aren looked at the chains around his wrists.
Lian was silent for a moment. Why would these fools want to do such a thing? Were they tired of their own world?
And more importantly... a short laugh escaped from his lips.
"Are they idiots?"
One of the guards frowned upon hearing his laugh, but since he didn’t understand the words, he didn’t interfere.
"They’re much weaker than our people. If they enter our world, they’ll be massacred."
This sentence, besides maintaining his cover, was consistent with his knowledge of the Ruined Realm.
The peak and ceiling of power in this world, compared to both Earth and the Ruined Realm, was extremely low.
The highest level of civilized and intelligent creatures barely reached level 35, and he doubted even that went higher.
Even monsters above that level are very rare in the two forests. Only in the Forest of Giants are the monsters strangely massive and powerful, which also has its own reasons.
"That’s true, but they don’t know that themselves." Aren said bitterly, and then his gaze fell on the guards. He was silent for a moment.
"And I don’t think they care anymore." His expression became more serious. The previous faint smile completely disappeared.
"Why?" Lian asked. He still didn’t understand and didn’t know why these fools wanted to enter their world.
"Because this world is dying."
This sentence made him focus more.
"Before I was captured, I spent a few years hiding in Emberroot and secretly gathering information." Aren continued.
"Did you know these creatures’ language?"
"Not at first." Aren laughed briefly with mockery.

"Their language is more damn complex than you think. Its written form is different from our language. Their words react to heat, and half of their terms don’t make sense without knowing their history."
"But I learned little by little."
"How much?"
"Enough to understand parts of their writings and the soldiers’ conversations." He looked at the guards again.
"Not enough to have a proper conversation with them."
This explained why the Cindari still needed a translator.
Aren might understand a limited number of their words and texts, but he either couldn’t speak fluently or had never intentionally revealed his knowledge.
"The tree they call the Forgotten Tree is drying up." He said.
Lian was shocked. The Forgotten Tree was drying up? That meant the heart of this world was dying.
"The Cindari are terrified of this."
"Only their leaders and high-ranking commanders talk about it directly, but its effects can be seen everywhere."
"What effects?"
"The number of soldiers they’ve sent to the borders."
"In the early years I was here, the borders weren’t guarded this heavily. Most of the forces were near the cities and trade routes."
"But in recent years, they’ve moved large groups to the paths between the three forests."
Lian thought of the military group that had surrounded them right after exiting the Cindervein Passage.
More than thirty soldiers, a commander, and ready watchtowers.
Perhaps their deployment was not only to prevent the entry of monsters or travelers.
The Cindari were waiting for something from the other forests’ side.
"As far as I understand, when the Forgotten Tree completely dries up, this world’s water cycle will be destroyed." Aren said.
Lian’s mind immediately went back to the Forest of Giants. Rivers whose flow was weaker than what the riverbed’s width suggested.
Dry lands, soil that was cracked in some areas.
Creatures fighting each other for water resources. At that time, all of these seemed like natural features or the result of the forest’s gradual destruction.
But if the water of the three forests was supplied by a shared structure, the drying of the Forgotten Tree could be the beginning of the collapse of the entire world’s natural cycle.
And as far as he knew, the Forgotten Tree was the world’s water supplier... and this tree was dying?
He now understood what was meant by this world dying.
"But the loss of water isn’t the worst part." Aren continued.
"What could be worse than that?" Lian kept his gaze on him. What could be worse than the water drying up?
However, his mind suddenly went in one direction... toward the contamination... the sitting giant.
Aren was silent for a few seconds, as if even saying information he himself had not fully understood was unpleasant.
"Something they call the carrier of the disease is awakening."
Lian’s mental movement stopped for a moment. The cells, the guards, and the quiet sound of the chains faded from his attention for a moment.
The image of a massive creature appeared in his mind.
The sitting Titan in the depths of the Giants’ Graveyard.
A body that had largely merged with the earth and roots, massive chains restricting his hands, shoulders, and body.
The Black Silence flowing in his depths, which could at any moment engulf the entire world again and cause another disaster...
It was being released...?

Despite all the years he had spent here and all the time he had spent in chains, part of his mind still expected that one day one of his people would find his messages and return to save him.
"Before I was captured, I scattered many stones throughout the forest."
"Many stones?" Lian’s eyebrows rose slightly.
"On each one, I wrote a request for help.
Near old paths, ruins, rivers, and anywhere I thought one of our people might pass." His gaze went to the distance for a moment.
"Sooner or later, someone will find them."
Lian thought of the metal piece Marcus had found.
He had imagined that message was the only evidence the prisoner had been able to leave behind.
But apparently, more samples were hidden throughout the forest.
If other Awakeners found one of them, they might gain similar information.
Or maybe the Cindari had collected many of them over the years.
"My name is Aren."
"Lian."
Aren nodded.
"What did he say?" the guard by the door asked.
"He said his name."
"Anything else?"
"No."
The guard touched the communication seal by his neck.
Tharos was probably watching the conversation from another room and waiting for a report.
Lian had to be careful.
If his translations were too short or suspicious, they might end the meeting.
"Why did they imprison you?" He asked Aren.
Aren gave a brief look at the four Cindari around the cell and then lowered his voice.
"Because they think I know a way to open the rift."
"The rift to our own world?"
"Yes."
"They want to escape this world and enter ours." Aren looked at the chains around his wrists.
Lian was silent for a moment.
Why would these fools want to do such a thing?
Were they tired of their own world?
And more importantly... a short laugh escaped from his lips.
"Are they idiots?"
One of the guards frowned upon hearing his laugh, but since he didn’t understand the words, he didn’t interfere.
"They’re much weaker than our people.
If they enter our world, they’ll be massacred."
This sentence, besides maintaining his cover, was consistent with his knowledge of the Ruined Realm.
The peak and ceiling of power in this world, compared to both Earth and the Ruined Realm, was extremely low.
The highest level of civilized and intelligent creatures barely reached level 35, and he doubted even that went higher.
Even monsters above that level are very rare in the two forests.
Only in the Forest of Giants are the monsters strangely massive and powerful, which also has its own reasons.
"That’s true, but they don’t know that themselves." Aren said bitterly, and then his gaze fell on the guards.
He was silent for a moment.
"And I don’t think they care anymore." His expression became more serious.
The previous faint smile completely disappeared.
"Why?" Lian asked.
He still didn’t understand and didn’t know why these fools wanted to enter their world.
"Because this world is dying."
This sentence made him focus more.
"Before I was captured, I spent a few years hiding in Emberroot and secretly gathering information." Aren continued.
"Did you know these creatures’ language?"
"Not at first." Aren laughed briefly with mockery.
"Their language is more damn complex than you think.
Its written form is different from our language.
Their words react to heat, and half of their terms don’t make sense without knowing their history."
"But I learned little by little."
"How much?"
"Enough to understand parts of their writings and the soldiers’ conversations." He looked at the guards again.
"Not enough to have a proper conversation with them."
This explained why the Cindari still needed a translator.
Aren might understand a limited number of their words and texts, but he either couldn’t speak fluently or had never intentionally revealed his knowledge.
"The tree they call the Forgotten Tree is drying up." He said.
Lian was shocked.
The Forgotten Tree was drying up?
That meant the heart of this world was dying.
"The Cindari are terrified of this."
"Only their leaders and high-ranking commanders talk about it directly, but its effects can be seen everywhere."
"What effects?"
"The number of soldiers they’ve sent to the borders."
"In the early years I was here, the borders weren’t guarded this heavily.
Most of the forces were near the cities and trade routes."
"But in recent years, they’ve moved large groups to the paths between the three forests."
Lian thought of the military group that had surrounded them right after exiting the Cindervein Passage.
More than thirty soldiers, a commander, and ready watchtowers.
Perhaps their deployment was not only to prevent the entry of monsters or travelers.
The Cindari were waiting for something from the other forests’ side.
"As far as I understand, when the Forgotten Tree completely dries up, this world’s water cycle will be destroyed." Aren said.
Lian’s mind immediately went back to the Forest of Giants.
Rivers whose flow was weaker than what the riverbed’s width suggested.
Dry lands, soil that was cracked in some areas.
Creatures fighting each other for water resources.
At that time, all of these seemed like natural features or the result of the forest’s gradual destruction.
But if the water of the three forests was supplied by a shared structure, the drying of the Forgotten Tree could be the beginning of the collapse of the entire world’s natural cycle.
And as far as he knew, the Forgotten Tree was the world’s water supplier... and this tree was dying?
He now understood what was meant by this world dying.
"But the loss of water isn’t the worst part." Aren continued.
"What could be worse than that?" Lian kept his gaze on him.
What could be worse than the water drying up?
However, his mind suddenly went in one direction... toward the contamination... the sitting giant.
Aren was silent for a few seconds, as if even saying information he himself had not fully understood was unpleasant.
"Something they call the carrier of the disease is awakening."
Lian’s mental movement stopped for a moment.
The cells, the guards, and the quiet sound of the chains faded from his attention for a moment.
The image of a massive creature appeared in his mind.
The sitting Titan in the depths of the Giants’ Graveyard.
A body that had largely merged with the earth and roots, massive chains restricting his hands, shoulders, and body.
The Black Silence flowing in his depths, which could at any moment engulf the entire world again and cause another disaster...
It was being released...?

chapters.title: Chapter 293: The Main Quest
paragraphs: Until that moment, Lian had assumed the awakening of that creature had begun after his and Seris’s entry.
They had killed the monsters around it, and blood had been spilled on the ground.
The blood and energy had been made available to the sitting giant, and that creature had reacted.
The chains had trembled. The Titan had shown a sign of awakening for the first time.
Lian had thought they were the main cause. Even the information and signs he had seen later had confirmed his reasoning.
But if the Forgotten Tree had been drying up for a long time...
If the world’s water cycle had been weakening for years...
If the chains were also connected to the power of that same tree and the world’s roots...
Then they had not started the Titan’s awakening. The process had begun long before.
He and Seris had only accelerated its speed for a short time by killing monsters and providing blood.
Even if they had never entered the Giants’ Graveyard, the Titan would still have opened its eyes sooner or later.
This situation was a disaster, a very great disaster... He now understood why the Cindari wanted to leave this world.
They neither had the ability nor the power to fight that giant, and if that giant awakened, the destruction of this world would be inevitable.
The power of that giant, according to the memories he had seen, at its peak was at least equal to an awakened one who had passed four evolutions.
"I don’t have complete information." Aren said, his voice pulling Lian out of his thoughts.
"I told you I barely learned their language. A large part of the writings are also encrypted or only accessible to high-ranking individuals."
"But I saw it several times in reports that when the tree dies, the disease will take over the entire world."
"What exact word did they use?" Lian asked.
Aren said a word in the Cindari language.
The System could not fully translate it, but a few concepts appeared in Lian’s mind.
Contamination.
Silence.
Spread.
Destruction of life.
No doubt remained. It was the same Black Silence.
"Some of their historical writings said that when the tree dies, the carrier of the disease awakens. I don’t know exactly what the disease is or what creature carries it." Aren continued.
But Lian knew. The disease was The Black Silence, and its carrier was the chained Titan.
At that same moment, a cold and emotionless voice echoed in his mind.
Not only for him.
A notification different from ordinary Quests was sent throughout the Special Area.
Every Awakener, in every forest, ruin, city, or dungeon they were in, received the same message.
[Hidden World Condition Discovered.]
He remained motionless. The blue light of the panel formed before his eyes.
[The Withering of the Forgotten Tree has reached a critical stage.]
[The restraints of the Corrupted Titan are collapsing.]
[Main Quest Issued.]
[Main Quest: Prevent the Awakening of the Corrupted Titan.]
[Objective: Stop the complete awakening of the Corrupted Titan before the Forgotten Tree dies.]
[Quest Participants: All Awakeners within the Special Area.]
The words appeared one after another, and then the reward section was displayed.
[Rewards:]
[200 Fragments.]
[+3 Levels.]
[250 Free Stat Points.]
[Return to Ruined Realm]
[Bonus rewards for awakened ones with the highest contribution.]
The reward was huge, much larger than any Quest he had seen until that moment.
Three full Levels, two hundred and fifty Stat Points, and 200 Fragments were only part of it.
The most important reward was considered to be leaving the Special Area. The System had finally announced the real path back.
But Lian was still not looking at the reward section. He was waiting for the failure penalty, and he had a guess about it too, a guess he hoped would not be correct.
The next line appeared.
[Failure Penalty: The Black Silence will gain access to Earth.]
For a few seconds, only that sentence remained before his eyes.
The Black Silence was not going to only devour this world.
If the Titan awakened completely, that disaster would find a way to Earth.
Lian’s mind began to analyze at high speed. The System had not brought hundreds of Awakeners into this Special Area without reason.
The main goal had never been just survival, hunting monsters, or finding opportunities to become stronger.
All of them had been brought in to prevent the Titan’s awakening. Perhaps the rift between worlds would open with the creature’s complete awakening.
Maybe The Black Silence had the ability to bypass the Special Area’s rules.
Or perhaps the Titan itself, as a contaminated creature, could break the path through which the Awakeners had entered, in reverse.
In any case, the result was the same. If they failed, Earth would face a disaster whose true power was still unknown.
Moreover, this disaster, whatever it is, has no clear way to be fought against or destroyed. Even this world’s heroes, by sacrificing themselves, could only seal it.
And now you’re telling me this damn thing is going to enter Earth?
"Damn it." Lian said under his breath. The situation was much, much worse than he had thought.
"Something wrong?" Aren furrowed his brows.
"No." Lian pushed the panel aside from his view. For now, he couldn’t do anything. He had to first listen to the rest of this native’s words.
And then find a way to get out of this city as soon as possible. He had to find a way to prevent that monster’s awakening.
If it awakened, they would have no chance!
"Tell me the rest." He then gestured briefly for him to continue.
"What did he say? Why did you pause?" one of the Cindari guards asked.
"He’s talking about the state of this world." Lian answered.
"What state?"
"He says resources are running out, and the Cindari are looking for a way out."
The guard frowned.
This translation was part of the truth, but it made no mention of the Forgotten Tree, the Titan, or the Main Quest.
If Tharos and the Rootspire commanders were really aware of the situation, they themselves knew what Aren was saying.
If they were unaware, Lian did not intend to be the first to gift them that information.
"These people think I know how to open the rift." Aren said, a bitter smile appearing on his face.
"If I knew a way, would I be here?" He raised the chains around his wrists.
"From our world’s perspective, I must have been trapped here for two hundred and fifty damn years."
"Excuse me, how many years?" Lian thought for a moment that he had misheard.
"Two hundred and fifty years."
"As far as I heard, each Cycle is twenty-five years." Lian frowned.
Aren was silent for a few seconds. His gaze changed, not in a suspicious way, but more like someone who had realized the person in front of him didn’t know obvious information.
"You don’t know?"
Lian gave no answer, and a bad feeling came over him. He felt this discussion was not going to end well.
The Ruined Realm native’s chain attached to his spine stretched, and his face contorted with pain for a moment.
"Twenty-five years have passed here, but in our world, two hundred and fifty years have passed."
"Time flows slower here. Every one year in this world equals ten years in our own world." Lian said nothing.
This information was even more unexpected than the Main Quest.
The Special Area was not only separated in space. Time also flowed at a different ratio there.
If Aren had spent twenty-five years in this world, two and a half centuries had passed in his original world.
Everyone he knew was probably dead. Their children were also dead. Perhaps even the governments, cities, and civilizations that were familiar to him had changed drastically.
That was exactly why he was happy when he found out the seven regions had not fallen yet.
Because two hundred and fifty damn years had passed!
The people who had entered the Special Area in the previous Cycle belonged to two hundred and fifty years ago in their own world.
Perhaps now they were only names in history books, or even completely forgotten.
But Aren was still talking hopefully about his stones being found and his people coming. All these years, he had been waiting for salvation from people whose generations had passed away.
"Are you sure?" Lian asked.
"Completely."
"When we entered, we didn’t know about the time difference. After comparing the dates we found in the ruins, Archives, and old writings, we understood."
"Every time, the rift opens for this world after twenty-five years, about two hundred and fifty years have passed in our world."

chapters.title: Chapter 294: The Previous Cycle
paragraphs: "So the ones who entered this time... ah, I must be your great-great-grandfather, maybe even older." Aren didn’t finish his sentence. He had probably just realized that Lian and his hypothetical companions came from a much later generation.
For this reason, not knowing some information or the difference in Lian’s accent could make more sense to him.

"This was one of the reasons we had never seen such a rift in our lives until that day. I mean, if it happened every 25 years, my father should have seen those rifts, right? But until that day, there was no other record of such a rift appearing."
He sighed.
"Then Third Region is probably no longer anything like what I remember."
Lian avoided answering. His mind was completely elsewhere right now.
Two hundred and fifty damn years?
That meant if he and the others spent one year here, it would be equivalent to ten years in their world! That number is insane! Equivalent to a whole generation!
His sense of urgency to leave this place multiplied several times. They had to complete the Quest as soon as possible and get out of this damn place.
Otherwise, if they wasted time, when they returned, Kain would have children and grandchildren! The tenth Ruined Realm might even have been fully cleansed.
Aren took the silence as confirmation and continued a few moments later.
"The Cindari thought for a long time that they could use the same rift we enter through."
"But the rift is one-way. When we enter, it closes behind us. No path remains to return." He gave a bitter laugh.
"We ourselves also realized it late."
"We thought we could return whenever we wanted... but we were badly mistaken." Aren lowered his gaze.
"When we entered, we imagined it was a long exploration. We would stay a few months, gather resources, and then return."
"But the rift closed behind us. No matter how hard we tried, we couldn’t find a way to open it."
Lian knew there were two ways to leave.
The Key.
Completing the Main Quest.
But the Quest was only for the Awakeners and his people. And the Key? He doubted the Ruined Realm natives knew anything about the Keys.
If they had known, they would have definitely tried to find it by any means and escape this small world.
"The Cindari waited for the next Cycle." Aren said.
"They thought when the rift opened again, they could enter from their side, but it doesn’t work that way." He looked at the guards.
"And the fools missed their chance again. Now they have to understand that there is no way for them to enter our world."
"Thank you for all the information. I need to share this with my companions, especially the matter of time flow in this world." Lian expressed his gratitude.
He had initially come to take advantage of this man and gather some information, but he had obtained much more than he had expected.
So much so that with this Ruined Realm native’s help, he had even been able to finally obtain the Main Quest.
Information that, if they hadn’t known, they would have surely been doomed... so a thank you in return for this information wasn’t too much.
"Besides you, how many others entered?
"Many." Lian answered.
"How many?"
"I don’t know the exact number." He truly didn’t know the exact number. He knew it was between dozens and at most a few hundred, it shouldn’t reach thousands.
"Where are they?" Aren asked with more anxiety.
"Some are scattered, but many are inside this same city. The Cindari have given them a section of the city to stay in while we’re here."
Aren just stared at him for a few seconds, then suddenly started laughing.
His laugh was weak, but it echoed in the cold cell. The guards looked at him with suspicion.
Of course, this laugh was not happy. It was a mixture of disbelief, mockery, and warning.
"These bastards gave you a place to stay?"
"Strange?" Lian asked.
Aren stopped laughing, his face became serious.
"With what we did to them, they should kill any Human they see on the spot."
"What did you do to them?" Another bad feeling came over Lian, and he felt he was about to get involved in another matter.
He lowered his gaze for a moment. His silence showed that the answer he wanted to give was not something he was proud of.
"In the first days we entered, we had nothing. We didn’t think the rift would close, and we hadn’t brought anything with us."
"Food was scarce. We had no Potions. There was no map, and none of us knew how to leave this world."
"Then we found the Cindari cities."
"And you attacked them." Lian said, rubbing his face. He could guess where this discussion was going.
He had no doubt that if Earth’s humans were in the same situation, they would have made exactly the same decision.
"Yes." Aren raised his head, his voice devoid of justification.
"We entered the border cities at night. We emptied their warehouses. We took Artifacts, Potions, weapons, maps, and any valuable item we could find."
One of the Cindari guards frowned upon hearing familiar words like Artifact and Potion, but didn’t understand the full meaning of the sentence.
"We thought maybe among their belongings there would be something that showed the way back."
"How many did you kill?" Lian asked. This was the main issue. A few Artifacts and food didn’t matter.
The question was whether these fools had started a massacre or not.
Aren was silent. The chain around his neck moved slightly with his deep breath.
"Many." He gave no number, nor tried to justify their actions as self-defense. His short answer was enough.
The humans of the previous Cycle were not innocent travelers who had been hunted by the Cindari.
They had also looted cities and killed many of their inhabitants. Perhaps some of them had no choice. Perhaps the Cindari had started the first attack.
But this truth didn’t change anything. A lot of blood had been spilled between the two races.
"At first, because we were together, they couldn’t fight back. Each of us was stronger than their ordinary soldiers, and we had Skills they didn’t recognize." Aren said and continued.
"But then we split up. To find a way out."
"There were three forests, and no one knew where the real path was."
"If we all stayed together, exploring the world would take years."
"We thought we didn’t have time."
"So you divided the groups, and the Cindari hunted you down one by one." Lian completed.
This was at least a decision he could understand, and it seemed logical, but it was a risky decision, and they should have created a defense mechanism for themselves before such a decision.
"Exactly." Aren gave a bitter smile. He leaned his head against the wall.
"When we split up, our numerical advantage was lost."
"They knew the forest better. They knew the secret paths, resources, cities, and monsters."
"They formed hunting groups and followed us from one area to the next."
"Every few months, news of another group’s death would arrive."
"When news of the first group’s death reached you, didn’t you think about what had happened and try to find a way to prevent it?" Lian Asked
He couldn’t understand these fools’ thought process.
After one or two groups died, they should have found a way to prevent more casualties by any means.
In an unknown world, having the advantage of numerical superiority was a huge advantage.
If they used it correctly, they could have conquered this entire world.
"Our communication was cut off. Some groups entered Glassthorn. Some chose the Forest of Giants, and the rest stayed in Emberroot."
"The distances were great, and the paths constantly changed. After a few years, I no longer knew who was alive."
For a moment, silence fell. Remembering those days was not easy for him. He had lost all his friends and companions.
Even he himself didn’t know how he had survived until today, and how much hardship he had endured to stay alive.
Remembering all those hellish days was not easy.
"One of us understood this world more than anyone else."
"He was a genius. Not the strongest member of the group, but no one analyzed as well as him."
"He traveled all three forests with a few others, recording paths, ruins, rivers, borders, and terrain changes for years." Aren continued.
"He even entered the Cindari Archives several times and stole information that no traveler could find from the outside."
"He was making a complete map." He moved his chained hand slightly, as if drawing an imaginary image in the air.

Two hundred and fifty damn years?
That meant if he and the others spent one year here, it would be equivalent to ten years in their world!
That number is insane!
Equivalent to a whole generation!
His sense of urgency to leave this place multiplied several times.
They had to complete the Quest as soon as possible and get out of this damn place.
Otherwise, if they wasted time, when they returned, Kain would have children and grandchildren!
The tenth Ruined Realm might even have been fully cleansed.
Aren took the silence as confirmation and continued a few moments later.
"The Cindari thought for a long time that they could use the same rift we enter through."
"But the rift is one-way.
When we enter, it closes behind us.
No path remains to return." He gave a bitter laugh.
"We ourselves also realized it late."
"We thought we could return whenever we wanted... but we were badly mistaken." Aren lowered his gaze.
"When we entered, we imagined it was a long exploration.
We would stay a few months, gather resources, and then return."
"But the rift closed behind us.
No matter how hard we tried, we couldn’t find a way to open it."
Lian knew there were two ways to leave.
The Key.
Completing the Main Quest.
But the Quest was only for the Awakeners and his people.
And the Key?
He doubted the Ruined Realm natives knew anything about the Keys.
If they had known, they would have definitely tried to find it by any means and escape this small world.
"The Cindari waited for the next Cycle." Aren said.
"They thought when the rift opened again, they could enter from their side, but it doesn’t work that way." He looked at the guards.
"And the fools missed their chance again.
Now they have to understand that there is no way for them to enter our world."
"Thank you for all the information.
I need to share this with my companions, especially the matter of time flow in this world." Lian expressed his gratitude.
He had initially come to take advantage of this man and gather some information, but he had obtained much more than he had expected.
So much so that with this Ruined Realm native’s help, he had even been able to finally obtain the Main Quest.
Information that, if they hadn’t known, they would have surely been doomed... so a thank you in return for this information wasn’t too much.
"Besides you, how many others entered?
"Many." Lian answered.
"How many?"
"I don’t know the exact number." He truly didn’t know the exact number.
He knew it was between dozens and at most a few hundred, it shouldn’t reach thousands.
"Where are they?" Aren asked with more anxiety.
"Some are scattered, but many are inside this same city.
The Cindari have given them a section of the city to stay in while we’re here."
Aren just stared at him for a few seconds, then suddenly started laughing.
His laugh was weak, but it echoed in the cold cell.
The guards looked at him with suspicion.
Of course, this laugh was not happy.
It was a mixture of disbelief, mockery, and warning.
"These bastards gave you a place to stay?"
"Strange?" Lian asked.
Aren stopped laughing, his face became serious.
"With what we did to them, they should kill any Human they see on the spot."
"What did you do to them?" Another bad feeling came over Lian, and he felt he was about to get involved in another matter.
He lowered his gaze for a moment.
His silence showed that the answer he wanted to give was not something he was proud of.
"In the first days we entered, we had nothing.
We didn’t think the rift would close, and we hadn’t brought anything with us."
"Food was scarce.
We had no Potions.
There was no map, and none of us knew how to leave this world."
"Then we found the Cindari cities."
"And you attacked them." Lian said, rubbing his face.
He could guess where this discussion was going.
He had no doubt that if Earth’s humans were in the same situation, they would have made exactly the same decision.
"Yes." Aren raised his head, his voice devoid of justification.
"We entered the border cities at night.
We emptied their warehouses.
We took Artifacts, Potions, weapons, maps, and any valuable item we could find."
One of the Cindari guards frowned upon hearing familiar words like Artifact and Potion, but didn’t understand the full meaning of the sentence.
"We thought maybe among their belongings there would be something that showed the way back."
"How many did you kill?" Lian asked.
This was the main issue.
A few Artifacts and food didn’t matter.
The question was whether these fools had started a massacre or not.
Aren was silent.
The chain around his neck moved slightly with his deep breath.
"Many." He gave no number, nor tried to justify their actions as self-defense.
His short answer was enough.
The humans of the previous Cycle were not innocent travelers who had been hunted by the Cindari.
They had also looted cities and killed many of their inhabitants.
Perhaps some of them had no choice.
Perhaps the Cindari had started the first attack.
But this truth didn’t change anything.
A lot of blood had been spilled between the two races.
"At first, because we were together, they couldn’t fight back.
Each of us was stronger than their ordinary soldiers, and we had Skills they didn’t recognize." Aren said and continued.
"But then we split up.
To find a way out."
"There were three forests, and no one knew where the real path was."
"If we all stayed together, exploring the world would take years."
"We thought we didn’t have time."
"So you divided the groups, and the Cindari hunted you down one by one." Lian completed.
This was at least a decision he could understand, and it seemed logical, but it was a risky decision, and they should have created a defense mechanism for themselves before such a decision.
"Exactly." Aren gave a bitter smile.
He leaned his head against the wall.
"When we split up, our numerical advantage was lost."
"They knew the forest better.
They knew the secret paths, resources, cities, and monsters."
"They formed hunting groups and followed us from one area to the next."
"Every few months, news of another group’s death would arrive."
"When news of the first group’s death reached you, didn’t you think about what had happened and try to find a way to prevent it?" Lian Asked
He couldn’t understand these fools’ thought process.
After one or two groups died, they should have found a way to prevent more casualties by any means.
In an unknown world, having the advantage of numerical superiority was a huge advantage.
If they used it correctly, they could have conquered this entire world.
"Our communication was cut off.
Some groups entered Glassthorn.
Some chose the Forest of Giants, and the rest stayed in Emberroot."
"The distances were great, and the paths constantly changed.
After a few years, I no longer knew who was alive."
For a moment, silence fell.
Remembering those days was not easy for him.
He had lost all his friends and companions.
Even he himself didn’t know how he had survived until today, and how much hardship he had endured to stay alive.
Remembering all those hellish days was not easy.
"One of us understood this world more than anyone else."
"He was a genius.
Not the strongest member of the group, but no one analyzed as well as him."
"He traveled all three forests with a few others, recording paths, ruins, rivers, borders, and terrain changes for years." Aren continued.
"He even entered the Cindari Archives several times and stole information that no traveler could find from the outside."
"He was making a complete map." He moved his chained hand slightly, as if drawing an imaginary image in the air.

chapters.title: Chapter 295: Another Emergency Quest
paragraphs: "A map that was supposed to connect this entire world."
"All three forests, secret paths, old routes between civilizations, passages, and anywhere important with valuable things."
Lian thought of the World Memory Map.
The map he had obtained from the three tribes, the map that was later combined with the A-rank Artifact, World Memory.
That map was probably made by this human from the previous Cycle.
That’s why there were details on it that even the current Cindari were unaware of. He had always been curious about who had made such a map.
He had guessed it was the work of a Ruined Realm native who had entered this world, because of the writing used on the map.
And now he finally heard the story behind it.
"I never saw the complete map. He disappeared near the end of his work. I thought he was killed, but they never found his body." Aren said.
"What happened to the map?" Lian asked.
"I don’t know. I only heard it was almost complete."
Lian kept this truth to himself. There was no need for Aren to know the map was now in his possession, and besides, that wasn’t important right now.
But the new information created a more important question.
If the humans of the previous Cycle had looted several Cindari cities and killed many of their people, Vhalaris’s current behavior made no sense.
Why hadn’t they killed the new humans at first sight? Why had they brought them to the city? Why had they given them Ashfall Ward?
Why had they allowed them to keep their weapons, form hunting groups, and become stronger by killing monsters?
Maelor could have disarmed all the Outsiders who entered Vhalaris on the first day.
But he hadn’t done so. Their outward behavior was hospitable.
But this hospitality, after a bloody past, couldn’t be from simple forgiveness.
The Cindari had a purpose.
Perhaps they knew that only humans could find a way out of this world.
Perhaps they were gathering the new humans to fight the Corrupted Titan.
Ashfall Ward might not be a shelter, but a place for gathering, controlling, and monitoring the Outsiders.
The listening device in Rindo’s building reinforced this possibility. They were monitoring the humans’ behavior, growth, and the information they found.
They might intend to first use the Awakeners to prevent the world’s destruction, and then take the secret of the rift or escape from them.
But there were also more arguments.
The Cindari might not be able to use the rift directly, but they might have found another way over these twenty-five years.
Perhaps that’s why they had kept the new humans alive.
Perhaps the presence of Awakeners, the Guest Sigils, Ashfall Ward, and all the seemingly peaceful behavior was part of a larger experiment.
The scope of the arguments was too large, and he had to understand what these bastards’ main goal was in giving shelter to the humans and what their true purpose was.
And this made the framing of his three friends even more annoying. What was their goal in doing this?
"Did the Cindari know about the new Cycle?" Lian asked Aren.
"Before my capture, they were waiting for it. All their calculations showed the rift should open again. Maybe that’s why they didn’t kill you. To use you. Maybe the fools think you know the way out."
This answer aligned with Lian’s thoughts. He had now obtained the main information.
The Forgotten Tree was on the verge of death.
The Corrupted Titan was awakening.
The Black Silence could enter Earth.
The Cindari had spent years trying to find a way to another world.
And their peaceful behavior toward the new humans was probably part of a larger plan.
Staying longer in the cell would only give Tharos time to examine the entire conversation and waste his own precious time.
After understanding that time here flows ten times slower, he realized how precious time was, and he had no intention of wasting even a second from this moment on.
Lian had to move before the Cindari decided he had obtained too much information.
He placed his chained hands on the ground and stood up. The rings were pulled with a heavy sound.
The golden veins of the Suppression seal became brighter, and the pressure in his Mana channels increased.
"What are you doing?" Aren raised his head in surprise.
Lian looked at the five layers of locks on the door. Four guards were standing outside the cell.
The memory-recording Artifacts on the walls were active. Tharos was probably watching all their movements from somewhere else.
"It’s time to leave this place."
"From here? Are you joking?" His expression showed he wasn’t sure if Lian was joking or had lost his mind.
"This is the lowest part of the Rootspire prison."
"I know."
"There are five gates between us and the main prison."
"I saw them."
Aren looked at his own chains and then at Lian’s chains.
"I’ve been trying to find a way to escape for a long time."
"You said you were waiting for someone to come and save you. Sorry I’m a little late." Lian turned his head toward him and gave a faint smile.
Aren really didn’t know what to answer.
At that same moment, the System reacted again. This time it wasn’t a global notification, and the panel only appeared before Lian.
[Emergency Quest Issued.]
Lian let out a quiet sigh.
When the System issued an Emergency Quest for a decision he hadn’t even begun to execute yet, it usually didn’t mean anything good.
[Quest: Escape Vhalaris.]
[Objective: Leave Vhalaris alive.]
[Optional Objective: Rescue the Prisoners of Rootspire.]
No name of Aren, Marcus, Ethan, or Cassian was mentioned. The System had placed all prisoners under one optional objective.
Then the main reward appeared.
[Rewards:]
[+1 Level.]
[10 Fragments.]
[50 Free Stat Points.]
The reward for an escape Quest was very high.
Especially a full Level up. For Lian, this was very important because with one Level up, he would exactly reach Level 20.
And upon reaching Level 20, he would finally receive his evolution Quest.
’So just by escaping this city, I can reach Level 20?’ He felt like the System was being too generous.
Of course, reaching Level 20 alone did not mean he could start and complete the evolution.
After reaching this level, he would obtain an Evolution Quest, which would only unlock the evolution option for him after completing it. Unfortunately, these types of Quests are time-limited.
That means if he doesn’t complete the Quest within the given time, he will lose the right to evolve... although there are ways to retry it, they are so difficult that they are not worth it.
Then the last line appeared.
[Failure Penalty: Death.]
He stared at the last word for a few seconds. The failure penalty was too clear.
Death.
The System had assessed the chance of leaving Vhalaris alive as so low that simply surviving was considered an Emergency Quest.
He took his gaze off the panel.
Five layers of seals on the door, guards behind the wall, Suppression chains on his Mana.
Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian on another level.
Aren with a weakened body and chains directly attached to his spine.
And the entire Vhalaris army above them.
Apparently, leaving Vhalaris was not going to be as simple as entering it had been.
