chapters.title: Chapter 296: The Escape Begins
paragraphs: For a few seconds, Aren just stared at Lian. At first, he thought Lian’s sentence was some kind of joke.
An inappropriate joke from a human he had only known for a few minutes.
But this man’s expression bore no resemblance to someone who intended to joke.

His eyes were still calm and indifferent, and even the Suppression chains that compressed the Mana inside his body with every movement had not been able to create the slightest sign of worry on his face.
Aren took his gaze off Lian’s face and looked around.
His own chains were attached to the wall and ceiling from four points. The black seals on his chest, shoulders, and the back of his neck glowed with a faint orange light.
Outside the cell, four Cindari guards stood with ready weapons.
Beyond them were five security gates.
Then the main prison.
Then the Rootspire’s military levels.
And finally, a city with thousands of soldiers.
"You said you want to leave this place?" He looked at Lian again. He didn’t want to believe that the human he had just met was literally insane.
But how else could he describe him? No other word came to his mind...
"Yeah."
Aren waited for a few moments, as if imagining Lian would give more explanation.
It was better not to judge too quickly... maybe this man really had an idea? A complete plan to escape or something like that.
"How?" When that didn’t happen, he asked.
Lian raised his chained hands.
The rings slid over each other with a heavy sound. The golden veins between the black metal lit up, and a faint pressure flowed through his Mana channels.
"By breaking everything in front of us."
"That’s the plan?"
"Yeah."
"Just that?"
"It’s worked so far." Lian shrugged.
If Seris were here, she would really be proud of him.
Aren stared at him with a look caught between disbelief and worry.
The man who had finally come to save him apparently had no secret path, exit Artifact, or complex plan.
He just wanted to break the doors, push the guards aside, and move straight from the lowest part of the Rootspire to outside Vhalaris.
For the first time, Aren considered the possibility that the human standing in front of him might be more dangerous than all the Cindari who had imprisoned him, or at least more insane.
Lian looked at his own chains.
Upon entering the cell, the guards had attached the extra part of his chains to a thick ring inside the wall.
They probably wanted to make sure that even approaching Aren wouldn’t be possible until the end of the meeting.
But after the conversation began, Lian had moved forward a few steps, and the guards had allowed the chain’s length to extend.
Now there was a short distance between him and the attachment point.
"Human? What do you think you’re doing?" A sudden voice echoed in the room. It was the guards’ voice. They couldn’t understand what this human was trying to do.
But Lian didn’t care. He pulled both his wrists apart. The golden veins on the chains immediately lit up.
The central seal on his chest reacted, and a heavy wave of pressure entered his Mana channels.
The pain rose from his wrists, passed through his arms, reached his shoulders and spine.
The skin under the metal rings quickly became hot, as if the chain intended to burn his flesh from the inside.
A System message appeared before him.
[Suppression Seal Output Increased.]
[Forced Resistance Detected.]
[Warning: Continued Resistance May Cause Mana Channel Damage.]
"Wait." Aren said immediately upon seeing the chains’ light.
Lian did not stop the pressure.
"Those chains get stronger with resistance. The more Mana you push in, the more pressure they return."
"I know."
"If you continue, your Mana channels will tear."
"Then they need to break before that." Lian gave him a brief look.
He took a deep breath.
He activated Diamond Skin. For a moment, the Skill didn’t respond.
The Suppression seal had made the Mana flow in his channels heavy and slowed the activation of any ability.
Lian pushed again. More Mana passed through the barrier of the chains.
A sharp pain formed in his chest, then the skin on his arms and shoulders became harder.
The muscles beneath them contracted, and faint gray veins of light appeared on his body.
[Diamond Skin Activated at Reduced Efficiency.]
Then he activated Iron Fortress.
This time, instead of spreading the defense over his entire body, he concentrated it on his shoulders, chest, and arms.
Heavy pressure formed around his upper body.
The air compressed for a moment. The chains were pulled with a loud sound.
The ring attached to the wall trembled.
The four guards outside the cell immediately noticed the movement.
"What the hell are you doing? Are you trying to break the chains? Are you insane?" One of them stepped forward.
"Stop resisting and get on your knees right now!"
Lian didn’t even look at him. He pulled both his hands in opposite directions. The golden veins on the chains lit up with more intensity.
The Suppression seal on his chest became like molten metal.
Blood came out from under the locked rings around his wrists and flowed over his fingers.
Aren looked at the chain’s attachment point.
"These chains were made for high-level prisoners. Even if your physical power isn’t restricted, you can’t—"
The sound of metal cracking echoed in the cell.
Aren fell silent.
One of the chain’s rings had deformed. Not enough to open, but the flat surface had bent under the pressure of Lian’s hands.
The guards raised their weapons. They had just realized that these chains seemed breakable!
But how? Was this human that powerful? No one had ever been able to do such a thing with these chains before!
"Final warning!" the commander shouted.
Lian applied pressure for the second time. This time, his target was not the chain itself.
He changed his body’s direction and applied all of Iron Fortress’s force to the attachment point.
The chain stretched, and the metal ring inside the wall resisted.
But the stone and old roots around it began to crack.
A thin crack spread from beside the base, and dust fell from the wall.
"Impossible..." Aren whispered in disbelief... what was he witnessing right now...?
Lian planted his right foot firmly on the ground. The muscles in his back and shoulders contracted.
With a short shout, he pulled the chain toward himself, and part of the wall exploded.
A large piece of old stone, black roots, and the metal base came out together. The broken piece fell on the cell floor with a heavy sound in the enclosed space.
The chain was still wrapped around his hands, shoulders, and chest, but it no longer connected him to the wall.
He dropped the stone piece hanging from the chain’s end.
"One less."
The guards didn’t wait for orders. All four attacked at the same time, the tips of their spears and the edges of their swords lighting up with red Mana.
They didn’t know what kind of monster they were facing, or what kind of monster had the ability to do such a thing.
But they couldn’t just wait for these chains to be destroyed and this monster to be freed!
"Get on your knees!" the group commander shouted loudly.
Lian grabbed the long chain attached to his right wrist. He had no intention of kneeling.
The first soldier came forward with a spear.
His movement was fast and direct. The weapon’s tip went toward Lian’s shoulder; a point that could disable his right arm’s muscles without killing him.
Lian stepped aside, swung the chain in the air, and the heavy iron rings moved like a metal whip, hitting the soldier’s side.
The impact sound echoed in the cell. The guard’s black armor dented, his body was lifted off the ground and slammed into the wall beside the entrance.
The armor prevented his bones from completely shattering, but the air in his lungs was forced out, and he fell to the ground.
The next two soldiers attacked from two directions. One blocked the direct path with a spear, and the other brought his sword from the side toward Lian’s neck.
Lian wrapped the chain around the spear’s shaft. With a sudden pull, he unbalanced the soldier.
The guard’s body was pulled toward him.
Lian brought his shoulder forward.
[Iron Fortress]
His reinforced shoulder hit the soldier’s chest center. Part of the armor cracked with a dry sound.
The guard was thrown back and collided with the sword-wielding soldier. Both fell on the ground, but the second one got up faster.
He moved his sword from low to high.
The blade reached Lian’s back.
Diamond Skin prevented deep penetration, but the heated edge passed over the skin’s surface, creating a bloody line from below his shoulder blade to his side.
He turned and grabbed the soldier’s wrist.
The man tried to free his hand, but Lian’s fingers were locked around his bone like a metal clamp.
The pressure increased, and the wrist joint made a short sound.
The sword fell from the guard’s hand. Before he could step back, Lian brought his head forward.
His forehead hit the soldier’s face, and the sound of the helmet’s nose guard breaking was heard.
The guard’s body went limp and fell to the ground. The last soldier stepped back. Terror had taken over his entire being.
They are not mindless monsters who can’t feel fear! And now, seeing a real monster in front of him... he was terrified.
He threw away all desire to fight and perform his duties... what did this damn prison have to do with him anyway?
Instead of attacking, he placed his hand on the red seal beside his armor.
Lian saw his movement, but the distance was too great to stop him.
The seal activated with intense light, and all the lights in the corridor and cell went out at that same moment.
Absolute darkness took over everything. At the same time, the sound of a deep bell rose from within the walls.
[Prison Breach Detected.]
[Classified Prisoner Containment Compromised.]
[Lower Rootspire Lockdown Initiated.]
The roots inside the walls began to tremble. The distant gates closed one after another.
"Damn it." Aren said in the darkness. He really felt like everything had been going too well.
But how was escaping from this hell supposed to be that easy?
Lian lazily looked around. He couldn’t see anything, but that wasn’t a problem... he activated Night Eyes.
The darkness gradually faded. The cell’s environment appeared before his eyes in shades of gray, faint green, and cold shadows.
Even the darkness was not going to stop him from leaving this place...

sentences.text: For a few seconds, Aren just stared at Lian.
At first, he thought Lian’s sentence was some kind of joke.
An inappropriate joke from a human he had only known for a few minutes.
But this man’s expression bore no resemblance to someone who intended to joke.

His eyes were still calm and indifferent, and even the Suppression chains that compressed the Mana inside his body with every movement had not been able to create the slightest sign of worry on his face.
Aren took his gaze off Lian’s face and looked around.
His own chains were attached to the wall and ceiling from four points.
The black seals on his chest, shoulders, and the back of his neck glowed with a faint orange light.
Outside the cell, four Cindari guards stood with ready weapons.
Beyond them were five security gates.
Then the main prison.
Then the Rootspire’s military levels.
And finally, a city with thousands of soldiers.
"You said you want to leave this place?" He looked at Lian again.
He didn’t want to believe that the human he had just met was literally insane.
But how else could he describe him?
No other word came to his mind...
"Yeah."
Aren waited for a few moments, as if imagining Lian would give more explanation.
It was better not to judge too quickly... maybe this man really had an idea?
A complete plan to escape or something like that.
"How?" When that didn’t happen, he asked.
Lian raised his chained hands.
The rings slid over each other with a heavy sound.
The golden veins between the black metal lit up, and a faint pressure flowed through his Mana channels.
"By breaking everything in front of us."
"That’s the plan?"
"Yeah."
"Just that?"
"It’s worked so far." Lian shrugged.
If Seris were here, she would really be proud of him.
Aren stared at him with a look caught between disbelief and worry.
The man who had finally come to save him apparently had no secret path, exit Artifact, or complex plan.
He just wanted to break the doors, push the guards aside, and move straight from the lowest part of the Rootspire to outside Vhalaris.
For the first time, Aren considered the possibility that the human standing in front of him might be more dangerous than all the Cindari who had imprisoned him, or at least more insane.
Lian looked at his own chains.
Upon entering the cell, the guards had attached the extra part of his chains to a thick ring inside the wall.
They probably wanted to make sure that even approaching Aren wouldn’t be possible until the end of the meeting.
But after the conversation began, Lian had moved forward a few steps, and the guards had allowed the chain’s length to extend.
Now there was a short distance between him and the attachment point.
"Human?
What do you think you’re doing?" A sudden voice echoed in the room.
It was the guards’ voice.
They couldn’t understand what this human was trying to do.
But Lian didn’t care.
He pulled both his wrists apart.
The golden veins on the chains immediately lit up.
The central seal on his chest reacted, and a heavy wave of pressure entered his Mana channels.
The pain rose from his wrists, passed through his arms, reached his shoulders and spine.
The skin under the metal rings quickly became hot, as if the chain intended to burn his flesh from the inside.
A System message appeared before him.
[Suppression Seal Output Increased.]
[Forced Resistance Detected.]
[Warning: Continued Resistance May Cause Mana Channel Damage.]
"Wait." Aren said immediately upon seeing the chains’ light.
Lian did not stop the pressure.
"Those chains get stronger with resistance.
The more Mana you push in, the more pressure they return."
"I know."
"If you continue, your Mana channels will tear."
"Then they need to break before that." Lian gave him a brief look.
He took a deep breath.
He activated Diamond Skin.
For a moment, the Skill didn’t respond.
The Suppression seal had made the Mana flow in his channels heavy and slowed the activation of any ability.
Lian pushed again.
More Mana passed through the barrier of the chains.
A sharp pain formed in his chest, then the skin on his arms and shoulders became harder.
The muscles beneath them contracted, and faint gray veins of light appeared on his body.
[Diamond Skin Activated at Reduced Efficiency.]
Then he activated Iron Fortress.
This time, instead of spreading the defense over his entire body, he concentrated it on his shoulders, chest, and arms.
Heavy pressure formed around his upper body.
The air compressed for a moment.
The chains were pulled with a loud sound.
The ring attached to the wall trembled.
The four guards outside the cell immediately noticed the movement.
"What the hell are you doing?
Are you trying to break the chains?
Are you insane?" One of them stepped forward.
"Stop resisting and get on your knees right now!"
Lian didn’t even look at him.
He pulled both his hands in opposite directions.
The golden veins on the chains lit up with more intensity.
The Suppression seal on his chest became like molten metal.
Blood came out from under the locked rings around his wrists and flowed over his fingers.
Aren looked at the chain’s attachment point.
"These chains were made for high-level prisoners.
Even if your physical power isn’t restricted, you can’t—"
The sound of metal cracking echoed in the cell.
Aren fell silent.
One of the chain’s rings had deformed.
Not enough to open, but the flat surface had bent under the pressure of Lian’s hands.
The guards raised their weapons.
They had just realized that these chains seemed breakable!
But how?
Was this human that powerful?
No one had ever been able to do such a thing with these chains before!
"Final warning!" the commander shouted.
Lian applied pressure for the second time.
This time, his target was not the chain itself.
He changed his body’s direction and applied all of Iron Fortress’s force to the attachment point.
The chain stretched, and the metal ring inside the wall resisted.
But the stone and old roots around it began to crack.
A thin crack spread from beside the base, and dust fell from the wall.
"Impossible..." Aren whispered in disbelief... what was he witnessing right now...?
Lian planted his right foot firmly on the ground.
The muscles in his back and shoulders contracted.
With a short shout, he pulled the chain toward himself, and part of the wall exploded.
A large piece of old stone, black roots, and the metal base came out together.
The broken piece fell on the cell floor with a heavy sound in the enclosed space.
The chain was still wrapped around his hands, shoulders, and chest, but it no longer connected him to the wall.
He dropped the stone piece hanging from the chain’s end.
"One less."
The guards didn’t wait for orders.
All four attacked at the same time, the tips of their spears and the edges of their swords lighting up with red Mana.
They didn’t know what kind of monster they were facing, or what kind of monster had the ability to do such a thing.
But they couldn’t just wait for these chains to be destroyed and this monster to be freed!
"Get on your knees!" the group commander shouted loudly.
Lian grabbed the long chain attached to his right wrist.
He had no intention of kneeling.
The first soldier came forward with a spear.
His movement was fast and direct.
The weapon’s tip went toward Lian’s shoulder; a point that could disable his right arm’s muscles without killing him.
Lian stepped aside, swung the chain in the air, and the heavy iron rings moved like a metal whip, hitting the soldier’s side.
The impact sound echoed in the cell.
The guard’s black armor dented, his body was lifted off the ground and slammed into the wall beside the entrance.
The armor prevented his bones from completely shattering, but the air in his lungs was forced out, and he fell to the ground.
The next two soldiers attacked from two directions.
One blocked the direct path with a spear, and the other brought his sword from the side toward Lian’s neck.
Lian wrapped the chain around the spear’s shaft.
With a sudden pull, he unbalanced the soldier.
The guard’s body was pulled toward him.
Lian brought his shoulder forward.
[Iron Fortress]
His reinforced shoulder hit the soldier’s chest center.
Part of the armor cracked with a dry sound.
The guard was thrown back and collided with the sword-wielding soldier.
Both fell on the ground, but the second one got up faster.
He moved his sword from low to high.
The blade reached Lian’s back.
Diamond Skin prevented deep penetration, but the heated edge passed over the skin’s surface, creating a bloody line from below his shoulder blade to his side.
He turned and grabbed the soldier’s wrist.
The man tried to free his hand, but Lian’s fingers were locked around his bone like a metal clamp.
The pressure increased, and the wrist joint made a short sound.
The sword fell from the guard’s hand.
Before he could step back, Lian brought his head forward.
His forehead hit the soldier’s face, and the sound of the helmet’s nose guard breaking was heard.
The guard’s body went limp and fell to the ground.
The last soldier stepped back.
Terror had taken over his entire being.
They are not mindless monsters who can’t feel fear!
And now, seeing a real monster in front of him... he was terrified.
He threw away all desire to fight and perform his duties... what did this damn prison have to do with him anyway?
Instead of attacking, he placed his hand on the red seal beside his armor.
Lian saw his movement, but the distance was too great to stop him.
The seal activated with intense light, and all the lights in the corridor and cell went out at that same moment.
Absolute darkness took over everything.
At the same time, the sound of a deep bell rose from within the walls.
[Prison Breach Detected.]
[Classified Prisoner Containment Compromised.]
[Lower Rootspire Lockdown Initiated.]
The roots inside the walls began to tremble.
The distant gates closed one after another.
"Damn it." Aren said in the darkness.
He really felt like everything had been going too well.
But how was escaping from this hell supposed to be that easy?
Lian lazily looked around.
He couldn’t see anything, but that wasn’t a problem... he activated Night Eyes.
The darkness gradually faded.
The cell’s environment appeared before his eyes in shades of gray, faint green, and cold shadows.
Even the darkness was not going to stop him from leaving this place...

chapters.title: Chapter 297: Breaking Everything
paragraphs: Lian saw the fourth guard.
The man was retreating toward the door, dragging one hand on the wall to find the exit path.
He covered the distance in two long steps. His hand closed around the guard’s throat. Before the man could make a sound, he was lifted off the ground.
His legs moved in the air... and terror had taken over his entire mind, disrupting his ability to think and decide.
"Where is the key to the chains?"
The guard tried to free his hand, but Lian’s finger pressure increased.
"There’s... no key..."
"Then how do they open?"
"The seal... Warden Keln..."
Lian looked at him for a few moments and then slammed the guard against the wall. The strike wasn’t strong enough to kill him, but it was enough to knock him unconscious.
The Cindari’s body fell to the ground.
"What happened?" Aren asked in the darkness.
"He said we need to find the prison head."
"You can see in the dark?"
"Yeah."
"Great, because I can’t see anything."
Lian turned toward him.
Night Eyes allowed him to examine the details of Aren’s chains in the darkness, but showed nothing beyond what could be seen with the eye.
Three main seals were directly on his body.
One on his chest, another behind his neck, and the third near his spine.
The chains attached to them extended like metal roots to the wall and ceiling.
"You can’t break my chains the same way." Aren said.
"Why?"
"Three seals are directly connected to my main Mana channels." He pointed at the marks on his body with a limited movement.
"If you destroy the seals, the Mana backflow will burn my body from the inside."
Lian looked at the chain connections.
"Then I won’t break the seals."
"You’re going to pull the bases out of the wall?" It took Aren a few seconds to understand.
"Yeah."
"This cell was built to hold powerful prisoners. The entire wall is reinforced with the Rootspire’s main roots, and I can’t endure pain like you." Aren gave a short, disbelieving laugh.
Lian wrapped his hand around the chain attached to the ceiling.
"Let’s see how well they built it."
He pulled the chain. The seals on Aren’s body immediately lit up.
Severe pain passed through his body. His jaw clenched, and his breath stopped for a moment.
"Slower, damn it!"
Lian stopped the pressure. Pulling directly transmitted too much force to Aren’s body.
He wrapped the chain around his own arm, then positioned himself so the pressure would be applied directly to the ceiling base instead of the prisoner’s body.
Iron Fortress was still active. He planted his feet firmly on the ground.
Then he pulled down with all his strength, and the sound of stone cracking was heard from above.
Dust spread in the dark space.
Aren lowered his head to keep particles out of his eyes. The metal base resisted, and the surrounding roots stretched.
Lian applied pressure a second time. The muscles in his arm contracted, and the chain trembled like a stretched wire.
This time, part of the ceiling collapsed. The metal base, along with a piece of stone and a few black roots, broke free.
The freed chain fell on the cell floor.
Aren looked at the stone piece hanging from it. Even in the darkness, disbelief could be heard in his voice.
"Your plan really is to break everything?"
"How many times do you need to ask?" Lian moved to the next connection.
The second base was inside the wall. He wrapped both hands around the chain and pulled.
This time, the wall showed more resistance.
He released the chain, stepped back a few steps, and instead of pulling, used the free end of his own chain like a hammer, striking around the base.
The first strike cracked the stone. The second broke part of the roots. On the third strike, the base loosened.
Lian grabbed Aren’s chain and pulled it out with all his force.
Another part of the wall collapsed. One after another, the ceiling and wall connections were broken.
A few minutes later, Aren still had the main chains and Suppression seals on his body, but he was no longer attached to the cell.
He placed both his hands on the ground and tried to stand up. It had been a while since he had stood properly, so it was a little difficult.
His muscles existed, but they were weak and stiff.
On the first attempt, his knees buckled, and his body fell toward the ground.
Aren lost his balance again at that same moment and had to grab the wall.
The sound of forces moving was heard from behind several gates.
The Rootspire was reacting to the escape. Lian placed one of Aren’s arms over his shoulder and pulled him up.
"Let me help you."
Aren did not object. He had probably realized himself that pride was only worth it if they got out of the prison alive.
A sound came from the eye-like Artifacts on the wall.
"Lian." Tharos’s voice echoed in the cell.
"Stop resisting right now."
Lian turned his head toward one of the Artifacts.
With Night Eyes, he could see a black, oval-shaped object on the wall with a very faint light coming from its center.
"No." He answered calmly, and a few seconds of silence followed.
"You are in the lowest part of the Rootspire. You are completely surrounded!" Tharos continued with the same cold calmness.
"I know."
"You have no way out."
"Then why are you so worried?" Lian leaned Aren against the wall near the entrance.
Tharos’s voice cut off for a moment and then played again.
"Release the classified prisoner and get on your knees."
"If you do, your punishment will only be limited to long-term imprisonment. A good offer?" Of course, he wasn’t actually going to give such a small punishment to this bastard.
He planned to torture this human himself every day for a whole year once he surrendered! Freedom? Impossible. This human would be their slave for the rest of his life!
"Enjoy your last moments. I’ll be coming to see you soon, Mr. Prison Head." Lian nodded calmly, then raised his hand and struck the Artifact with his fist.
The black object inside the wall shattered. Orange sparks scattered for a moment, and Tharos’s voice cut off.
His goal from the start had been to leave this place, and he had no interest in hearing offers.
He and Aren left the cell. The first security gate was completely closed.
Thick plates had been placed on top of each other, and living roots had filled all the gaps. Normally, opening it required several security seals and guard confirmation.
"How are you going to open it?" Aren looked at the gate.
"I won’t open it." Lian took the remaining chain around his hand.
"Then what?
He swung the chain in the air, and the heavy metal end struck the gate’s center. An explosion-like sound echoed in the corridor.
Only a small dent was created on the outer plate.
Lian raised the chain again. The second strike shook the surrounding roots, and dried leaves and black chips fell on the ground.
The third strike was deeper.
One of the plates bent slightly inward.
He really had to give credit to the material used. Breaking them was not easy.
"You’re going to go all the way like this?" Aren looked at the gate and then at Lian.
"Yeah."
"This method might work for one door. What about the next ones?"
"Then after this one, we’ll talk about the next."
He concentrated Iron Fortress over his entire body. Defensive pressure formed around his shoulders, chest, and legs.
Then he ran at full speed toward the gate and slammed his shoulder into the center of the metal plate.
The impact sound shook the entire corridor.
Aren was forced to place his hand on the wall to keep his balance. The gate bent in the middle, and the surrounding roots stretched and tore.
Lian stepped back a few steps, ran again, and the second strike broke the internal locks.
The plates separated from the frame and were thrown into the next corridor. A large cloud of dust, chips, and hot steam covered the space.
"One broken." He passed through the gap.
"Four more left."
"I know."
The second gate was thicker.
More roots moved around it and twisted defensively as Lian approached.
He placed his palm on the gate’s surface and activated Cataclysm Pulse.
The Suppression seal on his chest immediately reacted. Severe pain spread through his Mana channels.
Blood ran down from his nose, and the veins beside his temples bulged, but the Skill took form.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
The compressed wave entered directly.
The entire gate surface trembled inward for a moment, then the explosion occurred from the other side.
The plates separated from the frame and scattered in the corridor behind the gate.
The backlash pushed Lian back a step. A thin line of blood ran down from his right ear.
"Your body can’t take many of those strikes." Aren said.
He was really getting worried about this insane human. He didn’t want the most insane human he had ever seen to die here like this.
"Then I hope there aren’t many doors left. There should be three left, right?" Lian wiped the blood under his nose with the back of his hand.
The third gate had a different structure.
Living roots grew back as soon as a small part of its surface was broken, closing the gap.
Lian struck once with the chain. The roots split, but before the second strike, they reconnected.
"Interesting. This door regenerates itself." It seemed each door was built so that if another was destroyed, it could hold the attacker longer.
He raised his right hand. To activate Glacial Reaper Claw, he had to push more Mana through the seal’s barrier.
The chains around his chest became hot. Burning pain twisted through his body.
But ice gradually formed around his fingers.
[Glacial Reaper Claw.]

chapters.title: Chapter 298: The Final Gate
paragraphs: Lian placed the ice claw on the gate’s roots. The cold spread from the point of contact.
The roots moved to regenerate, but their moist tissue froze one after another. A white and transparent layer covered the entire door’s surface.
He stepped back and punched the center of the frozen structure.
The roots shattered like glass. Frozen pieces scattered on the ground. The metal plates behind them also came loose under the impact’s pressure.
’Finally opened. If it weren’t for these damn Suppression seals, they would have broken much sooner.’
The path opened.
"At least that one involved a little thinking." Aren, who was still holding part of his weight on the wall, said.
"I froze it and broke it." Lian shrugged. It wasn’t always about brute force. Sometimes you had to use your mind.
The fourth gate was much thicker than the previous three.
He struck it several times with the chain, but only a narrow gap formed between two plates.
He released the chain and inserted the fingers of both hands into the gap.
"What are you doing?" Aren asked upon seeing his movement.
"Opening it."
"With your hands?"
Lian didn’t answer. He planted both feet firmly on the ground and activated Iron Fortress once more.
He pulled his hands in opposite directions. The metal plates didn’t budge at first. The red veins on the door lit up, and the surrounding roots twisted tighter.
Lian increased the pressure. The muscles in his forearms bulged, and the wounded skin on his wrists split again, spilling blood on the black metal.
The plates trembled for a moment, and then the gap between them widened slightly.
Aren watched in disbelief.
Lian let out a short shout. The two plates separated, and the internal locks broke one after another.
The gap opened wide enough for one person to pass through.
He first pushed Aren through the gap, then entered the next corridor himself.
They had now passed four gates, and finally, only one remained.
The fifth gate was at the end of that same corridor, but before reaching it, the sound of heavy footsteps was heard from the opposite side.
A large number of soldiers were approaching.
"They’re here."
Lian picked up his chain from the ground. The lights were still off. The entire lower part of the Rootspire was in complete darkness.
For him, Night Eyes showed the corridor, walls, and objects clearly.
But the soldiers had to use the small flames on their armor and weapons to see.
Orange light appeared from behind the fifth gate. A few roots moved aside.
The gate opened, and twelve Rootbound Wardens entered the corridor. Large shields were in the front row.
Spearmen stood behind them, and four other warriors raised their flaming weapons.
"Return the prisoners to their cells!" the group commander shouted.
Lian sat Aren behind one of the broken plates of the fourth gate.
"Stay here." Without waiting for an answer, he entered the darkness.
The guards only heard the sound of a chain being dragged on the ground.
The commander raised his hand. One of the soldiers created a large flame on his spear’s tip, and the light illuminated the entire corridor for a moment.
But Lian was no longer in front of them. He had moved from the right side, near the wall.
The first Warden only noticed his presence when the chain wrapped around his leg.
The young Vorhelm pulled the chain. The soldier was lifted off the ground and fell face-first onto the corridor floor. Before he could raise his shield, Lian grabbed his body.
He lifted the heavy, armored Warden off the ground and then threw him like a human hammer at the two nearby soldiers.
All three hit the wall together. A spear came from the darkness toward his side, but Night Eyes allowed him to see its direction.
Lian moved his head and shoulder aside. The blade passed by his body. His hand closed around the spear’s shaft, pulled it, and the weapon’s owner came toward him.
Lian’s knee strike hit the soldier’s chest center.
His armor bent, and a muffled sound came from his throat. He fell to the ground.
The soldiers, with shouts, created more flames.
The corridor filled with orange light. Two waves of fire moved toward Lian from both sides.
He had an escape route. He could step back or take cover behind the wall.
But he didn’t. He kept Diamond Skin active.
He walked directly into the fire. The flames caught his clothes. Parts of his armor turned red, and the heat burned the skin on his face and hands.
But his steps didn’t stop. The soldiers standing behind the fire stepped back for a moment.
Lian’s silhouette emerged from the flame wave. The golden chains were still wrapped around his body.
Fire burned on his shoulders and back. Blood ran down from his nose, ears, and the wounds on his arms.
But his gaze remained cold.
"Is this really Human?" one of the Wardens said in disbelief.
"He’s different from all the humans we’ve seen before! Damn it, he’s like a monster!"
"Capturing him without harming him is impossible!"
"Commander, please give the order to kill! If we don’t kill him, we’ll be killed!"
Lian’s fist hit his helmet before the sentence ended. The metal dented, and the soldier fell unconscious on the ground.
The group commander took a broad sword with both hands. He activated his Skill, and a layer of compressed fire formed on the blade.
With a shout, he attacked. The strike came down from above, and Lian wrapped the chain around his forearm, placing his hand against the blade.
The sword hit the chain. Sparks and flames scattered in the corridor. The impact pressure bent Lian’s knee slightly.
But his hand didn’t lower. With his other hand, he grabbed the commander’s throat, slammed him against the wall.
The stone behind the man cracked, and then, without releasing him, he slammed him against the wall once more.
The commander’s eyes closed. His body remained motionless. He was dead.
The remaining soldiers hesitated for a moment. Terror had taken over their beings. They didn’t want to fight a monster.
And that moment was enough.
Lian entered among them. He swung the chain horizontally. Three Wardens were thrown back at the same time.
He picked up one of the spears from the ground and struck the fourth soldier’s knee with its blunt end.
The man lost his balance. The next strike hit the side of his head and knocked him unconscious.
The battle lasted less than two minutes, but when the last soldier fell on the ground, the corridor floor was covered with armor pieces, broken weapons, and unconscious bodies.
Aren came out from behind the door plate. His legs were still unsteady, but he moved using one of the fallen spears as a cane.
He said nothing. He had nothing to say. He didn’t even want to grumble anymore. Perhaps even he instinctively feared this fellow human of his.
Lian said nothing either. They passed through the fifth gate.
After a few short corridors, they reached the secret elevator, but before Lian could get close, several flames lit up in the space ahead.
Tharos stood in front of the elevator. Six Guards were on both sides of him.
But it was clear these were not ordinary soldiers. Their armor, unlike the Rootbound Wardens, was dark gray, and a layer of black ash-like mist moved around their bodies.
With just one look, Lian realized all six of them were Level 29. The strongest soldiers he had encountered so far.
The prison head dragged his long robe on the ground. The black lens on his left eye was lit with a narrow light.
The orange veins on his face had also intensified with anger. His gaze first fell on the unconscious and dead guards behind Lian.
Then he saw Aren, and the calm on his face completely shattered.
"What was all this for?"
"I’m going to get my friends and leave this place." Lian gathered the chains around his hands.
"Do you think I’ll let you reach the upper levels? If you don’t surrender right now, this will be your grave!" Tharos stepped forward.
"Of course, do you have any other choice?" Lian said with an indifference full of contempt.
"Human, I warned you!" The veins on Tharos’s face lit up. Black ash came out from his sleeves and around his robe.
The particles spread in the air, filling the corridor with the smell of burning and hot metal.
[Ashen Inquisitor.]
The Guards moved forward at the same time, and Tharos raised his hand.
The ash rushed toward Lian. Black particles settled on his skin, armor, and chains, and a burning pain began from the points of contact.
But that wasn’t their only effect. The ash entered his Mana channels, making the energy flow heavier.
Vague images formed at the corner of Lian’s vision.
Soldiers that didn’t exist. Walls moving toward him. Voices shouting his name from behind.
He understood. This prison head had the ability to create illusions and false pain.
The ash created hallucinations, weakness, and sensory disruption.
But unfortunately, this fool had chosen the wrong enemy today. The illusions of such a weak creature had no effect on him.
[True Sequence Anchor]
All the illusions disappeared, as if they had never existed.
Lian moved straight forward. Tharos closed his fingers. The central Suppression seal on the young Vorhelm’s chest lit up with intense light.
Unbearable pressure spread through his body. All his Mana channels contracted simultaneously.
Diamond Skin flickered off for a moment.
Iron Fortress trembled.
Lian’s knees bent. One of his feet hit the ground.
’Damn it! This seal is more annoying than I thought.’ The Suppression seals, although they couldn’t completely disable him, were enough to weaken him.
And it was slowly becoming more and more annoying.
"Lian!" Aren shouted in worry.
"Did you think that because you defeated a few ordinary soldiers, you could leave the Rootspire?" Tharos came closer. This time, it was he who spoke with contempt.
"I thought this damn thing was bothering me too much." Lian raised his head. Blood dripped from the corner of his lips.
He activated Cataclysm Pulse.
Not toward Tharos, not toward the guards, but directly into the lock on his chest.
The Suppression seal immediately reacted.
The pain he was about to feel was probably enough to make him wish for death... but nevertheless, the time had come to destroy the Suppression seal at any cost!

chapters.title: Chapter 299: No Method, Only Chaos
paragraphs: For a moment, he felt like something had exploded inside his chest.
Several Mana channels cracked. More blood came out of his mouth.
He felt like all the veins in his body were about to explode! The pain was so sudden and terrible that even describing it was impossible for him.
How the hell had these bastards made such powerful Suppression seals?
But Cataclysm Pulse passed through the lock’s center. The seal’s structure began to tremble.
"Stop him!" Tharos stepped back for the first time. A bad feeling came over him! A feeling that he had to stop this.
The Guards moved.
But it was too late. A golden explosion formed on Lian’s chest, and the central lock shattered.
Molten metal pieces scattered in the corridor. The chains around his chest, shoulders, and arms loosened.
Some fell on the ground. The secondary seals still remained on his wrists, but the main pressure was gone.
[Primary Mana Suppression Destroyed.]
[Skill Efficiency Restored to 81%.]
Tharos looked at the broken lock in disbelief.
How? How was it possible to break the seal? This had never happened before! This was unprecedented!
Lian immediately took out a healing potion from his storage space and drank it. All the pain and internal damage disappeared in an instant.
He sighed in relief. At that moment, he had felt like even his soul was trembling, but now was not the time to complain. There were more important things to do.
Then he activated Thunder Step.
This time, lightning formed around his body without serious delay. Blue light split the corridor’s darkness for a moment.
The sound of thunder exploded in the enclosed space.
Lian disappeared from in front of Tharos. A moment later, he appeared right in front of him.
The prison head didn’t have time to raise his hand. Lian’s chain-wrapped fist hit his face.
The black lens on Tharos’s left eye shattered, and the black glass scattered in the air. His body slid several meters on the ground and hit the wall.
The Guards attacked Lian. Two blades came toward him from two directions.
He took the first strike with his forearm. The chain around his hand prevented the blade from penetrating. The second strike cut his side.
Lian, without stepping back, slammed his shoulder into the first soldier and knocked him to the ground. Then he grabbed the second soldier by the collar and threw him toward the third Guard.
Tharos’s ash rose again, this time in the form of several black strands that wrapped around Lian’s arms and legs.
Severe pain formed in his muscles. The corridor’s image multiplied.
Five Tharos appeared in front of him, from five different directions.
But Lian didn’t care which one was real. He dispelled the illusions again and attacked directly into the middle of them.
Three images passed through his body. The fourth faded. The fifth was the real Tharos.
Lian hit his chest with his shoulder.
Tharos stepped back and placed his palm on his body.
[Ashen Brand.]
A black mark formed on Lian’s side. Flame and ash simultaneously penetrated his wounds.
The pain turned his vision white for a moment.
"This is my domain! Even if you’re a monster, you must surrender!" Tharos shouted.
"For now." Lian grabbed his throat.
The prison head suddenly felt terror and tried to release more ash.
But Lian lifted him off the ground and slammed him against the wall with all his strength. The black roots behind him cracked.
He slammed him a second time.
Blood came out of Tharos’s mouth. The remaining Guards attacked to save their leader.
Lian spun the prison head’s body and used him as a shield in front of himself. The soldiers were forced to stop their strikes.
He used this hesitation. He threw Tharos toward them, and all three fell on the ground together.
Lian landed on the first Guard. His fist strike to his helmet crushed his skull.
The second soldier tried to get up. Lian grabbed his wrist and twisted his arm behind his back.
With more pressure, his shoulder came out of its socket. His scream echoed in the corridor.
The third Guard stepped back and raised his weapon. Glacial Reaper Claw formed around Lian’s hand again.
The claw hit the soldier’s blade. White ice covered the entire weapon.
Lian punched the frozen surface. The sword shattered, and the next strike hit the soldier’s chest, throwing him against the wall.
Tharos tried to get up. Half of his face was covered in blood.
His eye lens was broken, and a deep wound had formed around it, but he had not yet lost consciousness.
Lian walked toward him.
The prison head gathered the ash and sent a black wave toward him.
Lian walked straight through it.
Pain.
Weakness.
Hallucinations.
All spread through his body, but none could stop his movement.
Every time Tharos pushed him back, Lian advanced again.
There was no trick, no calculated retreat, no searching for a weak point. Only a distance that had to be covered.
The power gap between them was so great that nothing could compensate for it.
When he reached Tharos, he closed his hand around his throat and lifted him off the ground again. The prison head’s legs moved in the air.
"Now I have an offer for you. You answer, and I let you live. Where are Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian?" Lian said calmly.
"Do you think I’ll tell you?" Tharos smiled with blood on his teeth.
Lian increased the pressure of his hand. The prison head’s body hit the wall, and the roots behind him cracked.
"Yes, you have no other choice."
Seconds passed. Tharos’s face became darker.
His hands closed around Lian’s arm, but he didn’t have the strength to free himself.
"If you kill him, we won’t be able to open the doors." Aren, using a spear as a cane, came closer.
"That’s why he’s still alive." Lian didn’t take his gaze off Tharos. After thinking, he began to apply pressure to his skull.
He would squeeze until it crushed. If he answered, good, and he would live. But if he didn’t answer, his skull would be crushed, and he would find his friends his own way.
"Third... level... western military section." The prison head, feeling the terrible pain in his skull that could shatter at any moment, finally answered.
"Which cell?" He reduced the pressure slightly.
"Cell five."
"How do we get there?"
"The elevator... behind me."
Lian didn’t release him. He unwrapped the broken chain around his hand and wrapped it around Tharos’s wrist.
He tied the other end to his own hand. The prison head was now a prisoner with them.
"Was this part of your plan too?" Aren said upon seeing the scene. He never thought he would live to see the famous prison head and torturer being dragged around like a slave.
Lian pulled Tharos toward the elevator.
"It is now."
Aren looked behind them for a moment.
The dead guards, the shattered gates, the black ash scattered in the corridor, and the prison head being dragged behind Lian.
"I think I’m slowly starting to understand your method, and I like it."
"There is no method. This madman just destroys everything! I assure you, sooner or later you’ll regret it!" Tharos said with anger.
Lian stood in the elevator.
The prison head was forced to place his hand seal on the elevator panel.
The orange veins activated, and the platform began to rise. At that same moment, a new alarm echoed throughout the Rootspire.
[Classified Prisoner Escaped.]
[Warden Tharos Compromised.]
[All Lower Levels Entering Execution Lockdown.]
Aren looked at Tharos.
"What does Execution Lockdown mean?"
"It means if they can’t recapture you, they’ll destroy the entire prison sections along with you." Tharos answered with a bloody smile.
The Ruined Realm native’s face changed.
"Then we need to be faster." Lian only said.
The elevator rose faster. Along the way, tremors could be felt inside the walls.
Parts of the Rootspire were beginning to change.
Corridors were closing. The main roots were contracting like massive muscles.
Mana was gathering inside the structure to seal or destroy the lowest levels.
The elevator stopped at the third level.
The door opened. Dozens of guards stood in the corridor ahead.
The front row had tall shields. Archers were positioned behind them.
Rootbound Wardens and a few Guards were also ready on both sides of the path.
Their commander hesitated for a moment upon seeing Tharos chained.
Lian leaned Aren against the wall inside the elevator, then looked at Tharos.
"Stay back."
"Are you going to defeat all of them alone?" Aren said.
"Still yes. At the same time, he’ll open those doors." Lian picked up the remaining chain from the ground and nodded toward Tharos.
"He’ll open those doors."
"Never." The prison head said with anger and gritted teeth.
The young Vorhelm pulled the chain around his wrist. Tharos was pulled forward.
"Then first I’ll separate your arm from your shoulder, and then I’ll place your own hand on the seals myself." Lian looked at his right hand.
Tharos stared at his face for a few seconds. His lie-detecting lens was broken.
But he didn’t need it. Lian’s expression showed he wasn’t joking.
"I’ll open the western door. Nothing more." And then he calmed himself and said.
"For now, that’s enough." Lian stepped out of the elevator.
"Release him right now!" the soldiers’ commander shouted.
"Come and get him." Lian wrapped the chain around his fist.
The shield line advanced, and the young Vorhelm also moved. His collision with the first shield was like the crash of two monsters.
Iron Fortress activated on his shoulder, and the shield bent.
The soldier behind it was thrown backward.
Lian entered the gap. He swung the chain from below, and the legs of two soldiers were lifted off the ground.
The archers released their arrows.
He picked up one of the fallen shields and held it in front of his body. The arrows hit its surface, creating small red explosions.
The shield cracked under the pressure. Lian threw it toward the archers.
The rear line scattered. A Rootbound Warden from the left attacked with a heavy axe.
Lian caught the strike with the chain. The axe and chain locked together for a moment.
He pulled the man toward himself and punched his stomach with his free fist.
The armor dented.
The Warden fell on his knee. The second strike hit the side of his head, and his body fell on the ground.
A wave of fire came from the right. Lian bent down on the ground, and the flame passed over his head.
He activated Thunder Step.
Blue lightning exploded among the soldiers. He appeared behind the first line. He wrapped the chain around two archers’ bodies and threw both of them together toward the wall.
Cassian, Marcus, and Ethan were located beyond these forces.
So Lian had no reason to stop. With every strike, a soldier fell, and with every step, the defensive line broke further.
Aren watched the scene from inside the elevator. Years ago, he had seen powerful people. Heroes from different regions. Warriors who could destroy cities.
But the monster in front of him... his method was very different from theirs...

Five Tharos appeared in front of him, from five different directions.
But Lian didn’t care which one was real.
He dispelled the illusions again and attacked directly into the middle of them.
Three images passed through his body.
The fourth faded.
The fifth was the real Tharos.
Lian hit his chest with his shoulder.
Tharos stepped back and placed his palm on his body.
[Ashen Brand.]
A black mark formed on Lian’s side.
Flame and ash simultaneously penetrated his wounds.
The pain turned his vision white for a moment.
"This is my domain!
Even if you’re a monster, you must surrender!" Tharos shouted.
"For now." Lian grabbed his throat.
The prison head suddenly felt terror and tried to release more ash.
But Lian lifted him off the ground and slammed him against the wall with all his strength.
The black roots behind him cracked.
He slammed him a second time.
Blood came out of Tharos’s mouth.
The remaining Guards attacked to save their leader.
Lian spun the prison head’s body and used him as a shield in front of himself.
The soldiers were forced to stop their strikes.
He used this hesitation.
He threw Tharos toward them, and all three fell on the ground together.
Lian landed on the first Guard.
His fist strike to his helmet crushed his skull.
The second soldier tried to get up.
Lian grabbed his wrist and twisted his arm behind his back.
With more pressure, his shoulder came out of its socket.
His scream echoed in the corridor.
The third Guard stepped back and raised his weapon.
Glacial Reaper Claw formed around Lian’s hand again.
The claw hit the soldier’s blade.
White ice covered the entire weapon.
Lian punched the frozen surface.
The sword shattered, and the next strike hit the soldier’s chest, throwing him against the wall.
Tharos tried to get up.
Half of his face was covered in blood.
His eye lens was broken, and a deep wound had formed around it, but he had not yet lost consciousness.
Lian walked toward him.
The prison head gathered the ash and sent a black wave toward him.
Lian walked straight through it.
Pain.
Weakness.
Hallucinations.
All spread through his body, but none could stop his movement.
Every time Tharos pushed him back, Lian advanced again.
There was no trick, no calculated retreat, no searching for a weak point.
Only a distance that had to be covered.
The power gap between them was so great that nothing could compensate for it.
When he reached Tharos, he closed his hand around his throat and lifted him off the ground again.
The prison head’s legs moved in the air.
"Now I have an offer for you.
You answer, and I let you live.
Where are Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian?" Lian said calmly.
"Do you think I’ll tell you?" Tharos smiled with blood on his teeth.
Lian increased the pressure of his hand.
The prison head’s body hit the wall, and the roots behind him cracked.
"Yes, you have no other choice."
Seconds passed.
Tharos’s face became darker.
His hands closed around Lian’s arm, but he didn’t have the strength to free himself.
"If you kill him, we won’t be able to open the doors." Aren, using a spear as a cane, came closer.
"That’s why he’s still alive." Lian didn’t take his gaze off Tharos.
After thinking, he began to apply pressure to his skull.
He would squeeze until it crushed.
If he answered, good, and he would live.
But if he didn’t answer, his skull would be crushed, and he would find his friends his own way.
"Third... level... western military section." The prison head, feeling the terrible pain in his skull that could shatter at any moment, finally answered.
"Which cell?" He reduced the pressure slightly.
"Cell five."
"How do we get there?"
"The elevator... behind me."
Lian didn’t release him.
He unwrapped the broken chain around his hand and wrapped it around Tharos’s wrist.
He tied the other end to his own hand.
The prison head was now a prisoner with them.
"Was this part of your plan too?" Aren said upon seeing the scene.
He never thought he would live to see the famous prison head and torturer being dragged around like a slave.
Lian pulled Tharos toward the elevator.
"It is now."
Aren looked behind them for a moment.
The dead guards, the shattered gates, the black ash scattered in the corridor, and the prison head being dragged behind Lian.
"I think I’m slowly starting to understand your method, and I like it."
"There is no method.
This madman just destroys everything!
I assure you, sooner or later you’ll regret it!" Tharos said with anger.
Lian stood in the elevator.
The prison head was forced to place his hand seal on the elevator panel.
The orange veins activated, and the platform began to rise.
At that same moment, a new alarm echoed throughout the Rootspire.
[Classified Prisoner Escaped.]
[Warden Tharos Compromised.]
[All Lower Levels Entering Execution Lockdown.]
Aren looked at Tharos.
"What does Execution Lockdown mean?"
"It means if they can’t recapture you, they’ll destroy the entire prison sections along with you." Tharos answered with a bloody smile.
The Ruined Realm native’s face changed.
"Then we need to be faster." Lian only said.
The elevator rose faster.
Along the way, tremors could be felt inside the walls.
Parts of the Rootspire were beginning to change.
Corridors were closing.
The main roots were contracting like massive muscles.
Mana was gathering inside the structure to seal or destroy the lowest levels.
The elevator stopped at the third level.
The door opened.
Dozens of guards stood in the corridor ahead.
The front row had tall shields.
Archers were positioned behind them.
Rootbound Wardens and a few Guards were also ready on both sides of the path.
Their commander hesitated for a moment upon seeing Tharos chained.
Lian leaned Aren against the wall inside the elevator, then looked at Tharos.
"Stay back."
"Are you going to defeat all of them alone?" Aren said.
"Still yes.
At the same time, he’ll open those doors." Lian picked up the remaining chain from the ground and nodded toward Tharos.
"He’ll open those doors."
"Never." The prison head said with anger and gritted teeth.
The young Vorhelm pulled the chain around his wrist.
Tharos was pulled forward.
"Then first I’ll separate your arm from your shoulder, and then I’ll place your own hand on the seals myself." Lian looked at his right hand.
Tharos stared at his face for a few seconds.
His lie-detecting lens was broken.
But he didn’t need it.
Lian’s expression showed he wasn’t joking.
"I’ll open the western door.
Nothing more." And then he calmed himself and said.
"For now, that’s enough." Lian stepped out of the elevator.
"Release him right now!" the soldiers’ commander shouted.
"Come and get him." Lian wrapped the chain around his fist.
The shield line advanced, and the young Vorhelm also moved.
His collision with the first shield was like the crash of two monsters.
Iron Fortress activated on his shoulder, and the shield bent.
The soldier behind it was thrown backward.
Lian entered the gap.
He swung the chain from below, and the legs of two soldiers were lifted off the ground.
The archers released their arrows.
He picked up one of the fallen shields and held it in front of his body.
The arrows hit its surface, creating small red explosions.
The shield cracked under the pressure.
Lian threw it toward the archers.
The rear line scattered.
A Rootbound Warden from the left attacked with a heavy axe.
Lian caught the strike with the chain.
The axe and chain locked together for a moment.
He pulled the man toward himself and punched his stomach with his free fist.
The armor dented.
The Warden fell on his knee.
The second strike hit the side of his head, and his body fell on the ground.
A wave of fire came from the right.
Lian bent down on the ground, and the flame passed over his head.
He activated Thunder Step.
Blue lightning exploded among the soldiers.
He appeared behind the first line.
He wrapped the chain around two archers’ bodies and threw both of them together toward the wall.
Cassian, Marcus, and Ethan were located beyond these forces.
So Lian had no reason to stop.
With every strike, a soldier fell, and with every step, the defensive line broke further.
Aren watched the scene from inside the elevator.
Years ago, he had seen powerful people.
Heroes from different regions.
Warriors who could destroy cities.
But the monster in front of him... his method was very different from theirs...

chapters.title: Chapter 300: No Plan, Only Forward
paragraphs: But Lian’s method was different. He didn’t fight like someone who intended to show off his Skills.
Every move was only for moving forward. If a shield blocked the path, he would push both the shield and its owner aside, sending them straight to the world after death.
If there was fire in the way, he would walk through it. If the number of enemies was large, he would throw the strongest one at the rest.
In the simplest sense, he would destroy as much as needed until he reached his goal, and this made Aren’s body shiver.
Aren thought to himself, had the way of fighting in his world changed during the time he had been in this world?
A few minutes later, the corridor was filled with dead guards.
Lian reached the last gate. The cell’s marker was on the wall beside it.
"Open it." He pulled Tharos forward.
The prison head still resisted. He understood that all ways to stop this monster were closed, and his escape was imminent.
He still wanted to try to buy time for more forces to arrive.
But Lian pulled the chain tighter, and the prison head angrily placed his hand on the seal.
The outer gate opened. Behind it was another short corridor.
Three cells could be seen at its end.
Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian were being held in a shared cell; probably after the meeting, they had been temporarily placed together to prepare for transfer or further interrogation.
Lian approached the cell. Inside, all three were ready for a fight upon hearing the alarms.
Ethan had wrapped his chains around his forearm.
Marcus stood by the door, and Cassian was a little further back, examining the situation.
When the corridor gate moved aside, all three expected a group of guards to enter.
But first they saw Lian. Blood had dried on his face, side, and wrists.
Broken chains were wrapped around his hands. Behind him, Aren stood with a weak body, and Tharos, wounded and chained, was being dragged on the ground.
Ethan just looked for a few seconds.
"So when you said what your plan was, you weren’t joking, were you?" He then asked.
"No."
Cassian looked through the bars at the corridor behind him. Dozens of guards’ bodies lay on the ground.
Parts of the wall were burned or broken.
"But you said you had a plan."
"I do." Lian pushed Tharos against the cell’s seal.
"What is the plan?" Marcus asked.
"We go out through the main gate." And then he pushed Tharos toward the door with his foot.
A few seconds of silence followed.
Marcus looked at Cassian.
Cassian looked at Lian.
Ethan suddenly started laughing, his laugh echoing in the prison corridor.
"So your plan really was just force?"
"Yeah." Lian looked at their chains’ seals.
Ethan was still laughing.
"Finally, someone crazier than me has appeared."
"This isn’t funny." Cassian said under his breath.
"A little bit." Marcus added.
"Open them." Lian pulled the chain around Tharos’s neck.
"If I open these seals, we’ll all die."
"If you don’t open them, you’ll die sooner."
Tharos looked into Lian’s eyes, then placed his bloody hand on the cell’s seal.
The first lock opened, and the gate moved aside. Then he was forced to deactivate the Suppression seals on Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian one by one.
Marcus’s chains opened. He moved his wounded shoulder and endured the pain.
After being freed, Cassian quickly checked the fallen guards’ weapons and equipment.
Ethan immediately picked up one of the heavy Cindari swords.
When the last chain was opened, the entire Rootspire shook.
Not a small tremor. The entire floor, walls, and ceiling moved like the body of a massive creature.
The red veins inside the roots changed to a glowing white.
The corridor’s heat rose. A deep and powerful voice spread from all the walls.
"All gates of Vhalaris have been closed." Maelor’s voice.
The glowing veins on the walls pulsed.
"The bridges have been cut."
"All military units have entered siege status." His voice became colder.
"No one will leave this city."
For a moment, silence fell among the group, and everyone looked at each other’s condition.
The sentences they just heard made them understand that the situation was probably worse than they thought, and escape was not going to be easy.
And then everyone’s gaze fell on the group’s thinker.
"Now what?" Cassian asked.
Lian raised his head. Between them and the exit from Vhalaris were the Rootspire’s levels, hundreds of soldiers, Rootbound Wardens, city commanders, Kael, and Maelor.
He wrapped the broken chain tighter around his fist.
"Now we go to the others."
He had no plan to get through Vhalaris’s army. But as long as his fists moved, he didn’t need a plan either.
And then they walked.
The sound of the Rootspire’s alarms could still be heard behind them.
The red veins inside the massive tower’s trunk pulsed with a fast rhythm, spreading the warning light through the surrounding streets.
The military gates were closing one after another, and groups of soldiers were moving from the main paths toward the city center.
But contrary to what Vhalaris’s commanders expected, the escapees had not headed toward the exit gates.
After freeing Marcus, Ethan, and Cassian, Lian had used Tharos to pass through the last security sections.
The prison head was valuable to them as long as his seals could open doors and elevators.
When they reached the service corridor near the city’s surface, Cassian had removed one of the security seals from Tharos’s belt and chained the prison head to the wall with his own chains.
Ethan had suggested breaking his neck so he couldn’t guide the forces, but Marcus had disagreed.
Tharos was now alive, wounded, and angry, left in one of the Rootspire’s service rooms.
This action had probably only bought them a few minutes, but those few minutes were enough to leave the tower.
Now Lian, Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and Aren were passing through one of Vhalaris’s side streets.
"Are we really going to the first place they’d look for us?" Marcus felt he had to ask this question.
"Everyone is there."
"I know that. The Cindari also know everyone is there." Ethan turned his head slightly toward him.
Cassian, who was moving behind them, listened to the city’s warning sounds.
"And the entire city’s army will be there in a few minutes."
"Then we don’t have to look for them." Lian said without worry.
Ethan stared at him for a moment and then gave a short laugh.
"At least your thinking is consistent."
"Returning to Ashfall is dangerous, but we have no other choice." He looked at the surrounding buildings.
The Cindari people were watching the escapees from windows and higher bridges.
Some stepped aside in fear, and others ran inside buildings to alert the guards.
"If we go directly to one of the city’s gates, the main forces will surround us before we arrive." Cassian continued.
"Ashfall at least has walls, a few limited entrances, and dozens of Awakeners."
"So we’re trapping ourselves in a district." Ethan said.
"We’re going somewhere with forces and support. Fighting an army alone isn’t easy." Lian answered. Even he wasn’t sure he could defeat all of them alone.
But with the help of the other Awakeners, defeating this city’s army shouldn’t be a problem.
Aren, who understood part of their conversation through the System’s translation, raised his head for a moment and looked at Lian.
Escaping from the lowest prison of the Rootspire apparently wasn’t the end of his insane behavior.
Lian wasn’t only not fleeing to a safe place, but he was heading toward an area where all his companions were gathered, and the enemy could easily surround them.
However, after seeing how Lian had broken through five security gates and captured the prison Warden with his own chains, Aren could no longer confidently say this decision was wrong.
Perhaps this young human really knew what he was doing, or perhaps his power allowed him to move forward even without knowing.
But he didn’t care either. Just being free again was enough for him. Besides, he could see more humans after a long time.
At the same time, inside Ashfall Ward’s temporary council building, a heavy atmosphere prevailed.
Several maps were open on the main table.
One was the general map of Emberroot that the Cindari had given Rindo upon entering the city.
Another map only showed the streets, bridges, and defensive paths of Ashfall.
The list of hunting groups, potion inventory, food amounts, and the wounded were also beside them.
Rindo stood at the head of the table.
He had placed both his hands on the wooden surface and was thinking about the Main Quest panel.
Thousands of problems had occurred all at once, and he had no idea which one to deal with first...
